# Lumiose

> Lumiose is a web framework for everything from static sites and SPAs to full-stack apps: TSX with scoped CSS built in, signals, and 0 kB of JavaScript until a page needs it.

These docs match lumiose 0.4.0. Installed projects have them in `node_modules/lumiose/docs`;
`lumiose docs <topic>` prints one and `lumiose explain <code>` explains a diagnostic.

<!-- source: README.md -->

# Lumiose docs

> Lumiose is a web framework for everything from static sites and SPAs to full-stack apps: TSX with scoped CSS built in, signals, and 0 kB of JavaScript until a page needs it.

**Feels like React. Runs like vanilla JS.** Components live in `.stsx` files (TSX plus raw-CSS `<style>` blocks), are set up once and
update through signals, and every route picks its rendering mode: static, server, islands or SPA.

These docs ship inside the package, so they always match the installed version. Read them from
`node_modules/lumiose/docs`, or from the terminal:

```sh
lumiose docs                    # this index
lumiose docs signals            # a topic, by name or path (concepts/signals)
lumiose docs "bind:value"       # search, when no topic matches
lumiose explain LUM2001         # the long-form explanation of a diagnostic
lumiose docs signals --format json
```

Every concept page has the same sections, in order: **Concept**, **API**, **Example**, **Common
mistakes** and **Related diagnostics**. Reference pages list every export with its signature. The
Coming from guides map another framework's concepts to the current API (they are not migration
guides) and share one outline: **Mental model**, **From _framework_ to Lumiose** (a table from its
APIs to Lumiose's), **What has no equivalent** (and what to do instead), **Example**, **Common
mistakes** and **Related**.

## Start here

- [Getting started](getting-started.md): Create a project, configure TypeScript and Vite, and render a first component.
- [Stability](stability.md): What 0.x allows, the 1.0 criteria and the API freeze, supported Node.js versions and browsers, and who maintains Lumiose.
- [When not to use Lumiose](when-not-to-use.md): The cases where another framework is the better choice today, and what to use instead.

## Coming from

- [React](coming-from/react.md): Hooks mapped to signals, React 19's forms and server components mapped to form actions and islands, what goes away (the rules of hooks, dependency arrays, stale closures, memoization) and the mistakes React habits cause.
- [Next.js](coming-from/nextjs.md): The App Router mapped to Lumiose: the same route file names, server components by default, `client:*` islands instead of `"use client"`, form actions instead of server actions, metadata, caching and rendering modes.
- [React Router](coming-from/react-router.md): Framework mode mapped to Lumiose: file routes instead of `routes.ts`, async components instead of loaders, form actions and `submit()` instead of actions and fetchers, middleware, the document and custom servers.
- [Solid](coming-from/solid.md): The closest model, so mostly differences: signal and store APIs, props destructuring, control flow as plain JSX, async components instead of resources, `.stsx` styles, islands, and SolidStart and Solid Router mapped to file routes, endpoints and form actions.

## Concepts

- [Components](concepts/components.md): Setup-once function components, props, children, refs and the `.stsx`/`.tsx`/`.ts` file types.
- [Signals and reactivity](concepts/signals.md): `signal`, `computed`, `effect`, `store`, owners, context and scheduling.
- [Sharing state](concepts/state.md): Component, context and module-scope state; recipes for stores with actions, families, persisted signals, external stores and state shared by islands.
- [JSX](concepts/jsx.md): Bindings, compiled idioms (`.map`, ternaries), `class`, `style`, events, `bind:`, `attach` and `ref`.
- [Styles](concepts/styles.md): Raw-CSS `<style>` blocks scoped by placement, `<style global>`, JS values in styles (`$name`), build-time math and runtime values.
- [Async components](concepts/async.md): `async` components on server and client, `<Suspense>`, `<ErrorBoundary>`, re-runs and in-flight state.
- [Islands](concepts/islands.md): `client:*` directives, serializable props, slots and server-only boundaries.
- [Routing](concepts/routing.md): File routes, layouts, params, typed `href()`, error pages and the SPA router.
- [Internationalization](concepts/i18n.md): Locale prefixes, per-page locale declarations, `locale()`, locale-aware `href()`, `hreflang` and canonical links, detection on entry.
- [Data and actions](concepts/data-and-actions.md): Read data with async components, serve endpoints, mutate with form actions and `submit()`.
- [Server](concepts/server.md): Request context, middleware, cookies, env, redirects and error helpers.
- [Rendering modes](concepts/rendering-modes.md): `static`, `server` and `spa` routes: choosing a mode, combining modes, islands and `<Suspense>`, patterns close to partial prerendering, a comparison with Astro islands, prerendered SPA pages, shell-first streaming, hydration and the build.
- [SVG imports](concepts/svg.md): `import Icon from "./icon.svg?component"` as an inline, optimised component, from your project or a package; `title`, `currentColor`, and Vite's own `.svg` imports.
- [Markdown and HTML imports](concepts/content.md): `.md` and `.html` files as static components; GFM, heading ids, frontmatter and its hook, scoped `<style>`, client `<script>`.
- [Head and document](concepts/head.md): `<Title>`, `<Meta>`, `<Head>` and a custom `document.stsx`.
- [Compiler and diagnostics](concepts/compiler.md): What the compiler does with `.stsx`/`.tsx`, and how `LUMxxxx` diagnostics work.
- [Dev tools](concepts/dev-tools.md): The in-page inspector of `lumiose dev` (Alt+Shift+L): the component tree with props and source locations, signals with their dependents and last write, islands with their hydration state, why something updated, and Alt+click to open any element's source.
- [Testing](concepts/testing.md): Component tests with Vitest and Testing Library (queries and user-event), server rendering as strings, and end-to-end tests with Playwright.
- [Security](concepts/security.md): A strict Content Security Policy with nonces and hashes (`lumiose({ csp: "strict" })`, `cspNonce()`), and the cross-site form check.

## Guides

- [Authentication with Better Auth](guides/auth.md): Email and password accounts with Better Auth and Prisma: the handler as an endpoint, the session in middleware, protected pages, form actions and the browser client in an island.
- [Icons with Lucide](guides/icons.md): Lucide's SVG files (`lucide-static`), or any SVG icon set, as inline components through `?component` imports: install, size, colour and stroke with CSS, labels, and why not `lucide-react`.
- [i18n with Paraglide JS and i18next](guides/i18n.md): Messages in server pages and islands with Paraglide JS (compile-time) or i18next (a `t` per request), keyed by `locale()`; a language switcher on `alternates()` that updates the detection cookie; `hreflang`, canonical and `site` for search engines.
- [Realtime](guides/realtime.md): Server-sent events from an endpoint to an island's `EventSource`, WebSockets with `ws` on the Node adapter's server, proxy configs and per-platform notes.
- [Payments with Stripe Checkout](guides/stripe.md): Checkout started from a form action, a return page, and webhooks received by a `route.ts` endpoint that verifies Stripe's signature.
- [Content from Sanity](guides/sanity.md): Sanity content read in async components and prerendered, draft previews on a server-rendered route behind a secret, and static rebuilds from Sanity's webhook.
- [Tracing with OpenTelemetry](guides/opentelemetry.md): Spans for requests, their phases and client navigations from the instrumentation files, a relay for the browser's spans, and setups for OpenObserve, SigNoz and Datadog.
- [Error reporting with Sentry](guides/sentry.md): Server errors from `onRequestError` and browser errors from `onError` reported to Sentry, with the source maps of both builds uploaded by Sentry's Vite plugin.
- [Product analytics with PostHog](guides/posthog.md): PostHog started in `src/instrumentation.client.ts`, page views on MPA pages and SPA navigations (`afterNavigate`), events from islands and feature flags evaluated on the server.
- [Editors](guides/editors.md): The language server in Neovim and Helix (file type, root markers, the server command), what works in Zed today, and GitHub highlighting through `.gitattributes`.
- [Web components](guides/web-components.md): Custom elements and web-component libraries: defining them in the browser, typing them in JSX, properties versus attributes (React 19's rule), events with `on:`, server rendering, and the Custom Elements Everywhere score (100).

## Deploy

- [Overview](deploy/README.md): What `lumiose build` writes, the production settings (`PORT`, `HOST`, `ORIGIN`, `LUMIOSE_SECRET`) and how far each target's guide was verified.
- [Docker](deploy/docker.md): A multi-stage Dockerfile: `node:24-alpine`, production dependencies only, a non-root user and a health check.
- [VPS](deploy/vps.md): `@lumiose/adapter-node` under systemd or pm2, behind Caddy or nginx; what the adapter already does for compression and caching.
- [Coolify](deploy/coolify.md): Deploy from the Dockerfile with Coolify's Dockerfile build pack.
- [Cloudflare Workers](deploy/cloudflare.md): `@lumiose/adapter-cloudflare`: the Worker, static assets, bindings as `ctx.platform.env`.
- [Vercel](deploy/vercel.md): `@lumiose/adapter-vercel`: the Build Output API, with a Node.js or Edge function.
- [Netlify](deploy/netlify.md): `@lumiose/adapter-netlify`: the site and a Netlify Function.
- [Bun](deploy/bun.md): `bun dist/server/entry.js`, static files included.
- [Deno](deploy/deno.md): `deno serve dist/server/entry.js`, static files included.
- [Fly.io](deploy/fly.md): The Docker image on Fly Machines, behind Fly's proxy.
- [Render](deploy/render.md): A Node web service (or the Docker image), and static sites.
- [Railway](deploy/railway.md): The Node adapter with Railway's Node builder, or the Docker image.
- [Static hosts](deploy/static.md): A fully prerendered site on Cloudflare, Netlify, GitHub Pages, S3 with CloudFront or any file server.
- [AWS Lambda](deploy/aws-lambda.md): A handler from Lambda's events to the server build's `fetch`.

## Reference

- [`lumiose`: reactivity](reference/reactivity.md): `signal`, `computed`, `effect`, `batch`, `flush`, `untrack`, `store`, owners, context (`createContext`, `useContext`), `useId`, `getAbortSignal`, `isPending`, `isBusy`, `resource`.
- [`lumiose`: components](reference/components.md): `Suspense`, `ErrorBoundary`, `Portal`, `Dynamic`, `ref`, `Head`, `Title`, `Meta`, `ViewTransition`, `viewTransition`.
- [`lumiose`: app layer](reference/app.md): `fetchJSON`, `submit`, `isSubmitting`, `actionData`, `invalidate`, `fail`, `redirect`, `notFound`, `error`, `href`, request APIs and types.
- [`lumiose`: server rendering](reference/server.md): `renderToStream`, `renderToString` and the `lumiose/server` subpath.
- [`lumiose/dom`](reference/dom.md): `render`, the compiler-runtime contract, `hydrate` (`lumiose/dom/hydrate`) and the island loader (`lumiose/dom/loader`).
- [`lumiose/router`](reference/router.md): The SPA router: `Link`, `navigate`, `isNavigating`, `searchParams`, `beforeNavigate`/`afterNavigate` and reactive route state.
- [`@lumiose/vite`](reference/vite.md): The Vite plugin and its options.
- [JSX types and tsconfig](reference/jsx.md): `lumiose/jsx-runtime`, `lumiose/env` and the required `tsconfig.json`.
- [CLI](reference/cli.md): `lumiose dev`, `build`, `preview`, `check`, `typegen`, `routes`, `lint`, `fmt`, `docs`, `explain`, `agents init` and `mcp`; `--format json` and exit codes.
- [MCP server](reference/mcp.md): `lumiose mcp` for coding agents: docs, `check` with fixes, routes, components, compiler output, rendered HTML and dev logs.
- [`@lumiose/adapter-node`](reference/adapter-node.md): `createServer`, `createHandler` and `createStaticHandler`: serve a build with Node.
- [Server build](reference/server-entry.md): `dist/server/entry.js`: `export default { fetch(request, platform?) }`, `ctx.platform`, `createHandler` and `config`; run it with Bun or Deno.
- [`@lumiose/query`](reference/query.md): TanStack Query for Lumiose (`useQuery`, `useMutation`, `useQueryClient`, `QueryClientProvider`), and when to use it instead of `fetchJSON`.

## Diagnostics

- [All diagnostics](errors/README.md): Every `LUMxxxx` code with its explanation and fix.

## Status of this version

Lumiose is pre-1.0, so APIs may change in any minor version ([Stability](stability.md)). The docs describe the
designed API; where this version does not implement something yet, the page says so in a
**Status** note. In short:

| Area                                                                                  | Status                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Signals, components, JSX compilation, client rendering (`lumiose/dom`)                | Available                                                                  |
| Async components, `<Suspense>`, `<ErrorBoundary>`                                     | Available                                                                  |
| Server rendering (`renderToStream`), shell-first streaming, head                      | Available                                                                  |
| File routes, typegen, request handler, middleware, actions, `fetchJSON`               | Available, with `lumiose dev`, `lumiose build` and `@lumiose/adapter-node` |
| `<style>` blocks                                                                      | Available                                                                  |
| Islands hydration and the island loader                                               | Available                                                                  |
| SPA mode and the SPA router (`lumiose/router`)                                        | Available, with `lumiose dev` and `lumiose build`                          |
| `lumiose check`, `lint`, `fmt`, `docs`, `explain`, language server, VS Code extension | Available                                                                  |
| `lumiose mcp`                                                                         | Available                                                                  |
| `create-lumiose` (templates `minimal`, `static`, `ssr`, `spa`), `lumiose agents init` | Available                                                                  |
| Testing: Vitest, Testing Library and Playwright                                       | Available, with stock tools (no adapter package)                           |

<!-- source: getting-started.md -->

# Getting started

> Set up a Lumiose project with TypeScript and Vite 8, write a first `.stsx` component and check it with `lumiose check`.

## Requirements

- Node.js 24 or later.
- TypeScript (`typescript@^7`). Lumiose uses stock `tsc`, with no TypeScript plugins.
- Vite 8.

## Create a project

```sh
pnpm create lumiose my-app --template ssr   # or: minimal, static, spa
cd my-app && pnpm install && pnpm dev
```

| Template  | `lumiose({ mode })` | What you get                                                 |
| --------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `minimal` | `static`            | One page.                                                    |
| `static`  | `static`            | A layout, pages, a blog with `staticPaths()` and a 404 page. |
| `ssr`     | `server`            | Streaming, a form action, a JSON endpoint and a Node server. |
| `spa`     | `spa`               | Pages and a persistent layout rendered in the browser.       |

Every template also sets `lumiose({ csp: "strict" })`, so new projects start with a strict Content
Security Policy: nonces on pages rendered per request, hashes on prerendered ones, and no inline
scripts or styles that Lumiose did not write ([Security](concepts/security.md)). Remove the option
to turn it off; projects set up by hand, as below, start without it.

Every project starts agent-ready: `AGENTS.md` (with a Lumiose section pointing at these docs),
`CLAUDE.md` referencing it, the `lumiose` skill in `.claude/skills/lumiose`, and `.gitattributes`
highlighting `.stsx` as TSX. In an existing project, `lumiose agents init` writes the same files
(re-run it after upgrading Lumiose; it only touches its own parts). With `--mcp`, both also register
the [Lumiose MCP server](reference/mcp.md) for Claude Code (`.mcp.json`) and Codex
(`.codex/config.toml`). Run `create-lumiose --help` for the options (`--yes`, `--force`, `--mcp`,
`--format json`).

The rest of this page sets a project up by hand, step by step.

## 1. Install

```sh
pnpm add lumiose
pnpm add -D @lumiose/vite @lumiose/cli vite typescript
```

Every Lumiose package shares one version. A project starts with three:

- `lumiose`: the runtime your app imports (signals, the DOM and server renderers, the router, the
  app runtime). It has no dependencies.
- `@lumiose/vite`: the Vite plugin, plus the dev server and the production build behind
  `lumiose dev` and `lumiose build`.
- `@lumiose/cli`: the `lumiose` command (`dev`, `build`, `preview`, `check`, `lint`, `fmt`, `docs`,
  `mcp`, …).

`@lumiose/compiler` (the native compiler) comes with them. Add
[`@lumiose/adapter-node`](reference/adapter-node.md) to preview a build (`lumiose preview`) and to
serve it on Node in production.

## 2. Configure TypeScript

`tsconfig.json` extends the tsconfig that Lumiose generates (`lumiose check` prints this file when it
is missing, and `lumiose agents init` writes it):

```jsonc
{
  // Lumiose's compiler options, shadow TSX and route types. lumiose dev, build, check and typegen
  // write the generated file; add your own options below.
  "extends": "./.lumiose/tsconfig.generated.json",
}
```

- `.lumiose/tsconfig.generated.json` sets `jsx: "preserve"` (the Lumiose compiler transforms JSX, not
  TypeScript), `jsxImportSource: "lumiose"`, bundler module resolution, `strict`, `types:
  ["lumiose/env"]`, and the `rootDirs` and `include` entries below. Lumiose keeps it current.
- `.lumiose/shadow`: TypeScript cannot read `.stsx`, so Lumiose writes a masked copy of each one (a
  _shadow file_, same line and column offsets) and `import "./X.stsx"` resolves to it.
- `.lumiose/types`: generated route types (`lumiose typegen`, run by `lumiose check`).
- `lumiose dev`, `build`, `check` and `typegen` write `.lumiose/`. Before a bare `tsc` in a fresh
  clone, run `lumiose typegen`. See [tsconfig](./reference/jsx.md#tsconfigjson).

Add `.lumiose/` to `.gitignore`, and `*.stsx linguist-language=TSX` to `.gitattributes` so GitHub
highlights `.stsx` files.

## 3. Configure Vite

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import lumiose from "@lumiose/vite";
import { defineConfig } from "vite";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [lumiose()],
});
```

## 4. Write a component

```stsx check file=Counter.stsx
// src/Counter.stsx
import { signal } from "lumiose";

export function Counter({ start = 0 }: { start?: number }) {
  const count = signal(start);

  return (
    <button class={{ hot: count() > 5 }} onClick={() => count.update((n) => n + 1)}>
      Clicked {count()} times
    </button>
  );
}

<style>
  button { font: inherit; padding: 0.5rem 1rem; }
  .hot { color: crimson; }
</style>
```

- The function body runs **once**. `count()` reads the signal; JSX that reads it updates on its own.
- The `<style>` block at the end of the file is scoped to this file: it styles the components
  defined here, and nothing else. One block per file, after the components, is the convention;
  [Styles](./concepts/styles.md) covers blocks nested in JSX.

## 5. Mount it

```html
<!-- index.html -->
<div id="app"></div>
<script type="module" src="/src/main.tsx"></script>
```

```tsx check file=main.tsx
// src/main.tsx
import { render } from "lumiose/dom";
import { Counter } from "./Counter.stsx";

render(() => <Counter start={1} />, document.getElementById("app")!);
```

Run `pnpm vite` and open the printed URL.

## 6. Check the project

```sh
pnpm lumiose check        # typegen + shadow files + tsc + Lumiose diagnostics
pnpm lumiose lint         # oxlint, .stsx included
pnpm lumiose fmt          # oxfmt for the TSX, plus each <style> block
```

`lumiose check` maps every TypeScript error in a shadow file back to the `.stsx` line and column.
`--format json` prints machine-readable diagnostics; every Lumiose diagnostic has a stable code that
`lumiose explain <code>` explains.

## Editor

Install the Lumiose VS Code extension (`lumiose-vscode`). It adds the `stsx` language and runs the
Lumiose language server, which proxies TypeScript for `.ts`, `.tsx` and `.stsx` files and adds:

- CSS features inside `<style>` blocks;
- class completion, definitions and rename that follow placement: the blocks enclosing the
  cursor (never a sibling subtree's), the file's, and the project's global classes (`<style global>`
  blocks and imported global `.css` files);
- `var(--…)` completion of every custom property declared in the project, with its value;
- descriptions of `<style global>` and of Lumiose attributes (`client:*`, `bind:*`, `on:*`, `attach`,
  `ref`, `key`), and the snippets `comp`, `acomp`, `route` and `island`;
- the compiler's diagnostics, with the project-wide ones (`LUM4003` server-only imports in the
  client graph, `LUM3012` unread custom properties) that follow the other files' edits;
- hovers on JSX expressions with their execution contract: tracked (re-runs when the signals it
  reads change, which it lists), once, untracked or deferred, and the runtime helper that runs it.

The extension bundles the server (it runs on VS Code's own Node.js) and uses the project's
`typescript`; install `@lumiose/language-server` as a dev dependency only to pin the server to your
`lumiose` version. See [Compiler and diagnostics](concepts/compiler.md). Neovim and Helix run the
same server: [Editors](guides/editors.md).

## Next

- [Components](concepts/components.md) and [Signals](concepts/signals.md): the component model.
- [Styles](concepts/styles.md): scoping by placement, JS values in styles and build-time math.
- [Rendering modes](concepts/rendering-modes.md): server-first pages with islands.

<!-- source: stability.md -->

# Stability

> What Lumiose promises today and at 1.0: when releases may break, what 1.0 needs, what the API freeze covers, the supported runtimes and browsers, and who maintains it.

## Before 1.0

Lumiose is 0.x. **Any minor release may break** the API (0.4 to 0.5), and until real usage starts,
breaking changes ship without migration paths: no deprecation aliases, no compatibility shims and
no upgrade guides. The docs always describe the current API only, and the changelog lists every
change.

That rule ends at the first known **external production app** or at 1.0, whichever comes first.
From then on, every breaking change comes with a migration path.

No external production app is known yet, so the rule above is in force.

## External production apps

An external production app is an app in production that:

- is on the opt-in [Used by](https://itsjavi.com/lumiose/showcase/#used-by) list, added through a
  pull request with its URL;
- is not run by the Lumiose maintainer (the maintainer's own sites, such as itsjavi.com, do not
  count).

Lumiose never collects telemetry: the Used by list is the only usage signal.

## The 1.0 criteria

Lumiose becomes 1.0 when all of these hold:

1. **The 1.0 essentials are done**: deploy targets and self-hosting, `useId`, head defaults, the
   authentication and realtime guides, View Transitions, the Next.js-aligned route files, i18n
   routing and a smoother dev reload (milestone M9 in the project's backlog).
2. **The extension points are done**: folder middleware with `ctx.route`, a client entry hook,
   router lifecycle hooks, per-instance form submissions, server and client instrumentation, a dev
   handler for custom servers, and the Coming from guides (milestone M10).
3. **The API is frozen** (below).
4. **Three external production apps** are on the Used by list.
5. **An external security review** by an independent reviewer has been done.

## What the freeze covers

From 1.0, everything public follows semantic versioning: only a major release breaks it.

- The exports of `lumiose` and of every `@lumiose/*` package released in lockstep with it.
- The file conventions: `src/routes` and its special files, `src/document.stsx`,
  `src/middleware.ts` and the other project files the framework reads.
- The config options of `lumiose()` and the adapters.
- The CLI commands and flags.
- The meaning of each `LUMxxxx` diagnostic code. Codes are never reused.

`@lumiose/ui` keeps its own 0.x versions and joins the freeze at its own 1.0.

**After 1.0, new APIs ship with an `unstable_` prefix** (`unstable_name`) until a minor release
promotes them, as React Router does. There are no `unstable_` names before 1.0, and no experimental
config flags.

## Runtimes

Lumiose runs on **Node.js 24 and later**. Node.js 22 is not supported (it reaches end of life in
April 2027); the [Node.js release schedule](https://nodejs.org/en/about/previous-releases) lists
the dates of each line. The server build also runs on Bun, Deno and the platforms of the
[deploy adapters](deploy/README.md).

## Browsers

The browser code targets the browsers covered by
[Baseline widely available](https://web.dev/baseline), re-checked at each release. A newer platform
feature is used only with a fallback (View Transitions and speculation rules are progressive: other
browsers navigate normally).

## Security

Until 1.0, only the latest minor release receives security fixes. Report vulnerabilities privately,
as described in the [security policy](https://github.com/itsjavi/lumiose/blob/main/SECURITY.md).

## Maintenance

- **Who:** Lumiose is designed and maintained by one person, Javi Aguilar
  ([itsjavi](https://github.com/itsjavi)). A second human maintainer is a goal; it is not a 1.0
  criterion.
- **Releases:** there is no fixed schedule. A minor release ships when a batch of work is ready
  (0.1 to 0.4 shipped within a week in October 2026), and security fixes ship in a new release of
  the latest minor. `lumiose` and the `@lumiose/*` packages are released in lockstep, with one
  version number.
- **Intent:** to reach 1.0 on the criteria above and to keep Lumiose maintained after it, under the
  stability rules on this page. Work is planned in the open, in the repository's backlog.

If these terms do not fit your project yet, read [When not to use Lumiose](when-not-to-use.md).

<!-- source: when-not-to-use.md -->

# When not to use Lumiose

> The cases where another framework is the better choice today, and what to use instead: projects that depend on the React ecosystem, teams that need long-term stability guarantees now, and teams that cannot take a pre-1.0 dependency with one maintainer.

Lumiose fits static sites, server-rendered apps, islands and SPAs that you write in TSX and want
to ship with little JavaScript. It is not the right choice for every project. If one of the cases
below describes yours, pick the alternative it names; people and coding agents should not
recommend Lumiose there.

## The project depends on the React ecosystem

Lumiose has no React interop: React components and hooks do not run in it, and there is no
compatibility layer and no React islands package. If the project needs React component libraries
(MUI, Radix and shadcn/ui, Mantine, Chakra), React-only libraries (react-hook-form, the React
adapters of TanStack Table or Virtual, React Three Fiber), React Native code sharing, or a team that
must stay on React, it would have to rebuild those parts.

**Use instead:** a React framework. Next.js or React Router (framework mode) for apps; Astro with
React islands for content sites that need a few React components.

**What Lumiose offers instead:** native elements (`<dialog>`, `popover`, `<details>`), web
components and framework-agnostic libraries. The [Coming from React](coming-from/react.md) guide lists what has no equivalent.

## The team needs long-term stability guarantees today

Lumiose is 0.x. Any minor release may break the API, and until the first known external production
app (or 1.0), breaking changes ship without migration paths. There is no long-term support line:
only the latest minor gets security fixes. The full terms are on the [Stability](stability.md)
page.

**Use instead:** a framework past 1.0 with a published support policy: Next.js, React Router,
Astro, SvelteKit or Nuxt.

**When to look again:** once Lumiose reaches 1.0, its API is frozen under semantic versioning.

## The team cannot take a pre-1.0 dependency with one maintainer

Lumiose is designed and maintained by one person, with no company behind it. Security reports have
response targets, not guarantees (see the
[security policy](https://github.com/itsjavi/lumiose/blob/main/SECURITY.md)). If your organization
requires a vendor, a support contract, a team of maintainers or a minimum project age, Lumiose does
not meet that today.

**Use instead:** a framework with a company or a large team behind it: Next.js (Vercel), React
Router (Shopify), Astro, SvelteKit or Nuxt.

**When to look again:** when the [Stability](stability.md) page names a second maintainer, or when
Lumiose reaches 1.0, whichever matters to your organization.

## Related

- [Stability](stability.md): what 0.x allows, the 1.0 criteria and the maintenance statement.
- [Coming from React](coming-from/react.md), [Next.js](coming-from/nextjs.md),
  [React Router](coming-from/react-router.md) and [Solid](coming-from/solid.md): what maps and what
  has no equivalent.

<!-- source: coming-from/react.md -->

# Coming from React

> Lumiose JSX reads like React, but components run once and never re-render, render on the server by default, and ship JavaScript only where a page asks for it.

This page maps React 19 habits to Lumiose's current API. The linked pages have the full rules.
Using a React framework too? [Coming from Next.js](nextjs.md) and
[Coming from React Router](react-router.md) cover its side.

## Mental model

In React, a state change re-runs the component function. Hooks keep their state between runs
by call order, and effects list their dependencies so React knows when to re-run them.

In Lumiose, the component body runs **once per instance**: it creates signals, effects and
handlers, then returns JSX. JSX expressions that read signals compile to bindings that update
their part of the DOM in place. When a signal changes, only the bindings, computeds and effects
that read it run again. Local variables are ordinary variables, and a closure reads the current
value because it calls `count()` when it runs ([Components](../concepts/components.md),
[Signals](../concepts/signals.md)).

The exception is an **async component**: when a prop or signal read in its body changes, the body
runs again, and signals created in the body start fresh ([Async components](../concepts/async.md)).

**Server first.** Every component renders on the server unless a page says otherwise, as React
Server Components do. A page ships no JavaScript until a usage site adds a `client:*` directive
(`<Clock client:load />` makes that one instance an [island](../concepts/islands.md)) or the route
is an `spa` route, whose whole subtree hydrates and navigates on the client
([Rendering modes](../concepts/rendering-modes.md)). There is no `"use client"` file boundary: the
same component is static on one page and interactive on another.

### What goes away

- **The rules of hooks.** `signal`, `computed`, `effect`, `onCleanup` and `useContext` are ordinary
  functions: call them in conditions, loops and helper functions. Nothing depends on call order.
- **Dependency arrays.** Effects and computeds subscribe to the signals they read, and collect them
  again on every run, so a dependency cannot be missing, and a branch that stops reading a signal
  stops depending on it.
- **Stale closures.** A handler or a timer callback calls `count()` when it runs, so it gets the
  current value. There is no closure from an older render to capture.
- **Memoization.** `useMemo`, `useCallback` and `React.memo` exist to limit re-renders, and there
  are none. Use `computed` only to cache an expensive derivation.
- **Context re-renders.** A context change does not re-render its consumers: provide a signal or a
  store, and only the code that reads it updates.

## From React to Lumiose

| React                                                   | Lumiose                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `const [count, setCount] = useState(0)`                 | `const count = signal(0)`: read `count()`, write `count.set(1)` or `count.update((n) => n + 1)`.                                                                                                       |
| `useReducer(reducer, init)`                             | A `store()` plus the functions that change it ([a store with actions](../concepts/state.md#a-store-with-actions-zustand-style)).                                                                       |
| `useMemo(() => a * b, [a, b])`                          | `computed(() => a() * b())`, or a plain function `() => a() * b()` for cheap derivations.                                                                                                              |
| `useCallback(fn, deps)`, `React.memo(Component)`        | Not needed: functions are created once and components don't re-render.                                                                                                                                 |
| `useEffect(fn, [deps])`                                 | `effect(fn)`: it tracks what it reads. Return a cleanup, as in React.                                                                                                                                  |
| `useEffect(fn, [])`                                     | `onMount(fn)`: runs once, untracked, after mount. It may return a cleanup.                                                                                                                             |
| `useLayoutEffect(fn, deps)`                             | `effect(fn)` or `onMount(fn)`: there is one kind of effect, and it runs after the DOM writes of the same flush.                                                                                        |
| Cleanup returned from `useEffect`, `AbortController`    | `onCleanup(fn)`, and `getAbortSignal()`, aborted when the owner is disposed or the effect re-runs.                                                                                                     |
| `useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null)`                        | `const input = ref<HTMLInputElement>()`, then `<input ref={input} />` and `input()?.focus()`.                                                                                                          |
| `useRef(value)` for a mutable value                     | A `let` variable in the component body: the body runs once.                                                                                                                                            |
| `<Ctx value={v}>` (`<Ctx.Provider>`), `useContext(Ctx)` | `<Ctx value={v}>`, `useContext(Ctx)`. The provider reads `value` once: provide a signal or a store for state that changes.                                                                             |
| `use(Context)`                                          | `useContext(Ctx)`, which may be called in conditions too.                                                                                                                                              |
| `use(promise)`, fetching in `useEffect`, TanStack Query | An `async` component that awaits `fetchJSON()` or `query()` ([Async components](../concepts/async.md)), or [`@lumiose/query`](../reference/query.md) for client-side polling and retries.              |
| `<Suspense>`, error boundary classes                    | `<Suspense fallback={…}>` and `<ErrorBoundary fallback={(error, reset) => …}>`.                                                                                                                        |
| `useTransition`, `isPending`                            | A re-run of an async component keeps the old UI until it resolves: `isPending()` inside it, and `isBusy()` for anything in flight.                                                                     |
| Server Components                                       | Every component, on `static` and `server` routes: it may be `async` and read server-only modules (`*.server.ts`).                                                                                      |
| `"use client"`                                          | A `client:*` directive where the component is used (`client:load`, `client:idle`, `client:visible`, …), or an `spa` route. Props must be serializable, as in React.                                    |
| `"use server"` functions, `<form action={fn}>`          | Form actions: `export const actions = { save(ctx) {…} }` in the page and `<form method="post" action="?/save">`, which works without JavaScript ([Data and actions](../concepts/data-and-actions.md)). |
| `useActionState(fn, initial)`                           | `actionData<typeof actions>()`, the last result of the page's actions, or the result that `await submit(event)` resolves to.                                                                           |
| `useActionState` per form instance                      | `submission<typeof actions.save>()` in the form's component: its own `isSubmitting()`, `result()` and `error()`, with `onSubmit={save.submit}` ([Data and actions](../concepts/data-and-actions.md)).  |
| `useFormStatus()`                                       | `isSubmitting()`, or `isSubmitting("save")` for one named action.                                                                                                                                      |
| `useOptimistic(state, update)`                          | `optimistic(source)`, with `.update(fn, submit(event))` ([optimistic updates](../concepts/data-and-actions.md)).                                                                                       |
| `<title>`, `<meta>`, `<link>` rendered in a component   | `<Title>`, `<Meta>` and `<Head>`: the deepest wins, and they work in server components too ([Head and document](../concepts/head.md)).                                                                 |
| `<ViewTransition>`, `startTransition` around it         | `<ViewTransition name? enter? exit?>`, and the update in `viewTransition(() => …)` ([reference](../reference/components.md#viewtransition)).                                                           |
| `useId()`, `identifierPrefix`                           | `useId()`, and `idPrefix` on `render()` and `renderToStream()` ([useId](../reference/reactivity.md#useid)).                                                                                            |
| `useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, get)`                  | A signal set from the store's `subscribe` ([an external store](../concepts/state.md#an-external-store-zustandvanilla-a-jotai-store-redux)).                                                            |
| `createPortal(children, node)`                          | `<Portal mount={node}>`.                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `createRoot(el).render(<App />)`, `hydrateRoot`         | `render(() => <App />, el)` from `lumiose/dom`; islands and `spa` routes hydrate on their own ([`lumiose/dom`](../reference/dom.md)).                                                                  |
| `{items.map((item) => <Row key={item.id} />)}`          | The same, with `items()`. It compiles to a keyed list; `key` is optional ([JSX](../concepts/jsx.md)).                                                                                                  |
| `className`, `htmlFor`, `style={{ fontWeight: 600 }}`   | `class`, `for`, `style={{ "font-weight": 600 }}` (kebab-case keys).                                                                                                                                    |
| `dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: html }}`            | `innerHTML={html}`.                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `onChange` on a text input (fires on every keystroke)   | `onInput`, or `bind:value={signal}`. Handlers get native events, so `onChange` fires when the value is committed.                                                                                      |
| CSS Modules, CSS-in-JS                                  | A `<style>` block in the `.stsx` file, scoped by where it is placed ([Styles](../concepts/styles.md)).                                                                                                 |

## What has no equivalent

| React                                               | Instead                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| React component libraries (Radix, shadcn/ui, MUI)   | No React interop. Use native elements (`<dialog>`, `popover`, `<details>`), web components (with `on:event` listeners for their custom events) or framework-agnostic libraries.                       |
| `React.lazy()`                                      | None. Islands load their module when they hydrate, and `spa` routes load a chunk per page and layout; `<Dynamic component={…}>` renders a component chosen at runtime.                                |
| `useDeferredValue`, transition priorities           | None: updates are fine-grained, not scheduled by priority. Debounce expensive input in the handler.                                                                                                   |
| `React.Children`, `cloneElement`                    | None: `children` is lazy and inserted once. Take a render prop (`renderItem: (item) => JSX.Element`) when a component needs to render content several times.                                          |
| Class components and lifecycle methods              | Function components; `onMount`, `onCleanup` and `effect`.                                                                                                                                             |
| React DevTools (components, props, why it rendered) | The in-page inspector of `lumiose dev` (Alt+Shift+L): the component tree with props, signals and why a binding updated, islands, and Alt+click to the source ([Dev tools](../concepts/dev-tools.md)). |
| `<StrictMode>` double invocation                    | None: setup runs once by design. `lumiose check` reports the reactive mistakes that strict mode helps find in React (`LUM2xxx`).                                                                      |
| Context provided by the page, read inside an island | Islands start a new root, so page context does not reach them ([LUM4010](../errors/LUM4010.md)): pass a prop, or share scoped state with `defineState` ([Sharing state](../concepts/state.md)).       |

## Example

A clock that pauses, in React 19:

```tsx
function Clock({ label }: { label: string }) {
  const [now, setNow] = useState(Date.now());
  const [paused, setPaused] = useState(false);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (paused) return;
    const id = setInterval(() => setNow(Date.now()), 1000);
    return () => clearInterval(id);
  }, [paused]);

  const toggle = useCallback(() => setPaused((p) => !p), []);
  return (
    <>
      <title>{`${label}: ${new Date(now).toLocaleTimeString()}`}</title>
      <button onClick={toggle}>{paused ? "Resume" : "Pause"}</button>
    </>
  );
}
```

The same clock in Lumiose. The effect lists no dependencies, the handler needs no `useCallback`,
and the title updates in place:

```tsx check file=components/Clock.tsx
// src/components/Clock.tsx
import { Title, effect, signal } from "lumiose";

export function Clock({ label }: { label: string }) {
  const now = signal(Date.now());
  const paused = signal(false);

  // Reads paused(): re-runs, after clearing the interval, when it flips.
  effect(() => {
    if (paused()) return;
    const id = setInterval(() => now.set(Date.now()), 1000);
    return () => clearInterval(id);
  });

  return (
    <>
      <Title>{`${label}: ${new Date(now()).toLocaleTimeString()}`}</Title>
      <button onClick={() => paused.update((p) => !p)}>{paused() ? "Resume" : "Pause"}</button>
    </>
  );
}
```

On a page, the directive makes this one usage interactive; the rest of the page stays server
HTML without JavaScript:

```tsx check file=routes/clock/page.tsx
// src/routes/clock/page.tsx
import { Clock } from "../../components/Clock.tsx";

export default function ClockPage() {
  return (
    <main>
      <h1>Lunch break</h1>
      <Clock client:load label="Lunch" />
    </main>
  );
}
```

## Common mistakes

| React habit                                                 | What happens in Lumiose                                 | Instead                                                                                       |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `const doubled = count() * 2` in the body                   | Computed once, never updates.                           | `const doubled = () => count() * 2`, or `computed` ([LUM2001](../errors/LUM2001.md)).         |
| `if (!user()) return <Login />`                             | Checked once, at setup.                                 | `{user() ? <Profile /> : <Login />}` in the JSX ([LUM2003](../errors/LUM2003.md)).            |
| `count.set(…)` in the body                                  | A write during render.                                  | Write in handlers and effects ([LUM2002](../errors/LUM2002.md)).                              |
| `effect(() => b.set(a() * 2))` to sync state                | A frame of staleness and an extra flush.                | `const b = computed(() => a() * 2)`.                                                          |
| Reading a signal in an effect only to use its current value | The effect re-runs whenever that signal changes.        | `untrack(() => s())` or `s.peek()` reads without subscribing.                                 |
| Asserting right after a write in a test                     | Effects run after the DOM updates, not synchronously.   | Call `flush()` before asserting.                                                              |
| `{Card({ title })}`                                         | Skips the component's owner and props handling.         | `<Card title={title} />` ([LUM2004](../errors/LUM2004.md)).                                   |
| `{children}` inserted twice                                 | The second insert moves or re-creates the nodes.        | Take a render prop such as `renderItem: () => JSX.Element` ([LUM2005](../errors/LUM2005.md)). |
| A signal created and read in an async component's body      | The read re-runs the body, which re-creates the signal. | Read it in JSX, handlers or effects ([LUM2007](../errors/LUM2007.md)).                        |
| A module-scope signal written on the server                 | Shared by every request.                                | Component state, context or `defineState` ([LUM4008](../errors/LUM4008.md)).                  |
| An interactive component on a page without `client:*`       | It renders on the server, and its handlers never run.   | Add a directive at the usage site, or make the route `spa`.                                   |
| Passing a function or a class instance to an island         | Island props are serialized into the page.              | Pass plain data, and keep handlers inside the island ([LUM4002](../errors/LUM4002.md)).       |
| Setting `document.title` in an effect                       | It fights with `<Title>`.                               | Render `<Title>`.                                                                             |

Destructuring props is fine: `({ title })` compiles to reads of `props.title`, which stay reactive.
Copying a signal's value into a variable is what freezes it.

## Related

- [Components](../concepts/components.md): setup once, props, children and refs.
- [Signals and reactivity](../concepts/signals.md): `signal`, `computed`, `effect`, owners and scheduling.
- [JSX](../concepts/jsx.md): bindings, compiled `.map()` and ternaries, and the React prop names that differ.
- [Islands](../concepts/islands.md): `client:*` directives, serializable props and slots.
- [Sharing state](../concepts/state.md): context, `defineState`, and what replaces Jotai, Zustand and Valtio.
- [Async components](../concepts/async.md): data loading, re-runs, `<Suspense>` and `isPending()`.
- [Data and actions](../concepts/data-and-actions.md): form actions, `submit()`, `actionData()` and `optimistic()`.

<!-- source: coming-from/nextjs.md -->

# Coming from Next.js

> The Next.js App Router mapped to Lumiose: the same route file names, server components by default, `client:*` islands instead of `"use client"`, form actions instead of server actions, head components instead of metadata, and rendering modes instead of caching rules.

This page maps the Next.js App Router (Next.js 16) to Lumiose's current API. For components and
hooks, read [Coming from React](react.md) first; this page covers the framework.

## Mental model

**The files look the same.** Lumiose's routes follow the App Router names: a folder under
`src/routes` is a URL segment, and `page`, `layout`, `route`, `error` and `not-found` files give it
behavior, with `[slug]`, `[...slug]`, `[[...slug]]`, `(group)` and `_private` folders
([Routing](../concepts/routing.md)). The Next.js files Lumiose does not have (`loading`,
`template`, `default`, `global-error`, `@slot` and `(.)` folders) are errors
([LUM5002](../errors/LUM5002.md)), so they never silently do nothing.

**Components are server components by default.** On `static` and `server` routes every component
renders on the server, may be `async`, and ships no JavaScript. Instead of a `"use client"` file
boundary, the page that uses a component decides: `<LikeButton client:visible />` makes that one
instance an [island](../concepts/islands.md) that hydrates in the browser, and the same component
stays static elsewhere. Children passed to an island render on the server and stay there, as
server components passed to a client component do. An `spa` route hydrates its whole subtree and
navigates on the client.

**The rendering mode is explicit, per route.** Next.js decides between static and dynamic rendering
from what a page reads, and caching rules decide how long results live. In Lumiose a route says
`export const mode = "static" | "server" | "spa"` (or inherits it from a layout or the project).
`static` is the default: built once, served as files. A `static` page that reads the request fails
the build ([LUM5001](../errors/LUM5001.md)) instead of turning dynamic
([Rendering modes](../concepts/rendering-modes.md)).

**No RPC.** Server actions are functions the client calls. Lumiose has form actions: a page exports
`actions`, a `<form method="post" action="?/name">` posts to one and works without JavaScript, and
`submit()` posts it from an island. Other calls from the browser go to endpoints (`route.ts`)
([Data and actions](../concepts/data-and-actions.md)).

**Caching is per request and per page.** `fetchJSON()` and `query()` dedupe the same URL or key
within a request on the server, and cache it for the page in the browser (stale-while-revalidate).
There is no data cache shared across requests and no incremental regeneration: for fresh-but-cheap
pages, render on the `server` and send `cache-control` headers to a CDN.

## From Next.js to Lumiose

### Routes and files

| Next.js                                                            | Lumiose                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `app/`                                                             | `src/routes/`.                                                                                                                                              |
| `page.tsx`, `layout.tsx`, `route.ts`, `not-found.tsx`, `error.tsx` | The same names, as `.stsx` (with styles) or `.tsx`; `route.ts` for endpoints.                                                                               |
| `[slug]`, `[...slug]`, `[[...slug]]`, `(group)`, `_folder`         | The same, plus `[[slug]]` for one optional segment.                                                                                                         |
| `PageProps<"/blog/[slug]">`, `await params`                        | `PageProps<"/blog/[slug]">` and `LayoutProps<"/blog">` from `lumiose`; `params` is a plain object.                                                          |
| `searchParams` page prop                                           | `url().searchParams` on `server` routes; `searchParams()` from `lumiose/router` in islands and `spa` routes.                                                |
| Root `layout.tsx` with `<html>` and `<body>`                       | `src/document.stsx` owns `<html>`, `<head>` and `<body>` (optional); `src/routes/layout.stsx` wraps the pages.                                              |
| `loading.tsx`                                                      | `<Suspense fallback>` in the page or layout: on `server` routes, the content inside streams after the shell.                                                |
| `error.tsx`                                                        | `error.stsx`, a page rendered with `{ status, error }` inside its folder's layouts. For a retry in place, `<ErrorBoundary fallback={(error, reset) => …}>`. |
| `not-found.tsx`, `notFound()`                                      | `not-found.stsx` (the nearest wins), `notFound()`.                                                                                                          |
| `global-error.tsx`                                                 | The root `error.stsx`: when a layout itself fails, it renders without layouts.                                                                              |
| `generateStaticParams()`                                           | `staticPaths()`, returning `[{ params: { slug } }]`.                                                                                                        |
| Typed routes, `` `/blog/${slug}` `` in `<Link href>`               | `href("/blog/[slug]", { slug })`, type-checked against the routes.                                                                                          |

### Components and data

| Next.js                                                  | Lumiose                                                                                                                                            |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Server components, `async` components                    | Every component on `static` and `server` routes. Async components also work in islands and `spa` routes, in the browser.                           |
| `"use client"`                                           | A `client:*` directive at the usage site: `client:load`, `client:idle`, `client:visible`, `client:media`; or an `spa` route.                       |
| `dynamic(() => import(…), { ssr: false })`               | `client:only`: rendered in the browser only.                                                                                                       |
| Serializable props of client components                  | The same rule for island props, which also accept `Date`, `Map`, `Set`, `URL` and `BigInt` ([LUM4002](../errors/LUM4002.md)).                      |
| `import "server-only"`                                   | `*.server.ts` modules or `src/server/`: importing them from browser code is [LUM4003](../errors/LUM4003.md).                                       |
| `fetch()` in a server component, `React.cache()`         | `await fetchJSON(url)` or `await query(key, fn)` in the component: one request per URL or key per request; same-origin URLs are served in-process. |
| `"use cache"`, `cacheLife`, `cacheTag`, `unstable_cache` | No cross-request data cache: the request cache above, `cache-control` headers for a CDN, or a cache of your own in a server module.                |
| `revalidateTag(tag)`, `updateTag(tag)`                   | In the browser, `invalidate(["tag"])` refetches the `query()` entries whose key starts with it.                                                    |
| `revalidatePath(path)`, `router.refresh()`               | `invalidate()`: re-runs the page's async components on `spa` routes, reloads `static` and `server` pages.                                          |
| `cookies()`, `headers()` (async)                         | `cookies()` and `request().headers` (synchronous), on `server` routes and in middleware, endpoints and actions.                                    |
| `after(fn)`                                              | `ctx.platform.waitUntil(promise)`.                                                                                                                 |
| `process.env.SECRET`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_*`                    | `env("SECRET")` in server code; `import.meta.env.PUBLIC_*` in browser code.                                                                        |

### Mutations

| Next.js                                         | Lumiose                                                                                                                                                   |
| ----------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `"use server"` and `<form action={createPost}>` | `export const actions = { create(ctx) {…} }` and `<form method="post" action="?/create">`, which works without JavaScript.                                |
| A server action called from a client component  | `submit(target, { action: "/posts?/create" })` from an island (a form, a submit event, `FormData` or a record), or an endpoint called with `fetchJSON()`. |
| `useActionState(action, initial)`               | `actionData<typeof actions>()`, or the result that `await submit(event)` resolves to.                                                                     |
| `useFormStatus()`                               | `isSubmitting()`, or `isSubmitting("create")` for one action.                                                                                             |
| `useOptimistic()`                               | `optimistic(source)` with `.update(fn, submit(event))`.                                                                                                   |
| `redirect()` in a server action                 | `redirect(to)` in the action: 303 after a POST.                                                                                                           |
| Returning validation errors from an action      | `return fail(400, { errors })`: the page re-renders with that status, and `actionData()` holds the errors.                                                |

### Server and head

| Next.js                                                                                      | Lumiose                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Route handlers: `GET(request, { params })`, `NextResponse.json()`                            | `export const GET: Endpoint<"/api/posts/[id]"> = (ctx) => Response`, with `ctx.request`, `ctx.params`, `ctx.url`, `ctx.cookies`; `Response.json()`.                                                                                                                      |
| `middleware.ts` (`proxy.ts` in Next.js 16)                                                   | `src/middleware.ts`: `(ctx, next) => Response`. `NextResponse.next()` is `next()`; request data goes on `ctx.locals`.                                                                                                                                                    |
| `config.matcher`                                                                             | A `middleware.ts` in the route folder it covers (`src/routes/dashboard/middleware.ts` for `/dashboard/:path*`); it runs after `src/middleware.ts`. `ctx.route`, the matched pattern, serves other checks.                                                                |
| `instrumentation-client.ts`                                                                  | `src/instrumentation.client.ts`: runs once per page load, before islands hydrate and the SPA starts, top-level `await` included; pages without JavaScript load only it ([Islands](../concepts/islands.md#concept)).                                                      |
| `onRouterTransitionStart(url, type)` in `instrumentation-client.ts`, a client error reporter | Its `instrumentations` export wraps each navigation (`navigate`: start and end, with the route), `submit`, `fetch` and island `hydrate`; its `onError(error, info)` receives island, router and `submit()` errors ([Islands](../concepts/islands.md#concept)).           |
| `instrumentation.ts`: `register()`, `onRequestError()`                                       | `src/instrumentation.server.ts` with the same exports: `register()` runs once per server instance, `onRequestError(error, info)` gets `{ request, route, params, phase, digest }`; `instrumentations` time each phase ([Server](../concepts/server.md#instrumentation)). |
| `metadata`, `generateMetadata()`                                                             | `<Title>`, `<Meta>` and `<Head>` rendered by the page or layout; an async page awaits its data first. The deepest wins ([Head and document](../concepts/head.md)).                                                                                                       |
| `generateViewport()`                                                                         | `<Meta name="viewport" … />`, or the tag in `document.stsx`.                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `sitemap.ts`, `robots.ts`                                                                    | Endpoints: `sitemap.xml/route.ts`, `robots.txt/route.ts`, written at build time on `static` routes.                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `next/script`                                                                                | `<Head><script src="…" async /></Head>`; under a strict CSP, see [Security](../concepts/security.md).                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `next/font`                                                                                  | `@font-face` in a `<style global>` block, with the font files in `public/`.                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `next/image`                                                                                 | No image component: `import photo from "./photo.jpg"` gives the fingerprinted URL; write `<img>` with `width`, `height`, `loading="lazy"` and `srcset`. Vite plugins that resize images at build time work in `vite.config.ts`.                                          |
| `next.config`: `headers()`, `basePath`, `trailingSlash`, `i18n`                              | `lumiose({ headers, trailingSlash, i18n })` and Vite's `base`, in `vite.config.ts`. Redirects go in middleware.                                                                                                                                                          |

### Navigation

| Next.js                                                                               | Lumiose                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `next/link`                                                                           | `<a href={href(…)}>`, or `<Link href prefetch>` from `lumiose/router`. MPA pages prefetch on hover by default; `prefetch="viewport"` matches Next.js.                       |
| Client-side navigation between pages                                                  | On `spa` routes, with persistent layouts. `static` and `server` pages load the next document, with optional View Transitions (`lumiose({ viewTransitions: true })`).        |
| `useRouter().push(href)`, `.replace(href)`                                            | `navigate(href)`, `navigate(href, { replace: true })` from `lumiose/router`.                                                                                                |
| `usePathname()`, `useSearchParams()`, `useParams()`                                   | `url().pathname`, `searchParams()` (and `searchParams.set()`), `params()` from `lumiose/router`.                                                                            |
| `useSelectedLayoutSegment()`                                                          | `route()`, the matched pattern: `route() === "/blog/[slug]"`.                                                                                                               |
| `onRouterTransitionStart(url, type)`, a `useEffect` on `usePathname()` for page views | `afterNavigate(fn)` from `lumiose/router`: after each completed navigation, and once on mount with `type: "enter"` ([hooks](../reference/router.md#navigation-hooks)).      |
| A `beforeunload` listener to protect unsaved changes                                  | `beforeNavigate((navigation) => navigation.cancel())`: it also stops SPA links, `navigate()` and back/forward; for a navigation that leaves the document, the browser asks. |
| `redirect()`, `permanentRedirect()`, `forbidden()`, `unauthorized()`                  | `redirect(to)`, `redirect(to, 308)`, `error(403)`, `error(401)`.                                                                                                            |

### Rendering and deployment

| Next.js                                                   | Lumiose                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Static rendering, `dynamic = "force-static"`              | `mode = "static"`, the default.                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Dynamic rendering, `dynamic = "force-dynamic"`            | `export const mode = "server"`.                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Partial prerendering, Cache Components                    | `server` + `<Suspense>`, or `static` + islands that call an endpoint ([Close to partial prerendering](../concepts/rendering-modes.md#close-to-partial-prerendering)).                                           |
| `output: "export"`                                        | Every route prerendered: the build writes no `dist/server`, and any static host serves `dist/client` ([Static hosts](../deploy/static.md)).                                                                     |
| Custom server: `next({ dev })` with `getRequestHandler()` | `createDevHandler({ server })` from `@lumiose/vite/dev` in dev and `createHandler()` from `@lumiose/adapter-node` in production, in one `server.ts` ([`@lumiose/vite`](../reference/vite.md#createdevhandler)). |
| `output: "standalone"`, `next start`                      | `dist/server/entry.js`, served by `@lumiose/adapter-node` (`createServer()`) or `lumiose preview`.                                                                                                              |
| Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare (OpenNext)                    | `lumiose({ adapter: vercel() })`, `netlify()` or `cloudflare()` ([Deploy](../deploy/README.md)).                                                                                                                |

## What has no equivalent

| Next.js                                                  | Instead                                                                                                                                                 |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Parallel routes (`@slot`, `default.tsx`)                 | Render the parts as components of one layout or page; branch on `route()` or a search param for conditional areas.                                      |
| Intercepting routes (`(.)photo`), route modals           | A `<dialog>` in an island, with the open item in `searchParams()`; or an `spa` route whose layout keeps the list mounted while the detail page renders. |
| ISR (`revalidate`), on-demand revalidation on the server | Rebuild `static` pages, or render on the `server` and set `cache-control: s-maxage=…, stale-while-revalidate=…` for a CDN.                              |
| A prebuilt shell with per-request holes (PPR)            | The two patterns in [Close to partial prerendering](../concepts/rendering-modes.md#close-to-partial-prerendering).                                      |
| `template.tsx`                                           | None: page state resets on every navigation, and `spa` layouts keep theirs by design.                                                                   |
| Middleware rewrites                                      | None: redirect instead, or render the same component from both routes.                                                                                  |
| Image optimization, `next/font` optimization             | None built in: see the `next/image` and `next/font` rows above.                                                                                         |
| Generated images (`opengraph-image.tsx`, `icon.tsx`)     | Static files in `public/`, or an endpoint that returns the image.                                                                                       |
| `forbidden.tsx`, `unauthorized.tsx`                      | `error(403)` and `error(401)` render `error.stsx`, which reads `status`.                                                                                |
| Draft mode                                               | A `server` route that reads a preview cookie.                                                                                                           |
| React component libraries                                | No React interop: native elements, web components or framework-agnostic libraries (see [Coming from React](react.md)).                                  |

## Example

A blog post in Next.js: a server component, a streamed part, a client component and a server
action.

```tsx
// app/articles/[slug]/page.tsx
import { notFound, redirect } from "next/navigation";
import { Suspense } from "react";
import { addComment, getComments, getPost } from "@/lib/posts";
import { Reactions } from "@/components/reactions"; // "use client" inside

export async function generateMetadata({ params }: PageProps<"/articles/[slug]">) {
  const post = await getPost((await params).slug);
  return { title: post?.title };
}

export default async function Article({ params }: PageProps<"/articles/[slug]">) {
  const { slug } = await params;
  const post = await getPost(slug);
  if (!post) notFound();

  async function comment(formData: FormData) {
    "use server";
    await addComment(slug, String(formData.get("text") ?? ""));
    redirect(`/articles/${slug}`);
  }

  return (
    <article>
      <h1>{post.title}</h1>
      <p>{post.body}</p>
      <Reactions initial={post.likes} />
      <Suspense fallback={<p>Loading comments…</p>}>
        <Comments slug={slug} />
      </Suspense>
      <form action={comment}>
        <textarea name="text" />
        <button>Comment</button>
      </form>
    </article>
  );
}

async function Comments({ slug }: { slug: string }) {
  const comments = await getComments(slug);
  return (
    <ul>
      {comments.map((c) => (
        <li key={c.id}>{c.text}</li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  );
}
```

The same page in Lumiose. The data module stays on the server:

```ts check file=lib/articles.server.ts
// src/lib/articles.server.ts: a database in a real app
interface Comment {
  id: number;
  text: string;
}

const articles = new Map([
  ["hello", { title: "Hello", body: "The first post.", likes: 3, comments: [] as Comment[] }],
]);

export async function getArticle(slug: string) {
  return articles.get(slug);
}

export async function getComments(slug: string) {
  await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 300)); // a slow query
  return articles.get(slug)?.comments ?? [];
}

export async function addComment(slug: string, text: string) {
  articles.get(slug)?.comments.push({ id: Date.now(), text });
}
```

The interactive part has no directive in its file:

```tsx check file=components/Reactions.tsx
// src/components/Reactions.tsx
import { signal } from "lumiose";

export function Reactions(props: { initial: number }) {
  const likes = signal(props.initial);
  return <button onClick={() => likes.update((n) => n + 1)}>Like ({likes()})</button>;
}
```

The page renders on the server per request, sends its shell (title, article, form) at once and
streams the comments in. `client:visible` hydrates the button when it scrolls into view. The form
posts to the `comment` action and works without JavaScript:

```stsx check file=routes/articles/[slug]/page.stsx
// src/routes/articles/[slug]/page.stsx
import { Suspense, Title, href, notFound, redirect, type ActionContext, type PageProps } from "lumiose";
import { Reactions } from "../../../components/Reactions.tsx";
import { addComment, getArticle, getComments } from "../../../lib/articles.server.ts";

export const mode = "server";

export const actions = {
  async comment(ctx: ActionContext<"/articles/[slug]">) {
    const text = String((await ctx.formData()).get("text") ?? "").trim();
    if (text !== "") await addComment(ctx.params.slug, text);
    redirect(href("/articles/[slug]", { slug: ctx.params.slug }));
  },
};

async function Comments(props: { slug: string }) {
  const comments = await getComments(props.slug);
  return (
    <ul>
      {comments.map((comment) => (
        <li key={comment.id}>{comment.text}</li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  );
}

export default async function Article({ params }: PageProps<"/articles/[slug]">) {
  const article = (await getArticle(params.slug)) ?? notFound();
  return (
    <article>
      <Title>{article.title}</Title>
      <h1>{article.title}</h1>
      <p>{article.body}</p>
      <Reactions client:visible initial={article.likes} />
      <Suspense fallback={<p>Loading comments…</p>}>
        <Comments slug={params.slug} />
      </Suspense>
      <form method="post" action="?/comment">
        <textarea name="text" />
        <button>Comment</button>
      </form>
    </article>
  );
}
```

A static page per slug, where Next.js uses `generateStaticParams()` and `generateMetadata()`.
`static` is the default mode, so the page needs no `mode` export:

```tsx check file=routes/handbook/[slug]/page.tsx
// src/routes/handbook/[slug]/page.tsx: built once per slug, served as files
import { Meta, Title, notFound, type PageProps } from "lumiose";

const chapters = new Map([
  ["intro", { title: "Introduction", summary: "Why the handbook exists." }],
```
