```tsx check file=routes/handbook/[slug]/page.tsx
  ["setup", { title: "Setup", summary: "Install and configure the tools." }],
]);

async function getChapter(slug: string) {
  return chapters.get(slug); // a CMS or the file system in a real site
}

export function staticPaths() {
  return [...chapters.keys()].map((slug) => ({ params: { slug } }));
}

export default async function Chapter({ params }: PageProps<"/handbook/[slug]">) {
  const chapter = (await getChapter(params.slug)) ?? notFound();
  return (
    <main>
      <Title>{chapter.title}</Title>
      <Meta name="description" content={chapter.summary} />
      <h1>{chapter.title}</h1>
    </main>
  );
}
```

`app/sitemap.ts` becomes an endpoint, written to `dist/client/sitemap.xml` at build time:

```ts check file=routes/sitemap.xml/route.ts
// src/routes/sitemap.xml/route.ts
import { href, type Endpoint } from "lumiose";

const site = "https://example.com";

export const GET: Endpoint<"/sitemap.xml"> = () => {
  const urls = ["intro", "setup"].map(
    (slug) => `<url><loc>${site}${href("/handbook/[slug]", { slug })}</loc></url>`,
  );
  return new Response(
    `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>\n<urlset xmlns="http://www.sitemaps.org/schemas/sitemap/0.9">${urls.join("")}</urlset>`,
    { headers: { "content-type": "application/xml" } },
  );
};
```

`middleware.ts` (`proxy.ts`) becomes `src/middleware.ts` for what runs on every request, and a
`middleware.ts` in a route folder for what a `matcher` scoped:

```ts check
// src/middleware.ts
import type { Middleware } from "lumiose";

const middleware: Middleware = async (ctx, next) => {
  const response = await next();
  response.headers.set("x-frame-options", "DENY");
  return response;
};

export default middleware;
```

```ts check file=routes/dashboard/middleware.ts
// src/routes/dashboard/middleware.ts: matcher "/dashboard/:path*", actions and endpoints included
import type { Middleware } from "lumiose";

const requireSession: Middleware<"/dashboard"> = (ctx, next) =>
  ctx.cookies.get("session") === undefined
    ? Response.redirect(new URL("/login", ctx.url), 307)
    : next();

export default requireSession;
```

## Common mistakes

- **`"use client"` at the top of a file.** It does nothing: the component still renders on the
  server only. Add a `client:*` directive where the page uses it.
- **Reading cookies or `searchParams` on a `static` page.** Next.js would switch the page to
  dynamic rendering; Lumiose stops the build with [LUM5001](../errors/LUM5001.md). Set
  `export const mode = "server"`.
- **Guarding a `static` page in middleware.** Prerendered pages are files in production, served
  without running middleware (it runs for them at build time; a folder middleware that covers
  them is [LUM5008](../errors/LUM5008.md)). Pages behind a sign-in are `server` or `spa` routes.
- **`loading.tsx`, `@modal` or `(.)photo`.** They are [LUM5002](../errors/LUM5002.md) errors. Use
  `<Suspense>`, components in the layout, and a dialog or an `spa` route.
- **`export const metadata`.** Nothing reads it. Render `<Title>` and `<Meta>`.
- **`<html>` and `<body>` in the root layout.** They belong in `src/document.stsx`; a layout
  renders inside `<body>`.
- **Importing a server action into an island.** There are no server functions: importing a
  `*.server.ts` module from browser code is [LUM4003](../errors/LUM4003.md). Post to a form action
  with `submit()`, or call an endpoint.
- **Expecting `fetch` results to be cached across requests.** The cache lives for one request on
  the server. Cache with HTTP headers, or keep the page `static`.
- **`await params`.** It works, but `params` is a plain object; read `params.slug` directly.
- **`NEXT_PUBLIC_` variables.** Browser code sees `import.meta.env.PUBLIC_*` only.

- [Routing](../concepts/routing.md): file routes, layouts, params, error pages and typed `href()`.
- [Islands](../concepts/islands.md): `client:*` directives, serializable props and slots.
- [Rendering modes](../concepts/rendering-modes.md): `static`, `server` and `spa` routes, streaming and the build.
- [Data and actions](../concepts/data-and-actions.md): endpoints, form actions, `submit()` and `invalidate()`.
- [Async components](../concepts/async.md): server and client async components and the request cache.
- [Head and document](../concepts/head.md): `<Title>`, `<Meta>`, `<Head>` and `document.stsx`.
- [Server](../concepts/server.md): middleware, cookies, env and redirects.
- [Deploy](../deploy/README.md): Node, Docker, Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare and static hosts.
- [Coming from React](react.md): hooks, components and JSX.

<!-- source: coming-from/react-router.md -->

# Coming from React Router

> React Router 7's framework mode mapped to Lumiose: file routes instead of `routes.ts`, async components instead of loaders, form actions and `submit()` instead of actions and fetchers, middleware, the document and custom servers.

This page maps React Router 7 in framework mode (the successor of Remix) to Lumiose's current API.
For components and hooks, read [Coming from React](react.md) first; this page covers the framework.

## Mental model

**Data lives in components, not in route modules.** A React Router route module exports a
`loader` that runs before the route renders, and the component reads `loaderData`. Lumiose has no
loaders: the page component is `async` and awaits its data where it uses it, on
every rendering mode. Components that await the same `fetchJSON()` URL or `query()` key share one
request, so a layout and a page, or two widgets, can each await what they need
([Async components](../concepts/async.md)).

**Actions are the familiar part.** A page exports `action` (or named `actions`), which receives the
request's `FormData` and returns data, `fail(status, data)` or a redirect. A plain
`<form method="post">` posts to it and works without JavaScript; `onSubmit={submit}` posts it
without a page load ([Data and actions](../concepts/data-and-actions.md)).

**Navigation is a choice per route.** React Router hydrates the whole app and navigates on the
client. In Lumiose, `static` and `server` routes are pages that ship no JavaScript except their
islands, and links load the next document (prefetched on hover, with optional View Transitions).
An `spa` route is the React Router experience: rendered on the server, hydrated, client-side
navigation with persistent layouts ([Rendering modes](../concepts/rendering-modes.md)). Most apps
mix them: `static` marketing pages, `server` account pages, an `spa` dashboard.

**Routes are files only.** There is no `routes.ts` and no route config in code: a
folder under `src/routes` is a URL segment, and `page`, `layout`, `route`, `error` and
`not-found` files give it behavior ([Routing](../concepts/routing.md)).

## From React Router to Lumiose

### Routes and types

| React Router                                                      | Lumiose                                                                                                                                                |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `app/routes.ts` with `route()`, `index()`, `layout()`, `prefix()` | Folders under `src/routes`; `lumiose routes` lists what the router sees.                                                                               |
| `index("routes/home.tsx")`, `_index.tsx`                          | `src/routes/page.stsx`; `about/page.stsx` for `/about`.                                                                                                |
| `:id`, `:lang?`, `*` (`params["*"]`)                              | `[id]`, `[[lang]]`, `[...rest]` (one or more segments) or `[[...rest]]` (zero or more), read as `params.rest`.                                         |
| `layout("routes/auth.tsx", [...])`, pathless `_auth.tsx`          | A group folder with a layout: `(auth)/layout.stsx`.                                                                                                    |
| `<Outlet />`                                                      | `props.children` in a layout.                                                                                                                          |
| Resource routes (a `loader` or `action` without a component)      | `route.ts` endpoints that export `GET`, `POST`, … as `(ctx) => Response`.                                                                              |
| `import type { Route } from "./+types/page"`                      | `PageProps<"/projects/[id]">`, `LayoutProps<"/projects">`, `ActionContext<"/projects/[id]">` and `Endpoint<"/api/x">`, generated by `lumiose typegen`. |
| `href("/projects/:id", { id })`                                   | `href("/projects/[id]", { id })`, type-checked against the routes.                                                                                     |

### Data

| React Router                                          | Lumiose                                                                                                               |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `loader` and `useLoaderData()`                        | An `async` page component that awaits its data; server-only code lives in `*.server.ts` modules or `src/server/`.     |
| `clientLoader`                                        | On `spa` routes the page component also runs in the browser: await `fetchJSON()` of an endpoint, or `query(key, fn)`. |
| Promises returned from a loader, `<Await>`            | An async component inside `<Suspense fallback>`: on `server` routes it streams after the shell.                       |
| `useRouteLoaderData()`, data from a parent route      | Await the same `fetchJSON()` URL or `query()` key again (one request per page), or provide a context from the layout. |
| `data(value, { status, headers })` from a loader      | `response().setStatus()` and `response().setHeader()` in the page, or a `headers(ctx)` export.                        |
| `throw data(…, { status: 404 })`, `throw redirect(…)` | `notFound()`, `error(status)` and `redirect(to)`, which throw ([Server](../concepts/server.md)).                      |
| `useRevalidator().revalidate()`                       | `invalidate()`; `invalidate("/api/x", ["key"])` refetches only those entries.                                         |
| `shouldRevalidate`                                    | Choose what refetches: `submit(form, { invalidate: ["/api/x"] })`, or `{ invalidate: false }`.                        |

### Mutations

| React Router                                                         | Lumiose                                                                                                                                |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `action` and `useActionData()`                                       | `export const action`, or `export const actions = { name }`, and `actionData<typeof actions>()`.                                       |
| `<Form method="post">`                                               | `<form method="post">`, which works without JavaScript; `onSubmit={submit}` in an island or `spa` route posts it without a page load.  |
| An `intent` field to tell submissions apart                          | Named actions: `action="?/archive"` on the form, or `formaction="?/archive"` on its button.                                            |
| `clientAction`                                                       | An `onSubmit` handler in an island or `spa` route: run browser code, then `await submit(event)`.                                       |
| `useSubmit()`                                                        | `submit(target, { action, method })`: a form, a submit event, `FormData`, `URLSearchParams` or a record.                               |
| `useFetcher()`: `fetcher.submit()`, `<fetcher.Form>`, `fetcher.data` | `submit(target, { action: "?/name" })`, which never navigates unless the action redirects, and resolves with `{ type, status, data }`. |
| `useFetcher()` per instance: `fetcher.state`, `fetcher.data`         | `submission<typeof actions.name>()`: this component's `submit`, `isSubmitting()`, `result()`, `error()`, `abort()` and `reset()`.      |
| `fetcher.load(href)`                                                 | An async component that awaits `fetchJSON(href)`; `invalidate(href)` loads it again.                                                   |
| `useNavigation().state`, `fetcher.state`                             | `isNavigating()` (`lumiose/router`), `isSubmitting(name?)`, and `isBusy()` for anything in flight.                                     |
| Optimistic UI from `fetcher.formData`                                | `optimistic(source)` with `.update(fn, submit(event))`.                                                                                |
| `createCookieSessionStorage()`, `createCookie()`                     | `cookies` and `signedCookie(name)` ([Server](../concepts/server.md)).                                                                  |

### Server, document and rendering

| React Router                                                                  | Lumiose                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `middleware` export and `context.set()` / `context.get()`                     | `src/middleware.ts` for every request, and a `middleware.ts` in a route folder for the routes below it: `(ctx, next) => Response`, run parent to child, with request data on `ctx.locals` (typed by augmenting `Locals`), read in pages with `locals()`.                 |
| `getLoadContext()`, `AppLoadContext`                                          | `ctx.platform` (the host's bindings, `waitUntil()`, the client address) and `env(name)`.                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `root.tsx`: `<Meta />`, `<Links />`, `<Scripts />`, `<ScrollRestoration />`   | `src/document.stsx` renders `{props.head}` and `{props.body}`; stylesheets, scripts and scroll restoration are built in.                                                                                                                                                 |
| `meta` and `links` exports                                                    | `<Title>`, `<Meta>` and `<Head>` in any component ([Head and document](../concepts/head.md)).                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `headers` export                                                              | `headers(ctx)` export, `response().setHeader()`, middleware, or `lumiose({ headers })` for every page.                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `ErrorBoundary` export, `isRouteErrorResponse()`                              | `error.stsx` and `not-found.stsx` (the nearest wins, with `{ status, error }`), and `<ErrorBoundary>` for an error in place.                                                                                                                                             |
| `HydrateFallback`                                                             | `<Suspense fallback>`, or the shell of an `ssr = false` route.                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `entry.server.tsx`: `handleRequest`, streaming                                | No file: the handler streams the shell, then `<Suspense>` boundaries; headers go in middleware.                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `handleError` in `entry.server.tsx`, server `instrumentations`                | `src/instrumentation.server.ts`: `onRequestError(error, info)` with the route and phase, and `instrumentations` that wrap `request`, `middleware`, `action`, `endpoint`, `render` and `stream`; `call()` never throws ([Server](../concepts/server.md#instrumentation)). |
| `entry.client.tsx`: `hydrateRoot`                                             | No file: the island loader and the SPA entry hydrate. Code that must run before hydration (an SDK, a polyfill) goes in `src/instrumentation.client.ts`, which every page runs first ([Islands](../concepts/islands.md#concept)).                                         |
| Client `instrumentations` (`router.navigate`, `router.fetch`), client errors  | The `instrumentations` export of `src/instrumentation.client.ts`: `navigate`, `submit`, `fetch` and island `hydrate` wrappers with the same rules, and `onError(error, info)` for island, router and `submit()` errors ([Islands](../concepts/islands.md#concept)).      |
| `ssr: false` (SPA mode)                                                       | `lumiose({ mode: "spa", ssr: false })`, or `export const ssr = false` on an `spa` route.                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `prerender: [...]`                                                            | `static` routes (the default) with `staticPaths()` for params, and `export const prerender = true` on `spa` pages.                                                                                                                                                       |
| `react-router-serve`                                                          | `@lumiose/adapter-node`'s `createServer()`, or `lumiose preview`; other hosts in [Deploy](../deploy/README.md).                                                                                                                                                          |
| Custom server: `createRequestHandler()` from `@react-router/express`          | `createHandler()` from `@lumiose/adapter-node`, a request listener or Express middleware; or `dist/server/entry.js`'s `fetch(request)`.                                                                                                                                  |
| Custom server in dev: Vite in middleware mode, `ssrLoadModule()` of the build | `createDevHandler({ server })` from `@lumiose/vite/dev`: the same kind of handler, with HMR and the overlay, so one `server.ts` serves dev and production ([`@lumiose/vite`](../reference/vite.md#createdevhandler)).                                                    |

### Navigation

| React Router                                                | Lumiose                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<Link to>`, `<NavLink>`                                    | `<a href={href(…)}>` or `<Link href>` from `lumiose/router`; `<Link>` sets `aria-current="page"` on the active link.                                                                                                                                             |
| `<Link prefetch="intent">`                                  | `<Link prefetch="hover">`, the default; MPA pages prefetch through speculation rules.                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `useNavigate()`                                             | `navigate(href, { replace })` from `lumiose/router`.                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `useParams()`                                               | `props.params`, or `params()` from `lumiose/router` (reactive, also on the server).                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `useSearchParams()`                                         | `searchParams()` and `searchParams.set()` from `lumiose/router`; `url().searchParams` in server code.                                                                                                                                                            |
| `useLocation()`                                             | `url()` from `lumiose/router`; `route()` is the matched pattern.                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `useBlocker()`, `unstable_usePrompt()`, `useBeforeUnload()` | `beforeNavigate((navigation) => navigation.cancel())` from `lumiose/router`: SPA links, `navigate()` and back/forward; for a navigation that leaves the document (`navigation.willUnload`), the browser asks ([hooks](../reference/router.md#navigation-hooks)). |
| A `useEffect` on `useLocation()` (page views, focus)        | `afterNavigate(fn)`: after each completed navigation, and once on mount with `type: "enter"`.                                                                                                                                                                    |

## What has no equivalent

| React Router                                    | Instead                                                                                              |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Routes defined in code (`routes.ts`, `route()`) | File routes only. Colocate components and helpers next to the route; `_private` folders never route. |
| `clientMiddleware`                              | None. Run the code in the `spa` layout (`effect`, `onMount`) or in the handler that navigates.       |
| `useFetchers()`                                 | None: `isSubmitting(name)` counts every submission to an action, `isBusy()` anything in flight.      |
| `handle` and `useMatches()`                     | Pass data down as props or context from the layout; compare `route()` with a pattern.                |
| `useNavigation().location` and `.formData`      | `isNavigating()` for pending UI, and `optimistic()` for the value being submitted.                   |

## Example

A project page with a loader, an action and a form, in React Router:

```tsx
// app/routes/projects.$id.tsx
import { data, Form, redirect, useNavigation } from "react-router";
import type { Route } from "./+types/projects.$id";
import { addTask, getProject } from "~/projects.server";

export async function loader({ params }: Route.LoaderArgs) {
  const project = await getProject(params.id);
  if (!project) throw data("Not found", { status: 404 });
  return { project };
}

export async function action({ request, params }: Route.ActionArgs) {
  const title = String((await request.formData()).get("title") ?? "").trim();
  if (title === "") return data({ error: "A title is required." }, { status: 400 });
  await addTask(params.id, title);
  return redirect(`/projects/${params.id}`);
}

export function meta({ data }: Route.MetaArgs) {
  return [{ title: data.project.name }];
}

export default function Project({ loaderData, actionData }: Route.ComponentProps) {
  const navigation = useNavigation();
  return (
    <main>
      <h1>{loaderData.project.name}</h1>
      <ul>
        {loaderData.project.tasks.map((task) => (
          <li key={task.id}>{task.title}</li>
        ))}
      </ul>
      <Form method="post">
        <input name="title" />
        <p>{actionData?.error}</p>
        <button disabled={navigation.state === "submitting"}>Add task</button>
      </Form>
    </main>
  );
}
```

The same page in Lumiose. The data access is unchanged:

```ts check file=lib/projects.server.ts
// src/lib/projects.server.ts: a database in a real app
interface Task {
  id: number;
  title: string;
}

const projects = new Map([["1", { name: "Write the docs", tasks: [] as Task[] }]]);

export async function getProject(id: string) {
  return projects.get(id);
}

export async function addTask(id: string, title: string) {
  projects.get(id)?.tasks.push({ id: Date.now(), title });
}
```

The page awaits the project in its component, and its action returns `fail()` for validation
errors. It is a `server` page: no JavaScript ships except the form's island.

```stsx check file=routes/projects/[id]/page.stsx
// src/routes/projects/[id]/page.stsx
import { Title, fail, href, notFound, redirect, type ActionContext, type PageProps } from "lumiose";
import { AddTask } from "../../../components/AddTask.stsx";
import { addTask, getProject } from "../../../lib/projects.server.ts";

export const mode = "server";

export const actions = {
  async add(ctx: ActionContext<"/projects/[id]">) {
    const title = String((await ctx.formData()).get("title") ?? "").trim();
    if (title === "") return fail(400, { error: "A title is required." });
    await addTask(ctx.params.id, title);
    redirect(href("/projects/[id]", { id: ctx.params.id }));
  },
};

export default async function Project({ params }: PageProps<"/projects/[id]">) {
  const project = (await getProject(params.id)) ?? notFound();
  return (
    <main>
      <Title>{project.name}</Title>
      <h1>{project.name}</h1>
      <ul>
        {project.tasks.map((task) => (
          <li key={task.id}>{task.title}</li>
        ))}
      </ul>
      <AddTask client:load />
    </main>
  );
}
```

The form is an island in its own module, so the server-only import above never reaches the
browser; it imports the action's type only. Without JavaScript the form posts and the page
re-renders with the error or follows the redirect; with it, `submit()` does the same without a
page load:

```stsx check file=components/AddTask.stsx
// src/components/AddTask.stsx
import { actionData, isSubmitting, submit } from "lumiose";
import type { actions } from "../routes/projects/[id]/page.stsx";

export function AddTask() {
  return (
    <form method="post" action="?/add" onSubmit={submit}>
      <input name="title" />
      <p class="error">{actionData<typeof actions>()?.error}</p>
      <button disabled={isSubmitting("add")}>Add task</button>
    </form>
  );
}

<style>
  .error { color: crimson; }
</style>
```

Context from middleware, where React Router uses `context.set()` in a `middleware` export:

```ts check
// src/middleware.ts
import { signedCookie, type Middleware } from "lumiose";

const session = signedCookie("session");

declare module "lumiose" {
  interface Locals {
    userId: string | null;
  }
}

const middleware: Middleware = async (ctx, next) => {
  ctx.locals.userId = (await session.get(ctx.cookies)) ?? null;
  return next();
};

export default middleware;
```

A route's `middleware` for its subtree is a `middleware.ts` in its folder. It runs after
`src/middleware.ts`, for every page, action and endpoint below the folder:

```ts check file=routes/projects/middleware.ts
// src/routes/projects/middleware.ts
import type { Middleware } from "lumiose";

const requireUser: Middleware<"/projects"> = (ctx, next) =>
  ctx.locals.userId === null ? Response.redirect(new URL("/login", ctx.url), 303) : next();

export default requireUser;
```

A custom server, where React Router uses `createRequestHandler()`:

```ts check
// server.ts: node server.ts after lumiose build
import { createServer } from "node:http";
import { createHandler } from "@lumiose/adapter-node";

const app = await createHandler(); // the build in dist/: static files, then the app

createServer((req, res) => {
  if (req.url === "/healthz") {
    res.end("ok");
    return;
  }
  app(req, res);
}).listen(Number(process.env.PORT ?? 3000));
```

## Common mistakes

- **Exporting a `loader`.** Nothing calls it. Await the data in the page component.
- **Expecting client-side navigation everywhere.** `static` and `server` routes load the next
  document. Make app-like areas `spa` (in their layout), and keep the rest as pages.
- **Expecting an MPA page to revalidate after `submit()`.** React Router reloads loaders after an
  action; on a `static` or `server` page `submit()` does not refresh the page. Redirect from the
  action (as above), update the island from the result, or call `invalidate()`. On `spa` routes a
  successful `submit()` refreshes the page's data.
- **Server code in an island's module.** An island's module ships to the browser, so importing a
  `*.server.ts` there is `LUM4003`. Keep islands in their own files and import action types with
  `import type`.
- **Throwing for validation errors.** A thrown error renders the `error` page; return
  `fail(400, data)` as you would return `data(…, { status: 400 })`.
- **Reading `params["*"]`.** A rest segment has a name: `[...path]` is `params.path`.
- **Reading the request in `spa` routes.** Their code also runs in the browser, so `cookies()` and
  `locals()` are not available there; call an endpoint ([LUM4003](../errors/LUM4003.md)).
- **Hard-coding `/projects/${id}`.** `href("/projects/[id]", { id })` fails type-checking when the
  route moves.

## Related

- [Routing](../concepts/routing.md): file routes, layouts, params, typed `href()` and the SPA router.
- [Data and actions](../concepts/data-and-actions.md): endpoints, form actions, `submit()`, `invalidate()` and `optimistic()`.
- [Async components](../concepts/async.md): awaiting data, the request cache, `<Suspense>` and streaming.
- [Server](../concepts/server.md): middleware, `locals`, cookies, redirects and env.
- [Rendering modes](../concepts/rendering-modes.md): `static`, `server` and `spa` routes, prerendering and the build.
- [`lumiose/router`](../reference/router.md): `Link`, `navigate`, `params`, `searchParams` and `isNavigating`.
- [`@lumiose/adapter-node`](../reference/adapter-node.md): `createServer` and `createHandler`.
- [Coming from React](react.md): hooks, components and JSX.

<!-- source: coming-from/solid.md -->

# Coming from Solid

> Solid is the closest model, components set up once with fine-grained signals, so this guide is about the differences: signal and store APIs, props, control flow as plain JSX, async components, `.stsx` styles, islands, and SolidStart and Solid Router mapped to file routes, endpoints and form actions.

This page maps Solid 1.x, Solid Router and SolidStart to Lumiose's current API. The linked pages
have the full rules.

## Mental model

**The same core idea.** As in Solid, a component body runs once, JSX expressions that read signals
compile to bindings that update their part of the DOM, and there is no virtual DOM. Owners,
`onCleanup`, context and `untrack` work the way you expect ([Signals](../concepts/signals.md)).
Lumiose's names follow Solid and React where the behaviour matches, without Solid's `create`
prefix: `signal`, `computed`, `effect`, `store`.

**The differences are in the details:**

- **A signal is one function**, not a `[get, set]` tuple: `count()` reads, `count.set(1)` and
  `count.update((n) => n + 1)` write.
- **Props destructure safely.** The compiler rewrites destructured component parameters, with
  defaults and `...rest`, into reads of `props.x`, so `({ title, size = "md" })` stays reactive. No
  `splitProps` or `mergeProps`.
- **Control flow is plain JSX.** There is no `<Show>`, `<For>` or `<Switch>`: the compiler turns
  `.map()` into a keyed list, ternaries and `&&` into memoised branches, and
  `item.id === selected()` inside `.map()` into a selector ([JSX](../concepts/jsx.md)).
- **Async components replace resources.** A component may be `async` and `await` its data on the
  server and in the browser; `<Suspense>` and `<ErrorBoundary>` work as in Solid
  ([Async components](../concepts/async.md)).
- **Styles live with the component.** `.stsx` files are TSX plus raw-CSS `<style>` blocks, scoped by
  where they are placed ([Styles](../concepts/styles.md)).

**Server first, with islands.** SolidStart renders the app on the server and hydrates all of it. In
Lumiose, `static` and `server` pages ship no JavaScript, and a `client:*` directive at the usage
site makes one component instance an [island](../concepts/islands.md): `<Todos client:load />`.
An `spa` route is the SolidStart experience: server-rendered, hydrated, client-side navigation with
persistent layouts ([Rendering modes](../concepts/rendering-modes.md)).

## From Solid to Lumiose

### Reactivity

| Solid                                                 | Lumiose                                                                                                                                              |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `const [count, setCount] = createSignal(0)`           | `const count = signal(0)`: `count()`, `count.set(1)`, `count.update((n) => n + 1)`, `count.peek()`.                                                  |
| `createSignal(v, { equals: false })`                  | `signal(v, { equals: false })`.                                                                                                                      |
| `createMemo(fn)`                                      | `computed(fn)`: lazy, cached, and `fn` receives the previous value.                                                                                  |
| `createEffect(fn)`                                    | `effect(fn)`; it may return its cleanup, or call `onCleanup()`.                                                                                      |
| `createRenderEffect`, `createComputed`                | JSX bindings and `computed`: effects run after the DOM writes of the same flush.                                                                     |
| `on(deps, fn)`                                        | Read the dependencies, then `untrack(() => …)` for the rest.                                                                                         |
| `onMount`, `onCleanup`, `batch`, `untrack`            | The same names.                                                                                                                                      |
| `createStore(value)` and `setStore(path…, value)`     | `store(value)`: a deep, mutable proxy, written directly (`state.todos[0].done = true`), like `createMutable`.                                        |
| `produce(fn)`                                         | Write to the store directly.                                                                                                                         |
| `reconcile(data)`                                     | `reconcile(target, data, { key })`, with Solid's semantics ([reference](../reference/reactivity.md#reconcile)).                                      |
| `unwrap(store)`                                       | `snapshot(store)`: a deep plain copy.                                                                                                                |
| `createSelector(selected)`                            | Compiled for you: `item.id === selected()` inside `.map()`.                                                                                          |
| `createContext`, `<Ctx.Provider value>`, `useContext` | `createContext`, `<Ctx value>` (the context is its own provider), `useContext`. Provide a signal or a store for state that changes.                  |
| `createUniqueId()`                                    | `useId()`, the same after hydration.                                                                                                                 |
| `createResource(source, fetcher)`                     | An `async` component that awaits `fetchJSON()` or `query()`; `resource(fetcher)` is the low-level form, with `loading()`, `error()` and `refetch()`. |
| `useTransition()`, `startTransition()`                | Async re-runs keep the old UI until the new data is ready: `isPending()` inside the component, `isBusy()` for anything in flight.                    |
| `isServer`                                            | `isServer` from `lumiose`, folded away in client builds.                                                                                             |

### Components and JSX

| Solid                                                            | Lumiose                                                                                                                 |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `splitProps(props, ["a"])`, `mergeProps(defaults, props)`        | `({ a, size = "md", ...rest })`: destructuring with defaults and rest stays reactive.                                   |
| `children(() => props.children)`                                 | Insert `children` once where it goes; take a render prop to render content several times.                               |
| `<Show when={user()} fallback={<Login />}>`                      | `{user() ? <Profile /> : <Login />}`, or `{user() && <Profile />}`.                                                     |
| `<Show when={user()} keyed>{(u) => …}</Show>`                    | `{user() ? <Profile user={user()!} /> : null}`: the branch switches when the condition flips, and the prop stays live.  |
| `<For each={items()}>{(item, i) => …}</For>`                     | `{items().map((item, i) => …)}`, keyed by reference or `key`; `i` is a reactive index, used as a number (`i + 1`).      |
| `<Index each={items()}>`                                         | No index-keyed list: keep objects in a `store` and change their properties, so rows update in place.                    |
| `<Switch>` and `<Match>`                                         | A chain of ternaries, or a function that returns JSX: `{view()}` with `const view = () => { switch (status()) { … } }`. |
| `<Dynamic component={…}>`, `<Portal mount={…}>`                  | The same: `<Dynamic component={…}>` and `<Portal mount={…}>`.                                                           |
| `<ErrorBoundary fallback={(err, reset) => …}>`, `<Suspense>`     | The same.                                                                                                               |
| `let el; <div ref={el} />`                                       | `const el = ref<HTMLDivElement>()`, `<div ref={el} />` and `el()`; or a callback `ref={(node) => …}`.                   |
| `use:tooltip={text}`                                             | `attach={[tooltip(text)]}`, where `tooltip(text)` returns `(el) => cleanup`.                                            |
| `classList={{ active: on() }}`                                   | `class={{ active: on() }}`; `class` also takes strings and arrays.                                                      |
| `style={{ "font-weight": 600 }}`, `on:click`, `onClick`          | The same: kebab-case style keys, native `on:` listeners and delegated `onX` handlers.                                   |
| `lazy(() => import("./Chart"))`                                  | No `lazy()`: islands load their module when they hydrate, and `spa` routes load a chunk per page and layout.            |
| `render(() => <App />, el)`, `hydrate`                           | `render(() => <App />, el)` from `lumiose/dom`; islands and `spa` routes hydrate on their own.                          |
| `renderToString`, `renderToStream`                               | The same names from `lumiose/server` ([reference](../reference/server.md)).                                             |
| CSS files, CSS Modules, `solid-styled`                           | A `<style>` block in the `.stsx` file, scoped by placement; `<style global>` for global rules.                          |
| `@solidjs/meta`: `<Title>`, `<Meta>`, `<Link>`, `<MetaProvider>` | `<Title>`, `<Meta>` and `<Head>` from `lumiose`, with no provider ([Head and document](../concepts/head.md)).           |

### SolidStart

| SolidStart                                                            | Lumiose                                                                                                                                                                         |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `app.config.ts` (Vinxi)                                               | `vite.config.ts` with the `lumiose()` plugin.                                                                                                                                   |
| `src/routes/index.tsx`, `about.tsx`                                   | `src/routes/page.stsx`, `about/page.stsx`: a folder is a URL segment.                                                                                                           |
| `blog/[slug].tsx`, `[[id]].tsx`, `[...rest].tsx`, `(group)`           | `blog/[slug]/page.stsx`, `[[id]]/page.stsx`, `[...rest]` (one or more segments) or `[[...rest]]` (zero or more), `(group)`.                                                     |
| `blog.tsx` next to `blog/` (a layout)                                 | `blog/layout.stsx`; `props.children` is the outlet.                                                                                                                             |
| API routes: `export function GET(event)`                              | `route.ts` endpoints: `export const GET: Endpoint<"/api/x"> = (ctx) => Response`.                                                                                               |
| `query(fn, "key")` and `createAsync(() => getUser(id))`               | `await query(["user", id], () => getUser(id))` in an async component (key first, an array as in TanStack Query), or `await fetchJSON(url)`.                                     |
| `"use server"` functions                                              | No RPC: form actions for mutations, endpoints for anything the browser fetches, and `*.server.ts` modules for server-only code.                                                 |
| `action(fn)` and `<form action={myAction} method="post">`             | `export const actions = { save(ctx) {…} }` and `<form method="post" action="?/save">`, which works without JavaScript.                                                          |
| `useAction(myAction)`                                                 | `submit(target, { action: "?/save" })` from an island or `spa` route.                                                                                                           |
| `useSubmission(myAction)`: `pending`, `result`                        | `submission<typeof actions.save>()`: `isSubmitting()`, `result()`, `error()`, `abort()` and `reset()` for this component; page-wide, `isSubmitting("save")` and `actionData()`. |
| `revalidate(key)`, `reload()`                                         | `invalidate(["key"])` refetches matching `query()` entries; `invalidate()` refreshes the page.                                                                                  |
| `redirect()`, `json()` from an action                                 | `redirect(to)` (it throws), and plain data as the return value; `fail(status, data)` for validation errors.                                                                     |
| `entry-server.tsx` with `<StartServer document>`                      | `src/document.stsx` renders `{props.head}` and `{props.body}`.                                                                                                                  |
| `entry-client.tsx`, `app.tsx` with `<Router root>` and `<FileRoutes>` | No files: the router is built in; `src/routes/layout.stsx` is the root layout. Code before hydration goes in `src/instrumentation.client.ts`.                                   |
| `createMiddleware({ onRequest, onBeforeResponse })`                   | `src/middleware.ts`: `(ctx, next) => Response`, code before and after `await next()`; a `middleware.ts` in a route folder for its routes.                                       |
| `event.locals`, `getRequestEvent()`                                   | `ctx.locals` (typed by augmenting `Locals`); `request()`, `locals()`, `cookies()` and `url()` during a server render.                                                           |
| `useSession()`                                                        | `cookies` and `signedCookie(name)` ([Server](../concepts/server.md)).                                                                                                           |
| `clientOnly(() => import("./Map"))`                                   | `client:only` on the usage: `<Map client:only />`.                                                                                                                              |
| `ssr: false`, prerendering (`server.prerender`)                       | `lumiose({ mode: "spa", ssr: false })`; `static` routes (the default) with `staticPaths()`, and `prerender = true` on `spa` pages.                                              |
| Deployment presets                                                    | `@lumiose/adapter-node`, or `lumiose({ adapter })` for Vercel, Netlify and Cloudflare ([Deploy](../deploy/README.md)).                                                          |

### Solid Router

| Solid Router                                     | Lumiose                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `<Router>` with `<Route path component>`         | File routes; `lumiose routes` lists them.                                                                                                                                                        |
| `<A href>`, `activeClass`                        | `<Link href>` from `lumiose/router`, with `aria-current="page"` on the active link; `href()` builds typed URLs.                                                                                  |
| `useNavigate()`, `<Navigate href>`               | `navigate(href, { replace })`; `redirect(to)` while rendering.                                                                                                                                   |
| `useParams()`, `useLocation()`, `useMatch()`     | `params()`, `url()` and `route()` (the matched pattern) from `lumiose/router`.                                                                                                                   |
| `useSearchParams()`: `[params, setParams]`       | `searchParams()` and `searchParams.set({ q })`.                                                                                                                                                  |
| `useIsRouting()`                                 | `isNavigating()`.                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `useBeforeLeave((e) => e.preventDefault())`      | `beforeNavigate((navigation) => navigation.cancel())`; for a navigation that leaves the document (`navigation.willUnload`), the browser asks ([hooks](../reference/router.md#navigation-hooks)). |
| A `createEffect` on `useLocation()` (page views) | `afterNavigate(fn)`: after each completed navigation, and once on mount with `type: "enter"`.                                                                                                    |
| `preload` functions on routes                    | None: data loads where it is awaited, and `<Link prefetch>` loads a page's modules ahead.                                                                                                        |

## What has no equivalent

| Solid                                                    | Instead                                                                                                                                                                   |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `createRoot`, `getOwner`, `runWithOwner`                 | Not public: components, effects and `render()` create owners, and async components restore theirs after each `await`.                                                     |
| `createDeferred`, `createReaction`, `observable`, `from` | None. Bridge an external source with a signal set from its subscription ([an external store](../concepts/state.md#an-external-store-zustandvanilla-a-jotai-store-redux)). |
| `<Index>`, `mapArray`, `indexArray`                      | `.map()` in JSX; see the `<Index>` row above.                                                                                                                             |
| `<SuspenseList>`                                         | None: give each `<Suspense>` its own fallback.                                                                                                                            |
| `lazy()`                                                 | None: code splits per island and per `spa` page.                                                                                                                          |
| Server functions (`"use server"`) called like functions  | Form actions and endpoints. Calling an endpoint with `fetchJSON()` from an island keeps the network boundary visible.                                                     |
| `useSubmissions()`                                       | None: `isSubmitting(name)` counts every submission to an action.                                                                                                          |
| `preload` and `query` preloading on hover                | `<Link prefetch>` loads the page's modules; data loads when the page renders.                                                                                             |
| Solid component libraries (Kobalte, Corvu)               | They target Solid's runtime and do not run. Use native elements (`<dialog>`, `popover`), web components or framework-agnostic libraries.                                  |

## Example

A filtered todo list, in Solid:

```tsx
import { createMemo, createSignal, For, Show } from "solid-js";
import { createStore } from "solid-js/store";

export function Todos(props: { title: string }) {
  const [todos, setTodos] = createStore([{ id: 1, text: "Write the docs", done: false }]);
  const [filter, setFilter] = createSignal<"all" | "open">("all");
  const visible = createMemo(() =>
    filter() === "open" ? todos.filter((todo) => !todo.done) : todos,
  );

  return (
    <section>
      <h2>{props.title}</h2>
      <button onClick={() => setFilter((f) => (f === "all" ? "open" : "all"))}>
        Show {filter() === "all" ? "open" : "all"}
      </button>
      <Show when={visible().length > 0} fallback={<p>Nothing to do.</p>}>
        <ul>
          <For each={visible()}>
            {(todo, i) => (
              <li classList={{ done: todo.done }}>
                <input
                  type="checkbox"
                  checked={todo.done}
                  onChange={() =>
                    setTodos(
                      (t) => t.id === todo.id,
                      "done",
                      (done) => !done,
                    )
                  }
                />
                {i() + 1}. {todo.text}
              </li>
            )}
          </For>
        </ul>
      </Show>
    </section>
  );
}
```

The same list in Lumiose, with its styles in the file. The props are destructured, the store is
written directly, and the control flow is a ternary and `.map()`:

```stsx check file=components/Todos.stsx
// src/components/Todos.stsx
import { computed, signal, store } from "lumiose";

export function Todos({ title }: { title: string }) {
  const todos = store([{ id: 1, text: "Write the docs", done: false }]);
  const filter = signal<"all" | "open">("all");
  const visible = computed(() =>
    filter() === "open" ? todos.filter((todo) => !todo.done) : todos,
  );

  return (
    <section>
      <h2>{title}</h2>
      <button onClick={() => filter.update((f) => (f === "all" ? "open" : "all"))}>
        Show {filter() === "all" ? "open" : "all"}
      </button>
      {visible().length > 0 ? (
        <ul>
          {visible().map((todo, i) => (
            <li key={todo.id} class={{ done: todo.done }}>
              <input
                type="checkbox"
                checked={todo.done}
                onChange={() => {
                  todo.done = !todo.done;
                }}
              />
              {i + 1}. {todo.text}
            </li>
          ))}
        </ul>
      ) : (
        <p>Nothing to do.</p>
      )}
    </section>
  );
}

<style>
  .done { color: gray; text-decoration: line-through; }
</style>
```

A SolidStart route that reads with `query()` and `createAsync()` and writes with an `action()`
becomes a page with an async component and a form action. Without JavaScript the form posts and
the page re-renders with the action's data:

```stsx check file=routes/members/[id]/page.stsx
// src/routes/members/[id]/page.stsx
import {
  Title,
  actionData,
  fail,
  href,
  notFound,
  query,
  redirect,
  type ActionContext,
  type PageProps,
} from "lumiose";
import { Todos } from "../../../components/Todos.stsx";

export const mode = "server";

const members = new Map([["1", { name: "Ada", bio: "" }]]); // a database in a real app

export const actions = {
  async save(ctx: ActionContext<"/members/[id]">) {
    const bio = String((await ctx.formData()).get("bio") ?? "");
    if (bio.length > 200) return fail(400, { error: "Keep it under 200 characters." });
    const member = members.get(ctx.params.id) ?? notFound();
    member.bio = bio;
    redirect(href("/members/[id]", { id: ctx.params.id }));
  },
};

export default async function Member({ params }: PageProps<"/members/[id]">) {
  // One query per request and key, however many components await it.
  const member = (await query(["member", params.id], async () => members.get(params.id))) ?? notFound();
  return (
    <main>
      <Title>{member.name}</Title>
      <h1>{member.name}</h1>
      <form method="post" action="?/save">
        <textarea name="bio">{member.bio}</textarea>
        <p>{actionData<typeof actions>()?.error}</p>
        <button>Save</button>
      </form>
      <Todos client:visible title={`${member.name}'s tasks`} />
    </main>
  );
}
```

## Common mistakes

- **Destructuring a signal tuple.** `const [count, setCount] = signal(0)` is a type error: a signal
  is one function with `.set()` and `.update()`.
- **`<Show>`, `<For>` or `<Switch>`.** They do not exist. Write ternaries and `.map()`; the compiler
  makes them fine-grained.
- **Calling the index: `i()`.** In `.map((item, i) => …)`, `i` is used as a number; the compiler
  keeps it reactive. Passing it out of the callback is [LUM2006](../errors/LUM2006.md).
- **`setStore` paths.** A store is written directly: `todo.done = true`,
  `state.items.push(item)`.
- **`splitProps` to keep props reactive.** Destructure instead; the compiler keeps the reads
  reactive. Copying a signal's value into a variable is what freezes it
  ([LUM2001](../errors/LUM2001.md)).
- **An early return on a signal.** `if (!user()) return <Login />` runs once, as in Solid; branch in
  the JSX ([LUM2003](../errors/LUM2003.md)).
- **`query(fn, "key")`.** Lumiose's `query` takes the key first, as an array: `query(["user", id], fn)`.
- **An interactive component on a page without `client:*`.** It renders on the server, and its
  handlers never run. Add a directive at the usage site, or make the route `spa`.
- **Expecting page context inside an island.** Islands start a new root, so context provided by the
  page does not reach them ([LUM4010](../errors/LUM4010.md)): pass a prop, or use `defineState`.
- **A server function imported into an island.** Importing a `*.server.ts` module from browser code
  is [LUM4003](../errors/LUM4003.md). Post to a form action or call an endpoint.

## Related

- [Signals and reactivity](../concepts/signals.md): `signal`, `computed`, `effect`, `store`, owners and scheduling.
- [JSX](../concepts/jsx.md): bindings, the compiled `.map()`, ternaries and selectors, `class`, `style`, `attach` and `ref`.
- [Components](../concepts/components.md): setup once, props destructuring, children and refs.
- [Styles](../concepts/styles.md): `<style>` blocks scoped by placement.
- [Async components](../concepts/async.md): awaiting data, `<Suspense>`, `<ErrorBoundary>` and the request cache.
- [Islands](../concepts/islands.md) and [Rendering modes](../concepts/rendering-modes.md): what ships to the browser.
- [Routing](../concepts/routing.md), [Data and actions](../concepts/data-and-actions.md) and [`lumiose/router`](../reference/router.md): the SolidStart and Solid Router side.

<!-- source: concepts/components.md -->

# Components

> A component is a function that returns JSX: its body runs once, as setup, and signals update the JSX in place.

## Concept

**Files.** Components live in `.stsx` files (TSX plus raw-CSS `<style>` blocks) or plain `.tsx`
files. A file may export many components. Logic, tokens, endpoints and server code live in `.ts`.

| Extension | Contents                                                              |
| --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.stsx`   | TSX plus `<style>` blocks. Use it for components with styles.         |
| `.tsx`    | Plain TSX. A `<style>` block here is `LUM1006` ("rename to `.stsx`"). |
| `.ts`     | Everything else.                                                      |

**Setup once.** The body of a component runs once per instance. There is no re-render: JSX
expressions that read signals become fine-grained bindings, and only those update. Local variables
are ordinary variables; state that changes lives in [signals](signals.md).

**Props.** Props are the single parameter. The compiler keeps them reactive, even when you
destructure them: `({ title, count = 0 })` is rewritten to reads of `props.title` and
`props.count`, so a parent passing a signal value keeps the child up to date. `...rest` stays
reactive too.

On the server, where nothing is reactive, a prop expression is evaluated **lazily and at most once
per component instance** (decision-28): the first read runs it, later reads reuse the value, and a
prop the component never reads never runs. `<Filters labels={listLabels()} />` queries the labels
once per render however often `Filters` reads `props.labels`. In the browser props stay live: each
read re-evaluates the expression, so keep prop expressions free of side effects.

**Children** are lazy: `children` is evaluated where you insert it. Insert it once; to render
something several times, take a render function as a prop. Named slots are ordinary props that hold
JSX.

**Refs.** `ref` takes a callback `(el) => void`. `ref<T>()` returns such a callback that can also be
read like a signal.

**Async.** Any component may be `async` and `await` data in its body; see
[Async components](async.md).

## API

| API                                      | Use                                                                             |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `function Name(props) { return <… /> }`  | A component. PascalCase, returns JSX.                                           |
| `children` prop                          | Lazy content passed between the tags. Insert once.                              |
| `ref<T>()`                               | A ref callback that reads like a signal (`input()`), `undefined` until mounted. |
| `useId()`                                | A unique id for `id`/`for` and `aria-*` pairs, the same after hydration.        |
| `viewTransition(fn)`, `<ViewTransition>` | Animate a state update; name the elements that enter, exit or move.             |
| `onMount(fn)`, `onCleanup(fn)`           | Run after mount; run when the component is disposed.                            |
| `<Dynamic component={X} … />`            | Render a component (or tag name) chosen at runtime.                             |
| `<Portal mount={node}>`                  | Render children elsewhere in the document.                                      |

Types: a component's return type is `JSX.Element`. Props are a plain interface; `children?:
JSX.Element` for content.

## Example

```stsx check
import { onMount, ref, signal } from "lumiose";

interface Props {
  label: string;
  initial?: string;
  children?: JSX.Element;
}

export function SearchBox({ label, initial = "", children }: Props) {
  const query = signal(initial);
  const input = ref<HTMLInputElement>();

  onMount(() => input()?.focus());

  return (
    <form class="search" onSubmit={(event) => event.preventDefault()}>
      <label>
        {label}
        <input ref={input} bind:value={query} />
      </label>
      <p>Searching for “{query()}”</p>
      {children}
    </form>
  );
}

export function Page() {
  return (
    <SearchBox label="Books">
      <small>Try “Dune”.</small>
    </SearchBox>
  );
}

<style>
  .search { display: grid; gap: 0.5rem; }
</style>
```

Both components share the `<style>` block at the end of the file: by convention, each `.stsx`
file has one, after its components ([Styles](styles.md)).

## Common mistakes

- **Reading a signal once in setup and expecting it to update.** `const doubled = count() * 2`
  is computed once. Use a function or `computed`: `const doubled = () => count() * 2`. The compiler
  warns with `LUM2001`.
- **Returning early on reactive state.** `if (!user()) return <Login />` runs once. Put the
  condition in the JSX: `{user() ? <Profile /> : <Login />}` (`LUM2003`).
- **Calling a component as a function.** `{Card({ title })}` skips the component's owner and
  props handling. Write `<Card title={title} />` (`LUM2004`).
- **Inserting `children` twice.** The second insert moves or re-creates the nodes. Take a render
  prop such as `renderItem: () => JSX.Element` instead (`LUM2005`).
- **Writing a signal in the component body.** Setup runs during render; a write there
  (`count.set(…)`) re-triggers bindings mid-render. Write in handlers or effects (`LUM2002`).
- **Expecting React re-renders.** There are no hooks rules and no dependency arrays: nothing
  re-runs except bindings and effects that read signals.
- **`className`, `htmlFor`.** Use `class` and `for`; the React names are type errors.

## Related diagnostics

- [LUM1006](../errors/LUM1006.md): raw CSS in a `.tsx` file.
- [LUM2001](../errors/LUM2001.md): stale derived value.
- [LUM2002](../errors/LUM2002.md): signal write during render.
- [LUM2003](../errors/LUM2003.md): reactive early return.
- [LUM2004](../errors/LUM2004.md): component called as a function.
- [LUM2005](../errors/LUM2005.md): children inserted twice.

See also: [JSX](jsx.md), [Signals](signals.md), [reference: components](../reference/components.md).

<!-- source: concepts/signals.md -->

# Signals and reactivity

> State lives in signals: read with `count()`, write with `count.set(v)`, and only the code that read a signal re-runs.

## Concept

Lumiose's reactive core is a push-pull signal graph (the alien-signals algorithm). Reading a signal
inside a tracked scope (a JSX binding, a `computed`, an `effect`) subscribes that scope; writing
the signal marks it dirty and re-runs only what depends on it.

- **Reads are synchronous.** `count()` always returns the current value, even right after a write.
- **Writes are batched.** Writes inside a delegated event handler are batched for the duration of
  the handler. Any other write schedules a microtask flush. `flush()` flushes immediately.
- **Flush order:** computeds are pulled, then DOM bindings run (parents before children), then user
  effects.
- **Owners.** Every component, effect and root is an _owner_. Owners scope cleanups
  (`onCleanup`), context (`<Ctx value>`/`useContext`), error handling and `getAbortSignal()`. Disposing an owner
  disposes everything created under it.
- **Equality.** A write that is `Object.is`-equal to the current value is not a change. Pass
  `{ equals }` to customize, or `{ equals: false }` to treat every write as a change.
- **On the server** signals are plain cells, computeds run once, and effects never run.

## API

| API                                                             | Shape                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `signal(value, { equals? })`                                    | `s()` reads, `s.set(v)` and `s.update(fn)` write, `s.peek()` reads untracked.                                                               |
| `computed(fn, { equals? })`                                     | `c()` reads. Lazy, cached and glitch-free; `fn` receives the previous value.                                                                |
| `effect(fn)`                                                    | Runs after the DOM updates and again when what it read changes. `fn` may return a cleanup. Returns a disposer.                              |
| `onMount(fn)`                                                   | Runs `fn` once, untracked, after the owner's DOM is mounted. May return a cleanup.                                                          |
| `onCleanup(fn)`                                                 | Runs `fn` when the current owner is disposed or re-runs.                                                                                    |
| `store(obj)`                                                    | Deep, mutable reactive proxy over a plain object or array (like Valtio's `proxy` or Solid's `createMutable`): mutate it directly.           |
| `snapshot(value)`                                               | A deep plain copy of a store, for `structuredClone`, `postMessage` and saving.                                                              |
| `untrack(fn)`                                                   | Runs `fn` without subscribing to what it reads.                                                                                             |
| `batch(fn)`                                                     | Groups writes; dependents run once at the end.                                                                                              |
| `flush()`                                                       | Runs pending bindings and effects now.                                                                                                      |
| `getAbortSignal()`                                              | An `AbortSignal` aborted when the owner is disposed, an effect re-runs, or an async run is superseded. On the server, the request's signal. |
| `createContext(default?)`, `<Ctx value={v}>`, `useContext(ctx)` | Values passed down the owner tree; they survive `await`. The provider reads `value` once: provide a signal or store for changing state.     |
| `resource(fetcher)`                                             | Low-level on-demand loading with `loading()`, `error()`, `refetch()`. Prefer [async components](async.md).                                  |

In-flight state (`isPending()`, `isBusy()`, `isSubmitting()`, `isNavigating()`) is covered in
[Async components](async.md) and [Data and actions](data-and-actions.md).

## Example

```tsx check
import { computed, createContext, effect, signal, store, useContext } from "lumiose";

const Theme = createContext<"light" | "dark">("light");

export function Cart() {
  const items = store([{ name: "Pen", price: 2, qty: 1 }]);
  const discount = signal(0);
  const total = computed(
    () => items.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.price * item.qty, 0) * (1 - discount()),
  );

  effect(() => {
    document.title = `Cart: ${total().toFixed(2)}`;
  });

  return (
    <Theme value="dark">
      <section>
        <button onClick={() => items.push({ name: "Ink", price: 5, qty: 1 })}>Add ink</button>
        <button onClick={() => (items[0]!.qty += 1)}>One more pen</button>
        <button onClick={() => discount.set(0.1)}>Apply 10%</button>
        <p>Total: {total().toFixed(2)}</p>
        <ThemeLabel />
      </section>
    </Theme>
  );
}

function ThemeLabel() {
  const theme = useContext(Theme);
  return <small>Theme: {theme}</small>;
}
```

## Common mistakes

- **Destructuring or copying a signal's value in setup.** `const n = count()` freezes the value.
  Read `count()` where you need it, or derive: `const double = () => count() * 2` (`LUM2001`).
- **Calling `set` with the same object after mutating it.** `list().push(x); list.set(list())` is
  not a change (`Object.is`). Write a new value (`list.update((l) => [...l, x])`), use `store()`,
  or create the signal with `{ equals: false }`.
- **Writing signals in the component body or in a `computed`.** That is a write during render
  (`LUM2002`). Computeds must be pure; write in handlers and effects.
- **Using `effect` to derive state.** `effect(() => b.set(a() * 2))` adds a frame of staleness and
  an extra flush. Use `computed(() => a() * 2)`.
- **Expecting an effect to run synchronously.** Effects run after the DOM updates. In tests, call
  `flush()` after a write before asserting.
- **Module-scope signals in server code.** On the server, a signal at module scope is shared by
  every request. Keep request data in components or context (`LUM4008`).
- **Posting a store to a worker.** `postMessage()` and `structuredClone()` throw on proxies: send
  `snapshot(state)`.
- **Expecting `store()` to wrap class instances, `Map`s or `Set`s.** Only plain objects and arrays
  become reactive; other values are returned as is.

## Related diagnostics

- [LUM2001](../errors/LUM2001.md): stale derived value.
- [LUM2002](../errors/LUM2002.md): signal write during render.
- [LUM2007](../errors/LUM2007.md): own signal read in an async body.
- [LUM4008](../errors/LUM4008.md): module-scope signal written during SSR.

See also: [reference: reactivity](../reference/reactivity.md), [JSX bindings](jsx.md), [Sharing state](state.md).

<!-- source: concepts/state.md -->

# Sharing state

> Where state should live: in a component, passed down with context, or shared by a page and its islands, with recipes for common store patterns.

## Concept

**Pick the narrowest place that works.**

| Where                                            | Lives as long as          | Shared with                                 | On the server                              |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| A component (`signal`, `store` in setup)         | the component             | its children, through props                 | one per request: safe                      |
| Context (`<Ctx value>` / `useContext`)           | the provider              | everything rendered inside it               | one per request: safe                      |
| Scoped state (`export const s = defineState(…)`) | the page (in the browser) | every component and island that calls `s()` | one per request, sent to the islands: safe |
| Module scope (`export const s = signal()`)       | the page (in the browser) | every component and island that imports it  | one per process: never write it during SSR |

**No state library needed.** Only the code that reads a signal (or a store property) re-runs, so
selectors and re-render tuning are not needed. What the popular libraries offer maps to:

| Library feature                                      | In Lumiose                                                                        |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Jotai `atom(v)`, derived atoms                       | `signal(v)`, `computed(fn)`                                                       |
| Jotai `atomFamily`                                   | a `store` keyed by id, or the family recipe below                                 |
| Jotai `atomWithStorage`, Zustand `persist`           | the persisted signal recipe below                                                 |
| Jotai `Provider`, Zustand `createStore` with context | a store with actions, provided through context (recipe below)                     |
| Zustand selectors, `subscribeWithSelector`           | not needed: `computed` for the slice, `effect` to react to it                     |
| Zustand `immer` middleware                           | `store()`: a mutable proxy, mutate it directly                                    |
| Zustand `devtools`                                   | `effect(() => console.debug(JSON.stringify(state)))` (tracks every property read) |
| Valtio `proxy`, `snapshot`                           | `store`, `snapshot`                                                               |
| Solid `reconcile`, TanStack structural sharing       | `reconcile(store, data)`: patch fresh data in, keeping unchanged items            |
| `zustand/vanilla`, a Jotai store, Redux              | the external store recipe below                                                   |

**Islands.** Each [island](islands.md) hydrates as its own root, so context provided by the page
does not reach an island, and one island cannot provide to another. The server renders islands
the same way, so their HTML matches. Islands share the Lumiose runtime and the modules they import,
so islands share state through **scoped state**: `defineState(factory)` returns an accessor whose
factory runs on first use, once per page in the browser and once per request on the server.

**Scoped state on the server.** The factory runs per request, so it can seed itself from the
request (`cookies()`, `locals()`, …); there is no separate seed API. When islands (or SPA routes)
import a state, the page sends its server values: the signals and stores the factory returned,
once per page, in the chunk where the state was first used. In the browser the factory runs again
(rebuilding computeds and functions) and the server values replace its signals and stores before
any island reads them, so hydration matches. A state that only server code imports is never sent.
Sent values must be plain data, like island props (`LUM4011`), and they are **public**: everyone
who can load the page can read them in its source. Never put secrets in a state that islands use.

**Scoped state in tests.** Under Vitest, `@lumiose/vite` resets scoped state before each test: each
test starts with fresh instances, in DOM tests and in server tests (where calls outside a render
share one instance per test).

## API

| API                                                        | Use it for                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `signal(v)`, `computed(fn)`, `store(obj)`                  | The state itself and what derives from it.                           |
| `createContext<T>()`, `<Ctx value={v}>`, `useContext(ctx)` | One instance per subtree (and per request on the server).            |
| `defineState(factory)`                                     | One instance per page, per request on the server; shared by islands. |
| `effect(fn)`, `onMount(fn)`                                | Syncing with the outside world (storage, logging); browser only.     |
| `onCleanup(fn)`                                            | Ending a subscription when its owner is disposed.                    |
| `snapshot(value)`                                          | A plain copy of a store, to save or send. Its reads are not tracked. |
| `reconcile(store, data, { key })`                          | Patching fresh data into a store, keeping unchanged items as is.     |

See [Signals and reactivity](signals.md) for each API.

## Example

### A store with actions (Zustand-style)

A function creates the state and returns it with the functions that change it. Provide one
instance through context: every component below shares it, each request on the server gets its
own, and tests call `createCart()` directly.

```tsx check
import { computed, createContext, store, useContext } from "lumiose";

export function createCart() {
  const state = store({ items: [] as { id: string; qty: number }[] });
  return {
    state,
```
