```tsx check
    count: computed(() => state.items.reduce((n, item) => n + item.qty, 0)),
    add(id: string) {
      const item = state.items.find((item) => item.id === id);
      if (item) item.qty += 1;
      else state.items.push({ id, qty: 1 });
    },
    clear() {
      state.items = [];
    },
  };
}

export type Cart = ReturnType<typeof createCart>;

const CartContext = createContext<Cart>();

export function getCart(): Cart {
  const cart = useContext(CartContext);
  if (cart === undefined) throw new Error("getCart() needs a <Shop> above it.");
  return cart;
}

export function Shop() {
  return (
    <CartContext value={createCart()}>
      <main>
        <AddButton id="pen" />
        <CartCount />
      </main>
    </CartContext>
  );
}

function AddButton({ id }: { id: string }) {
  const cart = getCart();
  return <button onClick={() => cart.add(id)}>Add {id}</button>;
}

function CartCount() {
  const cart = getCart();
  return <p>{cart.count()} items</p>;
}
```

### State shared by islands (defineState)

Define the state at module scope with `defineState` and call its accessor wherever it is used. The
server seeds it from the request; the islands start from the server's values and share one
instance in the browser.

```ts check file=lib/cart.ts
import { computed, cookies, defineState, isServer, store } from "lumiose";

export interface CartItem {
  id: string;
  qty: number;
}

export const cart = defineState(() => {
  // Request APIs exist only on the server; the browser gets the server's values instead.
  const saved = isServer ? cookies().get("cart") : undefined;
  const state = store({ items: saved ? (JSON.parse(saved) as CartItem[]) : [] });
  return {
    state, // sent to the browser (a store)
    count: computed(() => state.items.reduce((n, item) => n + item.qty, 0)), // derived again
    add(id: string) {
      const item = state.items.find((item) => item.id === id);
      if (item) item.qty += 1;
      else state.items.push({ id, qty: 1 });
    },
  };
});
```

```stsx check file=components/CartIslands.stsx
import { cart } from "../lib/cart.ts";

export function AddToCart(props: { id: string }) {
  const { add } = cart();
  return <button onClick={() => add(props.id)}>Add to cart</button>;
}

export function CartBadge() {
  const { count } = cart();
  return <span class="badge">{count()}</span>;
}
```

```stsx check file=routes/shop-islands/page.stsx
import { AddToCart, CartBadge } from "../../components/CartIslands.stsx";
import { cart } from "../../lib/cart.ts";

export const mode = "server";

export default function ShopPage() {
  return (
    <main>
      <header>
        Cart <CartBadge client:idle />
      </header>
      <p>{cart().count()} items, rendered on the server for this request</p>
      <AddToCart client:visible id="pen" />
    </main>
  );
}
```

What the page sends is `cart`'s store (`{ items: [...] }`): `count` and `add` are created again in
the browser. `@lumiose/vite` names each state after its module and export
(`/src/lib/cart.ts#cart`), the way it names islands, so define states at module scope and export
them (or the binding). For state that lives only in the browser, a module-scope `signal` works too,
as long as it is written only in handlers and effects, which never run on the server.

### Families (atomFamily)

A `store` tracks each key separately, so a record keyed by id is already a family: setting
`selected[id]` re-runs only what read that id.

```ts check
import { store } from "lumiose";

export const selected = store<Record<string, boolean>>({});
// selected["todo-1"] = true; re-runs only the bindings that read selected["todo-1"]
```

When each entry must be a signal of its own (to pass it to a component, or to derive from it),
create them on first use:

```ts check
import { signal, type Signal } from "lumiose";

export function family<K, T>(initial: (key: K) => T) {
  const signals = new Map<K, Signal<T>>();
  return {
    get(key: K): Signal<T> {
      let entry = signals.get(key);
      if (entry === undefined) signals.set(key, (entry = signal(initial(key))));
      return entry;
    },
    delete(key: K): void {
      signals.delete(key);
    },
  };
}

export const drafts = family((_postId: string) => "");
// drafts.get("post-1").set("Hello"); drafts.get("post-1")()
```

### Fresh data into a store (reconcile)

Replacing a store's array with a new fetch result (`state.books = fresh`) gives every row a new
object, so a list re-renders every row and loses its local state. `reconcile` patches the data in
instead: rows are matched by `id` (or by `{ key }`), unchanged rows keep their identity, and only
the fields that changed notify.

```ts check
import { reconcile, store } from "lumiose";

interface Book {
  id: number;
  title: string;
}

export const books = store<Book[]>([]);

export async function refresh(): Promise<void> {
  const fresh = (await (await fetch("/api/books")).json()) as Book[];
  reconcile(books, fresh); // only changed titles and added or removed rows update the page
}
```

It works on a part of a store too: `reconcile(state.books, fresh)`. Keys missing from the new
data are deleted, nested objects are merged, and other values are replaced.

### A persisted signal (atomWithStorage, persist)

Call it in a component. The saved value loads in `onMount`, after hydration, so the server HTML
and the first browser render agree; other tabs stay in sync through the `storage` event.

```tsx check
import { effect, onMount, signal, type Signal } from "lumiose";

export function persisted<T>(key: string, initial: T): Signal<T> {
  const value = signal(initial);
  let loaded = false;
  onMount(() => {
    const saved = localStorage.getItem(key);
    if (saved !== null) value.set(JSON.parse(saved) as T);
    loaded = true;
    const sync = (event: StorageEvent) => {
      if (event.key === key && event.newValue !== null) value.set(JSON.parse(event.newValue) as T);
    };
    window.addEventListener("storage", sync);
    return () => window.removeEventListener("storage", sync);
  });
  effect(() => {
    const current = value();
    if (loaded) localStorage.setItem(key, JSON.stringify(current));
  });
  return value;
}

export function ThemeToggle() {
  const theme = persisted<"light" | "dark">("theme", "light");
  return (
    <button onClick={() => theme.update((t) => (t === "light" ? "dark" : "light"))}>
      Theme: {theme()}
    </button>
  );
}
```

In a `client:only` island or an SPA, which render nothing on the server, you can read
`localStorage` directly in `signal(…)` instead.

### An external store (zustand/vanilla, a Jotai store, Redux)

Mirror any store with `getState()` and `subscribe()` into a signal. Call it in a component (or
under another owner) so the subscription ends with it.

```ts check
import { onCleanup, signal } from "lumiose";

export interface ExternalStore<T> {
  getState(): T;
  subscribe(listener: () => void): () => void;
}

export function fromStore<T>(source: ExternalStore<T>): () => T {
  const state = signal(source.getState());
  onCleanup(source.subscribe(() => state.set(source.getState())));
  return state;
}
```

A `zustand/vanilla` store fits as it is: `fromStore(bearStore)`. For a Jotai store, adapt one
atom: `fromStore({ getState: () => jotai.get(countAtom), subscribe: (fn) => jotai.sub(countAtom, fn) })`.
Derive slices with `computed(() => state().bears)`.

## Common mistakes

- **Writing module-scope state during SSR.** A module-scope signal written in a component body or
  a server path leaks one request's state into the next (`LUM4008`). Use `defineState`, whose
  factory runs once per request, or keep it in context.
- **Reading page context inside an island.** Each island starts a new context root, on the
  server as in the browser, so `useContext()` inside it does not see what the page provided outside
  it and returns the context's default (`LUM4010` warns in dev). Pass the value as an island prop,
  provide the context inside the island, or share scoped state (`defineState`).
- **Calling request APIs in a state's factory without a guard.** The factory also runs in the
  browser, where `cookies()` and `locals()` throw `LUM4003`. Read them only on the server
  (`isServer ? cookies().get("cart") : undefined`); the server's values arrive anyway.
- **Putting secrets or class instances in a state that islands use.** Its signals and stores are
  sent with the page, readable by anyone, and must hold plain data (`LUM4011`). Keep secrets in
  server-only modules; keep other values in computeds or functions, which are not sent.
- **Calling a state's accessor at module scope on the server.** There is no request there, so it
  throws. Call it in components, middleware, endpoints or actions.
- **Creating a state inside a function.** Only module-scope states get an id, so a state created
  in a component or helper is never sent and the browser starts from the factory's values.
- **Reading `localStorage` in setup in a server-rendered component.** The server cannot read it,
  so the first browser render differs from the HTML (`LUM4006`). Load it in `onMount`, as the
  persisted recipe does.
- **Copying state between stores with `effect`.** `effect(() => b.set(a()))` adds a frame of
  staleness. Derive with `computed`, or keep one source of truth.
- **Expecting `snapshot()` in an effect to track.** Its reads are not tracked. To log every change,
  read through the store (`JSON.stringify(state)`).
- **Assigning a fresh fetch result over a store's array.** `state.rows = await res.json()` replaces
  every row, so lists re-create their rows and lose row state. Use `reconcile(state.rows, data)`.
- **Wrapping a class instance, `Map` or `Set` in `store()`.** Only plain objects and arrays become
  reactive. Use a record keyed by id, or the family recipe.

## Related diagnostics

- [LUM4008](../errors/LUM4008.md): module-scope signal written during SSR.
- [LUM4011](../errors/LUM4011.md): non-serializable scoped state value.
- [LUM4010](../errors/LUM4010.md): island reads context provided by the page.
- [LUM4006](../errors/LUM4006.md): hydration mismatch.
- [LUM2002](../errors/LUM2002.md): signal write during render.

See also: [Signals and reactivity](signals.md), [Islands](islands.md), [Async components](async.md).

<!-- source: concepts/jsx.md -->

# JSX

> JSX reads like React but compiles to cloned templates with fine-grained bindings, so only the expressions that read signals update.

## Concept

**Bindings.** The compiler looks at each JSX expression:

- Literals and plain identifiers are **static**: written once.
- Calls and member access (`count()`, `user.name`, `props.title`) become **bindings** that re-run
  when a signal they read changes, and write only the part of the DOM they own.
- `untrack(() => …)` opts an expression out.

**Compiled idioms.** There are no `<For>` or `<Show>` components; ordinary JavaScript compiles to
the efficient form:

| Source                                              | Compiled to                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `{items().map((item, i) => <Row key={item.id} />)}` | A keyed list. `key` is optional (items are keyed by reference otherwise). `i` becomes a reactive index only if you use it.                                                                                                            |
| `item.id === selected()` inside `.map`              | An O(1) selector: a selection change touches two rows.                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `{c() ? <A /> : <B />}`, `{c() && <A />}`           | A memoised branch: switches only when the condition flips.                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `{count() * 2}`, ``{`#${id}`}``, `{String(x)}`      | Provably text: a text node of the template, updated with `setText` (written once when nothing reactive is read). Applies to sole children and to children between elements; a `const` initialised with such an expression counts too. |
| `{row.label()}`, `{id}`, `{props.title}`            | Maybe text, alone between nodes (or the only child): also a text node of the template, written by `insertText`. Text values update the node in place; nodes, arrays and other values render in a region before it.                    |
| `{fn()}` next to text or another `{…}`              | A dynamic insert (a region), since adjacent text nodes would merge when the HTML is parsed.                                                                                                                                           |

**Elements.**

| Prop                         | Rule                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `class`                      | A string, an array, or a `{ name: boolean }` record (nested arrays allowed). `className` is a type error.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `style`                      | A string, or an object with **kebab-case** keys, including `--custom` properties. Each key updates on its own.                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `aria-*`, `spellcheck`, …    | Booleans are written as `"true"`/`"false"` (`aria-pressed={false}` renders `aria-pressed="false"`): `aria-*`, `contenteditable`, `draggable`, `spellcheck` and the other enumerated attributes, static or not. Other attributes: `true` adds the attribute empty (`hidden`); `false`, `null` and `undefined` leave it out. |
| `onClick`, `onKeyDown`, …    | camelCase handlers. Bubbling events are delegated (one listener per type at `document`); non-bubbling ones (`onFocus`, `onMouseEnter`, `onScroll`) get a direct listener.                                                                                                                                                  |
| `on:click`, `on:my-event`    | A native `addEventListener` listener with the exact event name. Use it for custom and web-component events.                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Props of a custom element    | The element's property when it defines one (arrays and objects as they are), else the attribute, as in React 19. See [Web components](../guides/web-components.md).                                                                                                                                                        |
| `bind:value`, `bind:checked` | Two-way binding to a writable signal, on `input`, `select` and `textarea`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `attach={[fn]}`              | Runs `fn(el)` with the element in a tracked scope; it may return a cleanup.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `ref={fn}`                   | Called with the element. `ref<T>()` makes a callback you can read like a signal.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `innerHTML`                  | Sets unescaped HTML. The lint rule `no-unsafe-html` warns.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `key`                        | Allowed on intrinsic elements and components (list identity).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `client:*`                   | Island directives, on components only. See [Islands](islands.md).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

Handlers receive the **native** event, with `currentTarget` typed as the element. There are no
synthetic events.

## API

JSX types come from `lumiose/jsx-runtime` (via `jsxImportSource: "lumiose"`) and the global `JSX`
namespace from `lumiose/env`:

| Type                     | Meaning                                                                      |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `JSX.Element`            | Anything JSX can render: nodes, strings, numbers, arrays, functions, `null`. |
| `JSX.ClassValue`         | The `class` prop value.                                                      |
| `JSX.CSSProperties`      | The `style` object (kebab-case keys and `--custom` properties).              |
| `JSX.EventHandler<E, T>` | A handler: the native event `E` with `currentTarget: T`.                     |
| `JSX.Ref<T>`             | The value of `ref<T>()`.                                                     |
| `JSX.HTMLProps<T>`       | Props of an HTML element, for wrappers and custom elements.                  |

See [JSX types and tsconfig](../reference/jsx.md) for custom elements and the full rules.

## Example

```tsx check
import { signal } from "lumiose";

interface Todo {
  id: number;
  title: string;
}

export function TodoList() {
  const todos = signal<Todo[]>([
    { id: 1, title: "Write docs" },
    { id: 2, title: "Ship" },
  ]);
  const selected = signal(1);
  const draft = signal("");
  const progress = signal(40);

  const add = (event: SubmitEvent) => {
    event.preventDefault();
    todos.update((list) => [...list, { id: Date.now(), title: draft() }]);
    draft.set("");
  };

  return (
    <section style={{ "--progress": `${progress()}%`, "max-inline-size": "40rem" }}>
      <form onSubmit={add}>
        <input bind:value={draft} on:focus={(event) => event.currentTarget.select()} />
        <button disabled={draft() === ""}>Add</button>
      </form>
      {todos().length === 0 ? (
        <p>Nothing to do.</p>
      ) : (
        <ul>
          {todos().map((todo) => (
            <li
              key={todo.id}
              class={["todo", { active: todo.id === selected() }]}
              onClick={() => selected.set(todo.id)}
            >
              {todo.title}
            </li>
          ))}
        </ul>
      )}
    </section>
  );
}
```

## Common mistakes

- **React prop names.** `className` → `class`, `htmlFor` → `for`, `onclick`/`onKeydown` →
  `onClick`/`onKeyDown` (camelCase after `on`). The wrong forms are type errors.
- **camelCase style keys.** `style={{ fontWeight: 600 }}` is a type error; write
  `{ "font-weight": 600 }`, as in CSS. Numbers get no units: write `"12px"`.
- **Passing a value to `bind:value`.** It needs the signal itself: `bind:value={draft}`, not
  `bind:value={draft()}`.
- **Custom events with `onX`.** `onMyEvent` is not an event prop; write `on:my-event`.
- **Using the index outside the row.** The `i` of `.map((item, i) => …)` is a reactive index that
  belongs to its row; storing it in an outer variable or closure that outlives the row is
  `LUM2006`.
- **Wrapping lists in helper components.** `{items().map(…)}` already compiles to a keyed list;
  there is no `<For>`.
- **`innerHTML` with user input.** It is not escaped. Prefer text children.

## Related diagnostics

- [LUM2004](../errors/LUM2004.md): component called as a function.
- [LUM2005](../errors/LUM2005.md): children inserted twice.
- [LUM2006](../errors/LUM2006.md): reactive index escapes its callback.
- [LUM1001](../errors/LUM1001.md): syntax error.

See also: [Components](components.md), [Styles](styles.md), [reference: JSX types](../reference/jsx.md).

<!-- source: concepts/styles.md -->

# Styles

> Write plain CSS in `<style>` blocks: where a block sits decides its scope, and CSS can read JS constants at build time.

## Concept

**One block per file, at the end.** The default is a single top-level `<style>` after the
components. It styles every template in the file, so several components share it, and it reads
any top-level `const` declared above it. The JSX stays free of CSS, and the file reads like a
component file with its stylesheet:

```stsx check
import { signal } from "lumiose";

const accent = "#5546ff";
const radius = "10px";

export function Counter() {
  const count = signal(0);

  return (
    <div class="counter">
      <button onClick={() => count.update((n) => n + 1)}>{count()}</button>
      <Reset onReset={() => count.set(0)} />
    </div>
  );
}

export function Reset(props: { onReset: () => void }) {
  return (
    <button class="reset" onClick={props.onReset}>
      Reset
    </button>
  );
}

<style>
  .counter { display: flex; gap: 0.5rem; }
  button {
    padding: 0.5rem 1rem;
    border: 0;
    border-radius: $radius;
    background: $accent;
    color: white;
  }
  .reset { background: transparent; color: $accent; }
</style>
```

`Counter` and `Reset` share the block: `button` matches the buttons of both, and of no other file.

**Placement decides scope.**

| Placement                                                                            | Scope                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| File top level (by convention, one block at the end of the file)                     | Every template in the file.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Inside a component's JSX, as a child of an intrinsic element or fragment (any depth) | Its **enclosing element and everything written inside it** in that component, including `.map` callbacks and JSX passed as children there. A block directly under the component's root element therefore covers the whole component. Sibling subtrees are not affected, and it never reaches other components' own templates. |
| `<style global>` (anywhere a block is valid)                                         | The whole app, unscoped. Usually at the end of the root `layout.stsx`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

**Nested blocks, for two jobs.** A block inside a component's JSX is still valid. Reach for one
when the file-level block cannot do the job:

- **Scoping one element's subtree,** so a selector such as `p` or `.note` cannot match anything
  else in the file.
- **Reading a constant declared inside a component** (`const gap = 12` in its body). A file-level
  block only sees top-level constants.

```stsx
export function Panel() {
  const gap = 12;

  return (
    <div class="panel">
      <aside class="side">…</aside>                 {/* not styled by the <style> below */}
      <section class="body">
        <p class="note">…</p>
        <style> p { color: tomato; } </style>      {/* only the <p> of this <section> */}
      </section>
      <style> .panel { gap: calc($gap * 1px); } </style>   {/* reads the component's `gap` */}
    </div>
  );
}

<style>
  .panel { display: grid; }
</style>
```

Everything else goes in the file-level block. Moving a block from a component's root to the end
of the file widens its scope to every component in the file: check that its selectors (bare
element selectors in particular) do not start matching another component's elements.

**How scoping works.** Each scope with styles gets a token `data-l-<hash>`, a stable hash of the
file path plus the component name, with one token per style-bearing element. Every element in the
scope carries the token: the whole file for top-level blocks, and the enclosing element's lexical
subtree for blocks inside a component. The last compound of each selector gets `[data-l-<hash>]`,
a +0,1,0 specificity bump. Dynamic classes always work, because no element is pruned.

- `:global(.sel)` leaves a selector unscoped; `:deep(.sel)` scopes only the part before it.
- `@keyframes` names are scoped, and `animation` references are rewritten. A block sees its own
  keyframes, then those of the blocks of enclosing elements (innermost first), then the file's, so
  a nested block can animate with keyframes defined under the component's root. Custom properties
  are not scoped.
- **Class passthrough.** When a parent passes `class` to a child component, the parent's scope
  tokens at that call site travel with it: the file token plus every enclosing style subtree. So
  `.cta { … }` in the parent styles `<Button class="cta" />` wherever `Button` applies
  `props.class`. The child applies it on every element whose `class` value may contain it:
  `class={["btn", props.class]}`, a destructured `class` prop or `...rest`, a helper that gets
  `props` (`class={variantClass(props)}`), or a local value or function built from them
  (`const classes = () => ["btn", props.class]`). A class that reaches the element any other way
  (a module-level variable, a context) loses the parent's scope, so read `props.class` in the
  component. Forwarding works through intermediate components: when `Field` passes its own
  `class` prop on (`<Input class={["field", props.class]} />`), `Input`'s element gets `Field`'s
  tokens and those of `Field`'s caller.
- Within a file, file-level CSS comes first, then component blocks in source order.
- **In the editor**, class completion follows the same scopes: in a `class` attribute it offers
  the classes of the blocks that apply there (innermost first), then the project's global classes
  (`<style global>` blocks and imported global `.css` files), never a sibling subtree's.
  `var(--…)` offers every custom property declared in the project, with its value.

**Blocks are plain CSS:** no Sass, no `lang`, `media` or other attributes (only `global`). For CSS
that is not a component's own (a reset, theme tokens, a stylesheet from another project, Tailwind),
import `.css` files or CSS modules: see "Stylesheets, CSS Modules and Tailwind" below.

> **Status:** available. `@lumiose/vite` serves each file's CSS as a CSS module, and style-only or
> constant-only edits hot-update the CSS without remounting. `LUM3012` (a custom property set in a
> `style` prop that no stylesheet reads) needs the whole project: `lumiose build`, `lumiose check` and
> the language server report it.

**In builds**, a page needs few render-blocking stylesheets. `lumiose build` merges the stylesheets
every page starts with (the document's, the root layouts', shared components') into one file that
all pages link and browsers cache, then puts each page's own stylesheets after it: inline in one
`<style>` when they total 4 kB or less, else merged into one file for that page. The cascade
order is the same as in dev, where each file's CSS stays a separate stylesheet for HMR. In the
sample apps a first view went from 6–8 stylesheet requests to one, with about 30% fewer CSS bytes (brotli).
A page that links a stylesheet also gets `<script>/* waits for the stylesheets above */</script>`
after its stylesheet tags (54 bytes, in dev too). The browser parses the body only once the
stylesheets before that script have loaded, so the body's first layout is styled. Without it,
Chrome could lay out the unstyled body when a scrolled page is reloaded, restore the scroll
position from that layout, and paint the first frames at the wrong place until `load`.
The first paint waits for the stylesheets either way. With `csp: "strict"` the script gets the
nonce or its hash (see [Security](security.md)).
Each tag lists the stylesheets it holds in `data-l-css`, so an island or an SPA route that imports
one does not load it again. Pages link the CSS files the build output contains: when another Vite
plugin rewrites a stylesheet under a new name after Lumiose recorded it, the build follows it (by
the chunks that import it, the name it was emitted with, or the one new CSS file), and warns about
a linked stylesheet the output no longer has.

### JS values in styles

`$name` and `$obj.key` put a JS value into CSS. The compiler evaluates the reference at build time
and inlines the result, so the output is plain CSS: no runtime lookup and no JS inside CSS.
TypeScript checks each reference like any other expression. Imports used only by `$` references
are removed from the JS output, and editing them hot-reloads the CSS only.

**What a reference can name:** a `const` whose value the compiler can work out without running the
app.

| Declared as                                                                                  | Readable from                                                                                                    |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A top-level `const` of the file                                                              | Every block of the file. A top-level block must come after it.                                                   |
| A `const` of the enclosing component                                                         | Blocks inside that component, `<style global>` included.                                                         |
| An `export const` (or `export default`) of an imported `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.stsx` or JSON module | Every block of the importing file: named, default or namespace imports (`$theme.space.md`), re-exports included. |

Imports are resolved the way the rest of the toolchain resolves them: by Vite in `lumiose dev` and
builds (aliases included), and like TypeScript in `lumiose check` and the editor (relative paths,
tsconfig `paths`, package `exports` and `imports`). An import that cannot be resolved, or that has
no such export, is reported as [LUM3008](../errors/LUM3008.md) at each reference.

The value may be built from literals, template literals, arithmetic (`+ - * / % **`, unary `-`),
other constants, and object literals with their members at any depth (`$theme.color.brand`),
including spreads, destructuring, `as const` and `satisfies`. Mark token objects `as const`: a plain
object literal folds too, as written, but only `as const` keeps the JS read-only like the CSS.

**How values are written.** Strings are inserted verbatim, without quotes (`"12px"` becomes
`12px`; for a CSS string, put the quotes inside: `'"→"'`). Numbers are inserted as plain numbers
(`const gap = 8` gives `8`), so give them a unit with `calc($gap * 1px)` (which ships as `8px`, see below) or keep the unit in the
constant (`"8px"`, `` `${gap}px` ``). A bare number where a length, angle or time is required
(`gap: $gap`, `rotate: $angle`) is [LUM3018](../errors/LUM3018.md), with `calc($gap * 1px)` as the
fix: Lightning CSS happens to read a bare length as pixels, but angles and times are dropped, and in
custom properties or math functions the number stays unitless. A unit written after the reference
(`$gap px`) does not attach to it ([LUM3019](../errors/LUM3019.md)).

**What cannot be referenced.** The compiler reports it; the CSS keeps the `$` text, which browsers
ignore.

| Reference                                                                                                   | Diagnostic                      | Fix                                                                                                    |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `$space(2)`: a function call, or a `const` holding a function or a call's result (`Date.now()`, `signal()`) | [LUM3008](../errors/LUM3008.md) | Compute it as a constant: `calc($space * 2px)` with `const space = 4`, or name the steps: `$space.md`. |
| `$count` where `count` is a `let` (or `var`)                                                                | [LUM3008](../errors/LUM3008.md) | Make it a `const`, or pass it at runtime (below).                                                      |
| `$open`, `$props.width`: signals, props, parameters                                                         | [LUM3008](../errors/LUM3008.md) | Pass it at runtime (below).                                                                            |
| `$sizes.0`: an array item (`sizes.0` is not JS)                                                             | [LUM3008](../errors/LUM3008.md) | An `as const` object with named keys: `$sizes.sm`.                                                     |
| `$brand-primary`: a hyphen, read as `$brand` minus `primary`                                                | [LUM3009](../errors/LUM3009.md) | `$brand.primary`, or a camelCase constant: `$brandPrimary`.                                            |
| A component's `const` in a block outside it (file level, or another component)                              | [LUM3008](../errors/LUM3008.md) | Move the `const` to the top level, or the block into the component.                                    |
| A top-level block above the `const` it reads                                                                | [LUM3013](../errors/LUM3013.md) | Move the block below it; by convention, to the end of the file.                                        |

`LUM3008`'s message says which case it is (a `let` binding, computed by a call at runtime, an array,
not declared in scope, an import that does not export the name, …).

**Where `$` is read:** in property values (`gap: calc($gap * 1px)`) and in `@media`, `@container`
and `@supports` preludes (`@media (width < $narrow)`). Everywhere else `$` is left to CSS:

- In selectors, `$` keeps its CSS meaning: `[href$=".pdf"]` is "ends with". `.size-$md` is not a
  reference but an invalid selector, which Lightning CSS drops (`LUM3015`).
- Property names, strings (`content: "$gap"`), comments and `url($file)` are not substituted. Put
  the whole value in the constant instead: `const hero = 'url("/hero.png")'` and
  `background-image: $hero`.

**Runtime values.** A `$` reference is fixed at build time. For a value that changes (a signal, a
prop, a measurement), set a custom property with the `style` prop and read it with `var()`. Custom
properties are not scoped and inherit, so descendants can read them too.

```stsx
<div class="bar" style={{ "--fill": `${pct()}%` }}>
  <style>
    .bar { inline-size: var(--fill); }
  </style>
</div>
```

Tokens usually live in their own module:

```ts check file=theme.ts
// src/theme.ts
export const space = { sm: 4, md: 8, lg: 16 } as const;
export const radius = "6px";
export const narrow = "40rem";
```

```stsx check file=components/Meter.stsx
// src/components/Meter.stsx
import * as theme from "../theme.ts";

const track = theme.space.sm * 2;
const shadow = `0 1px ${track / 4}px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.2)`;

export function Meter(props: { label: string; value: number }) {
  const border = 1;

  return (
    <div class="meter" style={{ "--value": `${props.value}%` }}>
      <span>{props.label}</span>
      <div class="track">
        <div class="fill" />
      </div>

      <style>
        .meter {
          --pad: calc($theme.space.md * 2px);
          display: grid;
          gap: calc($theme.space.sm * 1px);
          padding: var(--pad);
          border: calc($border * 1px) solid;
          border-radius: $theme.radius;
        }
        .track { block-size: calc($track * 1px); border-radius: calc($track * 1px / 2); box-shadow: $shadow; }
        .fill { inline-size: var(--value); block-size: 100%; background: currentColor; }
        @media (width < $theme.narrow) {
          .meter { max-inline-size: calc(100% - $theme.space.lg * 2px); }
        }
      </style>
    </div>
  );
}
```

The compiler's CSS output for that file (`data-l-lw1tegds` is the component's scope token). Every
`$` reference and every constant `calc()` is gone; only the runtime `var(--value)` and the
`%`-relative width are left to the browser:

```css
.meter[data-l-lw1tegds] {
  --pad: 16px;
  padding: var(--pad);
  border: 1px solid;
  border-radius: 6px;
  gap: 4px;
  display: grid;
}

.track[data-l-lw1tegds] {
  border-radius: 4px;
  block-size: 8px;
  box-shadow: 0 1px 2px #0003;
}

.fill[data-l-lw1tegds] {
  inline-size: var(--value);
  background: currentColor;
  block-size: 100%;
}

@media (width < 40rem) {
  .meter[data-l-lw1tegds] {
    max-inline-size: calc(100% - 32px);
  }
}
```

Lightning CSS also minifies values (`rgb(0 0 0 / 0.2)` becomes `#0003`) and may reorder or merge
declarations, so the output is equivalent to the source, not identical.

#### Build-time math

Constant math never reaches the browser. It is computed in two steps:

1. **JS math, by the Lumiose compiler.** Arithmetic in constants and template literals is evaluated
   before the value is inserted: `const track = theme.space.sm * 2` inlines `8`.
2. **CSS math, by Lightning CSS.** After substitution, Lightning CSS reduces `calc()`, `min()`,
   `max()`, `clamp()`, `round()`, `abs()`, the trigonometric functions and the other CSS math
   functions whenever the operands are concrete values in compatible units. `calc($gap * 2px)`
   becomes `calc(8 * 2px)`, which ships as `16px`.

| Source (`$gap` is `8`)                    | Output                                | Why                                            |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `padding: calc($gap * 2px)`               | `padding: 16px`                       | `calc(8 * 2px)` reduces.                       |
| `inline-size: min(10px, 20px)`            | `inline-size: 10px`                   |                                                |
| `block-size: clamp(4px, 8px, 12px)`       | `block-size: 8px`                     |                                                |
| `transform: rotate(calc(45deg * 2))`      | `transform: rotate(90deg)`            | Math inside other functions reduces too.       |
| `inset: calc(2px + 3px) calc(1rem + 4px)` | `inset: 5px calc(1rem + 4px)`         | Each value on its own: `rem` plus `px` stays.  |
| `width: calc(100% - $gap * 2px)`          | `width: calc(100% - 16px)`            | The constant part reduces; `%` stays.          |
| `font-size: calc(2 * 1rem)`               | `font-size: 2rem`                     | One unit: nothing to convert.                  |
| `font-size: clamp(1rem, 2vw, 3rem)`       | unchanged                             | `rem` and `vw` are only known in the browser.  |
| `max-width: calc(var(--w) + $gap * 2px)`  | `max-width: calc(var(--w) + 8 * 2px)` | A declaration with `var()` is kept as written. |
| `--space: calc($gap * 2px)`               | `--space: 16px`                       | A custom property, folded by Lumiose (below).  |
| `padding-left: calc($gap * 1px - 12px)`   | `padding-left: 0`                     | Negative in a non-negative property (below).   |
| `margin-left: calc($gap * 1px - 12px)`    | `margin-left: -4px`                   | Margins can be negative.                       |

**What cannot fold.** A math function is replaced only by a value that means the same thing
wherever it is used. Absolute units convert into each other (`calc(1in + 4px)` is `100px`) and a
unit combines with itself (`calc(2 * 1rem)` is `2rem`), but context-dependent units mixed with
others need the browser: `%` resolves against the containing block (or the font size, depending on
the property), `vw` and `vh` against the viewport, `em` against the element's font size and `rem`
against the root's. A `var()` is only known when the browser computes styles, so Lightning CSS keeps
any declaration containing one exactly as written, constant parts included. To precompute those,
do the arithmetic in JS: with `` const extra = `${gap * 2}px` ``, `calc(var(--w) + $extra)` ships as
`calc(var(--w) + 16px)`.

**Custom properties.** Lightning CSS keeps custom property values as written, because it cannot
know where they will be used. Lumiose folds each math function in them that reduces to a single value
in compatible units: `--space: calc($gap * 2px)` becomes `16px`, `--turn: rotate(calc(45deg * 2))`
becomes `rotate(90deg)`, and `var(--x, calc($gap * 3px))` becomes `var(--x, 24px)`. Anything with
`var()`, `env()` or context-dependent units mixed with other units stays whole, without the partial
reduction regular properties get (`--inset: calc(100% - $gap * 2px)` stays `calc(100% - 8 * 2px)`).
Negative results and fractional numbers stay inside `calc()` (`calc(-3px)`, `calc(.333333)`),
because a bare value can behave differently where the property is read: `calc()` clamps to the
property's range and rounds where an integer is expected.

**Negative results.** Some properties cannot be negative: padding, sizes (`width`, `min-height`,
…), border widths, `gap`, `font-size`, `line-height` and others. In the browser, a `calc()` that
comes out negative there is clamped to 0, while a negative value written out is invalid and the
whole declaration is dropped. So that folding does not change the meaning, a negative result in such
a property ships as `0`: `padding-left: calc($gap * 1px - 12px)` gives `padding-left: 0`, and
`font-size: calc(1rem - 2rem)` gives `font-size: 0`. This mirrors the upstream Lightning CSS fix
([lightningcss#1329](https://github.com/parcel-bundler/lightningcss/pull/1329)), which Lumiose
applies until a release includes it. Properties that accept negative values, such as margins and
`inset`, keep them.

Folding regular properties, minification and browser targets come from
[Lightning CSS](https://lightningcss.dev), the CSS parser, transformer and minifier from the Parcel
project, which Lumiose's CSS compiler is built on. Lumiose adds `$` constants, scoping and the
custom-property folding.

### Stylesheets, CSS Modules and Tailwind

Style blocks hold a component's own styles. Three other ways to style work next to them through
Vite, in `lumiose dev` and in builds: imported `.css` files, CSS modules and Tailwind v4. A smoke
test (`examples/ssr-styles-e2e`) checks each one in Chromium: server-rendered, without
JavaScript, and in a hydrated island. StyleX is not supported yet (below); Sass is not covered.

**Imported `.css` files are global.** Nothing in them is scoped, and `$` references are not read.
A page links a stylesheet when its import graph reaches it: the page, its layouts and the
components they import. Import a stylesheet from the root layout to link it on every page, or from
one route's page or layout to link it on that route only. The server-rendered HTML links it, so
the page is styled before any script runs; builds merge it with the page's other stylesheets (see
"In builds" above).

```stsx check
// src/routes/layout.stsx
// Global CSS first: the file's style block comes after it in the cascade.
import "../styles/app.css";

export default function Root(props: { children?: JSX.Element }) {
  return <div class="shell">{props.children}</div>;
}

<style>
  .shell { max-inline-size: 60rem; margin-inline: auto; }
</style>
```

**Cascade order.** A page's stylesheets come in import order: a file's imports (stylesheets and
the components it renders) before its own style blocks, and a layout before its page. Rules of the
same specificity resolve in that order. A scoped selector carries an extra attribute (+0,1,0), so a
block's `.card` beats a stylesheet's `.card` wherever the two come. Keep base styles (resets,
typography, tokens) in a global stylesheet and refine them in blocks.

**CSS Modules** suit stylesheets shared by several files or brought from another project. Vite
processes `*.module.css` files: it hashes each class name (`.pill` becomes `_pill_1x2y3_1`), and
the default export maps the names to the hashed classes, typed as a read-only class map by
`lumiose/env`. The server render and the browser get the same names in `lumiose dev` and in builds,
so islands hydrate without mismatches. Pass the classes to `class` like any string, alone or in an
array with other classes:

```css
/* src/components/Badge.module.css */
.pill {
  border-radius: 999px;
  padding: 0 0.5rem;
}
.warn {
  background: gold;
}
```

```stsx check file=components/Badge.stsx
// src/components/Badge.stsx
import styles from "./Badge.module.css";

export function Badge(props: { warn?: boolean; class?: string; children?: JSX.Element }) {
  return (
    <span class={["badge", styles.pill, props.warn && styles.warn, props.class]}>
      {props.children}
    </span>
  );
}

<style>
  .badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; }
</style>
```

A CSS module is global CSS with unique names: placement scoping, `$name` constants and the
`LUM3xxx` diagnostics apply to style blocks only. Prefer a style block for a component's own
styles; class completion in the editor covers style blocks and global stylesheets, not CSS
modules. Other preprocessors' module files (`.module.scss`) work through Vite, typed by
`vite/client`.

**Tailwind v4.** Install `tailwindcss` and `@tailwindcss/vite`, add Tailwind's Vite plugin next to
Lumiose's, and import Tailwind from a global stylesheet that the root layout imports (the
`src/styles/app.css` of the layout above):

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import lumiose from "@lumiose/vite";
import tailwindcss from "@tailwindcss/vite";
import { defineConfig } from "vite";

export default defineConfig({ plugins: [tailwindcss(), lumiose()] });
```

```css
/* src/styles/app.css */
@import "tailwindcss";
```

Tailwind's scanner reads every source file Git does not ignore, `.stsx` files included, and
generates the utilities it finds. Write them in `class` as a string, an array or a record. As
Tailwind requires, each class appears whole in the source, also the ones a signal turns on later:

```stsx check file=components/Toggle.stsx
// src/components/Toggle.stsx
import { signal } from "lumiose";

export function Toggle(props: { label: string }) {
  const on = signal(false);

  return (
    <button
      type="button"
      class={[
        "rounded-lg px-3 py-1",
        { "font-bold": on(), underline: on() },
        on() ? "bg-emerald-500 text-white" : "bg-gray-200",
      ]}
      onClick={() => on.update((value) => !value)}
    >
      {props.label}
    </button>
  );
}
```

- **Utilities lose to style blocks.** Tailwind v4 puts utilities in `@layer utilities`. Style
  blocks and the unlayered rules of your stylesheets are in no layer, so they win at any
  specificity: `<p class="note p-8">` keeps a block's `.note { padding: 2px; }`. Set a property in
  one place, or make the utility important (`p-8!`).
- **In style blocks, read Tailwind's theme variables:** `color: var(--color-emerald-500)`,
  `padding: calc(var(--spacing) * 4)`. Tailwind emits the variables it finds in the sources.
- **`@apply`, `theme()` and `--spacing()`** work in a block that starts with
  `@reference "../styles/app.css";` (the stylesheet that imports Tailwind), as in any CSS that
  Tailwind processes on its own. Without it, the build fails with "Cannot apply unknown utility
  class". The block's selectors stay scoped: `.card { @apply p-6; }` styles only this file's
  `.card`.

  ```stsx
  <style>
    @reference "../styles/app.css";
    .card {
      @apply rounded-lg p-6 font-bold;
      margin: --spacing(4);
      border: 2px solid theme(--color-red-500);
    }
  </style>
  ```

  The compiler keeps Tailwind's at-rules as written for Tailwind's Vite plugin and does not report
  them: `@apply`, `@reference`, `@theme`, `@utility`, `@variant`, `@custom-variant` (with
  `@slot`), `@source`, `@plugin` and `@config`. Other unknown at-rules are still
  [LUM3015](../errors/LUM3015.md) warnings, and so is `@APPLY`: Tailwind matches the names
  case-sensitively.

- **In the editor,** Lumiose's class completion lists the classes of style blocks and global
  stylesheets, not Tailwind's utilities. Tailwind CSS IntelliSense for VS Code gives those once it
  treats `.stsx` like JSX, in the workspace settings:
  `"tailwindCSS.includeLanguages": { "stsx": "javascriptreact" }`.

**StyleX is not supported yet** in server-rendered apps (spiked with StyleX 0.19 and its Vite
plugin, `@stylexjs/unplugin`):

- **`.stsx` files are not compiled.** The plugin only transforms `.js`, `.ts`, `.jsx` and `.tsx`
  files, so `stylex.create()` in an `.stsx` file throws when the page renders. In `.ts` and `.tsx`
  modules it compiles.
- **Production builds lose rules.** The plugin appends all rules to one stylesheet (renamed under
  a new hash, which pages follow), while Lumiose links each route's own stylesheets: only the pages
  that link that one file get the rules. Pointing its `cssInjectionTarget` at a stylesheet the root
  layout imports stops the build in Vite (`vite:css-post`), since the plugin deletes a file Vite
  still reads.
- **In `lumiose dev`** the rules are served at `/virtual:stylex.css` but not linked; a document
  must link them itself: `{import.meta.env.DEV && <link rel="stylesheet" href="/virtual:stylex.css" />}`.
- **Apply styles with `stylex.attrs()`,** which returns `class` and a `style` string, the attributes
  Lumiose's JSX takes: `<h1 {...stylex.attrs(styles.title)}>`. `stylex.props()` returns React's
  `className` and a camelCase `style` object, which Lumiose does not read.

## API

| Syntax                                   | Meaning                                                                                                   |
| ---------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<style>…</style>` at module top level   | File-scoped CSS, shared by every component of the file. By convention one block, at the end of the file.  |
| `<style>…</style>` in component JSX      | CSS scoped to its enclosing element's subtree (the whole component when placed under the root element).   |
| `<style global>…</style>`                | Unscoped, app-wide CSS.                                                                                   |
| `$name`, `$obj.key`                      | A JS constant, inlined at build time, in property values and `@media`/`@container`/`@supports` preludes.  |
| `calc()`, `min()`, `max()`, `clamp()`, … | Folded at build time when every operand is a concrete value in compatible units.                          |
| `:global(sel)`, `:deep(sel)`             | Escape or extend the scope.                                                                               |
| `style={{ "--x": value }}` + `var(--x)`  | Runtime values.                                                                                           |
| `import "./app.css"`                     | A global stylesheet, linked on the pages whose import graph reaches it (every page from the root layout). |
| `import styles from "./x.module.css"`    | A CSS module: `styles.name` is the hashed class of `.name`.                                               |

## Example

```stsx check
// tokens are usually in their own module: `export const radius = { sm: "4px", lg: "12px" } as const;`
const radius = { sm: "4px", lg: "12px" } as const;
const BREAKPOINT = "40rem";

export function Card(props: { title: string; progress: number; class?: string }) {
  return (
    <article class={["card", props.class]} style={{ "--progress": `${props.progress}%` }}>
      <h2>{props.title}</h2>
      <div class="bar" />
    </article>
  );
}

export function Dashboard(props: { columns: number }) {
  const gap = 12;

  return (
    <main class="dashboard" style={{ "--columns": props.columns }}>
      <Card class="featured" title="Uploads" progress={40} />
      <Card title="Downloads" progress={75} />

      <style>
        .dashboard { gap: calc($gap * 1px); }
      </style>
    </main>
  );
}

<style>
  .dashboard { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(var(--columns), 1fr); }
  .card { display: grid; gap: 0.5rem; border-radius: $radius.lg; }
  .card h2 { margin: 0; }
  .bar { inline-size: var(--progress); block-size: 4px; background: currentColor; }
  .featured { outline: 2px solid gold; }
  @media (width < $BREAKPOINT) { .card { border-radius: $radius.sm; } }
</style>
```

`Card` and `Dashboard` share the file-level block, which reads the top-level constants. `.featured`
is set by `Dashboard` and styles the `<article>` inside `Card`: both are in the file's scope (from
another file, the class would get there through class passthrough). The nested block in
`Dashboard` is there because it reads `gap`, a constant of the component.

## Common mistakes

- **A block inside `{…}`, a conditional, a `.map` callback, or a component element** such as
  `<Suspense>` or `<Card>`. Move it into an intrinsic element of the component (`LUM3010`).
- **Returning a block, or using it as an expression** (`return <style>…`, `=> <style>`). Put it
  inside the returned element (`LUM3011`).
- **Hyphenated references.** `$brand-primary` reads `$brand` minus `primary`. Use an object
  member: `$brand.primary` (`LUM3009`).
- **Non-constant references.** `$count` where `count` is a signal, a prop or a `let`, or a call
  such as `$space(2)`, is `LUM3008`. Pass runtime values with `style={{ "--count": count() }}` and
  `var(--count)`; replace calls with constant math (`calc($space * 2px)`).
- **Array items.** `$sizes.0` is not JS (`LUM3008`). Use an `as const` object: `$sizes.sm`.
- **A unit after a reference.** `margin: $gap px` ships as `8 px`, which browsers ignore
  (`LUM3019`). Write `calc($gap * 1px)` or keep the unit in the constant.
- **A unitless number in a length, angle or time.** `gap: $gap` with `const gap = 8` relies on
  Lightning CSS reading `8` as pixels, and `rotate: $angle` is dropped (`LUM3018`). Multiply by the
  unit (`calc($angle * 1deg)`) or keep the unit in the constant.
- **`$` in selectors, strings or `url()`.** It is not substituted there (`[href$=".pdf"]` is CSS's
  "ends with"). Put the whole value in a constant, `url()` included.
- **A top-level block before the `const`s it reads.** Move the block to the end of the file
  (`LUM3013`).
- **`<style>` in a `.tsx` file.** It is a type error in `.tsx` (and `LUM1006` for raw CSS); rename the file to `.stsx`.
- **Attributes on `<style>`.** Only `global` is allowed (`LUM1005`).
- **Expecting a parent's styles to reach into children from another file.** A file's blocks
  never style the templates of components defined in other files; pass `class` (passthrough) or
  use `:deep()`.
- **Expecting a nested block to style sibling subtrees.** A `<style>` inside an element only
  styles that element's subtree. Move its rules to the file-level block at the end of the file,
  or the block up to the common ancestor.
- **Styling JSX returned by a helper function.** In `const field = () => <label class="field">…`
  inside a component, the helper's JSX is not inside the element that holds a nested `<style>`, so
  `.field` matches nothing there (`LUM3005`). Move the block to the top level of the file (it
  styles every element of the file), or render that JSX inside the styled element.
- **Expecting a Tailwind utility to override a style block.** Utilities are in a cascade layer,
  which loses to every style block. Set the property in one place, or make the utility important
  (`p-8!`).
- **`@apply` without `@reference`** fails the build ("Cannot apply unknown utility class"). Start
  the block with `@reference` to the stylesheet that imports Tailwind.
- **Tailwind classes built from pieces** (`` `bg-${color}-500` ``). Tailwind's scanner cannot find
  them; write every class whole, for example in a record (`{ "bg-red-500": error() }`).
- **`stylex.create()` in an `.stsx` file.** StyleX does not compile `.stsx` files and is not
  supported yet in server-rendered apps.

## Related diagnostics

- [LUM1004](../errors/LUM1004.md), [LUM1005](../errors/LUM1005.md), [LUM1006](../errors/LUM1006.md): unclosed block, unknown attribute, raw CSS in `.tsx`.
- [LUM3005](../errors/LUM3005.md): unused scoped selector.
- [LUM3008](../errors/LUM3008.md), [LUM3009](../errors/LUM3009.md), [LUM3013](../errors/LUM3013.md): `$` reference problems.
- [LUM3010](../errors/LUM3010.md), [LUM3011](../errors/LUM3011.md): misplaced blocks.
- [LUM3012](../errors/LUM3012.md): custom property set but never read.
- [LUM3014](../errors/LUM3014.md), [LUM3015](../errors/LUM3015.md): CSS syntax error, invalid CSS dropped (such as `$` in a selector).
- [LUM3017](../errors/LUM3017.md): a declaration value browsers would ignore, or no value.
- [LUM3020](../errors/LUM3020.md): an unknown property name, with a fix for close typos.
- [LUM3018](../errors/LUM3018.md), [LUM3019](../errors/LUM3019.md): a unitless `$` number, a unit separated from a reference.

See also: [Components](components.md), [JSX `style` and `class`](jsx.md).

<!-- source: concepts/async.md -->

# Async components

> Components can be async and await their data, on the server and in the browser, with Suspense for loading states and error boundaries for failures.

## Concept

Async components are **the** way to read data in Lumiose (there are no route loaders). The same
component works in every rendering mode.

**The await rewrite.** The compiler rewrites `await` only where the nearest enclosing function is
the component itself; awaits inside handlers and callbacks are ordinary awaits. Around each
component-level `await`, the runtime restores the owner, context and tracking, so `useContext()`,
`getAbortSignal()` and signal reads keep working after it.

**Re-runs.** Props and signals read in the body (before or after an `await`) are tracked. When one
changes, the component **re-runs**:

- the previous run's `getAbortSignal()` signal aborts (cancel your fetches with it);
- the old UI stays on screen until the new run resolves, then swaps atomically;
- signals created in the body start fresh on each run;
- `isPending()` is true while the re-run is in flight.

**Boundaries.**

- `<Suspense fallback={…}>` shows its fallback for **new** pending content: the first load, and
  branches mounted later. Re-runs of content already shown keep the stale UI instead (use
  `isPending()` to dim it).
- `<ErrorBoundary fallback={(error, reset) => …}>` catches rejections and render errors below it.
- With no boundary: on the server the component becomes part of the page shell (the response waits
  for it); on the client nothing renders until it resolves; errors go to the `error` page.

**In-flight state** (all are reactive and safe to read anywhere):

| Helper                | True while                                                                                             |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `isPending()`         | this async component's own re-run is in flight (inside the component or its UI).                       |
| `isSubmitting(name?)` | a form action submission is in flight. See [Data and actions](data-and-actions.md).                    |
| `isNavigating()`      | an SPA navigation is in flight. See [Routing](routing.md).                                             |
| `isBusy()`            | anything above is in flight, or any `<Suspense>` shows its fallback. Use it for a global progress bar. |

**Caching.** Component-level awaits of `fetchJSON` and `query` go through a keyed cache:

- A GET `await fetchJSON(url)` is keyed by its absolute URL, so it needs no key.
- `await query(key, fn)` caches anything else (a database call, an SDK) under a TanStack-style
  array key such as `["stats", "books"]`: JSON-serializable values, hashed stably. `fn` receives
  `{ signal, queryKey }` (TanStack's query function context); pass `signal` on to cancel the work
  once no component waits for it.
- Components awaiting the same entry share one request: per request on the server, per page in the
  browser (every island and the SPA tree, kept across client navigations).
- In the browser, a cached entry shows at once (no `<Suspense>` fallback for a new component) and
  refetches in the background (stale-while-revalidate, TanStack defaults: `staleTime` 0, `gcTime`
  5 minutes). If the data changed, the components that awaited it re-run.
- `invalidate("/api/books/1")` refetches that URL's entry and `invalidate(["stats"])` the entries
  whose key starts with `["stats"]`. Only the components that awaited them re-run, keeping their
  UI until the new data arrives. `invalidate()` with no target refreshes the whole page.
- Only awaits in async component bodies are cached. `fetchJSON` in event handlers, middleware,
  endpoints and actions is a plain request, and so are non-GET requests and
  `fetchJSON(url, { cache: "no-store" })`, the opt-out for data that must always be fresh: never
  deduped, kept or sent with the page payload.
- Errors are never cached: the next await tries again. Aborting one component's wait (a superseded
  run) never cancels a request another component still awaits.

**Islands.** Inside an [island](islands.md), each awaited value is recorded during SSR and
replayed during hydration, so the client does not fetch it again. Cached values (`fetchJSON`,
`query`) are sent once per page instead, however many islands await them, and fill the browser
cache. Those values must be plain data (`LUM4007`), and **everything awaited inside an island is
sent to the browser**.

> **Status:** async components, the `await` rewrite, re-runs, `<Suspense>`, `<ErrorBoundary>`,
> `isPending()`, `isBusy()`, server streaming and the keyed cache (`fetchJSON`, `query`,
> `invalidate(...targets)`) are available, and so is replaying awaited values when an island
> hydrates (see [Islands](islands.md)).

## API

| API                                                              | Shape                                                                                                      |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `async function Name(props) { const x = await …; return <… /> }` | An async component.                                                                                        |
| `<Suspense fallback={…}>`                                        | Fallback for new pending content below.                                                                    |
| `<ErrorBoundary fallback={(error, reset) => …}>`                 | Fallback after an error below; `reset()` renders the children again. `fallback` may also be plain content. |
| `isPending()`                                                    | Whether this component's re-run is in flight.                                                              |
| `isBusy()`                                                       | Whether anything in the app is in flight.                                                                  |
| `getAbortSignal()`                                               | `AbortSignal` of the current run; aborted when superseded or disposed.                                     |
| `fetchJSON<T>(url, init?)`                                       | Isomorphic JSON fetch that returns plain data; cached by URL when awaited in a component.                  |
| `query(key, fn)`                                                 | Awaited in a component, caches what `fn` resolves to under `key` (an array).                               |
| `invalidate(...targets)`                                         | Refetches the entries of URLs and key prefixes, re-running their components; no target: the whole page.    |

## Example

```tsx check
import { ErrorBoundary, Suspense, fetchJSON, getAbortSignal, isPending, signal } from "lumiose";

interface Book {
  id: string;
  title: string;
  summary: string;
}

export async function BookDetails({ id }: { id: string }) {
  const book = await fetchJSON<Book>(`/api/books/${id}`, { signal: getAbortSignal() });
  const expanded = signal(false);

  return (
    <article class={{ stale: isPending() }}>
      <h2>{book.title}</h2>
      <button onClick={() => expanded.update((open) => !open)}>Details</button>
      {expanded() && <p>{book.summary}</p>}
    </article>
  );
}

export function BookPage({ ids }: { ids: string[] }) {
  const current = signal(ids[0] ?? "");

  return (
    <main>
      <nav>
        {ids.map((id) => (
          <button onClick={() => current.set(id)}>{id}</button>
        ))}
      </nav>
      <ErrorBoundary
        fallback={(error, reset) => (
          <p>
            Could not load the book ({String(error)}). <button onClick={reset}>Retry</button>
          </p>
        )}
      >
        <Suspense fallback={<p>Loading…</p>}>
          <BookDetails id={current()} />
        </Suspense>
      </ErrorBoundary>
    </main>
  );
}
```

Clicking another id re-runs `BookDetails`: the old book stays (dimmed through `isPending()`) until
the new one arrives; `<Suspense>` only showed its fallback for the first load. Going back to a book
already seen shows it at once from the cache, then revalidates it.

Data that does not come from `fetchJSON` goes through `query`, and a mutation refreshes only what it
changed:

```tsx check
import { invalidate, query } from "lumiose";

declare const db: { stats(): Promise<{ total: number }>; addBook(title: string): Promise<void> };

export async function Stats() {
  const stats = await query(["stats", "books"], () => db.stats());
  return <p>{stats.total} books</p>;
}

export function AddBook() {
  return (
    <button
      onClick={async () => {
        await db.addBook("Dune");
        await invalidate(["stats"], "/api/books"); // re-runs Stats and the components of /api/books
      }}
    >
      Add
    </button>
  );
}
```

## Common mistakes

- **Reading the component's own signals in its body.** A signal created in the body and read in
  the body re-runs the component, which re-creates the signal. Read it in JSX or handlers instead
  (`LUM2007`).
- **Not passing `getAbortSignal()` to fetches.** Without it, a superseded run's request keeps going. Pass
  `{ signal: getAbortSignal() }`.
- **Passing a key as a string to `invalidate()`.** A string is a URL: `invalidate("stats")` matches
  no `query()` entry (development builds warn). Pass the key array: `invalidate(["stats"])`.
- **Mutating cached data.** Every component that awaited an entry gets the same object. Copy it
  before changing it, or keep editable state in a signal or `store`.
- **Expecting `fetchJSON` in an event handler to use the cache.** Only component-level awaits are
  cached; a handler's call is a plain request (call `invalidate(url)` after a mutation instead).
- **Awaiting a `Response` inside an island.** `await fetch(url)` gives a non-serializable value.
  Use `await fetchJSON(url)` (`LUM4007`).
- **Putting secrets in awaited values inside islands.** They are serialized into the HTML. Fetch
  only what the browser may see.
- **Wrapping a re-run in `<Suspense>` and expecting the fallback again.** Revealed content keeps
  its stale UI; show progress with `isPending()` or `isBusy()`.
- **`await using` in a component body.** Not supported in v1 (`LUM1007`).
- **Expecting `resource()` on the server.** It never runs there; use an async component.

## Related diagnostics

- [LUM1007](../errors/LUM1007.md): `await using` in a component.
- [LUM2007](../errors/LUM2007.md): own signal read in an async body.
- [LUM4006](../errors/LUM4006.md): hydration mismatch (including replay key mismatches).
- [LUM4007](../errors/LUM4007.md): non-serializable awaited value.

See also: [Islands](islands.md), [Rendering modes](rendering-modes.md), [reference: components](../reference/components.md).

<!-- source: concepts/islands.md -->

# Islands

> Pages ship no JavaScript by default: add a `client:*` directive to a component and only that island hydrates in the browser.

## Concept

An **island** is a component instance that runs in the browser. You declare it at the **usage
site**, so the same component can be static on one page and interactive on another:

```tsx
<TeamPanel client:visible ids={ids} />
```

On the server, the call compiles to an island record: the component's module and export name, its
props, its slots and the hydration strategy. The page HTML contains the server-rendered island
between comment markers (`<!--l:ID-->…<!--/l:ID-->`) plus a JSON record; a small loader (about 1
kB) reads the records, arms the triggers and imports the island's module when one fires. Clicks,
input, submits and key presses that happen before hydration are replayed. An island whose module
fails to load or whose hydration throws is logged with its module, and those events get their
default actions (a link still navigates, a form still submits); a module that failed to load is
loaded again on the next interaction ([details](../reference/dom.md#lumiosedomloader)). Islands work in `static`
and `server` pages; how they compare with Astro's is in
[Compared with Astro islands](rendering-modes.md#compared-with-astro-islands), and how a built page
gets per-reader parts through an island in
[Close to partial prerendering](rendering-modes.md#close-to-partial-prerendering).

**Directives** (components only):

| Directive                                   | Hydrates                                            |
| ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `client:load`                               | Immediately.                                        |
| `client:idle`                               | When the browser is idle (at the latest after 2 s). |
| `client:visible` / `client:visible="200px"` | When it enters the viewport (optional root margin). |
| `client:media="(max-width: 600px)"`         | When the media query matches.                       |
| `client:only`                               | Client-rendered only: no server HTML.               |

**Props must be serializable**: JSON values plus `undefined`, `NaN`/`Infinity`, `BigInt`, `Date`,
`URL`, `Map` and `Set`. Functions, symbols, class instances (a `Response` too), promises and cycles
are `LUM4002`.

**Children and JSX props are slots.** They are rendered on the server and stay server components:
they never ship their own JS. A slot the island rendered on the server is adopted in place when it
hydrates; one it did not render yet (behind a condition) is sent as `<template data-l-slot="name">`
and inserted when the island renders it.

**What hydration does.** The island's component runs again in the browser, with the props the
server serialized, and its compiled code claims the server's nodes instead of creating new ones:
the DOM, focus and text selections stay. Awaits replay the values recorded during SSR instead of
fetching again, while still tracking what they read, so a later change re-runs the component and
fetches. Everything outside islands stays server HTML that never hydrates. `client:only` renders on
the client without server HTML. An island inside a streamed `<Suspense>` waits for its content
before hydrating.

**Nested directives.** A `client:*` inside an island's own render is just a component: it is
already client-side.

**Context starts at the island.** An island hydrates as its own root, so context the page provided
outside it (a `<Ctx value>` provider in a layout or page) does not reach it, and the server renders it the same
way: `useContext()` inside an island returns the context's default, unless the island or a component
inside it provides the value. Contexts provided inside the island work on both sides. To hand page
data to an island, pass it as a prop; to share state between islands, use scoped state
(`defineState`, [Sharing state](state.md)): one instance per page, seeded on the server and sent
with the page. In dev, an island that reads a context the page provided warns
`LUM4010`. Slots are page content, so they keep seeing the page's context. `<Suspense>`,
`<ErrorBoundary>`, request APIs (`locals()`, `cookies()`, …) and `getAbortSignal()` work inside islands
during SSR as everywhere else.

**Server-only boundaries.** `*.server.ts` files and everything under `src/server/` may not be
imported from code that reaches the browser (`LUM4003`): keep database access, secrets and
`env()` there. `lumiose dev` and `lumiose build` fail with the chain of importers when the client graph
reaches one, and `lumiose check` reports the import. Server-only APIs (`request()`, `cookies()`,
`env()`, …) throw `LUM4003` in the browser build.

**Awaited data** inside an island is recorded during SSR and replayed during hydration, so the
browser does not fetch it again; it must be plain data (`LUM4007`), and it is visible in the page
source. Cached awaits (`fetchJSON`, `query`) are sent once per page however many islands await
them, and fill the browser cache, so later awaits and `invalidate(url)` start from them. So are the values of scoped state that islands import (`defineState`, `LUM4011`): the page
sends them once, before the islands that read them hydrate. The loader and `hydrate()` are described in [`lumiose/dom`](../reference/dom.md).

**The loader script.** `lumiose dev` and `lumiose build` add the loader to every page that renders an
island, once, as `<script type="module" async>`: in the `<head>` when the shell has islands,
otherwise with the first streamed chunk that does. In a build, pages without islands load no
JavaScript; the loader is the client entry, and each island is a chunk it imports when the island's
trigger fires. The loader's chunk also holds the Lumiose runtime the islands share (signals, DOM,
hydration), so a page loads one runtime file before its islands: about 8 to 10 kB min+brotli in
the sample apps (`pnpm --filter lumiose size:apps` reports them; `pnpm --filter lumiose size` checks
the 10 kB cap on what an islands page ships and the 15 kB cap on the whole client runtime). With your own server, pass its URL as
`renderToStream(root, { loaderUrl })`.

**Code before hydration: `src/instrumentation.client.ts`.** The place for what must run in the
browser before any island hydrates: an error-reporting or analytics SDK, a polyfill, global
listeners. The file is optional (`.ts`, `.js` or `.mjs`), and Lumiose loads it once per document
load on every page the app serves, as the first `<script type="module">` of the head (in a build,
with `<link rel="modulepreload">` for the chunks it imports):

- **Before hydration.** Its top-level code completes, top-level `await` included, before any
  island hydrates and before the SPA router starts (prerendered SPA pages and `ssr = false` shells
  included). Meanwhile the loader already captures clicks, input and submits on islands, and
  replays them once the islands hydrated. Client navigations of an SPA do not run it again.
- **Pages without islands or SPA routes** load it as their only script, without the Lumiose
  runtime.
- **Failures.** What it throws is logged, and the page hydrates anyway.
- **Keep it short.** `lumiose dev` warns when it takes longer than 16 ms (one frame) from the
  start of its module to the end of its top-level code; `import()` what is not needed at once.
- **Client code.** It is bundled like an island: only `PUBLIC_*` env reaches it, and importing
  server-only code is `LUM4003`. An edit reloads the page in `lumiose dev`. With
  `lumiose({ csp: "strict" })` its tags carry the nonce like the loader's.

**Errors and tracing: `onError` and `instrumentations`.** Two optional exports of the file
receive what happens in the browser, as `src/instrumentation.server.ts` does on the server:

```ts check file=instrumentation.client.ts
// src/instrumentation.client.ts
import type { ClientErrorInfo, ClientInstrumentation } from "lumiose";

export function onError(error: unknown, info: ClientErrorInfo) {
  console.info("report", error, info.phase, info.route, info.island);
}

export const instrumentations: ClientInstrumentation[] = [
  {
    navigate: async (call, info) => {
      const start = performance.now();
      const result = await call();
      console.info(`${info.to?.route}: ${result.status} in ${performance.now() - start} ms`);
    },
    hydrate: async (call, info) => {
      performance.mark(`hydrate ${info.island}`);
      await call();
    },
  },
];
```

- **`onError(error, info)`** receives errors of islands, `"hydrate"` (the island's module did not
  load or its hydration threw), `"render"` (an async component, or what an `<ErrorBoundary>`
  caught) and `"effect"` (an effect or binding after hydration), of the SPA router, `"navigate"`
