  (a page that throws or whose module does not load), and of `submit()`, `"submit"` (a rejection;
  not an abort). `info` is `{ phase, route, island }`: the SPA route (undefined on MPA pages) and
  the island's `module#export`. Errors keep reaching the console as before.
- **`instrumentations`** wrap `navigate` (`{ type, from, to }`, until the page is on screen),
  `submit` (`{ action, url }`), `fetch` (each `fetchJSON()` request, `{ url }`, or `query()`
  function, `{ key }`) and `hydrate` (each island, `{ island }`), each with the current `route`.
  The rules are the server's: call `call()` where the phase runs and await it to time it; it never
  throws and resolves to `{ status: "success" }` or `{ status: "error", error }`. A wrapper only
  observes, what it or `onError` throws is logged, and the first observer is the outermost.
- **Cost.** They are read before the first island hydrates, so its hydration is observed too.
  Apps without the file ship none of this code: `lumiose build` turns the runtime's calls on only
  for apps that have it (about 0.7 kB brotli with islands, the router, actions and `fetchJSON`).

`src/instrumentation.server.ts` is its server counterpart ([Server](server.md#instrumentation)).
Types: [`lumiose`](../reference/app.md#instrumentation-types).

**Build output.** `lumiose build` puts the Lumiose runtime in one chunk: the island loader's, the SPA
entry's when the app has no islands, or a shared `lumiose-[hash].js` when it has both. The router's
History API fallback is a separate chunk, loaded only by browsers without the Navigation API.

Which runtime goes where follows one rule: the runtime chunk holds what the loader (or the SPA
entry) imports, plus the runtime that two or more islands (or SPA pages) import; runtime that only
one island imports goes into that island's chunk. A page's JavaScript then depends on its own
islands, not on every island of the app: the keyed selector the compiler emits for one island's
list, or `submit()` used by one form island, loads only on the pages that render that island. The trade-off: runtime shared
by several islands stays in the runtime chunk, so a page with none of them still loads it, but no
page loads more files than it has islands (a chunk per group of islands would cost one more request
each). Imports through `lumiose` and `lumiose/dom` count only the modules that declare what they
import. `fetchJSON` follows the same rule. One exception stays in the runtime chunk: a few bytes
that guard `fetchJSON`'s cache, so the minifier can drop the cache in apps without async components
or resources, which it can only do within one chunk.

Dynamic imports go through a smaller preload helper than Vite's: it still adds the imported chunk's
stylesheets (and waits for them, skipping those the page already holds in its merged or inline
styles), module preloads and the CSP nonce of `<meta property="csp-nonce">`, but dispatches no `vite:preloadError` event (the router loads the
URL with a document navigation when a page's module does not load).

**Islands from other packages.** Components of a linked workspace package (`"@acme/ui": "workspace:*"`)
can be or render islands too. Island records name modules without build-machine paths:
root-relative inside the project (`/src/components/LikeButton.stsx#LikeButton`), package-relative
outside it (`@acme/ui/src/Nav.stsx#Nav`), or by the import's bare name
(`import { Nav } from "@acme/ui"` gives `@acme/ui#Nav`). Either way, the `modulepreload` hint of a
`client:load` island points at its chunk in a build and at Vite's URL of the module in dev. Builds
also look for island call sites in the linked packages that depend on `lumiose`, so each of their
islands gets its chunk even when only server code renders it. Folders inside such a package that
are projects of their own (with a `package.json`, `tsconfig.json` or `vite.config.*`, such as a
showcase app) are left out.

> **Status:** available: island calls and records (`LUM4001`, `LUM4002`), the loader with its
> triggers and event replay, and hydration (`LUM4006` on a mismatch), in `lumiose dev` and builds.

## API

| API                                                                                     | Use                                                                              |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `client:load`, `client:idle`, `client:visible`, `client:media`, `client:only`           | Make a component instance an island.                                             |
| `export function X`                                                                     | Islands must be exported, so the browser can import them (`LUM4001`).            |
| `*.server.ts`, `src/server/**`                                                          | Server-only modules.                                                             |
| `import.meta.env.PUBLIC_*`                                                              | Env values that may reach islands.                                               |
| `src/instrumentation.client.ts`                                                         | Runs once per page load, before islands hydrate and the SPA starts.              |
| `onError`, `instrumentations` exports of it; `ClientErrorInfo`, `ClientInstrumentation` | Report browser errors; observe hydration, navigations, submissions and requests. |

## Example

```stsx check file=components/LikeButton.stsx
// src/components/LikeButton.stsx: an island; exported so the browser can import it
import { signal } from "lumiose";

export function LikeButton({ initial, children }: { initial: number; children?: JSX.Element }) {
  const likes = signal(initial);

  return (
    <button class="like" onClick={() => likes.update((n) => n + 1)}>
      {children} {likes()}
    </button>
  );
}

<style>
  .like { border-radius: 999px; }
</style>
```

```stsx check file=routes/posts/[id]/page.stsx
// src/routes/posts/[id]/page.stsx: a server component; only LikeButton ships JS
import { params } from "lumiose";
import { LikeButton } from "../../../components/LikeButton.stsx";

export default function Post() {
  const { id } = params<"/posts/[id]">();

  return (
    <main>
      <h1>Post {id}</h1>
      <LikeButton client:visible initial={3}>
        <strong>Like</strong>
      </LikeButton>
    </main>
  );
}
```

## Common mistakes

- **A non-exported island.** `function Counter` used with `client:load` cannot be imported by the
  browser. Export it (`LUM4001`).
- **Passing functions or class instances as island props.** `onSave={() => …}` cannot be
  serialized. Pass data, and do the work inside the island, or post a form (`LUM4002`).
- **Importing server code into an island.** `import { db } from "../server/db.server.ts"` in an
  island's graph is `LUM4003`. Call an endpoint with `fetchJSON` instead.
- **Touching `window` or `document` at module scope** in a module that also runs on the server.
  Move it into `onMount` or an effect (`LUM4004`).
- **Reading page context inside an island.** An island hydrates as its own root, so it does not
  see values the page provided outside it with a `<Ctx value>` provider, and it renders the same way on the
  server: `useContext()` returns the context's default unless the island (or a component inside it)
  provides the value. Pass the value as a prop, or share scoped state (`defineState`,
  [Sharing state](state.md)); dev warns with `LUM4010` when the page did provide it.
- **Different output on server and client**, for example from `Math.random()` or `Date.now()` in
  render. Hydration reports `LUM4006` in dev and client-renders the range in production.
- **Expecting `submit()` to refresh the page.** On MPA pages a successful `submit()` does not
  reload: the island owns its state and updates itself from the result. Call `invalidate()` when
  the page needs fresh server HTML ([Data and actions](data-and-actions.md)).
- **Starting an SDK inside an island.** It runs only where that island renders, and after other
  islands may have hydrated. Start it in `src/instrumentation.client.ts`, which every page runs
  first.
- **Making a whole page an island to get interactivity.** Mark only the interactive parts, or use
  an `spa` route ([Choosing a mode](rendering-modes.md#choosing-a-mode)).

## Related diagnostics

- [LUM4001](../errors/LUM4001.md): island component is not exported.
- [LUM4002](../errors/LUM4002.md): non-serializable island prop.
- [LUM4003](../errors/LUM4003.md): server-only module in a client graph.
- [LUM4004](../errors/LUM4004.md): browser API at module scope.
- [LUM4006](../errors/LUM4006.md): hydration mismatch.
- [LUM4007](../errors/LUM4007.md): non-serializable awaited value.
- [LUM4010](../errors/LUM4010.md): island reads context provided by the page.
- [LUM4011](../errors/LUM4011.md): non-serializable scoped state value.

See also: [Rendering modes](rendering-modes.md), [Async components](async.md), [Sharing state](state.md) (state shared by islands).

<!-- source: concepts/routing.md -->

# Routing

> Routes are folders under `src/routes`, named like the Next.js App Router: pages, layouts, endpoints and error pages, with typed params.

## Concept

```
src/
  routes/
    layout.stsx                     root layout; a nested layout.stsx per folder
    page.stsx                       /
    about/page.stsx                 /about
    blog/page.stsx                  /blog
    blog/[slug]/page.stsx           /blog/:slug
    blog/[slug]/Comments.stsx       colocated module, not a route
    blog/_lib/posts.ts              private folder: nothing below it routes
    docs/[[...path]]/page.stsx      /docs and /docs/*  (optional rest)
    files/[...path]/page.stsx       /files/*  (rest: one or more segments)
    [[lang]]/contact/page.stsx      /contact and /:lang/contact  (optional param)
    (marketing)/pricing/page.stsx   /pricing  (a group folder adds no URL segment)
    api/posts/route.ts              endpoint: export GET / POST / … = (ctx) => Response
    admin/middleware.ts             runs for the pages, actions and endpoints below /admin
    sitemap.xml/route.ts            endpoint at /sitemap.xml
    not-found.stsx  error.stsx      error pages, nearest one wins
  document.stsx                     optional: owns <html>, <head> and <body>
  middleware.ts                     optional: export default (ctx, next) => Promise<Response>
```

- **A folder is a URL segment; special files give it behavior:** `page.stsx` or `page.tsx` (the
  page), `route.ts` (an endpoint), `middleware.ts` (folder middleware), and `layout`, `not-found`
  and `error` (`.stsx` or `.tsx`).
  There is no `index` and no flat page file: `about/page.stsx` is the page at `/about`, and
  `about.stsx` is not a route. A folder has a page or a `route.ts`, not both (`LUM5003`).
- **Colocation:** any other file in `src/routes` (components, helpers, styles, tests) is ignored
  by the router, so it can live next to the route that uses it. A folder whose name starts with
  `_` is private: nothing below it routes, not even a `page.stsx`.
- **Segments:** `[param]` matches one segment, `[[param]]` zero or one, `[...rest]` one or more
  and `[[...rest]]` zero or more (joined with `/`); `(group)` folders add no segment. A rest
  segment is the last one of the URL. An optional param that matched nothing is absent:
  `params.lang` is `undefined` at `/contact`.
- **Matching priority:** segment by segment, static beats `[param]`, which beats `[...rest]`. A
  route with optional segments competes with each URL shape it serves: `/[[lang]]/contact` serves
  `/contact` as a static route. Two files that serve the same URL are `LUM5003`, including a
  `[[...rest]]` folder next to a page for the URL without it.
- **Next.js files Lumiose does not have** are `LUM5002`, so they never silently do nothing:
  `loading`, `template`, `default` and `global-error` files, `@slot` folders (parallel routes)
  and `(.)` folders (intercepting routes).
- **Layouts** wrap every page below their folder and receive `{ params, children }`. `children`
  is the page (the outlet).
- **Folder middleware:** a `middleware.ts` runs for every page, form action and endpoint below its
  folder (group folders included), after `src/middleware.ts` and outermost folder first. It is the
  place for a section's auth, since a layout does not see the folder's actions and endpoints. See
  [Server](server.md#concept); `src/routes/middleware.ts` is `LUM5002` (use `src/middleware.ts`).
- **Pages** export a `default` component (it may be `async`), which receives `{ params }`. Other
  page exports: `mode`, `ssr`, `prerender`, `staticPaths`, `action`/`actions`, `headers` and
  `limits` (see
  [Rendering modes](rendering-modes.md), [Data and actions](data-and-actions.md) and
  [Security](security.md)). Endpoints may export `limits` too.
- **Error pages:** `not-found` renders unmatched URLs and `notFound()`; `error` renders thrown
  errors and `error(status)`. Both receive `{ status, error }`. Outside dev, unexpected errors are
  masked as 500. An error page renders inside the layouts of its folder, like a page there: the
  root `not-found` gets the root `layout` (header, navigation), so it only renders its own
  content. If a layout itself fails, the error page renders without layouts. To give errors a
  different frame, move the regular pages into a group with their own layout
  (`(app)/layout.stsx`) and keep the error page outside it.

**Locales.** With `lumiose({ i18n })`, the router also serves each page under the prefixes of the
locales it declares (`/es/about` from `about/page.stsx`), and `href()`, `<html lang>` and the
`hreflang` links follow. See [Internationalization](i18n.md).

**Typed routes.** `lumiose typegen` (run by `lumiose check` and the dev server) writes
`.lumiose/types/routes.d.ts`, which augments `RouteMap` (pages and endpoints) and `LayoutMap`
(the folders with a layout or a middleware file). Every route-bound type then takes the route pattern as a string literal, checked
against that table: an unknown or stale pattern is a type error, and editors complete it.

- `href("/blog/[slug]", { slug })` builds a URL and type-checks the pattern and params; the URL
  includes Vite's `base` and follows `trailingSlash` ([reference](../reference/app.md#href));
- `PageProps<"/blog/[slug]">` types a page's props, `LayoutProps<"/blog">` a layout's
  (`{ params, children }`, with the params of the layout's URL scope; route groups such as `(app)`
  add nothing to it), and `params<"/blog/[slug]">()` the params anywhere on the server;
- `RequestContext<P>`, `ActionContext<P>` and `Endpoint<P>` type `ctx.params` of middleware
  helpers, actions and endpoints (see [Data and actions](data-and-actions.md)), and
  `Middleware<"/admin">` types a folder's middleware: `ctx.params` with the folder's params and
  `ctx.route` with the patterns below it;
- optional params are optional properties (`RouteParams<"/[[lang]]/contact">` is
  `{ lang?: string }`), and `href()` leaves out an optional segment whose param is missing or
  empty: `href("/docs/[[...path]]")` is `/docs`.

**Navigation.** Routes are MPA by default: links load the next document. Two `lumiose()` options in
`vite.config.ts` make these navigations smooth ([reference](../reference/vite.md#lumiose)); both are
progressive, so browsers without support navigate normally:

- **Prefetch** (`prefetch`, default `"hover"`). Pages get `<script type="speculationrules">` that
  prefetches same-origin links: when the pointer rests on a link (`"hover"`), early, as the browser
  sees fit (`"viewport"`), or never (`"none"`). Links to endpoints are never prefetched, since a GET
  endpoint may act (`/logout`). `spa` pages get no rules: there `<Link prefetch>` decides per link.
- **Per link**, `<Link prefetch>` from `lumiose/router` overrides the default on MPA pages too. There
  it renders a plain `<a>` (no JavaScript, no router) with a `data-l-prefetch` marker, and the
  rules prefetch it at its own level: `"none"` opts the link out, `"viewport"` prefetches it early,
  `"hover"` on hover. `<Link>` without `prefetch`, like a plain `<a>`, follows the default. The
  server `<Link>` tells the page it rendered a marker as it renders; a hand-written
  `data-l-prefetch` attribute on a plain `<a>` does not change the page's rules.
- **View Transitions** (`viewTransitions: true`, off by default). Every page opts into
  cross-document View Transitions (`@view-transition { navigation: auto }`), except for readers who
  prefer reduced motion: the old page cross-fades into the new one. An element morphs into its
  counterpart on the next page when both have the same CSS `view-transition-name`, unique on each
  page: in a style block (`.site-header { view-transition-name: site-header; }`) or per item with
  ``style={{ "view-transition-name": `cover-${post.slug}` }}``. Style the animation with the
  `::view-transition-*` pseudo-elements in a global style block.

```ts
// vite.config.ts
export default defineConfig({ plugins: [lumiose({ viewTransitions: true })] });
```

```tsx
import { Link } from "lumiose/router";

// In any page or component: the next page prefetches early, the archive never.
<Link href="/page/2" prefetch="viewport">Older →</Link>
<Link href="/archive" prefetch="none">Archive</Link>
```

Routes with `mode = "spa"` use the client router `lumiose/router` ([reference](../reference/router.md)):

- The SPA starts at the outermost `spa` layout (or the page itself) and covers every `spa` page
  below it; links between them navigate on the client, other links load the document.
- `<Link href prefetch>` (plain `<a>` links work too), `navigate(href, { replace })`, reactive
  `params()`, `route()` (the matched pattern), `url()`, `searchParams()` (`searchParams.set()` changes the
  query) and `isNavigating()`.
- Layouts persist: a layout's `children` is the outlet, and layouts shared by the old and the new
  page keep their state. A page with other param values (`songs/[id]`) is a new page.
- A navigation holds the old page until the new page's async content is ready, then swaps. With
  `viewTransitions: true`, a navigation to another page swaps inside
  [`viewTransition()`](../reference/components.md#viewtransition) (a query change on the same page
  does not), and `<ViewTransition>` names the elements that morph.
- Scroll restoration, focus reset, an announcement of each new page for screen readers (its
  `<Title>`, else its first `<h1>`), `not-found` for unknown URLs and `notFound()`, `error` for
  errors. See [Behaviour](../reference/router.md#behaviour).
- Navigation hooks: `beforeNavigate(fn)` runs before each navigation and may `cancel()` it (to
  confirm leaving unsaved changes; the browser asks for one that unloads the document), and
  `afterNavigate(fn)` runs after each completed one and once on mount (page views, focus). They
  belong to the component that calls them during setup, and work in islands of MPA pages too
  (`"leave"` and `"enter"` only). See [Navigation hooks](../reference/router.md#navigation-hooks).

```tsx
import { signal } from "lumiose";
import { afterNavigate, beforeNavigate } from "lumiose/router";

export function Editor() {
  const dirty = signal(false);
  beforeNavigate((navigation) => {
    if (!dirty()) return;
    if (navigation.willUnload) navigation.cancel(); // the browser asks
    else if (!confirm("Discard your changes?")) navigation.cancel();
  });
  afterNavigate((navigation) => console.info("page view", navigation.to?.url.pathname));
  return <textarea onInput={() => dirty.set(true)} />;
}
```

> **Status:** file routes, the manifest, matching, typegen, `href()`, the request handler, MPA
> prefetch and View Transitions, and the SPA router (`lumiose/router`) are available, served by
> `lumiose dev`, `lumiose build` and `lumiose preview`.

## API

| API                                                                                                   | Use                                                                                    |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `export default function Page(props: PageProps<"/x/[id]">)`                                           | A page component.                                                                      |
| `export default function Layout(props: LayoutProps<"/x">)`                                            | A layout: `{ params, children }`.                                                      |
| `params<"/x/[id]">()`                                                                                 | The matched route's params, typed by pattern (server).                                 |
| `href(pattern, params?)`                                                                              | Build a URL from a typed route pattern.                                                |
| `Routes`, `RouteParams<P>`, `RouteMap`, `LayoutMap`                                                   | Route types.                                                                           |
| `ErrorPageProps`                                                                                      | Props of `not-found` and `error` pages.                                                |
| `notFound()`, `error(status, message?)`, `redirect(to, status?)`                                      | Stop rendering; see [Server](server.md).                                               |
| `lumiose/router`: `Link`, `navigate`, `isNavigating`, `searchParams`, reactive `url`/`params`/`route` | SPA routes and islands ([reference](../reference/router.md)).                          |
| `lumiose/router`: `beforeNavigate(fn)`, `afterNavigate(fn)`                                           | Run around navigations; cancel one ([hooks](../reference/router.md#navigation-hooks)). |

## Example

```stsx check file=routes/layout.stsx
// src/routes/layout.stsx
import { href, type LayoutProps } from "lumiose";

export default function Layout(props: LayoutProps<"/">) {
  return (
    <div class="app">
      <nav>
        <a href={href("/")}>Home</a>
        <a href={href("/blog/[slug]", { slug: "hello-world" })}>First post</a>
      </nav>
      {props.children}
    </div>
  );
}

<style global>
  body { margin: 0; font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; }
</style>
```

```stsx check file=routes/blog/[slug]/page.stsx
// src/routes/blog/[slug]/page.stsx
import { Title, notFound, type PageProps } from "lumiose";

const posts: Record<string, string> = { "hello-world": "Hello, world" };

export const mode = "server";

export default function Post({ params }: PageProps<"/blog/[slug]">) {
  // A function, so the JSX re-reads it when the params change (a plain const would be LUM2001).
  const title = () => posts[params.slug] ?? notFound();

  return (
    <article>
      <Title>{title()}</Title>
      <h1>{title()}</h1>
    </article>
  );
}
```

```tsx check file=routes/not-found.tsx
// src/routes/not-found.tsx: renders inside routes/layout.stsx above (its nav and styles), so only
// the page content goes here
import type { ErrorPageProps } from "lumiose";

export default function NotFound({ status, error }: ErrorPageProps) {
  return (
    <main>
      <h1>{status}</h1>
      <p>{error.message}</p>
    </main>
  );
}
```

```tsx check file=routes/page.tsx
// src/routes/page.tsx
export default function Home() {
  return <h1>Home</h1>;
}
```

## Common mistakes

- **A flat or `index` page file.** `src/routes/about.stsx` and `src/routes/blog/index.stsx` are
  colocated modules, not routes: name them `about/page.stsx` and `blog/page.stsx`. `lumiose routes`
  lists what the router sees.
- **A `[...rest]` folder for its parent's URL.** `docs/[...path]/page.stsx` does not match
  `/docs`: use `docs/[[...path]]/page.stsx`, or add `docs/page.stsx`.
- **Two files for one URL.** `cart/page.stsx` and `(shop)/cart/page.stsx` both match `/cart`, and
  so do `feed/page.stsx` and `feed/route.ts` (`LUM5003`).
- **Hard-coded URLs.** `"/blog/" + slug` breaks silently when a route moves; `href("/blog/[slug]",
  { slug })` fails type-checking instead.
- **Reading params from `window.location` in a server component.** Use `props.params` or
  `params()`.
- **Matching `url().pathname` to know which route is showing.** `route() === "/songs/[id]"`
  compares the matched pattern, type-checked against the app's routes.
- **Route loaders.** There are none: load data in the async page component itself (decision-18).
- **A custom dialog for leaving the document.** For a navigation that unloads the page
  (`navigation.willUnload`), `cancel()` makes the browser show its own prompt; a `confirm()` or a
  modal cannot run there. Ask with your own UI only for navigations inside the SPA.
- **`mode` that is not a string literal.** `export const mode = getMode()` cannot be read at build
  time (`LUM5002`).

## Related diagnostics

- [LUM5002](../errors/LUM5002.md): invalid route file.
- [LUM5003](../errors/LUM5003.md): duplicate route.
- [LUM5001](../errors/LUM5001.md): request API used during prerender.
- [LUM5008](../errors/LUM5008.md): folder middleware covering prerendered routes.

See also: [Rendering modes](rendering-modes.md), [Server](server.md), [reference: app layer](../reference/app.md), [`lumiose/router`](../reference/router.md).

<!-- source: concepts/i18n.md -->

# Internationalization

> Built-in locale routing: one set of route files served under each locale's prefix, with locale-aware links, `hreflang` and canonical URLs.

## Concept

```ts
// vite.config.ts
lumiose({
  i18n: {
    locales: ["en", "es", "fr"],
    defaultLocale: "en", // served unprefixed (/about); the others are prefixed (/es/about)
    missing: "404", // or "redirect" to the default locale's page; site-wide
    detect: false, // or { cookie: "locale", acceptLanguage: true }: only on entry
  },
  site: "https://example.com", // the origin of prerendered pages' absolute URLs
});
```

**URLs.** Locales are URL path segments (`en`, `pt-BR`). The router reads the prefix and matches
the rest against the routes, so `src/routes/about/page.stsx` serves `/about` (the default locale)
and `/es/about`, `/fr/about` for the locales it declares. The default locale has no prefix:
`/en/about` is not a URL. There is no `[locale]` folder (a route param named `locale` is
[LUM5007](../errors/LUM5007.md)).

**Declaring locales.** A page exists in the locales it declares; without a declaration, only in the
default locale, so a site can translate some pages and never serves an untranslated duplicate:

- `export const locales = ["en", "es"]`: these locales; `"all"`: every configured locale.
- `export async function locales({ params })`: content-driven pages decide per params (a blog post
  translated into some languages). It runs per request, and once per path while prerendering.
- A layout's `locales` applies to every page below it; a page's own export wins. Endpoints
  (`route.ts`) declare locales the same way.
- A locale the config does not list is a `LUM5002` error.

**Missing translations.** A page requested in a locale it does not declare is a 404 (the
`not-found` page, in that locale), or with `missing: "redirect"` a redirect to the default
locale's URL when the page exists there (302, or 307 for other methods than GET).

**The request's locale.** `locale()` from `lumiose` reads it on the server (the URL prefix, else
the default locale), `ctx.locale` in middleware, actions and endpoints, and `locale()` from
`lumiose/router` is reactive in SPA routes (and the page's locale in islands). `Locale` is the
union of the configured locales, from typegen. Without `lumiose({ i18n })` they are `undefined`,
and typed `string | undefined`. The document's `<html lang>` follows: the default
document writes it, a custom `src/document.stsx` gets the `lang` of its `<html>` set, and SPA
navigations update it.

**Links.** `href()` builds URLs in the current locale: `href("/about")` is `/es/about` on a Spanish
page. The `locale` key switches it: `href("/blog/[slug]", { slug, locale: "fr" })`. `href()` does
not check that the page declares the locale; `alternates()` lists the URLs that exist.

**Alternates and search engines.** `alternates()` returns the current page in every locale it
declares, `[{ locale, href }]`, for language switchers. `alternates(pattern, params?)` does the same
for another route, to link a page translated into fewer locales than the current one
(`alternates("/about")`); its params are typed like `href()`'s. A route whose locales come from a
`locales({ params })` function throws there: rendering cannot wait for it, so build those links
from the translations your content lists. A page that declares more than one locale also gets, in
its `<head>`:

- `<link rel="alternate" hreflang="…">` for each declared locale, and nothing for the others (no
  `x-default`), so search engines never see a URL that does not exist;
- `<link rel="canonical">` to the page's own URL in its locale (each locale is canonical for
  itself). A canonical the page or a layout renders with `<Head>` replaces it.

In `spa` routes the client router keeps them current: after each navigation it writes the new
page's links, or removes them for a page that declares a single locale, and a canonical that the
new page renders with `<Head>` still replaces Lumiose's. Hreflang links of the configured locales
belong to Lumiose there: do not write them with `<Head>`.

These URLs are absolute: the request's origin for pages rendered per request, and
`lumiose({ site })` for prerendered pages, which have no request; after an SPA navigation, the
page's origin (`location.origin`). Without `site`, prerendered pages
get root-relative URLs, which search engines ignore, and `lumiose build` warns. The origin is
joined with the `href()` path, which already has Vite's `base`: a site with a path
(`"https://example.com/docs"`) sets the base when the config has none, and must match it
otherwise.

**Prerendering.** A `static` page (or an `spa` page with `prerender`) renders once per locale it
declares, for each path of its `staticPaths()`: `about/index.html`, `es/about/index.html`, … A
`locales()` function is asked for each path's params.

**Detection** (`detect`, off by default) runs only on entry, never on every request:

- On a first visit (no `cookie`), the visitor's `Accept-Language` locale (with
  `acceptLanguage: true`): a page that declares it redirects there (`/about` → `/es/about`), and
  the cookie records the locale either way.
- On `/`, the cookie's locale: a visitor who chose Spanish lands on `/es`.
- Deep links never redirect once the cookie exists, prefixed URLs never do, and without a `cookie`
  only `/` detects (first visits cannot be told apart).
- These responses send `Vary: Cookie, Accept-Language` and `Cache-Control: private, no-store`.
- A prefetch never keeps a decision, since a language switcher may change the cookie before the
  navigation: the speculation rules leave out `/`, and a detecting request that carries
  `Sec-Purpose: prefetch` (another prefetcher, a prerender) gets a `503` the browser discards, so the
  navigation itself detects.

A language switcher must update the cookie (`cookies().set("locale", "es")` in an action, or
`document.cookie` in an island); the cookie is not `HttpOnly`, so client code can. Detection runs in
the request handler: a prerendered `/` served as a file never redirects, so render the entry page
per request (`export const mode = "server"`) to detect there.

**SPA routes.** The client router matches prefixed URLs too, for the locales a page declares in a
list; a page with a `locales()` function, or a locale it does not declare, loads as a document and
the server answers. That is a trade-off: the function runs on the server (it usually reads content
or a database), and only the server knows whether the URL exists, so it answers with the page, a
404 or a redirect, and its `hreflang` links. A navigation to another locale renders every level
again.

**Messages.** Lumiose does not translate or format messages: use a library such as Paraglide JS
(compile-time messages, only what a page uses) or i18next, keyed by `locale()`. The
[i18n guide](../guides/i18n.md) shows both end to end.

> **Status:** locale routing, declarations, `missing`, detection, `locale()`, `alternates()`,
> locale-aware `href()`, `<html lang>`, `hreflang` and canonical links, and per-locale
> prerendering are available. Locales per domain (`example.es`) come after 1.0.

## API

| API                                                                | Use                                                                |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `lumiose({ i18n: { locales, defaultLocale, missing?, detect? } })` | Configure locale routing ([reference](../reference/vite.md)).      |
| `lumiose({ site })`                                                | The site's URL, for the absolute URLs of prerendered pages.        |
| `export const locales = [...] \| "all"`                            | The locales a page, endpoint or layout (and everything below) has. |
| `export async function locales({ params })`                        | The locales of a content-driven page, per params.                  |
| `locale()`, `ctx.locale`                                           | The request's locale (server).                                     |
| `locale()` from `lumiose/router`                                   | The current locale, reactive in SPA routes.                        |
| `href(pattern, { ...params, locale })`                             | A URL in the current locale, or in `locale`.                       |
| `alternates()`                                                     | `[{ locale, href }]`: the current page in each declared locale.    |
| `alternates(pattern, params?)`                                     | The same for another route, from its `locales` list.               |
| `Locale`                                                           | The configured locales (typegen).                                  |

## Example

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import lumiose from "@lumiose/vite";

export default {
  plugins: [
    lumiose({
      i18n: {
        locales: ["en", "es"],
        defaultLocale: "en",
        detect: { cookie: "locale", acceptLanguage: true },
      },
      site: "https://example.com",
    }),
  ],
};
```

```stsx
// src/routes/layout.stsx: every page below exists in both locales, with a language switcher
import { alternates, locale, type LayoutProps } from "lumiose";

export const locales = "all";

const names = { en: "English", es: "Español" };

export default function Layout(props: LayoutProps<"/">) {
  return (
    <div>
      <nav>
        {alternates().map((alternate) => (
          <a href={alternate.href} aria-current={alternate.locale === locale() ? "true" : undefined}>
            {names[alternate.locale]}
          </a>
        ))}
      </nav>
      {props.children}
    </div>
  );
}
```

```stsx
// src/routes/blog/[slug]/page.stsx: a post exists in the languages it was translated into
import { href, locale, notFound, type PageProps } from "lumiose";
import { getPost } from "../../../lib/posts.ts";

export async function locales({ params }: { params: { slug: string } }) {
  return (await getPost(params.slug))?.translations ?? [];
}

export default async function Post(props: PageProps<"/blog/[slug]">) {
  const post = (await getPost(props.params.slug, locale())) ?? notFound();
  return (
    <article>
      <h1>{post.title}</h1>
      <a href={href("/blog")}>{post.back}</a>
    </article>
  );
}
```

## Common mistakes

- **A `[locale]` folder.** The router handles the prefix: `src/routes/about/page.stsx` serves
  every locale it declares, and a param named `locale` is `LUM5007`.
- **Expecting every page in every locale.** Without `export const locales` (on the page or a
  layout), a page exists only in the default locale; `/es/about` is then a 404.
- **`href()` to a page that is not translated.** On a French page `href("/about")` is
  `/fr/about`; pick a locale from `alternates("/about")`.
- **Hard-coded prefixes.** `"/es" + path` breaks for the default locale and below a `base`; use
  `href(pattern, { locale })`.
- **A switcher that does not update the detection cookie.** The visitor's next visit to `/` sends
  them back to the locale in the cookie.
- **Detection on a prerendered `/`.** A static file never redirects; render the entry page per
  request.
- **No `site` for a prerendered site.** `hreflang` and canonical URLs stay root-relative, which
  search engines ignore; `lumiose build` warns.

## Related diagnostics

- [LUM5007](../errors/LUM5007.md): route param named `locale`.
- [LUM5002](../errors/LUM5002.md): an invalid `locales` export, or a locale the config does not
  list.

See also: [i18n with Paraglide JS and i18next](../guides/i18n.md), [Routing](routing.md),
[`lumiose`: app layer](../reference/app.md), [`lumiose/router`](../reference/router.md),
[`@lumiose/vite`](../reference/vite.md).

<!-- source: concepts/data-and-actions.md -->

# Data and actions

> Read data in async components, serve APIs from endpoints and change data with form actions: one way to do each, with no loaders or RPC.

## Concept

**Reading: async components.** Await data in the component that needs it. Server-only data
access (databases, secrets) lives in `*.server.ts` modules or `src/server/`. See
[Async components](async.md).

**HTTP APIs: endpoints.** A `route.ts` file under `src/routes` exports handlers named after HTTP
methods: `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE` (and `HEAD`, `OPTIONS`), each
`(ctx) => Response`. Islands, SPA code and other clients call them with `fetch` or `fetchJSON`.

**`fetchJSON<T>(url, init?)`** fetches JSON and returns plain data, so awaited results stay
serializable inside islands. Non-2xx responses throw a `FetchError` (an `HttpError` with `status`,
`url` and the parsed body as `data`); if a server component lets it escape, the page renders
`error` (or `not-found`) page with that status. **During SSR, same-origin URLs are served in-process**, with
the page request's cookies, without a network round-trip. **Awaited in an async component, a GET
is cached by URL**: components awaiting the same URL share one request, and in the browser cached
data shows at once and revalidates in the background; `{ cache: "no-store" }` opts a request out.
`query(key, fn)` caches other data under an array key, and passes `fn` TanStack's
`{ signal, queryKey }`. See [Async components](async.md) and [reference: query](../reference/app.md#query).

**Mutations: form actions.** A page exports `action(ctx)` or named `actions = { name(ctx) }`. A
`<form method="post">` posts to the page (or to `?/name` for a named action) and works without
JavaScript. A named action's URL may keep the page's other query parameters: the action is the
parameter that starts with `/`, wherever it is, so `?status=open&/close` runs `close`, and
`ctx.url` still has `status=open` (useful to redirect back to a filtered list). An action receives
`ctx.formData()` and returns:

| Return                         | Result                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `redirect(to)` or a `Response` | Sent as is (303 after a POST).                                                                  |
| plain data                     | The page re-renders (200) and `actionData()` returns the data.                                  |
| `fail(status, data)`           | The page re-renders with `status`; `actionData()` returns `data`. Use it for validation errors. |

An Origin check protects page POSTs and form-encoded endpoint requests by default (403 for
cross-site requests).

**Enhancing forms.** Inside an island, `onSubmit={submit}` posts the form without a page load.
`submit()` resolves to `{ type: "success", status, data }`, `{ type: "failure", status, data }` or
follows a redirect, and sets `actionData()`. It rejects only for unexpected errors, with a
`FetchError`. `isSubmitting(name?)` is true while a submission is in flight.

**Per-instance submissions.** `isSubmitting(name)` and `actionData()` are page-wide: rows of a
list that post the same action would share one pending flag and overwrite each other's result.
`submission()` gives a component its own handle, created during setup:
`const toggle = submission<typeof actions.toggle>()`, then `onSubmit={toggle.submit}`.
`toggle.isSubmitting()`, `toggle.result()` (the last `{ type: "success" | "failure", status, data }`,
typed from the action) and `toggle.error()` (the last unexpected `FetchError`) are this instance's
only. `toggle.submit()` takes what `submit()` takes and returns the same promise; a new submission
on the handle aborts the one in flight, `toggle.abort()` cancels it (the handle is idle at once,
and an abort is no error), `toggle.reset()` clears the result and the error, and disposing the
component aborts too. A handle never sets `actionData()`, while `isSubmitting(name)` still counts
it; SPA refreshing, `invalidate` targets and `optimistic()` work as with `submit()`. Errors land
in `error()`, so `onSubmit={toggle.submit}` reports no unhandled rejection; redirects navigate
and leave `result()` as it was.

**Refreshing.** `invalidate()` re-runs the current page's async components (SPA; the stale UI stays
until the new data arrives), or reloads the page (MPA). On client-routed (SPA) pages a successful
`submit()` runs it for you, so the page shows the mutation without extra code; pass
`submit(form, { invalidate: false })` to keep the page as it is. On MPA pages a successful
`submit()` never reloads: an island owns only its own state, so it updates itself from the result
(`result.data`, `actionData()`). Call `invalidate()` yourself when the page needs fresh
server-rendered content; on MPA pages that reloads and resets `actionData()`.

**Refreshing only what changed.** `invalidate(...targets)` refetches cache entries and re-runs only
the async components that awaited them, on SPA and MPA pages alike (islands included, no reload):
a string is a URL (the `fetchJSON` entry of that URL), an array a `query()` key prefix.
`submit(form, { invalidate: ["/api/books/1", ["stats"]] })` does the same after a successful
submission, instead of refreshing the whole page. Components rendered only on the server (outside
islands) are not re-run by a target: use `invalidate()` for those.

**Optimistic updates.** `optimistic(source)` follows `source` (a getter such as `() => props.likes`,
or a signal) and shows an overlay while a promise is pending: `likes.update((n) => n + 1,
submit(event))` or `likes.set(value, promise)`. When the promise settles the overlay drops:
on success the source already holds the new value, on failure (a `fail()` result or a rejection)
the value rolls back. On SPA pages `submit()` resolves after its `invalidate()`, so the refreshed
data replaces the overlay in the same task, with no flicker back. On MPA pages read the new value
from the result (`actionData()?.likes ?? props.likes` as the source), or pass
`submit(event).then(() => invalidate())`: the MPA `invalidate()` reloads and never settles, so the
overlay holds until the page unloads. Overlays apply in call order and drop independently, and an
`update` re-applies over the latest source. `optimistic` does not re-throw a rejection: await
`submit()` yourself to handle errors.

**Typed results.** Type an action's parameter with its page pattern,
`(ctx: ActionContext<"/books/new">)`, and let TypeScript infer what it returns:
`actionData<typeof actions>()` (or `typeof action`) is the union of the data the actions return
and the data they pass to `fail()`, or `undefined` before a submission. `submit<typeof actions.create>(form)`
resolves with `{ type: "success", data }` or `{ type: "failure", data }` typed from that action,
so the two are told apart by `type`; `actionData()` data is told apart by its shape.
`ActionData<typeof actions>` names that type for a child component's props. An island that posts to another page's action imports the
type only: `import type { actions } from "../routes/reading-list/page.stsx"`.

## API

| API                                                                  | Shape                                                                     |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `export const GET: Endpoint<"/api/x"> = (ctx) => Response`           | An endpoint method; `ctx.params` typed by the pattern.                    |
| `export const action = async (ctx: ActionContext<"/x">) => …`        | The default form action of a page.                                        |
| `export const actions = { name: (ctx: ActionContext<"/x">) => … }`   | Named actions, posted to `?/name`.                                        |
| `ctx.formData()`                                                     | The request body as `FormData` (400 if it is not a form).                 |
| `fail(status, data?)`                                                | A failed action result.                                                   |
| `actionData<typeof actions>()`                                       | The last action's data or `fail` data, typed by the actions. Reactive.    |
| `submit(target, { action?, method?, signal?, invalidate? })`         | Post a form, submit event, `FormData`, `URLSearchParams` or a record.     |
| `submit(target, { invalidate: [url, key] })`                         | The same, refetching only those cache entries after a success.            |
| `submit<typeof actions.name>(…)`                                     | The same, resolving with that action's typed success and failure data.    |
| `isSubmitting(name?)`                                                | Whether a submission (to `?/name`) is in flight.                          |
| `submission<typeof actions.name>()`                                  | This component's `{ submit, isSubmitting, result, error, abort, reset }`. |
| `invalidate()`                                                       | Refresh the current page's server data.                                   |
| `invalidate(...targets)`                                             | Refetch the entries of URLs and `query()` key prefixes.                   |
| `query(key, fn)`                                                     | Awaited in a component, cache what `fn` resolves to under `key`.          |
| `optimistic(source)`, `.set(value, promise)`, `.update(fn, promise)` | A value with overlays held while their promises are pending.              |
| `fetchJSON<T>(url, init?)`, `isFetchError(e)`                        | JSON fetch with typed errors; cached by URL in components.                |

## Example

```ts check file=routes/api/books/route.ts
// src/routes/api/books/route.ts: GET /api/books?q=…
import type { Endpoint } from "lumiose";

const books = [{ id: "1", title: "Dune" }];

export const GET: Endpoint<"/api/books"> = ({ url }) => {
  const q = url.searchParams.get("q")?.toLowerCase() ?? "";
  return Response.json(books.filter((book) => book.title.toLowerCase().includes(q)));
};
```

```stsx check file=routes/books/new/page.stsx
// src/routes/books/new/page.stsx: a form that works without JS, enhanced when it hydrates
import { actionData, fail, redirect, submit, isSubmitting, type ActionContext } from "lumiose";

interface Errors {
  title?: string;
}

export const mode = "server";

export const actions = {
  async create(ctx: ActionContext<"/books/new">) {
    const form = await ctx.formData();
    const title = String(form.get("title") ?? "").trim();
    if (title === "") return fail(400, { title: "A title is required." } satisfies Errors);
    // await db.books.insert({ title });
    redirect("/books");
  },
};

export function NewBookForm() {
  return (
    <form method="post" action="?/create" onSubmit={submit}>
      <input name="title" />
      <p class="error">{actionData<typeof actions>()?.title}</p>
      <button disabled={isSubmitting("create")}>Add book</button>
    </form>
  );
}

export default function NewBook() {
  return (
    <main>
      <h1>New book</h1>
      <NewBookForm client:load />
    </main>
  );
}
```

```tsx check
import { fetchJSON, isFetchError } from "lumiose";

export async function BookSearch({ q }: { q: string }) {
  try {
    const books = await fetchJSON<{ id: string; title: string }[]>(
      `/api/books?q=${encodeURIComponent(q)}`,
    );
    return (
      <ul>
        {books.map((book) => (
          <li key={book.id}>{book.title}</li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    );
  } catch (error) {
    if (isFetchError(error) && error.status === 404) return <p>No books.</p>;
    throw error;
  }
}
```

A like button that counts at once and rolls back if the post fails. The page is MPA, so the island
reads the new count from the action's result; on an SPA page `() => props.likes` is enough, as
`submit()` refreshes the props before it resolves:

```stsx check file=routes/likes/[id]/page.stsx
// src/routes/likes/[id]/page.stsx
import { actionData, optimistic, submit, type ActionContext } from "lumiose";

export const mode = "server";

let count = 3; // a database in a real app

export const actions = {
  like(_ctx: ActionContext<"/likes/[id]">) {
    count += 1;
    return { likes: count };
  },
};

export function LikeButton(props: { likes: number }) {
  const likes = optimistic(() => actionData<typeof actions>()?.likes ?? props.likes);
  return (
    <form
      method="post"
      action="?/like"
      onSubmit={(event) => likes.update((n) => n + 1, submit(event))}
    >
      <button>Like ({likes()})</button>
    </form>
  );
}

export default function Post() {
  return <LikeButton client:load likes={count} />;
}
```

Rows that post the same action, each with its own pending state and result:

```stsx check file=routes/checklist/page.stsx
// src/routes/checklist/page.stsx
import { submission, type ActionContext } from "lumiose";

export const mode = "server";

const done = new Set<string>(); // a database in a real app

export const actions = {
  async toggle(ctx: ActionContext<"/checklist">) {
    const id = String((await ctx.formData()).get("id"));
    if (done.has(id)) done.delete(id);
    else done.add(id);
    return { id, done: done.has(id) };
  },
};

export function Row(props: { id: string; label: string; done: boolean }) {
  const toggle = submission<typeof actions.toggle>();
  const isDone = () => {
    const result = toggle.result();
    return result?.type === "success" ? result.data.done : props.done;
  };
  return (
    <form method="post" action="?/toggle" onSubmit={toggle.submit}>
      <input type="hidden" name="id" value={props.id} />
      <button disabled={toggle.isSubmitting()}>
        {isDone() ? "✓" : "○"} {props.label}
      </button>
      {toggle.error() ? <span class="error">Not saved</span> : null}
    </form>
  );
}

export default function Checklist() {
  return (
    <ul>
      {["milk", "eggs", "bread"].map((item) => (
        <li>
          <Row client:load id={item} label={item} done={done.has(item)} />
        </li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  );
}
```

Keeping the page's filters through a named action:

```stsx check file=routes/issues/page.stsx
// src/routes/issues/page.stsx: the list is filtered by ?status=; "Close" keeps the filter
import { redirect, url, type ActionContext } from "lumiose";

export const mode = "server";

export const actions = {
  async close(ctx: ActionContext) {
    // await db.issues.close((await ctx.formData()).getAll("ids"));
    const back = new URL(ctx.url);
    back.searchParams.delete("/close"); // the action key; the filters stay
    redirect(back.pathname + back.search);
  },
};

export default function Issues() {
  const search = url().search; // "?status=open", or ""
  return (
    <form method="post" action={`${search === "" ? "?" : `${search}&`}/close`}>
      {/* rows with <input type="checkbox" name="ids" value={id} /> */}
      <button>Close selected</button>
    </form>
  );
}
```

## Common mistakes

- **Route loaders.** Lumiose has none. Await data in the page component; it is the same code on every
  route mode.
- **Calling server code from an island.** Import nothing from `*.server.ts` in island code
  (`LUM4003`); expose an endpoint and call it with `fetchJSON`.
- **`fetch()` instead of `fetchJSON()` inside islands.** A `Response` is not serializable
  (`LUM4007`).
- **One `isSubmitting(name)` for several forms.** Rows that post the same action share it, and
  `actionData()` holds whichever answered last. Give each row a `submission()`.
- **Expecting `submit()` to reject on validation errors.** `fail()` resolves with
  `{ type: "failure" }`; only unexpected errors reject.
- **Calling `invalidate()` after a successful `submit()` on an SPA page.** `submit()` already did;
  a second call refreshes twice.
- **Reaching for a client cache library first.** `fetchJSON` and `query` already dedupe, cache and
  revalidate component awaits on the server and in the browser. Use
  [`@lumiose/query`](../reference/query.md) for client data that needs polling, refetching on focus,
  retries or per-query stale times.
- **Expecting an MPA page to refresh after `submit()`.** On MPA pages `submit()` never reloads.
  Update the island from the result (a toggle sets its own state, a list removes its own row), or
  call `invalidate()` explicitly if the page must show fresh server HTML.
- **Leaving an optimistic overlay up after the request.** Pass the promise to `set`/`update`
  rather than resetting by hand, and on MPA pages give the island a source that changes
  (`actionData()`, or an explicit `invalidate()`), or the value returns to the old one on success.
- **Forms without `method="post"`.** Actions only run for POST; `submit()` refuses a form that does
  not say `method="post"`, as the no-JS form would not post either.
- **Throwing for validation errors.** A thrown error renders the `error` page. Return
  `fail(400, data)`.
- **Casting action data.** `actionData<{ errors: … }>()` is a type error: pass `typeof actions`.
  Annotating the export with `Action` (`export const action: Action = …`) hides what it returns,
  so annotate the parameter instead, or check it with `satisfies Action<"/x">`. Add
  `satisfies YourFailure` to `fail()` data whose string literals should stay literal.
- **Disabling the Origin check to make a cross-site form work.** Allow the specific origin instead
  (`lumiose({ csrf: { allowedOrigins } })` in `vite.config.ts`).

## Related diagnostics

- [LUM4003](../errors/LUM4003.md): server-only module in a client graph.
- [LUM4007](../errors/LUM4007.md): non-serializable awaited value.
- [LUM5004](../errors/LUM5004.md): head or status change inside a streamed boundary.

See also: [Server](server.md), [Routing](routing.md), [reference: app layer](../reference/app.md).

<!-- source: concepts/server.md -->

# Server

> Middleware, endpoints, form actions and server renders all get the request context: URL, params, cookies, locals and the response.

## Concept

**Request context.** Middleware, endpoints and actions receive
`ctx = { request, url, params, route, locals, cookies, env, platform }`, where `route` is the
matched pattern (`"/users/[id]"`; `undefined` in `src/middleware.ts` for a URL no route matches).
During a server render, the same values are
available through functions scoped to the current request (they work after `await` too):
`request()`, `url()`, `params()`, `route()` (the matched pattern), `locals()`, `cookies()`,
`response()` and `env(name)`.

**Platform.** `ctx.platform` is what the host adds to a request: `env` (the platform's bindings,
such as Cloudflare's KV or D1; `{}` elsewhere), `waitUntil(promise)` (work that continues after the
response) and `clientAddress` (the client's IP as the host sees it). Each has a fallback, so the
same code runs on every host ([server build](../reference/server-entry.md#platform)). Type the
bindings by augmenting `PlatformEnv`. A server component that needs them gets them from middleware,
through `locals`.

**Middleware.** `src/middleware.ts` default-exports `(ctx, next) => Promise<Response>` (or an array,
run in order) and runs for every request. Use it for sessions, auth and headers. Put request data on
`ctx.locals`, and type it by augmenting `Locals`:

```ts
declare module "lumiose" {
  interface Locals {
    user: { id: string; name: string } | null;
  }
}
```

**Folder middleware.** A `middleware.ts` (or `.js`) in a route folder has the same default export and
runs for every page, form action and `route.ts` endpoint in that folder and below it. That makes it
the place for a section's auth: a layout guard (`locals()` plus `redirect()`) covers the folder's
pages, but not their actions or endpoints. Group folders count: `(account)/middleware.ts` covers
every route in the group without a URL segment.

- **Order.** The trailing-slash redirect and the cross-site check answer first. Then
  `src/middleware.ts`, and inside its `next()` the route's locale checks (`/es/admin` runs the
  `/admin` middleware), the folder middleware from the outermost folder to the innermost, and the
  route. Responses unwind in reverse. URLs that match no route run `src/middleware.ts` only.
- **Errors.** What folder middleware throws (`redirect()`, `error()`, any error) renders the
  route's error page outside the chain, as for `src/middleware.ts`.
- **Types.** `Middleware<"/admin">` takes the folder's URL scope (the pattern `LayoutProps` takes):
  `ctx.params` holds the folder's params and `ctx.route` the patterns below it.
- **SPA routes.** Client navigations between `spa` pages do not reach the server. The middleware
  runs for the document request and for the actions and endpoints below the folder, which is what
  protects an SPA's data.
- **Prerendered routes.** Like `src/middleware.ts`, folder middleware runs whenever the app handles
  a route: per request for server routes, for every route in `lumiose dev`, and at build time for
  prerendered pages, whose files production serves without the app. It cannot guard those, so
  `lumiose check` and the build warn ([`LUM5008`](../errors/LUM5008.md)).
- `src/routes/middleware.ts` is an error ([`LUM5002`](../errors/LUM5002.md)): the app's middleware
  is `src/middleware.ts`. `lumiose routes` prints each route's middleware chain.

**Control flow.** `redirect(to, status?)`, `notFound()` and `error(status, message?)` throw; the
framework turns them into a redirect or the nearest `not-found`/`error` page. Without a status,
`redirect()` uses 302 for GET/HEAD and 303 for other methods.

**Cookies.** `cookies.get/getAll/set/delete`. Defaults: `path=/`, `httpOnly`, `sameSite=lax`, and
`secure` on HTTPS and in production. `signedCookie(name)` signs values with HMAC-SHA256 (secret:
`LUMIOSE_SECRET`, or rotate with an array of secrets); signing protects integrity, not
confidentiality. Secrets must be at least 32 bytes: a shorter one throws in production and warns
in development, unless you pass `{ allowWeakSecret: true }`. Generate one with
`openssl rand -base64 32`.

**Status and headers.** `response().setStatus()` and `setHeader()` change the page response, and
a page may export `headers(ctx)`. They are writable **until the shell is sent** (see
[Rendering modes](rendering-modes.md)); a change inside a streamed `<Suspense>` boundary is
`LUM5004`. So is `response().setStreaming(false)`, which makes the page wait for every
`<Suspense>` boundary and send one fully resolved document instead of streaming them
([for crawlers](#crawlers-get-one-resolved-document)).

**Env.** `env("NAME")` reads server env variables (the adapter's env, else `process.env`) in
server-only code. Only `import.meta.env.PUBLIC_*` reaches client code (`@lumiose/vite` sets Vite's
`envPrefix` to `"PUBLIC_"` unless the config sets its own); `publicEnv()` returns that subset.

**Server-only code** lives in `*.server.ts` modules and under `src/server/`. Importing it from code
that reaches the browser is `LUM4003`, also through a web worker, `new URL("…", import.meta.url)`
or a `?raw`/`?url` import. `lumiose dev` does not serve these files over HTTP either: they are added
to Vite's `server.fs.deny` unless the config sets its own list (the server still loads them).

### Crawlers get one resolved document

Crawlers that do not run JavaScript index what the HTML holds: with streaming, the fallbacks, and
the content only inside `<template>` elements at the end. Lumiose ships no list of crawlers; test
the user agent in middleware, for example with the [`isbot`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/isbot)
package, and turn streaming off for them:

```ts
// src/middleware.ts
import { isbot } from "isbot";
import { response, type Middleware } from "lumiose";

const middleware: Middleware = (ctx, next) => {
  if (isbot(ctx.request.headers.get("user-agent"))) response().setStreaming(false);
  return next();
};

export default middleware;
```

Everyone else still gets the shell first. The response waits up to `lumiose({ streamTimeout })`
(30 seconds by default), then the boundaries still pending fail ([`LUM5009`](../errors/LUM5009.md)).
A shared cache that stores such pages should vary on the user agent, or store neither version.

### Instrumentation

`src/instrumentation.server.ts` (also `.js` or `.mjs`; server-only by its `.server.` segment) is
where error reporting and tracing start. `lumiose dev`, `lumiose preview`, the server build
(`dist/server/entry.js` on any host) and the deploy adapters load it; prerendering at build time
does not, since errors there fail the build. Its three exports are optional:

- **`register()`** runs once per server instance (per isolate on workers), before the first
  request, which waits for it: start an SDK here. `lumiose dev` runs it again after an edit of the
  file. What it throws is logged, and the server goes on.
- **`onRequestError(error, info)`** receives the unexpected errors of a request on every host,
  `lumiose dev` included: those that render the `error` page or answer 500, errors of streamed
  `<Suspense>` boundaries (also those `streamTimeout` ended), rejected `ctx.platform.waitUntil()`
  work, and errors an `<ErrorBoundary>` caught, with the `digest` its fallback shows outside dev. `redirect()`,
  `notFound()` and `error(status)` are not errors. `info` is `{ request, route, params, phase,
  digest }`, with `phase` one of `"middleware"` (also the route's locale checks), `"action"`,
  `"endpoint"`, `"render"`, `"stream"` or `"waitUntil"`. The handler's `onError` (the host's log,
  `console.error` by default) still gets each error first, except those an `<ErrorBoundary>`
  caught in dev.
- **`instrumentations`**, an array of observers with optional wrappers per phase: `request` (a
  request until its response is ready to send, `call()`'s result adds `response.status`),
  `middleware` (each middleware file, `info.file`), `action` (`info.name`: the key in `actions`,
  or `"default"`), `endpoint` (`info.method`), `render` (a page or error page until its shell is
  ready) and `stream` (each streamed boundary). A wrapper gets `call` and `info`
  (`{ request, route, params }` plus those): call `call()` where the phase runs and await it to
  time it. It never throws and resolves to `{ status: "success" }` or `{ status: "error", error }`.
  A wrapper only observes: the phase runs once, also when the wrapper never calls `call()`, its
  result is the phase's own, and what a wrapper throws is logged. The first observer is the
  outermost. Static files are served before the app and are not observed; a `fetchJSON()` the
  render handles in-process gets its phases observed, not a `request` of its own.

Without the file nothing loads; with it, a phase without wrappers costs one check. Its browser
counterpart, `src/instrumentation.client.ts`, runs on every page before hydration
([Islands](islands.md#concept)).

> **Status:** the request handler, middleware, endpoints, cookies, env, error pages and
> instrumentation are available, served by `lumiose dev` and by the build output
> (`lumiose preview`, [`@lumiose/adapter-node`](../reference/adapter-node.md), the deploy adapters).

## API

| API                                                                               | Use                                                                                  |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `RequestContext<P>` (`ctx`)                                                       | `{ request, url, params, route, locals, cookies, env, platform }`.                   |
| `Middleware<P?>`                                                                  | `(ctx, next) => Response \| Promise<Response>`; `P`: a folder's scope.               |
| `request()`, `url()`, `params<P>()`, `route()`, `locals()`, `cookies()`           | Request APIs during a server render.                                                 |
| `response()`                                                                      | `{ status, setStatus, getHeader, setHeader, setStreaming }` until the shell is sent. |
| `redirect(to, status?)`, `notFound(message?)`, `error(status, message?)`          | Throw to stop rendering.                                                             |
| `isRedirect(e)`, `isHttpError(e)`                                                 | Recognize those when you catch errors.                                               |
| `signedCookie(name, options?)`                                                    | `{ get(cookies), set(cookies, value), delete(cookies) }`.                            |
| `env(name)`, `publicEnv(source?)`                                                 | Server env; the `PUBLIC_*` subset.                                                   |
| `Locals`                                                                          | Interface to augment with your request data.                                         |
| `Platform`, `PlatformEnv`                                                         | `ctx.platform`; the interface to augment with your bindings.                         |
| `src/instrumentation.server.ts`: `register`, `onRequestError`, `instrumentations` | Observes the server ([Instrumentation](#instrumentation)).                           |
| `RequestErrorInfo`, `ServerInstrumentation`                                       | `onRequestError`'s `info`; one observer of `instrumentations`.                       |

## Example

```ts check file=middleware.ts
// src/middleware.ts
import { signedCookie, type Middleware } from "lumiose";

const session = signedCookie("session");

declare module "lumiose" {
  interface Locals {
    userId: string | null;
  }
}

const middleware: Middleware = async (ctx, next) => {
  ctx.locals.userId = (await session.get(ctx.cookies)) ?? null;
  const res = await next();
  res.headers.set("x-frame-options", "DENY");
  return res;
};

export default middleware;
```

```ts check file=routes/account/middleware.ts
// src/routes/account/middleware.ts: every page, action and endpoint under /account
import type { Middleware } from "lumiose";

const requireUser: Middleware<"/account"> = (ctx, next) => {
  if (ctx.locals.userId === null) return Response.redirect(new URL("/login", ctx.url), 303);
  return next();
};

export default requireUser;
```

```tsx check file=routes/account/page.tsx
// src/routes/account/page.tsx
import { locals, redirect, response } from "lumiose";

export const mode = "server";

export default function Account() {
  const { userId } = locals();
  if (userId === null) redirect("/login");
  response().setHeader("cache-control", "private, no-store");

  return <h1>Signed in as {userId}</h1>;
}
```

```ts check file=instrumentation.server.ts
// src/instrumentation.server.ts
import type { RequestErrorInfo, ServerInstrumentation } from "lumiose";

export async function register() {
  // Once per server instance, before the first request: start an SDK here.
}

export function onRequestError(error: unknown, info: RequestErrorInfo) {
  const where = `${info.request.method} ${info.route ?? "(no route)"} [${info.phase}]`;
  console.error(where, info.digest ?? "", error);
}

export const instrumentations: ServerInstrumentation[] = [
  {
    request: async (call, info) => {
      const start = performance.now();
      const result = await call();
      const status = result.status === "success" ? result.response?.status : "failed";
      const ms = Math.round(performance.now() - start);
      console.log(`${info.request.method} ${info.route ?? "-"} ${status} ${ms} ms`);
    },
  },
];
```

Tracing with [OpenTelemetry](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/languages/js/): install
`@opentelemetry/api` and an SDK (`@opentelemetry/sdk-node` with an exporter), start the SDK in
`register()`, and open a span per phase. Spans nest as the phases do: middleware inside the request,
the action, endpoint or render inside the middleware. Instrumenting other libraries automatically
(database drivers, `fetch`) still needs `node --import`, as OpenTelemetry documents.

```ts
// src/instrumentation.server.ts
import { SpanStatusCode, trace, type Attributes } from "@opentelemetry/api";
import type { ServerInstrumentation } from "lumiose";

export async function register() {
  const { NodeSDK } = await import("@opentelemetry/sdk-node");
  new NodeSDK({ serviceName: "my-app" }).start(); // exporters from OTEL_* env variables
}

const tracer = trace.getTracer("my-app");

/** A span around one phase, failed when the phase failed. */
const span =
  (name: string, attributes: Attributes) =>
  (call: () => Promise<{ status: "success" | "error"; error?: unknown }>) =>
    tracer.startActiveSpan(name, { attributes }, async (s) => {
      const result = await call();
      if (result.status === "error") {
        s.recordException(result.error as Error);
        s.setStatus({ code: SpanStatusCode.ERROR });
      }
      s.end();
    });

export const instrumentations: ServerInstrumentation[] = [
  {
    request: (call, info) =>
      tracer.startActiveSpan(`${info.request.method} ${info.route ?? ""}`, async (s) => {
        s.setAttributes({
          "http.request.method": info.request.method,
          "http.route": info.route ?? "",
        });
        const result = await call();
        if (result.status === "success" && result.response !== undefined) {
          s.setAttribute("http.response.status_code", result.response.status);
          if (result.response.status >= 500) s.setStatus({ code: SpanStatusCode.ERROR });
        }
        s.end();
      }),
    middleware: (call, info) => span("middleware", { "code.file.path": info.file })(call),
    action: (call, info) => span(`action ${info.name}`, { "http.route": info.route ?? "" })(call),
    endpoint: (call, info) =>
      span(`${info.method} handler`, { "http.route": info.route ?? "" })(call),
    render: (call, info) => span("render", { "http.route": info.route ?? "" })(call),
    stream: (call, info) => span("stream", { "http.route": info.route ?? "" })(call),
  },
];
```

## Common mistakes

- **Reporting errors from middleware with `try`/`catch` around `next()`.** The error page, the
  `500` of an endpoint and streamed boundaries never throw there. Use `onRequestError` in
  `src/instrumentation.server.ts`.
- **Changing the request in an instrumentation wrapper.** Wrappers observe: they cannot change
  arguments, results or the response. Use middleware for that.

- **Guarding a section in a layout.** A layout's `redirect()` does not cover the folder's form
  actions or endpoints. Put the check in the folder's `middleware.ts`.
- **Guarding prerendered routes with folder middleware.** It runs at build time only for them
  (`LUM5008`). Set `export const mode = "server"` on the routes it protects.
- **Reading request APIs in a `static` route.** `cookies()`, `request()` and friends throw
  `LUM5001` while prerendering. Set `export const mode = "server"`.
- **Setting headers or status after the shell.** Inside a streamed `<Suspense>` boundary it is too
  late (`LUM5004`). Do it before the boundary, in the page body outside `<Suspense>`, in
  `headers(ctx)` or in middleware.
- **Reading secrets with `import.meta.env`.** Only `PUBLIC_*` values exist there. Use `env("NAME")`
  in server-only modules.
- **Catching `redirect()` by accident.** It throws. In a `try`/`catch`, rethrow when
  `isRedirect(error) || isHttpError(error)`.
- **Storing request data in module-scope variables.** Modules are shared by every request. Use
  `locals`, context or component state (`LUM4008`).
- **Expecting signed cookies to hide data.** They are tamper-proof, not encrypted.

## Related diagnostics

- [LUM4003](../errors/LUM4003.md): server-only module in a client graph.
- [LUM4008](../errors/LUM4008.md): module-scope signal written during SSR.
- [LUM5001](../errors/LUM5001.md): request API used during prerender.
- [LUM5002](../errors/LUM5002.md): invalid route file, such as `src/routes/middleware.ts`.
- [LUM5004](../errors/LUM5004.md): head or status change inside a streamed boundary.
- [LUM5008](../errors/LUM5008.md): folder middleware covering prerendered routes.
- [LUM5009](../errors/LUM5009.md): boundary still pending when `streamTimeout` expired.

See also: [Data and actions](data-and-actions.md), [Routing](routing.md), [reference: app layer](../reference/app.md).

<!-- source: concepts/rendering-modes.md -->

# Rendering modes

> Each route renders as static HTML, on the server per request, or as a client-routed SPA, with the same components, mixed freely in one app.

## Concept

| Mode               | HTML                                                                                                                | JS shipped        | Navigation                              |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `static` (default) | At build time, for each path from `staticPaths()`                                                                   | Islands only      | MPA (prefetch, opt-in View Transitions) |
| `server`           | Per request: the shell, then streamed boundaries                                                                    | Islands only      | MPA (prefetch, opt-in View Transitions) |
| `spa`              | Server-rendered (per request, or at build time with `prerender`) and hydrated, or a client shell with `ssr = false` | The whole subtree | Client router (`<Link prefetch>`)       |

A route sets `export const mode = "server"` (a string literal); pages inherit the mode of their
nearest layout that sets one, else the project default set in `vite.config.ts` with
`lumiose({ mode: "server" })` (`"static"` when unset). `export const ssr = false` applies to `spa`
routes: the build emits a static shell and the page renders in the browser. `lumiose({ ssr: false })`
makes that the default for every `spa` route, so `lumiose({ mode: "spa", ssr: false })` turns the
whole project into a client-rendered SPA built as static files. `export const prerender = true`
renders an `spa` page (or, in a layout, every `spa` page below it) at build time instead of per
request, and `lumiose({ prerender: true })` makes that the default for every `spa` page (see
[Prerendered SPA routes](#prerendered-spa-routes)).

### Choosing a mode

Pick the mode by what the page needs, per route, not once for the whole app:

| Mode                  | For                                                                                                        | Typical pages                                                                     | Costs                                                                                                           | Sample app                                                                                                                                                               |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `static`              | Content that is the same for every visitor and known at build time                                         | Docs, marketing, blog posts, catalogs                                             | Rendered once per build. Any static host (a form `action` still needs a server for the POST). JS: islands only. | [ssg-travel-journal](https://github.com/itsjavi/lumiose/tree/main/examples/ssg-travel-journal), this website                                                             |
| `server`              | Pages that depend on the reader or the request, or must be fresh                                           | Account pages, dashboards, `?q=` search results, forms that re-render with errors | Rendered on every request: a server or a serverless function. JS: islands only.                                 | [ssr-auth](https://github.com/itsjavi/lumiose/tree/main/examples/ssr-auth), [ssr-bookshelf](https://github.com/itsjavi/lumiose/tree/main/examples/ssr-bookshelf)         |
| `spa`                 | App-like areas (client navigation, layout state kept across pages) whose first view depends on the request | Signed-in app areas                                                               | Rendered on every request, then the whole subtree ships and hydrates.                                           | [spa-router-e2e](https://github.com/itsjavi/lumiose/tree/main/examples/spa-router-e2e) (test app)                                                                        |
| `spa` + `prerender`   | App-like areas whose pages are the same for everyone and should work without JS and be indexed             | Public app pages, music tools, galleries                                          | Rendered once per build; any static host. The whole subtree ships and hydrates.                                 | [spa-chiptune](https://github.com/itsjavi/lumiose/tree/main/examples/spa-chiptune), [spa-dotmatrix](https://github.com/itsjavi/lumiose/tree/main/examples/spa-dotmatrix) |
| `spa` + `ssr = false` | Code that cannot run on the server, where an empty first view is acceptable                                | Editors, canvas or audio tools, admin screens behind a sign-in                    | A static shell; nothing renders until the JS has loaded.
