```ts
      type: "link" | "navigate" | "popstate";
      from: NavigationTarget | null; // lumiose/router
      to: NavigationTarget | null;
    },
  ): unknown; // until the page is on screen
  submit?(call: () => Promise<Result>, info: ClientInfo & { action: string; url: string }): unknown;
  fetch?(
    call: () => Promise<Result>,
    info: ClientInfo & ({ url: string } | { key: readonly unknown[] }),
  ): unknown; // each fetchJSON() request or query() function; cache hits are not requests
  hydrate?(call: () => Promise<Result>, info: ClientInfo & { island: string }): unknown;
}
```

## Example

```ts check file=routes/api/session/route.ts
// src/routes/api/session/route.ts
import { isHttpError, type Endpoint } from "lumiose";

// Per request: it reads cookies and accepts POST, so it cannot be prerendered (LUM5005).
export const mode = "server";

export const GET: Endpoint<"/api/session"> = ({ cookies }) =>
  Response.json({ theme: cookies.get("theme") ?? "light" });

export const POST: Endpoint<"/api/session"> = async ({ request, cookies }) => {
  try {
    const { theme } = (await request.json()) as { theme: string };
    cookies.set("theme", theme, { maxAge: 60 * 60 * 24 * 365 });
    return new Response(null, { status: 204 });
  } catch (error) {
    if (isHttpError(error)) throw error;
    return Response.json({ error: "Invalid JSON" }, { status: 400 });
  }
};
```

<!-- source: reference/server.md -->

# `lumiose`: server rendering

> `renderToStream` and `renderToString` render components to HTML on the server.

Most apps never call these directly: the request handler (and `lumiose dev` / `lumiose build`) does.
Use them for custom servers, tests and tools. Concepts:
[Rendering modes](../concepts/rendering-modes.md).

## renderToStream

```ts
function renderToStream(
  root: () => unknown,
  options?: RenderToStreamOptions,
): Promise<RenderedShell>;

interface RenderToStreamOptions {
  /** Aborts the render: rejects a pending shell, ends the stream and aborts getAbortSignal(). */
  signal?: AbortSignal;
  /** SSG/prerender: render every Suspense boundary into the shell; no fallbacks, no stream. */
  resolveAll?: boolean;
  /** CSP nonce for the $swap scripts and strict-mode <style> rules. */
  nonce?: string;
  /** CSP strict mode: style props become nonce'd <style> rules. */
  strictStyles?: boolean;
  /** Maps an island module specifier to its URL for modulepreload hints. */
  islandUrl?: (specifier: string) => string;
  /**
   * URL of the island loader (lumiose/dom/loader). A page with islands gets it once, as
   * <script type="module" async>: in `head` when the shell has islands, else in the first
   * streamed chunk with island records. Default: none (islands render but do not hydrate).
   */
  loaderUrl?: string;
  /** Errors of streamed boundaries that no ErrorBoundary handled. Default: console.error. */
  onError?: (error: unknown) => void;
  /**
   * Prepended to every useId() of the render, its islands included (they reuse it when they
   * hydrate). Keeps the ids of several renders or apps on one page apart. Default: "".
   */
  idPrefix?: string;
}

interface RenderedShell {
  /** Collected <Title>/<Meta>/<Head> HTML, modulepreload hints and strict-mode styles. */
  head: string;
  /** The shell HTML, followed by the shell's island records. */
  body: string;
  /** Streamed boundary chunks to append inside <body>; null when nothing is pending. */
  stream: ReadableStream<string> | null;
}
```

Renders `root` shell-first (decision-19): resolves once everything outside `<Suspense>` is ready,
and rejects with the first error thrown while rendering the shell (so the caller can render an
error page with the right status). The stream then delivers each boundary as it resolves, out of
order.

## renderToString

```ts
function renderToString(
  root: () => unknown,
  options?: Omit<RenderToStreamOptions, "resolveAll">,
): Promise<string>;
```

Renders everything resolved (no fallbacks, no stream) and returns the body HTML. Used for
prerendering and tests.

Both are server-only: in the browser build of `lumiose` they throw `LUM4003`. With `idPrefix`, the
island records carry the prefix, so [`useId()`](reactivity.md#useid) returns the same ids after
hydration.

## `lumiose/server`

The server runtime that compiled server code imports (`ssr`, `escape`, `insert`, `list`, `branch`,
`branchArm`, `createComponent`, `island`, `$await`, …). It is the compiler-runtime contract, not an
application API: its members may change between versions without notice. It also re-exports
`renderToStream` and `renderToString`.

## Example

```tsx check
import { renderToStream } from "lumiose";

function App() {
  return <h1>Hello</h1>;
}

export async function handle(request: Request): Promise<Response> {
  const { head, body, stream } = await renderToStream(() => <App />, { signal: request.signal });
  const encoder = new TextEncoderStream();
  const writer = encoder.writable.getWriter();
  void (async () => {
    await writer.write(`<!doctype html><html><head>${head}</head><body>${body}`);
    if (stream) for await (const chunk of stream) await writer.write(chunk);
    await writer.write("</body></html>");
    await writer.close();
  })();
  return new Response(encoder.readable, {
    headers: { "content-type": "text/html; charset=utf-8" },
  });
}
```

<!-- source: reference/dom.md -->

# `lumiose/dom`

> `render` mounts a component tree into the DOM; the rest of `lumiose/dom` is what compiled code imports.

## render

```ts
function render(code: () => JSX.Element, container: Element, options?: RenderOptions): () => void;

interface RenderOptions {
  /** Prepended to every useId() of the app: keeps the ids of several apps on one page apart. */
  idPrefix?: string;
}
```

Renders `code()` into `container` (appended after its existing content) under a new root owner, and
marks the container as a delegation boundary. Returns a disposer that disposes the owner and
removes the rendered nodes. With the Vite plugin, an entry module that imports `render` re-renders
the app on hot updates. Solid's `render` has the same signature, without `options`.
[`useId()`](reactivity.md#useid) in the app returns `idPrefix` followed by a counter.

## Compiler-runtime contract

`template`, `bind`, `insert`, `insertText`, `branch`, `list`, `selector`, `createComponent`, `mergeProps`,
`restProps`, `spread`, `delegateEvents`, `listen`, `attach`, `bindValue`, `bindChecked`,
`useRef`, `$async`, `$await`, `$leave` and friends are what the compiler emits calls to. They are
not an application API and may change between versions; write JSX instead.

## `lumiose/dom/hydrate`

```ts
function hydrate<P extends object>(
  component: Component<P>,
  props: P,
  start: Node,
  end: Node,
  awaits?: Record<string, unknown>,
  slots?: readonly string[],
  fresh?: boolean,
  idPrefix?: string,
): () => void;
```

Hydrates the server-rendered range between the comments `start` and `end` (an island's
`<!--l:ID-->` and `<!--/l:ID-->`): it renders `component` with `props`, and the compiled code
claims the server's nodes instead of creating new ones, so element identity, focus and text
selections survive. Returns a disposer.

- **Awaits are replayed.** `awaits` maps each first-run `await` of an async component to the value
  the server recorded (`"instancePath:site:occurrence"` keys), so hydration does not fetch again.
  The awaited expression still runs for tracking, with its fetch held off: when a signal it reads
  changes later, the component re-runs and fetches as usual.
- **Slots** (`slots`, the names of children and JSX props) become props holding the server's HTML:
  the nodes rendered inline (`<!--l:s:NAME-->…<!--/l:s-->`) are adopted where the island renders
  the slot; a slot the server did not render comes from its `<template data-l-slot="NAME">` when
  the island renders it later.
- **Mismatch.** When the client renders a different structure than the server's (another branch,
  element or list length), the island is disposed, its range cleared and rendered on the client;
  in dev, [LUM4006](../errors/LUM4006.md) is logged. A missing await record makes the client await
  again (also LUM4006 in dev).
- `fresh` (`client:only`) renders on the client without claiming.
- **Ids.** [`useId()`](reactivity.md#useid) returns the server's ids while the island hydrates: they
  come from the island id (in `start`) and each component's position. `idPrefix` is the server
  render's (the island record's `idPrefix`).

Importing `lumiose/dom/hydrate` also installs the hydration cursor that the compiled walk uses. Only
the island loader and hydrating entries import it; bundles that never hydrate do not include it.

## `lumiose/dom/loader`

The island loader: a client entry, with no exports, that `lumiose dev` and `lumiose build` add to every
page that renders an island (`<script type="module" async>`, see [Islands](../concepts/islands.md));
with your own server, pass its URL as `renderToStream(root, { loaderUrl })`. It imports the app's
island manifest (`virtual:lumiose/islands`, from `@lumiose/vite`), and (apps with
`src/instrumentation.client.ts` get a variant from `lumiose dev` and `lumiose build` whose islands
first wait for it, [Islands](../concepts/islands.md#concept)):

- reads the island records (`<script type="application/json" data-l-islands>`) as each streamed
  chunk arrives, and finds each island's range;
- arms its trigger: `client:load` and `client:only` at once, `client:idle` on
  `requestIdleCallback` with a 2 s timeout (a busy main thread cannot leave the island inert), `client:visible` when the range's first element intersects the viewport
  (the value is the `rootMargin`), `client:media` when the query matches;
- waits for an island whose range still holds a streamed `<Suspense>` fallback until its content
  (and the await records sent with it) arrives;
- imports the island's module and calls `hydrate()`;
- catches `click`, `input`, `submit` and `keydown` on an island that is not hydrated yet: it
  hydrates that island at once and dispatches the events again on their targets afterwards (an
  `input` restores the value typed meanwhile).

Islands inside slots that an island inserts later are hydrated when they appear.

**When an island fails.** A module that does not load (a deploy replaced its chunk, a network
error) or a component that throws while it hydrates is logged with the island's ref
(`Lumiose: hydrate error in island /src/Counter.tsx#Counter`), not left as an unhandled promise
rejection. The events the island caught are dispatched again without being held back, so their
default actions run: a link navigates, a form submits to its `action`. A module that did not load
is imported again on the next interaction with the island; an island whose hydration threw stays
server HTML. With `src/instrumentation.client.ts`, its `onError` receives
the error too (`phase: "hydrate"`), and its `hydrate` wrappers observe each island
([Islands](../concepts/islands.md#concept)).

## Example

```tsx check
import { signal } from "lumiose";
import { render } from "lumiose/dom";

function App() {
  const name = signal("world");
  return <input bind:value={name} placeholder={`Hello, ${name()}`} />;
}

render(() => <App />, document.getElementById("app")!);
```

<!-- source: reference/router.md -->

# `lumiose/router`

> The client router for `spa` routes: links, navigation, navigation hooks, reactive route state, persistent layouts, transitions, scroll restoration, focus reset and page announcements.

`lumiose/router` works inside `spa` routes (`export const mode = "spa"`, or `lumiose({ mode: "spa" })`
for the whole project); `<Link>`, `beforeNavigate()` and `afterNavigate()` work on MPA pages too (see [Link](#link) and
[Navigation hooks](#navigation-hooks)). Pages and layouts of an SPA import it like any module; on the server
(`ssr` pages, rendered per request or prerendered at build time) the same names read the request: `params()`, `route()`, `url()` and `searchParams()` return the
request's values, `<Link>` renders its `<a>`, `isNavigating()` is `false`, `beforeNavigate()` and
`afterNavigate()` register nothing, and `navigate()` and `searchParams.set()` throw (call them from
event handlers and effects). Concepts:
[Routing](../concepts/routing.md), [Rendering modes](../concepts/rendering-modes.md).

## Components

### Link

```ts
function Link(props: LinkProps): JSX.Element;

type LinkProps = Omit<JSX.IntrinsicElements["a"], "href" | "children"> & {
  href: string;
  /** Default "hover" in spa pages; on MPA pages, lumiose({ prefetch }). */
  prefetch?: "hover" | "viewport" | "none";
  children?: JSX.Element;
};
```

An `<a href>` with every attribute and event of `<a>`. The router navigates plain `<a>` links too;
`<Link>` adds:

- **Prefetch.** It loads the target route's modules ahead of the click: when the pointer enters
  the link or it gets focus (`hover`), when it enters the viewport (`viewport`), or not (`none`).
  Data still loads when the page renders. `spa` pages get no speculation rules, so this is the
  prefetch of their links.
- **On MPA pages** (static and server routes) there is no router: `<Link>` renders a plain `<a>`,
  outside islands without any JavaScript, and `prefetch` sets how the page's speculation rules from
  `lumiose({ prefetch })` treat it ([Routing](../concepts/routing.md)). The `<a>` gets
  `data-l-prefetch="<level>"`; the rules skip `none` links, prefetch `viewport` links with `eager`
  and `hover` links with `moderate` eagerness, and give unmarked links (`<Link>` without
  `prefetch`, plain `<a>`) the project default. With `lumiose({ prefetch: "none" })`, only pages that
  have `hover` or `viewport` links get rules. Browsers prefetch URLs: a `none` link to a URL that
  another link on the page prefetches does not stop it.
- **`aria-current="page"`** while its path is the current URL's path (style it with
  `a[aria-current="page"]`).

Build `href` with [`href()`](app.md#href) so the route and its params type-check.

## Navigation

### navigate

```ts
function navigate(href: string | URL, options?: NavigateOptions): Promise<void>;

interface NavigateOptions {
  /** Replace the current history entry instead of adding one. */
  replace?: boolean;
}
```

Navigates on the client when `href` belongs to the current SPA, else loads the document. Resolves
once the new page is on screen (its async content ready), or when another navigation supersedes
it. Browser only. Only `http:` and `https:` URLs (relative ones included) navigate: any other
scheme, such as `javascript:`, throws a `TypeError`.

### isNavigating

```ts
function isNavigating(): boolean;
```

Whether a navigation is in flight: from the click until the new page is on screen. Reactive, and
counted by [`isBusy()`](reactivity.md) (decision-20).

## Navigation hooks

SvelteKit's `beforeNavigate` and `afterNavigate` (decision-50). Call them during component setup,
like `onMount`: the hook runs while the component is mounted and is removed when it is disposed.

### beforeNavigate

```ts
function beforeNavigate(fn: (navigation: BeforeNavigate) => void): void;

interface BeforeNavigate {
  type: "link" | "navigate" | "popstate" | "leave";
  from: NavigationTarget | null;
  /** `null` when the next document is outside the app (another origin, or `"leave"`). */
  to: NavigationTarget | null;
  /** The document unloads: the navigation is not a client-side one. */
  willUnload: boolean;
  cancel(): void;
}

interface NavigationTarget {
  url: URL;
  /** The matched route pattern (`/songs/[id]`); undefined when none matched. */
  route: Routes | undefined;
  params: Record<string, string>;
}
```

Runs before each navigation away from the current location, before the router loads anything.
`type` is what started it:

| `type`       | Navigation                                                                                   |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `"link"`     | A link click (or a `GET` form) to a URL of the SPA, or out of it (`willUnload`).             |
| `"navigate"` | `navigate()` or `searchParams.set()` (a thrown `redirect()` runs no hook: it continues one). |
| `"popstate"` | Back/forward.                                                                                |
| `"leave"`    | The document unloads otherwise: closing the tab, typing a URL, a reload, a `POST` form.      |

`navigation.cancel()` stops it, and the URL stays the current one:

- Inside the SPA, the navigation does not start. Back/forward that the browser does not let the
  page cancel happens, then the router returns to the entry it left (without the Navigation API,
  each history entry the router creates stores its index in `history.state` for that).
- For a navigation that unloads the document (`willUnload`: `"leave"`, or a link or `navigate()`
  to a page outside the SPA), the browser shows its own "Leave site?" prompt (`beforeunload`): a
  custom dialog cannot run there. The browser shows it only after the user interacted with the
  page.

A change of the URL's `#hash` alone is not a navigation for the hooks.

### afterNavigate

```ts
function afterNavigate(fn: (navigation: AfterNavigate) => void): void;

interface AfterNavigate {
  type: "enter" | "link" | "navigate" | "popstate";
  from: NavigationTarget | null;
  to: NavigationTarget | null;
  willUnload: boolean;
}
```

Runs once per completed client navigation, after the new page is on screen (after a view
transition's DOM update, not its animation), its scroll position restored, focus reset and the page
announced to screen readers. A
navigation that a newer one supersedes or a hook cancels never completes. It also runs once when
the component mounts, with `type: "enter"` and `from: null`, so the first page view counts too; a
component that a navigation created gets that navigation's call instead.

### On MPA pages

Islands of `static` and `server` pages have no router, and using the hooks loads none: there,
`beforeNavigate` sees only `"leave"` (a `beforeunload` listener, added while a hook is registered)
and `afterNavigate` fires once with `"enter"`, with `route` undefined.

## Route state

### params

```ts
function params<P extends Routes = never>(): RouteParams<P>; // untyped: Record<string, string>
```

The current route's params, reactive: `params<"/songs/[id]">().id`. Pages also receive them as
`props.params`.

### route

```ts
function route(): Routes | undefined;
```

The matched route pattern, reactive: `route() === "/songs/[id]"`. Compare patterns instead of
matching `url().pathname`; typegen makes an unknown pattern a type error. `undefined` on a `not-found`
page for an unknown URL (a matched route that throws `notFound()` keeps its pattern).

### url

```ts
function url(): URL;
```

The current URL, reactive. Do not mutate it.

### locale

```ts
function locale(): Locale;
```

With `lumiose({ i18n })`, the locale of the current URL (its prefix, else the default locale),
reactive inside SPA routes; in islands of other routes, the page's. `undefined` without
`lumiose({ i18n })`, typed `string | undefined`. A navigation to another locale renders every level again, and `<html lang>`
follows. See [Internationalization](../concepts/i18n.md).

### searchParams

```ts
interface SearchParams {
  (): URLSearchParams;
  set(
    next: SearchParamsInit | ((current: URLSearchParams) => SearchParamsInit),
    options?: NavigateOptions,
  ): Promise<void>;
}
const searchParams: SearchParams;

type SearchParamsInit =
  | URLSearchParams
  | string
  | Record<string, string | number | boolean | readonly string[] | null | undefined>;
```

`searchParams()` is the current URL's query, reactive (a new object per change). `searchParams.set()`
navigates to the current path with a new query, keeping the scroll position; `null` and
`undefined` values are left out. It adds a history entry unless `{ replace: true }`.

While a page is still loading during a navigation, `params()`, `route()`, `url()` and `searchParams()` called in it
(and its props) already describe the page it is loading; everything else keeps the shown URL until
the new page is on screen.

## Behaviour

- **Interception.** The router handles same-document navigations to URLs of its SPA: link clicks,
  `navigate()`, back/forward and (with the Navigation API) `GET` form submissions. URLs of other
  routes (`static` or `server` pages, endpoints, other SPAs) load the document. Without the
  Navigation API, a History API fallback intercepts link clicks and `popstate`; it is a chunk of its
  own that only those browsers load, shortly after the SPA starts (a click before it loads is a
  document navigation).
- **Persistent layouts.** A layout's `children` is the outlet. Layouts the old and the new page
  share stay mounted with their state; the first level that differs (another file, or other
  values of the params in its path, such as `songs/[id]/page.stsx` for another song) is replaced. A
  navigation that only changes the query keeps every level and updates `searchParams()`.
- **Transitions.** The new page is created off-screen. The old page stays until the new page's
  async content (async components and resources outside a `<Suspense>` of the new page) is ready;
  then the URL signals change and the pages swap in one step. A `<Suspense>` inside the new page
  shows its fallback instead.
- **Scroll and focus.** After a navigation the page scrolls to the top (or to the URL's `#hash`)
  and focus moves to the document (or the first focusable `[autofocus]` element), so the next Tab
  starts from the top of the page, as after a document load; back/forward restore the scroll
  position. Focus the new page moved while it loaded stays. `searchParams.set()` keeps both, and
  back/forward between entries that differ only in `#hash` keeps focus. Browsers without the
  Navigation API get the same behaviour from the History API fallback.
- **Announcements.** Screen readers announce a document load, not a client navigation, so the
  router reads each new page aloud: once it is on screen, scrolled and focused, a visually hidden
  live region (`aria-live="assertive"`, `aria-atomic="true"`, appended to `<body>` with a
  `data-l-announcer` attribute) gets its `document.title` (set by `<Title>`), else the text of its
  first `<h1>`, else its path. The first page is not announced (the screen reader reads the
  document), nor is a navigation that keeps the path (a query change) unless the title changed.
  Give each page a distinct `<Title>` so the announcement says where the user is. The region is
  created once the SPA has hydrated, outside it, and removed with it.
- **Errors.** `notFound()` and unknown URLs render the nearest `not-found` page of the SPA; other
  errors its `error` page (`{ status, error }` props), with the layouts kept. With
  `src/instrumentation.client.ts`, its `onError` receives the other errors (`phase: "navigate"`),
  and its `navigate` wrappers observe each navigation
  ([Islands](../concepts/islands.md#concept)). A thrown `redirect()`
  navigates. Without such a page, a minimal built-in error page replaces the SPA. A `not-found` page that
  the server rendered at the URL of a prerendered page with params (`404.html` on a static host)
  renders that page instead: see
  [Prerendered SPA routes](../concepts/rendering-modes.md#prerendered-spa-routes).
- **`invalidate()`** from `lumiose` re-runs the SPA's async components and resources (they keep
  their UI meanwhile) and resolves once they settled. `submit()` redirects navigate through the
  router, and a successful `submit()` invalidates (on MPA pages it does not: that would reload).
- **Stale modules.** A page module that fails to load (an old chunk after a deploy) loads the URL
  as a document instead (its hooks already ran: no `"leave"`).

## Example

```tsx check file=routes/music/layout.tsx
// src/routes/music/layout.tsx: an SPA under /music, with a persistent layout
import { href, type LayoutProps } from "lumiose";
import { Link, isNavigating } from "lumiose/router";

export const mode = "spa";

export default function Layout(props: LayoutProps<"/music">) {
  return (
    <div class="app">
      <nav>
        <Link href={href("/music")}>Songs</Link>
        <Link href={href("/music/settings")} prefetch="viewport">
          Settings
        </Link>
      </nav>
      {isNavigating() && <progress />}
      <main>{props.children}</main>
    </div>
  );
}
```

```tsx check file=routes/music/page.tsx
// src/routes/music/page.tsx: a filter kept in the query
import { searchParams } from "lumiose/router";

export default function Songs() {
  const query = () => searchParams().get("q") ?? "";
  return (
    <input
      type="search"
      value={query()}
      onInput={(event) =>
        searchParams.set({ q: event.currentTarget.value || null }, { replace: true })
      }
    />
  );
}
```

```tsx check file=routes/music/settings/page.tsx
// src/routes/music/settings/page.tsx: asks before leaving unsaved changes
import { href, signal } from "lumiose";
import { afterNavigate, beforeNavigate, navigate } from "lumiose/router";

export default function Settings() {
  const dirty = signal(false);

  beforeNavigate((navigation) => {
    if (!dirty()) return;
    if (navigation.willUnload) navigation.cancel(); // the browser asks
    else if (!confirm("Discard your changes?")) navigation.cancel();
  });

  afterNavigate((navigation) => {
    if (navigation.to !== null) console.info("page view", navigation.to.url.pathname);
  });

  return (
    <form>
      <input name="volume" onInput={() => dirty.set(true)} />
      <button
        type="button"
        onClick={() => {
          dirty.set(false);
          void navigate(href("/music"), { replace: true });
        }}
      >
        Done
      </button>
    </form>
  );
}
```

See also: [Routing](../concepts/routing.md), [Rendering modes](../concepts/rendering-modes.md),
[`lumiose`: app layer](app.md).

<!-- source: reference/vite.md -->

# `@lumiose/vite`

> The Vite 8 plugin: compiles `.stsx` and `.tsx` files, reports diagnostics in the overlay and reloads on edit.

Install it next to `lumiose` and Vite: `pnpm add -D @lumiose/vite vite`. Both are peer
dependencies, so the plugin, the compiled modules and its Vitest setup share the app's one copy of
`lumiose`.

## lumiose()

```ts
import lumiose from "@lumiose/vite";

function lumiose(options?: LumioseOptions): Plugin[];

interface LumioseOptions {
  /** Modules compiled by Lumiose. Default: .stsx and .tsx files. */
  include?: RegExp;
  /** Modules left to Vite. Default: anything in node_modules. */
  exclude?: RegExp;
  /** The project's default route mode; a layout's or route's `export const mode` overrides it. */
  mode?: "static" | "server" | "spa"; // default "static"
  /** Whether spa routes render their content on the server (false: the shell only). */
  ssr?: boolean; // default true
  /** Whether spa pages that render on the server are prerendered at build time; a layout's or page's `export const prerender` overrides it. */
  prerender?: boolean; // default false, and not with ssr: false
  /** Trailing slashes of page URLs: "always"/"never" redirect to the canonical form. */
  trailingSlash?: "ignore" | "always" | "never"; // default "ignore"
  /** The origin check of form posts (on by default); false turns it off. */
  csrf?: false | { allowedOrigins?: readonly string[] };
  /** `.svg?component` imports as inline components; false leaves them to Vite (URLs). */
  svg?: boolean | { optimize?: boolean | SvgoConfig; currentColor?: boolean }; // default true
  /** `.md` imports as components; the hook validates or transforms each file's frontmatter. */
  md?: boolean | { frontmatter?(data: Record<string, unknown>, ctx: { file: string }): unknown }; // default false
  /** `.html` imports as components. */
  html?: boolean; // default false
  /** View Transitions (not under reduced motion): between MPA pages, and for SPA navigations. */
  viewTransitions?: boolean; // default false
  /** Speculation rules that prefetch the same-origin links of MPA pages. */
  prefetch?: "hover" | "viewport" | "none"; // default "hover"
  /** A strict Content Security Policy: nonces per response, hashes for prerendered pages. */
  csp?: "strict";
  /** Response headers: a record for every response, or rules by path (below base). */
  headers?: Record<string, string> | { path: string; headers: Record<string, string> }[];
  /** Request body limits, in bytes or "512kb"/"1mb": larger requests get 413. */
  limits?: { body?: number | string; upload?: number | string }; // default { body: "1mb", upload: "10mb" }
  /** How long a page render waits for pending <Suspense> boundaries: milliseconds, "30s", "500ms", "2m", or false. */
  streamTimeout?: number | string | false; // default "30s"
  /** The deploy adapter: cloudflare(), vercel() or netlify() from their @lumiose/adapter-* packages. */
  adapter?: Adapter; // default: none, the Node build
  /** Locale routing: unprefixed default locale, prefixed others, per-page locale declarations. */
  i18n?: {
    locales: string[]; // URL path segments, such as "en" or "pt-BR"
    defaultLocale: string; // served without a prefix
    missing?: "404" | "redirect"; // default "404"
    detect?: false | { cookie?: string; acceptLanguage?: boolean }; // default false
  };
  /** The site's URL, for the absolute URLs of prerendered pages (hreflang, canonical); a path is the base. */
  site?: string; // such as "https://example.com" or "https://example.com/docs"
  /** The in-page inspector of `lumiose dev` (Alt+Shift+L, Alt+click to the source); dev only. */
  inspector?: boolean; // default true
}
```

The project options (`mode`, `ssr`, `prerender`, `trailingSlash`, `csrf`, `viewTransitions`,
`prefetch`, `headers`, `limits`, `streamTimeout`, `adapter`, `i18n`, `site`, `inspector`) are
read by `lumiose dev`, `lumiose build` and `lumiose routes`/`check` from the plugin's `api.options`.
Invalid values and unknown option names throw when the config loads, as does `prerender: true`
with `ssr: false` ([prerendered SPA routes](../concepts/rendering-modes.md#prerendered-spa-routes)). `csp: "strict"` is
described in [Security](../concepts/security.md): nonces on every inline script and style Lumiose
writes and on those written in JSX, static `style` strings as nonce'd rules, a `Content-Security-Policy` header for pages rendered per request, and a hash policy
`<meta>` in prerendered pages. `allowedOrigins` takes full
origins such as `"https://app.example.com"`, without a path or trailing slash.

**Response headers** (`headers`). Declare them once: a record applies to every response; rules
apply to the paths they match, below Vite's `base` (`*` matches one segment, `**` any number,
later rules win for the same header). `lumiose dev`, `lumiose preview` and `@lumiose/adapter-node` send
them on every response, static files included, and `lumiose build` writes them to
`dist/client/_headers`, the file Netlify and Cloudflare Pages read (`**` becomes `*`, a `*`
segment a `:name` placeholder). Headers that middleware, endpoints or `response().setHeader()` set
win. Two headers are sent by default, as Rails and Django do: `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and
`Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`; give them another value in `headers`, or `""`
to remove one (`_headers` gets `! name`).

**Locales** (`i18n`) and **site** (`site`). With `i18n`, route files stay unprefixed: the
default locale is served at `/about`, the others under their prefix (`/es/about`), and a page
exists in the locales it declares with `export const locales`. `missing` decides what a page
requested in another locale answers, `detect` redirects visitors to their locale on entry only. See
[Internationalization](../concepts/i18n.md). `site` is the site's URL (`"https://example.com"`):
prerendered pages have no request, so their absolute `hreflang` and canonical URLs are its origin
followed by the `href()` path, which already has Vite's `base` and the trailing-slash policy;
without `site` they are root-relative, and `lumiose build` warns. Pages rendered per request use
the request's origin. A path in `site` (`"https://example.com/docs"`, trailing slash optional) is
the app's base: it becomes Vite's `base` when the config sets none, and a config `base` that
differs from it is an error naming both, so the path is never counted twice.

**In-page inspector** (`inspector`, decision-59). `lumiose dev` mounts the inspector on every page
from its dev client: Alt+Shift+L or the corner button opens the component tree, signals, islands
and why something updated, and Alt+click opens an element's source through Vite's open-in-editor
endpoint ([Dev tools](../concepts/dev-tools.md)). In dev, the plugin also compiles every element that renders a box (not `<title>`, `<meta>` and
the like) with `data-lumiose-source="<file>:<line>:<column>"`, signal and computed variables with their names, and
component registrations with their locations, and the runtime records for the inspector behind the
`import.meta.env.LUMIOSE_INSPECTOR` define. Builds and Vitest get none of it. `inspector: false`
removes all of it from `lumiose dev` too.

**Body limits** (`limits`). `body` caps URL-encoded forms, JSON and any other non-multipart
request body (default `"1mb"`), `upload` caps `multipart/form-data` bodies (default `"10mb"`). A
route's `export const limits = { upload: "100mb" }` overrides them for its requests. Sizes are
bytes or strings with `b`, `kb`, `mb` or `gb` (1024-based); a size past 2^53 - 1 bytes is an
error. See [Security](../concepts/security.md).

**Streaming timeout** (`streamTimeout`). How long a page render waits for its pending
`<Suspense>` boundaries, from the start of the render: milliseconds, or a string with `ms`, `s` or
`m` (`"30s"`, the default). Once it expires, async components still waiting fail with
[`LUM5009`](../errors/LUM5009.md): the nearest `<ErrorBoundary>` renders its fallback into the
stream, a boundary without one keeps its `<Suspense>` fallback, `onRequestError` receives the error
with phase `"stream"`, and the response ends. It applies to `lumiose dev` and the build output on
every host, also to responses that `response().setStreaming(false)` resolves in full; prerendering
ignores it. `false` waits as long as the client stays connected. Values past 2^31 - 1 ms are an
error. See [Rendering modes](../concepts/rendering-modes.md#how-pages-render).

```ts
lumiose({
  headers: [
    { path: "/**", headers: { "cross-origin-opener-policy": "same-origin" } },
    { path: "/admin/**", headers: { "x-robots-tag": "noindex" } },
  ],
});
```

| Deployment                         | Where the headers come from                                                         |
| ---------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `lumiose dev`, `lumiose preview`   | `lumiose({ headers })`                                                              |
| `@lumiose/adapter-node`            | `lumiose({ headers })`, from the build (`config.headers` of `dist/server/entry.js`) |
| `dist/server/entry.js` (Bun, Deno) | `lumiose({ headers })`, from the build, on static files and the app's responses     |
| Cloudflare, Netlify adapters       | `dist/client/_headers` for static files; the build's handler for the rest           |
| Vercel adapter                     | `config.json` routes                                                                |
| Netlify, Cloudflare Pages          | `lumiose({ headers })`, as `dist/client/_headers`                                   |
| Other static hosts and CDNs        | The host's own header configuration, copied from `lumiose({ headers })`             |

Per-response headers that depend on the request belong in middleware or `response().setHeader()`.

**Deploy adapters** (`adapter`, decision-45). After prerendering, `lumiose build` hands the build to
the adapter, which writes the platform's output: `cloudflare()` from
`@lumiose/adapter-cloudflare` ([guide](../deploy/cloudflare.md)), `vercel({ runtime })` from
`@lumiose/adapter-vercel` ([guide](../deploy/vercel.md)), `netlify()` from
`@lumiose/adapter-netlify` ([guide](../deploy/netlify.md)). These platforms serve `dist/client`
themselves and compress on their own, so the build writes no `.br`/`.gz` copies and the server
build has no static file layer. Without an adapter, the output is the Node build that
`@lumiose/adapter-node`, Bun and Deno serve ([Deploy](../deploy/README.md)). The adapter packages
have named exports only:

```ts
import { cloudflare } from "@lumiose/adapter-cloudflare";

lumiose({ adapter: cloudflare() });
```

MPA navigation ([Routing](../concepts/routing.md)): the page documents that `lumiose dev` and
`lumiose build` render get, in `<head>`:

- `viewTransitions: true`:
  `<style>@media (prefers-reduced-motion:no-preference){@view-transition{navigation:auto}}</style>`,
  on every page, `spa` pages included (their client navigations are not cross-document: the SPA
  router swaps their pages inside [`viewTransition()`](components.md#viewtransition) instead).
- `prefetch`: a `<script type="speculationrules">` on every page except `spa` pages, whose
  `<Link prefetch>` prefetches instead. It matches the links below Vite's `base` (`href_matches`),
  except the URLs of endpoints, with `moderate` eagerness for `"hover"` (the pointer rests on the
  link, or it is pressed) and `eager` for `"viewport"` (as soon as the browser sees fit: desktop
  Chromium on a brief hover, mobile Chromium as links enter the viewport); `"none"` emits nothing.
  On a page with `<Link prefetch>` links (marked `data-l-prefetch`), the rules give each level its
  own `selector_matches` rule, and the default's rule skips links marked otherwise; with `"none"`,
  only such pages get rules ([`lumiose/router`](router.md#link)).

Both are inline elements: a Content-Security-Policy you set without `'unsafe-inline'` needs
`'inline-speculation-rules'` in `script-src` for the rules, and the hash of the `<style>` in
`style-src`.

What it does:

- Compiles Lumiose modules before Vite's own transform, which is told to skip them. Server consumers
  (SSR) get `lumiose/server` code; everything else gets `lumiose/dom` code.
- Resolves `lumiose` to its `browser` entry in client environments and its `node` entry in server
  environments, and keeps every `lumiose` entry out of dependency pre-bundling, so compiled code and
  the runtime share one module instance. Under Vitest, tests in a DOM environment (`happy-dom`,
  `jsdom`) get the `browser` entry too (see [Testing](../concepts/testing.md)).
- Turns compiler diagnostics into Vite warnings and errors with code frames (the dev overlay).
- Names scoped state: each module-scope `defineState()` binding imported from `lumiose` gets an id
  after its module and export (`/src/lib/cart.ts#cart`), as island refs do, where client code
  (islands, SPA routes) reaches it; pages send only those states' values
  ([`defineState`](reactivity.md#definestate)). Under Vitest it adds a setup file that resets
  scoped state before each test.
- Loads `.svg?component` imports (`./icon.svg?component`, or a package's
  `lucide-static/icons/house.svg?component`) as inline components for the environment's target,
  optimised with SVGO (`optimize`: `true` for Lumiose's defaults, `preset-default` plus
  `convertStyleToAttrs`; your SVGO config; or `false`). Scripts, event handlers and
  `javascript:` URLs are always removed and ids prefixed per file. `currentColor: true` replaces
  every colour with `currentColor` (SVGO's `convertColors`, before other plugins). Every other
  `.svg` import (bare, `?url`, `?inline`, `?raw`) is Vite's. See
  [SVG imports](../concepts/svg.md).
- With `md`/`html`, loads project `.md` and `.html` files as static components: their source
  becomes the Lumiose module `<file>.md.stsx` (`.html.stsx`), compiled like any `.stsx` file, with
  `frontmatter` from `<file>.md?lumiose-frontmatter`, `headings`, relative asset URLs as `?url`
  imports, and client scripts loaded by an island from `<file>.html?lumiose-script`. HTML entries (`index.html`, HTML build inputs) and `public/` files
  stay Vite's. See [Markdown and HTML imports](../concepts/content.md).
- Hot updates: an edited component re-renders in place, in every instance, and the rest of the page
  keeps its DOM and state (`lumiose dev` registers each named component of client code with
  `lumiose/dom/hot`). Only the components whose code changed re-render; an edit outside every
  component of the file (a constant, a helper) re-renders all of the file's components. Components
  hydrated in an island or on the SPA's first page update the same way once hydrated. A module
  whose exports are not all such components (a constant or signal export, a changed export list,
  an async or anonymous default component) falls back to the app entry: a client module that imports `render` from `lumiose/dom` accepts
  updates of every module it reaches and re-renders the app into the same container (component
  state resets; module-level signals of unchanged modules survive), else the page reloads.
- Style blocks become `<file>?lumiose&type=style&lang.css` modules handled by Vite's CSS pipeline.
  Modules that `$` references import constants from are tracked as dependencies of that CSS module.
  A style-only edit, or an edit to such a constants module, hot-updates the CSS without remounting.

> **Status:** compilation, environments, diagnostics, HMR, style-block CSS, `.svg`, `.md` and `.html` imports and the
> project options above are available. The designed option `css` is not.

## createDevHandler()

```ts
import { createDevHandler } from "@lumiose/vite/dev";

function createDevHandler(options?: DevHandlerOptions): Promise<DevHandler>;

interface DevHandlerOptions {
  /** Your HTTP server: Vite's HMR WebSocket upgrades there. Default: HMR on a port of its own. */
  server?: import("node:http").Server;
  root?: string; // default: the current directory
  configFile?: string | false; // default: vite.config.* in the root
  mode?: string; // Vite mode (.env files), default "development"
  routesDir?: string; // default "src/routes"
  logLevel?: LogLevel;
  customLogger?: Logger;
}

interface DevHandler {
  (req: IncomingMessage, res: ServerResponse, next?: (error?: unknown) => void): void;
  readonly vite: ViteDevServer; // Vite in middleware mode
  close(): Promise<void>; // stops Vite (watcher, HMR); your server stays open
}
```

`lumiose dev` inside your own Node server (decision-52). It starts Vite in middleware mode with the
project's `vite.config.ts` and returns a handler of the same kind as `@lumiose/adapter-node`'s
[`createHandler()`](adapter-node.md#createhandler): a request listener, or connect/Express
middleware (errors go to `next`). Everything `lumiose dev` does works through it: modules and
assets, the routes, the error overlay, HMR, in-place updates after server-only edits and typegen.
Pass your server as `server` so HMR shares its port: Vite takes only its own upgrades
(`Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: vite-hmr`) and leaves the others to your `upgrade` listeners, so
leave an upgrade alone, rather than destroying it, when your code does not handle it in dev.
`lumiose dev` stays the default; this is for projects that own their server. `@lumiose/vite` is a
dev dependency: import it only in dev, and production never loads Vite.

```ts
// server.ts: `node server.ts --dev` in dev, `node server.ts` after `lumiose build`
import { createServer } from "node:http";
import { createHandler } from "@lumiose/adapter-node";

const dev = process.argv.includes("--dev");
const server = createServer();
const handler = dev
  ? await (await import("@lumiose/vite/dev")).createDevHandler({ server })
  : await createHandler();
server.on("request", handler);
server.listen(3000);
```

## Example

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import lumiose from "@lumiose/vite";
import { defineConfig } from "vite";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [lumiose({ mode: "server", exclude: /[\\/](node_modules|legacy)[\\/]/ })],
});
```

<!-- source: reference/jsx.md -->

# JSX types and tsconfig

> The JSX and environment types, and the tsconfig settings a Lumiose project needs.

## tsconfig.json

A Lumiose project's `tsconfig.json` extends the tsconfig that Lumiose generates (decision-25). This is
what `create-lumiose` writes, what `lumiose agents init` writes when the file is missing, and what
`lumiose check` prints when there is none:

```jsonc
{
  // Lumiose's compiler options, shadow TSX and route types. lumiose dev, build, check and typegen
  // write the generated file; add your own options below.
  "extends": "./.lumiose/tsconfig.generated.json",
}
```

Add your own `compilerOptions` next to `extends`; they override the generated ones. `lumiose check`,
`lumiose typegen`, `lumiose dev`/`build`, `@lumiose/vite` and the language server write
`.lumiose/tsconfig.generated.json`, so it follows the installed Lumiose version and the workspace
layout. `.lumiose/` is not committed: in a fresh clone, run `lumiose typegen` (or `lumiose check`) before
a bare `tsc`.

The generated file, with paths relative to `.lumiose/`:

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "jsx": "preserve",
    "jsxImportSource": "lumiose",
    "module": "preserve",
    "moduleResolution": "bundler",
    "allowImportingTsExtensions": true,
    "noEmit": true,
    "strict": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "rootDirs": ["..", "./shadow"],
    "types": ["lumiose/env"]
  },
  "include": ["../src", "./shadow", "./types"]
}
```

| Option                                          | Why                                                                                       |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `jsx: "preserve"`, `jsxImportSource: "lumiose"` | The Lumiose compiler transforms JSX; TypeScript only checks it against Lumiose's types.   |
| `rootDirs` with `.lumiose/shadow`               | `import "./X.stsx"` resolves to the shadow file `X.stsx.tsx`.                             |
| `include` `.lumiose/shadow`, `.lumiose/types`   | Shadow files and generated route types are part of the program.                           |
| `types: ["lumiose/env"]`                        | The global `JSX` namespace, `import.meta.env`, `Locals` and `.svg`/`.md`/`.html` modules. |
| `allowImportingTsExtensions`                    | Imports name their extension: `./Card.stsx`, `./tokens.ts`.                               |
| `skipLibCheck`                                  | Dependencies' `.d.ts` files are not checked: faster, and their type errors are not yours. |

If you set `include` or `types` yourself, they replace the generated lists: keep `src`,
`.lumiose/shadow` and `.lumiose/types` in `include`, and `lumiose/env` in `types`. An array `extends`
keeps a shared base: `["../../tsconfig.base.json", "./.lumiose/tsconfig.generated.json"]` (later
entries win). `lumiose check` reports missing options (`LUM6001`).

### Imports outside `src/` and `.stsx` from other packages

The generated `rootDirs` pair a _mirror base_ with `.lumiose/shadow`. The mirror base is the nearest
directory that contains the project and the Lumiose packages it uses. These are the linked
dependencies that list `lumiose` as a dependency, plus the enclosing package of a project without its
own `package.json`. For a standalone project, it is the project root (`..` above).

Shadows mirror the paths below that base. For example, `apps/web/.lumiose/shadow/apps/web/src/` holds
the app's own shadows and `apps/web/.lumiose/shadow/packages/ui/src/` holds a package's. So a `.stsx`
import may leave `src/` (`../../lib/x.ts`), and a component that a workspace package re-exports
from its own `.stsx` files (`@acme/ui` → `./Button.stsx`) is type-checked with your project, with
errors pointing at its sources.

### Without `extends`

A tsconfig can also set the options itself:

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "jsx": "preserve",
    "jsxImportSource": "lumiose",
    "module": "preserve",
    "moduleResolution": "bundler",
    "allowImportingTsExtensions": true,
    "noEmit": true,
    "strict": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "rootDirs": ["src", ".lumiose/shadow/src"],
    "types": ["lumiose/env"]
  },
  "include": ["src", ".lumiose/shadow", ".lumiose/types"]
}
```

Its `rootDirs` pair only `src` with `.lumiose/shadow/src`, so `.stsx` files must stay inside `src/`:
a `.stsx` import that leaves `src/` does not resolve (TS2307), and the `.stsx` modules of workspace
packages have no shadow. `lumiose check` warns (`LUM6001`) when a used package has `.stsx` files that
the tsconfig's `rootDirs` leave out.

## The `JSX` namespace

| Type                                                        | Rule                                                                                                                                                    |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `JSX.Element`                                               | What JSX evaluates to: nodes, strings, numbers, booleans, `null`/`undefined`, arrays and functions of those.                                            |
| `JSX.ElementType`                                           | Intrinsic tags, and sync **or async** function components.                                                                                              |
| `JSX.IntrinsicElements`                                     | Every HTML (except `style`), SVG and MathML tag of lib.dom, plus custom elements (`my-widget`).                                                         |
| `JSX.IntrinsicAttributes`                                   | `key`, and on components `client:load`, `client:idle`, `client:visible` (`boolean \| string`), `client:media` (`string`), `client:only`.                |
| `JSX.ClassValue`                                            | `string \| false \| null \| undefined \| Record<string, boolean \| null \| undefined> \| ClassValue[]`.                                                 |
| `JSX.CSSProperties`                                         | Kebab-case CSS properties (`"font-weight"`, `"-webkit-line-clamp"`) and `--custom` properties; values `string \| number \| false \| null \| undefined`. |
| `JSX.EventHandler<E, T>`                                    | `(event: E & { currentTarget: T }) => void`.                                                                                                            |
| `JSX.Ref<T>`                                                | What `ref<T>()` returns: callable with the element, readable as `() => T \| undefined`.                                                                 |
| `JSX.HTMLProps<T>`, `JSX.SVGProps<T>`, `JSX.MathMLProps<T>` | Props of an element type, for wrappers.                                                                                                                 |

**Element props.** Every element accepts `children`, `class`, `style`, `ref`, `attach`, `innerHTML`,
`key`, its attributes, `onX` handlers and `on:x` listeners. `input` also accepts `bind:value`
(string or number signal) and `bind:checked` (boolean signal); `select` and `textarea` accept
`bind:value`.

**Rejected on purpose** (type errors with a hint): `className` (use `class`), `htmlFor` (use
`for`), camelCase `style` keys, exact-case or lowercase handlers (`onKeydown`, `onclick`), and
`<style>` in `.tsx` files.

**Event names.** `onX` handlers use React-style camelCase after `on` (`onClick`, `onKeyDown`,
`onDblClick`, `onPointerDown`, `onMouseEnter`); the DOM event is the suffix lowercased. Bubbling
events are delegated; non-bubbling ones (`focus`, `blur`, `mouseenter`, `mouseleave`,
`pointerenter`, `pointerleave`, `scroll`, `load`, `error`, media events) get a direct listener.
`on:name` adds a native listener with the exact name; any `on:${string}` is accepted for custom
events.

## Custom elements

Undeclared custom elements accept global attributes and any other attribute. Type one by
augmenting `IntrinsicElements`:

```tsx check
declare module "lumiose/jsx-runtime" {
  namespace JSX {
    interface IntrinsicElements {
      "rating-stars": JSX.HTMLProps<HTMLElement> & { value: number; max?: number };
    }
  }
}

export function Review() {
  return (
    <rating-stars
      value={4}
      on:rating-change={(event: CustomEvent<number>) => console.log(event.detail)}
    />
  );
}
```

A prop of a custom element goes to the element's property when the element defines one (not one
every element has, such as `id`), else to the attribute, as in React 19; `on:name` listens to the
event of that exact name. See [Web components](../guides/web-components.md).

## `lumiose/env`

```ts
interface ImportMetaEnv {
  readonly [publicVariable: `PUBLIC_${string}`]: string;
  BASE_URL: string;
  MODE: string;
  DEV: boolean;
  PROD: boolean;
  SSR: boolean;
}
declare module "lumiose" {
  interface Locals {}
}
declare module "*module.css" {
  // import styles from "./card.module.css": the hashed class of each name, class={styles.card}
  const classNames: { readonly [className: string]: string };
  export default classNames;
}
declare module "*.css" {} // import "./app.css": bundled into the page's CSS
declare module "*.css?url" {} // export default url: string
declare module "*.css?inline" {} // export default css: string
declare module "*.css?raw" {} // export default source: string
declare module "*.svg?component" {
  const Svg: (props: JSX.SVGProps<SVGSVGElement> & { title?: string }) => JSX.Element;
  export default Svg;
}
declare module "*.svg?url" {} // export default url: string
declare module "*.svg?raw" {} // export default raw: string
declare module "*.md" {
  const Content: () => JSX.Element;
  export default Content;
  export interface Frontmatter extends Record<string, unknown> {} // merge your fields into it
  export const frontmatter: Frontmatter;
  export interface Heading {
    depth: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6;
    text: string;
    id: string;
  } // read-only
  export const headings: ReadonlyArray<Heading>; // document order, ids of the rendered anchors
}
declare module "*.html" {
  const Content: () => JSX.Element;
  export default Content;
}
```

Declare known public variables by merging `interface ImportMetaEnv { readonly PUBLIC_API: string }`.
The built-in members match `vite/client`, so both can be loaded. `vite/client` types the other
asset imports, bare `.svg` URLs included (see [SVG imports](../concepts/svg.md)). TypeScript checks
side-effect imports (`noUncheckedSideEffectImports`), hence `*.css`. CSS modules (`*.module.css`)
are read-only class maps, with `lumiose/env` alone or with `vite/client` in either order: the
pattern is declared before `*.css`, which would otherwise match them first, and leaves out the dot
so that it does not merge with `vite/client`'s own `*.module.css` declaration (a duplicate default
export when `skipLibCheck` is off). See [Styles](../concepts/styles.md) for using them.

<!-- source: reference/cli.md -->

# CLI

> The `lumiose` command: every subcommand with its options, JSON output and exit codes.

The command comes with the `@lumiose/cli` package (`pnpm add -D @lumiose/cli`).

```sh
lumiose <command> [options]
lumiose <command> --help        # usage, options, exit codes and examples
lumiose help --format json      # every command, for agents
```

## Output contract

- **Exit codes:** `0` success, `1` problems found (errors, unformatted files, nothing found, a
  failed build, a server that could not start), `2` the tool itself failed or was misused (unknown
  command or option, missing tsconfig or oxlint, a project root that does not exist). Each
  command's `--help` lists its exit codes.
- **`--format json`:** stdout carries one JSON document, `{ "command": "<name>", "ok": <bool>, ... }`.
  `ok` is `true` exactly when the exit code is `0`. When the command could not do its job and no
  diagnostics explain why, `failure: { message, help? }` says so. Fields are only ever added.
  Usage errors are reported the same way (`lumiose chek --format json` prints `{ "command": "chek",
  "ok": false, "failure": {...}, "suggestions": ["check"] }`).
- **Logs** go to stderr with `--format json`, so stdout parses as JSON.
- **Typos** get suggestions: `lumiose chek` prints `Did you mean "lumiose check"?`.

| Option                   | Applies to   | Meaning                                                       |
| ------------------------ | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--root <dir>`, `--cwd`  | all          | Project root (default: the current directory).                |
| `--format human \| json` | all          | Output format (default `human`).                              |
| `-h, --help`             | all          | Help for the command.                                         |
| `-v, --version`          |              | The version (`{ command: "version", ok, version }` in JSON).  |
| `-p, --project <file>`   | check        | tsconfig path relative to the root (default `tsconfig.json`). |
| `--check`                | fmt          | List unformatted files and exit 1 instead of writing.         |
| `--port <n>`             | dev, preview | Port; `0` picks a free one.                                   |
| `--host <addr>`          | dev, preview | Listen address (`0.0.0.0`: all addresses).                    |

## lumiose dev

Starts the Vite dev server with SSR and HMR, until interrupted.

What an edit updates: a stylesheet or a file's `<style>` block updates in place; an edited
component in an island's own module re-renders its instances in place (the page, its scroll
position, the island's other components and the other islands keep their state; see
[hot updates](./vite.md)); an island module the compiler could not register re-renders the
island's instances from their props. An island module that other client modules import reloads
the page, since they would keep its old exports, and so does other client code (a module an
island or an SPA route imports).

Server-only code (pages, layouts and components that no island or SPA route imports, middleware,
the document) updates the page in place: the page fetches its URL again and patches its DOM to the
new HTML. Islands keep their DOM and state, and focus, scroll positions and form input survive; the
title, meta tags and stylesheets of the head follow the new page. The page reloads instead when
the new HTML changes the `<html>`, `<head>` or `<body>` attributes, adds or removes a script, or
changes an island's props, hydration strategy or slot content; when the response status changed,
redirected or is not HTML; when the page was the result of a form post; and when the render
reported errors (the reload shows the overlay).

```sh
lumiose dev --port 3000
lumiose dev --format json   # one line once listening: { "command": "dev", "ok": true, "url": "http://localhost:5173/", "urls": { "local": [...], "network": [...] } }
```

Every page gets the in-page inspector: Alt+Shift+L or the corner button opens it, and Alt+click
opens an element's source in your editor ([Dev tools](../concepts/dev-tools.md)).
`lumiose({ inspector: false })` turns it off.

Like Vite, the server stops when its stdin ends; start it with an open stdin when it runs in the
background. A project with its own Node server runs the same dev setup inside it with
[`createDevHandler()`](vite.md#createdevhandler).

## lumiose build

Builds the client and server bundles into `dist/`, then prerenders the `static` routes and the `spa`
pages with `prerender`. When every route is prerendered (no `server` route, no `spa` route rendered
per request, no form action), the build
removes `dist/server`: `dist/client` is the whole site, and `serverEntry` is `null`.
`lumiose({ headers })` is written to `dist/client/_headers`.
Route modules' chunks and stylesheets are named after their route folder, since every page is
`page.stsx`: `blog/[slug]/page.stsx` builds to `assets/blog-slug-page-[hash].js` (an `spa` page) and
`assets/blog-slug-page-[hash].css`, `(app)/layout.stsx` to `assets/app-layout-[hash].css`. A Vite
config that sets its own `entryFileNames`, `chunkFileNames` or `assetFileNames` keeps its names.
Servers and deploy adapters cache exactly the files the build named by content hash for a year;
files you put in `public/assets/` revalidate
([`@lumiose/adapter-node`](./adapter-node.md#createstatichandler)).

```sh
lumiose build --format json   # { outDir, clientDir, serverEntry, prerendered: [{ path, file, kind }] }
```

Route errors (`LUM5002`, `LUM5003`, `LUM5005`, `LUM5006`) and compile errors exit 1.

## lumiose preview

Serves the build output until interrupted. With `dist/server`, it serves it with
`@lumiose/adapter-node` (a dependency of the project), and the app runs with `NODE_ENV=production`
unless `NODE_ENV` is set. Without it (every route prerendered), it serves
`dist/client` as a static site, no adapter needed: page URLs map to `about/index.html` or
`about.html`, and unknown URLs get `404.html` with status 404, as static hosts do. Every response,
static files included, gets `lumiose({ headers })` and Vite's `preview.headers`, which default to
`server.headers` (as with `vite preview`)
([adapter `headers`](./adapter-node.md#createhandler)).
`--format json` prints one line once listening: `{ "command": "preview", "ok": true, "url" }`.

## lumiose check

Type-checks the project: runs typegen (`.lumiose/types/routes.d.ts`), writes shadow TSX files for
every `.stsx` (`.lumiose/shadow/`; also those of used Lumiose packages when the tsconfig extends
`.lumiose/tsconfig.generated.json`, as the template does, see
[tsconfig](./jsx.md#imports-outside-src-and-stsx-from-other-packages)), writes the generated
tsconfig, runs `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`, maps shadow positions back
to the `.stsx` sources (same line and UTF-16 column), and merges scanner, route, tsconfig and
compiler diagnostics for `.stsx` and `.tsx` files (such as `LUM1006` for a `<style>` block in a
`.tsx` file). For style diagnostics, the modules that `$` constants are imported from are resolved
like TypeScript resolves them (relative paths, tsconfig `paths`, package `exports`). Route
diagnostics use the project's default mode from `lumiose({ mode })`.

```sh
lumiose check
lumiose check --format json   # { command, ok, diagnostics: [...], summary: { errors, warnings, hints, files } }
```

Each JSON diagnostic has `source` (`ts`, `lumiose`, `oxlint`, `stylelint`), `code`, `severity`,
`file`, `line`, `column`, `endLine`, `endColumn`, `message`, and optional `help`, `docs` and
`fix`. A `fix` is `{ message, edits: [{ line, column, endLine, endColumn, text }] }`, with the same
positions as diagnostics; apply all its edits together.

TypeScript errors inside a raw-CSS `<style>` block of a `.tsx` file are dropped: `LUM1006` reports
the block, and renaming the file to `.stsx` removes them. TypeScript errors on an island call site
for a prop that cannot be serialized are reported as `LUM4002` on the prop (see
[LUM4002](../errors/LUM4002.md)). While the project has syntax errors, TypeScript reports no type
errors yet: the report then ends with a note (JSON: `notes: [...]`), and another run after the
fixes shows them.

## lumiose typegen

Writes the route types (`.lumiose/types/routes.d.ts`), the generated tsconfig
(`.lumiose/tsconfig.generated.json`) and syncs the shadow TSX files (`.lumiose/shadow/`), without
type-checking: what a bare `tsc` or an editor needs.

```sh
lumiose typegen --format json   # { routeTypes: { file, changed }, routes, shadows: { dir, files, written, deleted }, diagnostics, summary }
```

## lumiose routes

Lists the routes in match order, with their kind, mode (from the route, its layouts or the project
default `lumiose({ mode })`) and layouts. `spa (shell)` marks a `spa` page with `ssr = false`, and
`spa (prerendered)` a `spa` page rendered to HTML at build time, by its own `export const prerender`,
a layout's or `lumiose({ prerender })`.
With `lumiose({ i18n })`, the header names the locales and a `LOCALES` column lists the locales
each route declares (its own `locales` export, a layout's, or the default locale alone);
`locales() in <file>` marks a route whose `locales({ params })` function decides per params.
When the app has middleware, a `MIDDLEWARE` column shows each route's chain in the order it runs:
`src/middleware.ts`, then the folder `middleware.ts` files from the outermost folder in.

```sh
$ lumiose routes
Routes in src/routes (default mode: static): 2 pages, 1 endpoint

PATTERN        KIND      MODE    FILE                   LAYOUTS
/              page      static  page.stsx              layout.stsx
/api/search    endpoint  server  api/search/route.ts
/blog/[slug]   page      server  blog/[slug]/page.stsx  layout.stsx, blog/layout.stsx

$ lumiose routes   # with lumiose({ i18n })
Routes in src/routes (default mode: static, locales: en, es, fr (default en)): 3 pages, 0 endpoints

PATTERN       KIND  MODE    FILE                   LOCALES                             LAYOUTS
/             page  static  page.stsx              en, es, fr
/about        page  static  about/page.stsx        en, es
/blog/[slug]  page  static  blog/[slug]/page.stsx  locales() in blog/[slug]/page.stsx

$ lumiose routes   # with src/middleware.ts and src/routes/admin/middleware.ts
Routes in src/routes (default mode: server): 2 pages, 0 endpoints

PATTERN       KIND  MODE    FILE                   MIDDLEWARE                                LAYOUTS
/             page  server  page.stsx              src/middleware.ts                         layout.stsx
/admin/users  page  server  admin/users/page.stsx  src/middleware.ts > admin/middleware.ts  layout.stsx

$ lumiose routes --format json   # { routesDir, defaultMode, i18n?, routes: [{ pattern, file, kind, mode, ssr?, prerender?, layouts, middleware, params, locales?, localesFrom? }], diagnostics, summary }
```

Paths in JSON are project-relative. Exits 1 when the routes have errors.

## lumiose lint

Runs oxlint on the project, including `.stsx` files (through their shadow TSX, with diagnostics
inside style blocks dropped) and leaving out `node_modules` and `.lumiose`, and, when the project
installs and configures stylelint, on each
block's CSS with `$` references replaced by same-length identifiers. The JSON report has the shape
of `lumiose check`'s.

## lumiose fmt

```sh
lumiose fmt [paths...]        # default path: src
lumiose fmt --check
lumiose fmt --check --format json   # { check, files: [{ file, status, warnings, error? }], summary: { files, formatted, errors } }
```

Formats `.stsx` files: the TSX with oxfmt (each block replaced by a placeholder), then each block's
CSS separately with its `$` references protected, then re-indents and stitches the file together.
With `--check`, a `formatted` file is one that is not formatted yet.

## oxlint, ESLint and Prettier

Projects that run the tools themselves add Lumiose through plugins. The lint rules are thin
adapters over the compiler: they report its `LUMxxxx` diagnostics (with help, the docs topic and
fixes), so every tool agrees with `lumiose check`. Project-wide checks (`LUM4003`, `LUM3012`) and the
style diagnostics of `$` constants imported from other modules need the whole project: run
`lumiose check` for those.

**oxlint** (JS plugins, alpha in oxlint): lints `.tsx` files; oxlint cannot parse `.stsx` yet, so
`lumiose lint` covers those.

```json
// .oxlintrc.json
{
  "jsPlugins": ["@lumiose/eslint-plugin"],
  "rules": { "lumiose/compiler": "error", "lumiose/compiler-warnings": "warn" }
}
```

**ESLint 9** (flat config): the recommended config also lints `.stsx` files through a processor
that hands ESLint the masked TSX (same offsets, so positions and fixes apply to the source). Parse
TSX with a TypeScript parser, such as typescript-eslint's.

```js
// eslint.config.js
import lumiose from "@lumiose/eslint-plugin";
import tseslint from "typescript-eslint";

export default [
  ...lumiose.configs.recommended,
  { files: ["**/*.tsx", "**/*.stsx/*.tsx"], languageOptions: { parser: tseslint.parser } },
];
```

**Prettier**: `@lumiose/prettier-plugin` formats `.stsx` like `lumiose fmt` (the TSX and each block's
CSS with Prettier's printers, re-indented at their placement), following Prettier's options; a
file with scanner or syntax errors is reported, not changed. oxfmt has no plugin API, so
`lumiose fmt` remains the way to format `.stsx` with oxfmt.

```json
// .prettierrc.json
{ "plugins": ["@lumiose/prettier-plugin"] }
```

## lumiose docs

```sh
lumiose docs                  # the docs index
lumiose docs signals          # a topic by name...
lumiose docs concepts/signals # ...or by path
lumiose docs deploy           # a section's index (deploy/README), like errors
lumiose docs LUM2001          # a diagnostic page (also errors/LUM2001, diagnostics/LUM2001)
lumiose docs fetchJSON        # an exported name: its section of the API reference
lumiose docs bind:value       # no topic matches: search, best matches first
lumiose docs --format json    # { topics: [{ topic, title, summary }] }
lumiose docs signals --format json   # { topic, title, summary, related, content }
lumiose docs Link --format json      # { topic, heading, content }
lumiose docs "await island" --format json   # { query, results: [{ topic, title, score, snippet }] }
```

Prints the version-matched docs from `node_modules/lumiose/docs`. A bare name prefers concepts over
reference pages and lists the other matches. An exported name (case-sensitive, such as `signal`,
`Link` or `fail`) prints the section of the reference page that documents it. A search requires
every term to occur in a page.
Exits 1 when nothing matches.

## lumiose explain

```sh
lumiose explain LUM3010
lumiose explain lum3010 --format json   # { code, title, severity, category, topic, content }
```

Prints the long-form explanation of a diagnostic code: what it means, an example, and how to fix
it. Exits 1 for an unknown code and 2 for text that is not a code.

## lumiose agents init

```sh
lumiose agents init
lumiose agents init --mcp           # also .mcp.json (Claude Code) and .codex/config.toml (Codex)
lumiose agents init --format json   # { files: [{ file, action: "created" | "updated" | "unchanged" }] }
```

Makes an existing project agent-ready, as `create-lumiose` does for new ones: a Lumiose section in
`AGENTS.md` (between `<!-- lumiose:start … -->` and `<!-- lumiose:end -->`, pointing at
`node_modules/lumiose/docs`, the `.stsx` format, the key rules and `lumiose check`), a `CLAUDE.md`
that references `@AGENTS.md`, the `lumiose` skill (`.claude/skills/lumiose/SKILL.md`) and the
`*.stsx linguist-language=TSX` line in `.gitattributes`, and a `tsconfig.json` that extends
`.lumiose/tsconfig.generated.json` when the project has none (an existing one is left alone).
Re-running it updates only those parts. `--mcp` also registers `lumiose mcp` for Claude Code and
Codex, run with the package manager of the lockfile (see [MCP](mcp.md#register-it)); the JSON
report then has `mcp: { command, args, note }`.

## lumiose mcp

```sh
lumiose mcp
claude mcp add lumiose -- npx lumiose mcp   # register it with Claude Code
```

Starts the MCP server on stdio for coding agents: the tools `docs_search`, `docs_get`, `check`,
`routes`, `components`, `compile`, `render` and `dev_logs`, and the docs and the route manifest as
resources. It runs until the client disconnects. See [MCP server](mcp.md).

<!-- source: reference/mcp.md -->

# MCP server

> `lumiose mcp` serves your project to coding agents: version-matched docs, diagnostics with fixes, routes, compiler output and logs.

`lumiose mcp` starts a stdio MCP server for the project in the current directory (or `--root`). It
gives an agent the same answers as the CLI, as structured tool results, without parsing terminal
output. Related: [CLI](cli.md), [Compiler and diagnostics](../concepts/compiler.md).

## Register it

The agent starts the server itself. `create-lumiose --mcp` (new projects) and
`lumiose agents init --mcp` (existing ones) register it for both Claude Code and Codex, run with the
project's package manager (`npx lumiose mcp`, `pnpm exec lumiose mcp`, `yarn lumiose mcp` or
`bunx lumiose mcp`, from the lockfile):

- `.mcp.json`: the `lumiose` entry of `mcpServers` (Claude Code's project servers; it asks once
  before starting them). Other servers in the file are kept.
- `.codex/config.toml`: an `[mcp_servers.lumiose]` table. Codex reads project config only in
  trusted projects; otherwise register it with `codex mcp add` as below. The rest of the file is
  kept.

Or by hand, once in the project directory:

```sh
# Claude Code (add --scope project to write .mcp.json and share it with the team)
claude mcp add lumiose -- npx lumiose mcp

# Codex
codex mcp add lumiose -- npx lumiose mcp
```

Agents configured with a JSON file (Claude Code's `.mcp.json`, Cursor's `.cursor/mcp.json`):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "lumiose": { "command": "npx", "args": ["lumiose", "mcp"] }
  }
}
```

VS Code (`.vscode/mcp.json`):

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "lumiose": { "type": "stdio", "command": "npx", "args": ["lumiose", "mcp"] }
  }
}
```

The server runs until the agent disconnects. It exits with `2` when the project root does not
exist. stdout carries the protocol; console output of app code goes to stderr and to `dev_logs`.

## Tools

| Tool          | Input                                                 | Returns                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `docs_search` | `query`, `limit?` (10)                                | `{ query, results: [{ topic, title, summary, score, snippet }] }`, best first; every term must occur in a page.                                                                                                                                                              |
| `docs_get`    | `topic`                                               | The page as Markdown. A topic is a path (`concepts/signals`), a bare name (`signals`), a code (`LUM2001`) or `""` for the index. An exported name (`fetchJSON`) returns its reference section.                                                                               |
| `check`       | `files?`, `project?`                                  | `lumiose check` as `{ ok, summary, diagnostics, notes? }`. With `files`, only their diagnostics, and `projectSummary` for the whole project.                                                                                                                                 |
| `routes`      | none                                                  | `lumiose routes --format json`: `{ routesDir, defaultMode, i18n?, routes: [{ pattern, file, kind, mode, ssr?, prerender?, layouts, middleware, params, locales?, localesFrom? }], diagnostics, summary }`.                                                                   |
| `components`  | `file?`                                               | `{ files: [{ file, components, islands, fileScope, hasStyles, errors }] }` for one file, or for every `.stsx`/`.tsx` file under `src/`.                                                                                                                                      |
| `compile`     | `file?` or `source`, `target?` (`both`)               | `{ file, client: { code, css, cssDeps }, server: { code }, diagnostics }`: what the Vite plugin compiles, without source maps.                                                                                                                                               |
| `render`      | `path`, `method?`, `headers?`, `maxLength?`, `strip?` | `{ url, status, headers, body, truncated }` from an in-process dev server. Redirects are returned, not followed. `strip: true` returns only the visible markup of an HTML page (no scripts, styles, link/meta tags, templates, hydration comments or `data-l-*` attributes). |
| `dev_logs`    | `since?`, `level?`, `limit?` (100)                    | `{ available, entries: [{ id, time, level, source, message }] }`: the logs of the dev server that `render` started.                                                                                                                                                          |

- **Diagnostics** (`check`, `compile`, `components`) have the shape of `lumiose check --format json`:
  `source`, `code`, `severity`, `file`, 1-based `line`/`column`/`endLine`/`endColumn`, `message`,
  and optional `help`, `docs` (a topic for `docs_get`) and `fix`. A `fix` is
  `{ message, edits: [{ line, column, endLine, endColumn, text }] }`; apply all its edits together.
- **Components** list each component's `name`, `exported`, `async`, `location`, `props` and
  `styleScopes`. `props` is the first parameter as written (`{ parameter: "props: CardProps" }`),
  plus the `type` declaration when the props type is an interface or type alias of the same file;
  it is `null` for a component without props. `styleScopes` are the `data-l-*` attributes of the
  elements that hold `<style>` blocks. `islands` are the file's `client:*` call sites with their
  `ref`, `module`, `export` and `strategy`.
- **`compile`** takes the file's text from `source` when given (the file need not exist), and
  folds `$` constants imported from other modules like the build does.
- **`render`** starts the dev server on first use, on a free port of `127.0.0.1`, and keeps it
  running: later calls see file changes like `lumiose dev` does. Pages return their HTML; endpoints
  their response body. Render errors return the dev error page, and their details are in
  `dev_logs`.
- **`dev_logs`** returns `available: false` with an explanation until `render` started the dev
  server: the logs of a `lumiose dev` started in a terminal are not visible to the MCP server. Pass
  the last `id` you saw as `since` to read only newer entries; `level` is the minimum (`info`,
  `warn`, `error`); `source` is `vite` (the dev server and Lumiose's plugins) or `console` (app
  code).

## Resources

| URI                      | Content                                                             |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `lumiose://docs/<topic>` | Each docs page as Markdown, e.g. `lumiose://docs/concepts/signals`. |
| `lumiose://routes`       | The route manifest, as the `routes` tool returns it (JSON).         |

## Boundaries

- `render` requests the in-process dev server only: `path` must start with a single `/` (no
  absolute or `//host` URLs), so the request and its `headers` never reach another origin.
- `compile` and `components` read files inside the project root only, symlinks resolved: a path
