  that leaves the root (`../`, an absolute path elsewhere, a link pointing out) is refused.
- What the tools return (docs, source and compiled code, rendered HTML, response bodies, logs) is
  data from the project: an agent treats it as content to read, never as instructions. The
  server's instructions say so too.

## Workflow for agents

1. Look the feature up: `docs_search`, then `docs_get` (the docs match the installed version).
2. Make the change.
3. `check` and fix every error; `docs_get` with a diagnostic's `docs` topic explains it.
4. `render` the affected routes to see the HTML; `dev_logs` with `level: "warn"` shows problems.

<!-- source: reference/adapter-node.md -->

# `@lumiose/adapter-node`

> Serve a Lumiose build with Node: the static files first, then the app's streamed responses.

`lumiose preview` uses it, so a project that previews or deploys on Node depends on it. Concepts:
[Rendering modes](../concepts/rendering-modes.md) (build output), [Server](../concepts/server.md).

## createServer

```ts
function createServer(options?: ServerOptions): Promise<LumioseServer>;

interface ServerOptions extends HandlerOptions {
  /** Default: the `PORT` env variable, else 3000. `0` picks a free port. */
  port?: number;
  /** Default: the `HOST` env variable, else every address. */
  host?: string;
}

interface LumioseServer {
  readonly server: import("node:http").Server;
  /** The URL it listens on, e.g. `http://localhost:3000/` (with the app's `base`). */
  readonly url: string;
  close(): Promise<void>;
}
```

Loads the build and starts an HTTP server; resolves once it listens. A missing build fails with
"No build in dist … Run `lumiose build` first."

**`NODE_ENV`.** A build runs in production: `createServer` and `createHandler` set
`process.env.NODE_ENV` to `"production"` when it is unset, before they load the build, so the
app and every library it imports (many branch on `NODE_ENV`) see it from their first line. An
explicit value is kept (`NODE_ENV=staging node server.ts`). `dist/server/entry.js` does the same
when another server imports it directly.

## createHandler

```ts
function createHandler(options?: HandlerOptions): Promise<NodeHandler>;

interface HandlerOptions {
  /** The build output directory, holding `client/` and `server/entry.js`. Default: `dist`. */
  dir?: string | URL;
  /** The public origin (`https://example.com`) behind a proxy. Default: `ORIGIN`, else the request's. */
  origin?: string;
  /** `ctx.env` and `env()` of requests. Default: `process.env`. */
  env?: Readonly<Record<string, string | undefined>>;
  /** The app's unexpected errors, with the request. Default: `console.error`. */
  onError?: (error: unknown, request: Request) => void;
  /** Headers for every response; a response's own header of the same name wins. */
  headers?: import("node:http").OutgoingHttpHeaders;
  /** Compress responses for clients that accept brotli or gzip. Default: true. */
  compress?: boolean;
  /** Symbolic links in dist/client: follow them (warning about escapes) or "contain". */
  symlinks?: "follow" | "contain"; // default "follow"
}

type NodeHandler = (
  req: IncomingMessage,
  res: ServerResponse,
  next?: (error?: unknown) => void,
) => void;
```

The same request handling as a Node request listener, for your own `http.createServer` or as
connect/Express middleware (errors go to `next`). The app is the build's `createHandler()`
([server build](./server-entry.md#createhandler)); `ctx.platform.clientAddress` is the socket's
remote address (a proxy's, behind one). Set `origin` (or `ORIGIN`) when a proxy terminates
TLS or rewrites the host: request URLs, and the cross-site check of form posts, use it.

`onError` receives the app's unexpected errors (not `redirect()`, `notFound()` or
`error(status)`), as the build's `createHandler({ onError })` does; it replaces the default
`console.error`. `src/instrumentation.server.ts` runs with the build either way: its
`onRequestError` also receives them, with the route and phase
([Server](../concepts/server.md#instrumentation)).

`headers` go on every response, the static files (prerendered pages included) and the app's
alike: the place for headers that middleware cannot add to static files, such as
`Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy` and `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy` for a cross-origin isolated page.
They are set first, so a response's own header of the same name wins: a static file's
`cache-control`, a page's `response().setHeader()`, a middleware's response. `lumiose preview` passes
Vite's `preview.headers`, which default to `server.headers`. The build's `lumiose({ headers })`
([@lumiose/vite](./vite.md#lumiose)) apply too, by path, after these: prefer them, so dev, preview,
this adapter and static hosts send the same headers.

**Compression** is on by default. Static files are served from the `.br` and `.gz` copies that
`lumiose build` writes next to every text file of `dist/client` of at least 1 kB (brotli quality 11,
gzip level 9), so they cost no CPU per request. The app's own responses (pages, endpoints) with a
text content type (`text/*`, JSON, JavaScript, XML, SVG) are compressed on the fly: brotli at
quality 4, else gzip at level 6, as `Accept-Encoding` allows. Streamed pages stay streamed: the
compressor flushes whenever the render pauses, so the shell and each `<Suspense>` chunk reach the
browser as soon as they are rendered. Responses that are already encoded, below 1 kB with a known
length, `HEAD`, `204`/`304` or marked `Cache-Control: no-transform` are sent as they are; every
compressible response gets `Vary: Accept-Encoding`. Pass `compress: false` when a proxy or CDN in
front compresses, or to measure raw payloads.

**Compression and secrets (BREACH).** A compressed response's size can leak a secret it contains
(a CSRF token, a session value) when an attacker can make the victim's browser request pages that
also reflect attacker-chosen text, and can observe the sizes. Lumiose's form check uses the `Origin`
header, not a token in the page, so it is not exposed; for pages that render a secret next to
reflected input (a token in a form that also echoes a query parameter), send them with
`Cache-Control: no-transform` (`response().setHeader("cache-control", "private, no-transform")`),
which skips on-the-fly compression for that response, or turn compression off with
`compress: false`.

**Malformed requests** never reach the app and are not logged: a request target that is not a
path (`http://other/x`, `//host` is a path) or an invalid `Host` header gets `400`, `TRACE`/`TRACK`
`405`, `CONNECT` `501`. Request bodies are bounded by the app's limits (1 MB, 10 MB for
uploads, `lumiose({ limits })`; see [Security](../concepts/security.md)).

**Timeouts.** The server keeps Node's defaults (`headersTimeout` 60 s, `requestTimeout` 300 s,
`keepAliveTimeout` 5 s), which bound slow clients. On the open internet, put a reverse proxy
(nginx, Caddy, a load balancer) in front for TLS, connection limits and tighter timeouts, or set
them on `createServer(…).server` (`server.requestTimeout = 30_000`).

## createStaticHandler

```ts
function createStaticHandler(
  dir: string,
  config: BuiltAppConfig,
  options?: StaticOptions,
): StaticHandler;
type StaticHandler = (req: IncomingMessage, res: ServerResponse) => Promise<boolean>;
interface StaticOptions {
  /** Serve the precompressed `.br`/`.gz` copies to clients that accept them. Default: true. */
  compress?: boolean;
  /** Follow symbolic links that leave `dir` (with a warning), or "contain" them. */
  symlinks?: "follow" | "contain"; // default "follow"
}
```

Serves `GET` and `HEAD` requests below the app's `base` from `dir` (the build's `client/`), and
resolves `false` when no file answers. The files the build named by content hash (Vite's
`name-[hash].ext` in the assets directory) are cached for a year
(`immutable`); everything else, files you put in `public/assets/` included, revalidates with `ETag`
and `Last-Modified` (`304`). Page URLs
follow the build's `trailingSlash`: `/about` serves `about/index.html` (`"ignore"`), redirects to
`/about/` (`"always"`), or serves `about.html` (`"never"`, which redirects `/about/`). Paths with
`..` or dot files (other than `.well-known`) are never served. `config` is the build entry's
`config` export. With `compress`, a client that accepts brotli (else gzip) gets the file's `.br`
(else `.gz`) copy when the build wrote one, with `Content-Encoding` and `Vary: Accept-Encoding`.
`dir` is indexed once, when the handler is created: a build output does not change while it is
served, and requests no file answers (every page) cost no file system call. Files written into
`dir` later are not served until the server restarts. An entry that cannot be read is skipped with a
warning. Symbolic links are followed (as serve-static and nginx do); links that lead outside `dir`
are listed in a warning at startup, and `symlinks: "contain"` leaves them out.
`_headers` (rules for static hosts) and the `.br`/`.gz` copies are not served as files of their own.

## Example

```ts
// server.ts: run with `node server.ts` after `lumiose build`
import { createServer } from "@lumiose/adapter-node";

const app = await createServer({
  port: 8080,
  headers: {
    "cross-origin-opener-policy": "same-origin",
    "cross-origin-embedder-policy": "require-corp",
  },
});
console.log(`Listening on ${app.url}`);
```

One `server.ts` for dev and production, with
[`createDevHandler()`](vite.md#createdevhandler) from `@lumiose/vite/dev` in dev (HMR, the error
overlay) and the build here otherwise:

```ts
// server.ts: `node server.ts --dev`, or `node server.ts` after `lumiose build`
import { createServer } from "node:http";
import { createHandler } from "@lumiose/adapter-node";

const dev = process.argv.includes("--dev");
const server = createServer();
// @lumiose/vite is a dev dependency: production never loads it.
const handler = dev
  ? await (await import("@lumiose/vite/dev")).createDevHandler({ server })
  : await createHandler();
server.on("request", handler);
server.listen(Number(process.env.PORT ?? 3000));
```

As middleware in an existing server:

```ts
import { createHandler } from "@lumiose/adapter-node";
import express from "express";

const server = express();
server.use(await createHandler({ dir: new URL("./dist", import.meta.url) }));
server.listen(3000);
```

<!-- source: reference/server-entry.md -->

# Server build (`dist/server/entry.js`)

> What `lumiose build` writes for servers: one web-standard fetch handler for pages, endpoints, actions and static files.

Concepts: [Rendering modes](../concepts/rendering-modes.md) (the build), [Server](../concepts/server.md)
(the request context). For Node, use [`@lumiose/adapter-node`](adapter-node.md).

## default export

```ts
declare const handler: {
  fetch(request: Request, platform?: Partial<Platform>): Promise<Response>;
};
export default handler;
```

A request goes through, in order:

1. **Static files** (`GET` and `HEAD` below Vite's `base`): the files of `dist/client`, with the
   same rules as `@lumiose/adapter-node`: prerendered pages by URL (`/about` serves
   `about/index.html`, or `about.html` with `trailingSlash: "never"`, and the `"always"`/`"never"`
   policies redirect with `308`), the `.br`/`.gz` copies the build wrote for clients that accept
   them (`Vary: Accept-Encoding`), a year of caching (`immutable`) for content-hashed assets and
   revalidation (`ETag`, `Last-Modified`, `304`) for everything else. Dot files (other than
   `.well-known`), `..` and `_headers` are never served. The directory is read with `node:fs` and
   indexed on the first request: files added later are not served until a restart.
2. **The app**: endpoints, form actions and pages, rendered shell first and streamed
   (`<Suspense>`). The request's `signal` aborts the render when the client goes away. Bodies are
   bounded by `lumiose({ limits })` (`413`).
3. **Headers**: `lumiose({ headers })` for the path, and Lumiose's defaults
   (`X-Content-Type-Options`, `Referrer-Policy`), go on every response that does not set them
   itself.

It does not compress the app's responses on the fly (static files use their precompressed
copies): put a CDN or proxy that compresses in front. On Node, `@lumiose/adapter-node` compresses.

The function works detached (`const { fetch } = handler`). Builds made with a deploy adapter
(Cloudflare, Vercel, Netlify) leave the static files to the platform, which serves `dist/client`
before calling the function.

## platform

```ts
interface Platform {
  /** The platform's bindings (Cloudflare's env); {} where there are none. */
  readonly env: PlatformEnv;
  /** Keeps the host running `promise` after the response; elsewhere it just runs. */
  waitUntil(promise: Promise<unknown>): void;
  /** The client's IP address as the host sees it (a proxy's, behind one). */
  readonly clientAddress: string | undefined;
}
interface PlatformEnv {} // augment: declare module "lumiose" { interface PlatformEnv { … } }
```

The second argument becomes `ctx.platform` in middleware, endpoints and actions
([Server](../concepts/server.md)). Every field has a fallback: `env` is `{}`, `waitUntil` lets the
promise run and reports a rejection like any server error, `clientAddress` is `undefined`.
Server environment variables stay in `ctx.env` and `env(name)`.

What each host passes:

| Host                                   | `env`         | `waitUntil`     | `clientAddress`             |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------- | --------------- | --------------------------- |
| `@lumiose/adapter-node`, `lumiose dev` | `{}`          | fallback        | the socket's remote address |
| Bun (`Bun.serve` passes its server)    | `{}`          | fallback        | `server.requestIP(request)` |
| Deno (`deno serve` passes its info)    | `{}`          | fallback        | `info.remoteAddr.hostname`  |
| workerd (`fetch(request, env, ctx)`)   | the bindings  | `ctx.waitUntil` | `CF-Connecting-IP`          |
| Your own server                        | what you pass | what you pass   | what you pass               |

Behind a reverse proxy, `clientAddress` is the proxy's: read the header your proxy sets
(`X-Forwarded-For`, `X-Real-IP`) in middleware if you trust it.

Type your platform's bindings by augmenting `PlatformEnv`:

```ts
// src/env.d.ts
declare module "lumiose" {
  interface PlatformEnv {
    DB: D1Database; // Cloudflare D1, typed by @cloudflare/workers-types
  }
}
export {};
```

## createHandler

```ts
export function createHandler(options?: {
  /** ctx.env and env(). Default: process.env. */
  env?: Readonly<Record<string, string | undefined>>;
  /** Unexpected errors (not redirect(), notFound() or error(status)). Default: console.error. */
  onError?: (error: unknown, request: Request) => void;
}): { fetch(request: Request, platform?: Partial<Platform>): Promise<Response> };
```

The app alone: no static files and no `lumiose({ headers })`. `@lumiose/adapter-node` uses it
behind its own static file server.

`onError` is the host's log. With a [`src/instrumentation.server.ts`](../concepts/server.md#instrumentation),
the build bundles it into the server entry: every handler (the default export, `createHandler()`,
the adapters') runs its `register()` before the first request, once per server instance, and its
`onRequestError()` receives the same errors with the route and the phase, after `onError`.
Prerendering at build time does not load it.

## config

```ts
export const config: {
  base: string; // Vite's base, with slashes: "/" or "/docs/"
  trailingSlash: "ignore" | "always" | "never";
  assetsDir: string; // "assets": content-hashed files
  headers?: HeadersOption; // lumiose({ headers })
};
```

What servers of `dist/client` need to know about the build.

## Run it

Build first (`lumiose build`), then start the entry from the project directory, so that the npm
dependencies it imports resolve from `node_modules`.

**Bun** starts a server for a module whose default export has `fetch`
(`PORT`, default 3000):

```sh
NODE_ENV=production PORT=3000 bun dist/server/entry.js
```

**Deno** serves it with `deno serve` (`--port`, default 8000). It reads `dist/client` and the
environment:

```sh
deno serve --allow-net --allow-read --allow-env --port 3000 dist/server/entry.js
```

**Node**: use [`@lumiose/adapter-node`](adapter-node.md) (`createServer()`), which adds on-the-fly
compression and Node's streaming. Any server that takes a fetch handler works too:

```ts
// server.ts, with Hono's Node server: `node server.ts`
import { serve } from "@hono/node-server";
import handler from "./dist/server/entry.js";

serve({ fetch: (request) => handler.fetch(request), port: 3000 });
```

For Cloudflare, Vercel, Netlify, static hosts and the rest, see the
[deploy guides](../deploy/README.md).

## Example

Using the platform in an endpoint: record a visit after the response, without delaying it.

```ts check
import type { Endpoint } from "lumiose";

export const POST: Endpoint = (ctx) => {
  const visitor = ctx.platform.clientAddress ?? "unknown";
  ctx.platform.waitUntil(
    fetch("https://analytics.example.com/hit", { method: "POST", body: visitor }),
  );
  return new Response(null, { status: 204 });
};
```

<!-- source: reference/query.md -->

# `@lumiose/query`

> TanStack Query for Lumiose, with Solid Query's API and results in reactive stores.

An optional package, not part of `lumiose`: install it with `pnpm add @lumiose/query`. It is a thin
adapter. Caching, deduplication, retries, stale times, invalidation and refetching on focus or
reconnect come from `@tanstack/query-core`, so the [TanStack Query docs](https://tanstack.com/query/latest/docs/framework/solid/overview)
apply as written. Concepts: [Signals and reactivity](../concepts/signals.md),
[Data and actions](../concepts/data-and-actions.md).

## When to use it

Lumiose reads data without a library: async components `await` it, [`fetchJSON`](app.md#fetchjson)
fetches JSON, and `invalidate()` and `submit()` refresh what a page shows. Those awaits are cached:
[`fetchJSON`](app.md#fetchjson) by URL and [`query(key, fn)`](app.md#query) by key, deduplicated,
stale-while-revalidate, invalidated by URL or key prefix, and sent from the server to islands with
the page. Prefer the built-in primitives when:

- data is read by async components and refreshed by form actions or `invalidate(target)`,
- pages render on the server (`@lumiose/query` does not fetch there, see [Server rendering](#server-rendering)).

Use `@lumiose/query` for client-side data (`spa` routes and islands) that needs what a client cache
gives you:

- many components reading the same data, fetched once and kept in sync,
- polling (`refetchInterval`), refetching on window focus and reconnect, per-query `staleTime`,
- retries, pagination with `placeholderData: keepPreviousData`, dependent queries (`enabled`),
- mutations with optimistic updates and rollback (`onMutate`, `onError`),
- a team or code that already knows TanStack Query.

## QueryClientProvider

```ts
function QueryClientProvider(props: { client: QueryClient; children?: JSX.Element }): JSX.Element;
```

Provides `client` to everything rendered inside it, through a context. Once mounted it calls `client.mount()`, which refetches on window focus and reconnect and resumes
paused mutations, and `client.unmount()` when it is disposed. A client is usually created once, at
module scope:

```tsx
import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from "@lumiose/query";

const queryClient = new QueryClient();

export default function App() {
  return (
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
      <Books />
    </QueryClientProvider>
  );
}
```

Islands start a new root and do not see context provided outside them: wrap each island that uses
queries in its own provider. Pass the same module-scope client to share one cache between islands.

## useQueryClient

```ts
function useQueryClient(queryClient?: QueryClient): QueryClient;
```

`queryClient` if given, else the client of the nearest `QueryClientProvider`. Throws "No
QueryClient set, use QueryClientProvider to set one" when there is none. Call it while the
component sets up, and use the client later (`client.invalidateQueries(...)` in a handler).

## useQuery

```ts
function useQuery<TQueryFnData, TError, TData, TQueryKey>(
  options: () => QueryOptions<TQueryFnData, TError, TData, TQueryKey>,
  queryClient?: () => QueryClient,
): UseQueryResult<TData, TError>;
```

Subscribes to a query. `options` takes every [`QueryObserverOptions`](https://tanstack.com/query/latest/docs/reference/QueryObserver)
field except `structuralSharing`, plus `reconcile` (below). It is an accessor: when a signal it
reads changes, such as a part of the key or `enabled`, the query switches to the new options.

```tsx
function Book(props: { id: number }) {
  const book = useQuery(() => ({
    queryKey: ["book", props.id],
    queryFn: () => fetchJSON<Book>(`/api/books/${props.id}`),
  }));
  return (
    <article>
      {book.isPending ? (
        <p>Loading…</p>
      ) : book.isError ? (
        <p>{book.error.message}</p>
      ) : (
        <h2>{book.data.title}</h2>
      )}
      {book.isFetching && <small>Refreshing…</small>}
    </article>
  );
}
```

The result is a [store](reactivity.md#store) with the fields of TanStack's `QueryObserverResult`
(`data`, `error`, `status`, `isPending`, `isFetching`, `refetch`, …). Read fields where they are
used, as with any store: destructuring (`const { data } = book`) reads once and loses updates.

- **Structural sharing through `reconcile`.** A new `data` is written into the store with
  [`reconcile()`](reactivity.md#reconcile): array items are matched by `id`, unchanged objects keep
  their identity, and only the fields that changed notify. List rows and effects that read an
  unchanged item do not re-run after a refetch. `reconcile: "slug"` matches by another key;
  `reconcile: false` stores `data` as the cache holds it (replaced on each change);
  `reconcile: (old, next) => data` decides. query-core's own `structuralSharing` is turned off.
- **The store holds a copy of `data`.** The cache's object is shared by every observer of the
  query, and a store writes into the object it wraps. Writing to `book.data` therefore changes
  this component only: update the cache with `client.setQueryData()`.
- **Lifetime.** The observer subscribes after the component mounts, so the fetch starts then, and
  it unsubscribes when the component (its owner) is disposed. What `queryFn` reads is not tracked.
- Two `useQuery` calls with the same key share one fetch and one cache entry.

## useMutation

```ts
function useMutation<TData, TError, TVariables, TOnMutateResult>(
  options: () => MutationOptions<TData, TError, TVariables, TOnMutateResult>,
  queryClient?: () => QueryClient,
): UseMutationResult<TData, TError, TVariables, TOnMutateResult>;
```

A mutation. The result is a store with TanStack's `MutationObserverResult` fields (`status`,
`isPending`, `data`, `error`, `variables`, `reset`, …), plus:

- `mutate(variables, { onSuccess, onError, onSettled }?)`: runs `mutationFn`. It never rejects;
  errors go to `error` and the callbacks.
- `mutateAsync(variables, callbacks?)`: the same, as a promise that rejects on error.

```tsx
function AddBook() {
  const client = useQueryClient();
  const add = useMutation(() => ({
    mutationFn: (title: string) =>
      fetchJSON<Book>("/api/books", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify({ title }) }),
    onSuccess: () => client.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ["books"] }),
  }));
  return (
    <button disabled={add.isPending} onClick={() => add.mutate("Dune")}>
      {add.isPending ? "Adding…" : "Add"}
    </button>
  );
}
```

## Re-exports

Everything `@tanstack/query-core` exports is re-exported, as by `@tanstack/solid-query`:
`QueryClient`, `QueryCache`, `MutationCache`, `skipToken`, `keepPreviousData`, `hashKey`, its types,
and so on. The adapter's own types: `QueryOptions`, `UseQueryOptions`, `UseQueryResult`,
`DefinedUseQueryResult`, `UndefinedInitialDataOptions`, `DefinedInitialDataOptions`,
`MutationOptions`, `UseMutationOptions`, `UseMutationResult`, `UseMutateFunction`,
`UseMutateAsyncFunction` and `QueryClientProviderProps`. With `initialData`,
`useQuery`'s result is typed `DefinedUseQueryResult`: `data` is never `undefined`.

## Server rendering

Browser first: SPA routes and islands. In a server render, effects never run, so queries do not
subscribe and never fetch. `useQuery` shows what the client's cache already holds, otherwise the
pending state, and `QueryClientProvider` does not mount the client.

- Render the same thing on the server and in the browser's first render. With an empty cache on
  both sides, both render the pending state and the island fetches once it hydrates.
- A module-scope client on the server is shared by every request. Create one per request, or
  render only the pending state on the server.

Dehydrating the server's cache into the page (TanStack's `dehydrate`/`hydrate`) is not supported
yet.

## Not supported yet

- `<Suspense>`: queries do not suspend, and the `suspense` option has no effect. Render
  `isPending` instead.
- `throwOnError`: errors stay in the result instead of reaching an `<ErrorBoundary>`.
- `useQueries`, `useInfiniteQuery`, `useIsFetching`, `useIsMutating`, `useMutationState` and
  `queryOptions()`. The observers they wrap (`QueriesObserver`, `InfiniteQueryObserver`) are
  re-exported from query-core.

# LUM1001: Syntax error

**Severity:** error · **Category:** file format (1xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> The file is not valid TSX after its `<style>` blocks are masked.

**Reported by:** the compiler (Vite plugin, language server).

## What it means

The compiler could not parse the module. Lumiose masks `<style>` blocks first, so the error is in
the TSX itself: a missing bracket, an unterminated string, a stray `<` in JSX text, or TypeScript
syntax that OXC does not accept.

## Example

```tsx
export function Price() {
  return <p>Total: {total</p>;
}
```

## How to fix it

Fix the syntax at the reported span. The message comes from the parser and names what it
expected. If the error points into a `<style>` block, check that the block is closed (`LUM1004`)
and that `<style` is not part of an expression.

## Related

- [Compiler and diagnostics](../concepts/compiler.md)
- [JSX](../concepts/jsx.md)

# LUM1002: Unsupported by this compiler version

**Severity:** error · **Category:** file format (1xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> The code uses a construct or target that this compiler version does not support yet.

**Reported by:** the compiler.

## What it means

The construct parses, but this version of the Lumiose compiler cannot compile it, or the requested
compile target is not available. The message names the construct.

## How to fix it

Rewrite the code with a supported construct (the message suggests one when there is an obvious
alternative), or upgrade `lumiose`. If you believe the construct should be supported, report it with
the smallest file that triggers the diagnostic.

## Related

- [Compiler and diagnostics](../concepts/compiler.md)

# LUM1003: Scanner ambiguity

**Severity:** warning · **Category:** file format (1xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> The scanner read text in a way that may not be what you meant: a `<style` taken as a comparison, or blocks hidden by an unterminated string or comment.

**Reported by:** the scanner (compiler, `lumiose check`, language server). A warning.

## What it means

The `.stsx` scanner tracks JS, JSX, strings, template literals, comments and regular expressions to
find `<style>` blocks. Two situations are ambiguous, and the scanner reports which reading it took:

- `<style` right after an expression (`const a = b <style>`) is read as a `<` comparison, not as
  a block.
- An unterminated string, template literal or comment hides every `<style>` block after it.

## Example

```stsx
const a = b <style>
  .x { color: red; }
</style>
```

On the same line as an expression, `<style` continues the expression `b`.

## How to fix it

Start a top-level block on its own line (a `<style` at the start of a line at top level is
always a block), conventionally at the end of the file. For the second case, close the string, template
literal or comment that the message points to.

## Related

- [Styles](../concepts/styles.md)
- [Compiler and diagnostics](../concepts/compiler.md)

<!-- source: errors/LUM1004.md -->

<!-- Generated from crates/lumiose_compiler/src/diagnostics/registry.rs by packages/lumiose/scripts/gen-error-docs.ts. Edit the explanation below the end marker. -->

# LUM1004: Unclosed `<style>` block

**Severity:** error · **Category:** file format (1xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> A `<style>` block has no closing `</style>`.

**Reported by:** the scanner (compiler, `lumiose check`, language server).

## What it means

Block content runs up to the first `</style>`. Without one, the rest of the file would be CSS, so
the scanner stops and reports the block.

## Example

```stsx
export function Card() {
  return (
    <div class="card">
      <style>
        .card { padding: 1rem; }
    </div>
  );
}
```

## How to fix it

Close the block with `</style>` before the end of its parent element. A self-closing
`<style />` is not a block.

## Related

- [Styles](../concepts/styles.md)

<!-- source: errors/LUM1005.md -->

<!-- Generated from crates/lumiose_compiler/src/diagnostics/registry.rs by packages/lumiose/scripts/gen-error-docs.ts. Edit the explanation below the end marker. -->

# LUM1005: Unknown `<style>` attribute

**Severity:** error · **Category:** file format (1xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> A `<style>` block has an attribute other than `global`.

**Reported by:** the scanner (compiler, `lumiose check`, language server).

## What it means

Blocks are plain CSS scoped by placement. The only allowed attribute is `global`, which makes the
block unscoped. `lang`, `media`, `scoped`, `type` and others are not supported: there is no Sass
inside `<style>`, and media queries go inside the CSS.

## Example

```stsx
<style lang="scss">
  .card { .title { color: red; } }
</style>
```

## How to fix it

Remove the attribute. Use `@media` inside the block instead of `media=""`, CSS nesting instead of
Sass, or import a `.scss` file through Vite. For app-wide CSS, write `<style global>`.

## Related

- [Styles](../concepts/styles.md)

<!-- source: errors/LUM1006.md -->

<!-- Generated from crates/lumiose_compiler/src/diagnostics/registry.rs by packages/lumiose/scripts/gen-error-docs.ts. Edit the explanation below the end marker. -->

# LUM1006: Raw CSS in a `.tsx` file

**Severity:** error · **Category:** file format (1xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> A `.tsx` file contains a raw-CSS `<style>` block.

**Reported by:** the scanner (compiler, `lumiose check`).

## What it means

Raw CSS blocks are the one syntax addition of `.stsx` files. In a `.tsx` file, TypeScript and other
tools would read the CSS as JSX, so it is rejected (the JSX types also omit `style` from
intrinsic elements in `.tsx`).

## Example

```tsx
// Card.tsx
export function Card() {
  return (
    <div class="card">
      <style>.card { padding: 1rem; }</style>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## How to fix it

Rename the file to `.stsx` and update its imports (`./Card.stsx`).

## Related

- [Components: file types](../concepts/components.md)
- [Styles](../concepts/styles.md)

<!-- source: errors/LUM1007.md -->

<!-- Generated from crates/lumiose_compiler/src/diagnostics/registry.rs by packages/lumiose/scripts/gen-error-docs.ts. Edit the explanation below the end marker. -->

# LUM1007: `await using` in a component

**Severity:** error · **Category:** file format (1xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> A component body uses `await using`.

**Reported by:** the compiler.

## What it means

The compiler rewrites component-level `await` to restore the owner, context and tracking after
each await. `await using` (explicit resource management) needs disposal at scope exit, which this
rewrite does not support in v1.

## Example

```tsx
export async function Report() {
  await using db = await openConnection();
  return <p>{await db.count()}</p>;
}
```

## How to fix it

Acquire and release the resource inside a helper function, which the rewrite leaves alone, and
await that:

```tsx
async function loadCount() {
  await using db = await openConnection();
  return db.count();
}

export async function Report() {
  const count = await loadCount();
  return <p>{count}</p>;
}
```

## Related

- [Async components](../concepts/async.md)

# LUM1008: `<script>` in a Markdown file

**Severity:** error · **Category:** file format (1xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> A Markdown file imported as a component contains a `<script>` element.

**Reported by:** the Vite plugin (`lumiose({ md })`), in `lumiose dev` and builds, at the `<script>`
tag's line.

## What it means

Markdown imports are content only: the component renders the file's text and markup, and nothing
in it runs. Raw HTML is allowed in Markdown, but `<script>` is not, whatever its `type` (a module,
a classic script, JSON-LD). Only `.html` imports run their scripts. Script tags inside code spans,
fenced or indented code blocks and HTML comments are text, and are fine.

## Example

```md
# Counter

<button id="count">0</button>

<script type="module">
  document.querySelector("#count").onclick = (e) => e.target.textContent++;
</script>
```

## How to fix it

Move the markup and its script to an `.html` file, which runs its scripts as client modules, and
import that instead (or import it next to the Markdown):

```html
<!-- src/content/counter.html -->
<button id="count">0</button>
<script type="module">
  document.querySelector("#count").onclick = (e) => e.target.textContent++;
</script>
```

Or keep the Markdown as content and put the behaviour in a component that renders it, such as an
island in a `.stsx` route:

```stsx
import Post from "../content/post.md";
import { Counter } from "../components/counter.stsx";

export default function Page() {
  return (
    <article>
      <Post />
      <Counter client:load />
    </article>
  );
}
```

## Related

- [Markdown and HTML imports](../concepts/content.md)
- [Islands](../concepts/islands.md)

# LUM1009: Content nested too deeply

**Severity:** error · **Category:** file format (1xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> A Markdown or HTML import nests elements or block quotes deeper than 512 levels.

**Reported by:** the Vite plugin (`lumiose({ md, html })`), in `lumiose dev` and builds, at the first
element or line past the limit.

## What it means

The HTML tree builder and the Markdown block parser get slower with every level of nesting, and
a file with tens of thousands of unclosed `<div>`s or `>` markers would take seconds to compile
(or stall the dev server on every save). No real document nests this deep, so Lumiose checks the
depth before parsing and stops at 512 levels: elements that are opened and never closed, or block
quote markers on one line. Elements whose end tag is optional (`<p>`, `<li>`, `<td>`…), void
elements and self-closing tags do not count. The component is empty until the file is fixed.

## Example

```html
<!-- generated markup that never closes its wrappers -->
<div>
  <div>
    <div>
      <div><div>…</div></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

## How to fix it

Close the elements you open, or generate flatter markup. For a quote of a quote of a quote, a few
levels are plenty.

## Related

- [Markdown and HTML imports](../concepts/content.md)
- [Security](../concepts/security.md)

<!-- source: errors/LUM1010.md -->

<!-- Generated from crates/lumiose_compiler/src/diagnostics/registry.rs by packages/lumiose/scripts/gen-error-docs.ts. Edit the explanation below the end marker. -->

# LUM1010: Source nested too deeply

**Severity:** error · **Category:** file format (1xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> Brackets in a `.stsx`/`.tsx` file are nested more than 1000 levels deep, so the compiler refuses the file.

**Reported by:** the compiler, in `@lumiose/vite`, `lumiose check` and the language server. An error.

## What it means

Parentheses, brackets, braces and template substitutions (`${…}`) are counted while the file is
read; strings and comments do not count. Past 1000 open levels the file is not compiled: the
compiler's passes recurse once per level, and a file nested tens of thousands of levels deep would
exhaust the stack of the process that compiles it (the dev server, the language server). Real code
stays far below the limit; generated code (a serialized tree, a minified data blob) may not.

## Example

```ts
// Generated: 5000 nested arrays.
export const tree = [[[[[[/* … */]]]]]];
```

## How to fix it

Split the expression into named parts, or load deeply nested data as JSON (`import data from
"./tree.json"`, or `fetch`) instead of writing it as code.

## Related

- [LUM1001](LUM1001.md): syntax error.

<!-- source: errors/LUM2001.md -->

<!-- Generated from crates/lumiose_compiler/src/diagnostics/registry.rs by packages/lumiose/scripts/gen-error-docs.ts. Edit the explanation below the end marker. -->

# LUM2001: Stale derived value

**Severity:** warning · **Category:** reactivity (2xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> A value derived from a signal is computed once in setup and never updates.

**Reported by:** the compiler. A warning. Does not apply to async components, whose body re-runs.

## What it means

A component's body runs once. `const doubled = count() * 2` reads the signal at setup time and
stores a number, so JSX that uses `doubled` shows the first value forever.

The compiler treats a zero-argument call of a local or imported binding (`count()`,
`user.name()`) as a signal read, and so does a read of the component's props. Calls that can only
run on the server are not reads, so server pages can store request data in constants:

- `lumiose`'s request APIs: `url()`, `params()`, `locals()`, `cookies()`, `request()`,
  `response()` and `publicEnv()`. Inside SPA routes, `url()` and `params()` from `lumiose/router`
  are reactive and still count.
- `lumiose`'s control-flow APIs, which never return: `notFound()`, `redirect()` and `error()`, so
  `const project = getProject(slug) ?? notFound()` is fine.
- Anything imported from a server-only module (`*.server.ts`, `src/server/**`), such as
  `queries().getBook(isbn)`. Data functions from a workspace package (`getDashboard()` from
  `@acme/data`) are not known to be server-only: re-export them from a module under
  `src/server/` (`export { getDashboard } from "@acme/data";`) and import them from there.

```tsx
// src/routes/books/[isbn]/page.stsx (a server page): no warning
const user = locals().user ?? null;
const next = url().searchParams.get("next");
const featured = queries().featuredBooks(6);
```

Pages and layouts whose route mode is `static` or `server` render once per request (or build), so
their own props are plain values too: deriving from them is fine. Routes in `spa` mode, islands
and other components re-render with new props and still get the warning. `@lumiose/vite`,
`lumiose check` and the language server read the route modes the same way (`export const mode`,
the nearest layout's, then `lumiose({ mode })`).

```tsx
// src/routes/books/[slug]/page.stsx (mode `static` or `server`): no warning
export default function Book(props: { params: { slug: string } }) {
  const title = props.params.slug.replaceAll("-", " ");
  return <h1>{title}</h1>;
}
```

## Example

```tsx
export function Counter() {
  const count = signal(1);
  const doubled = count() * 2;
  return <button onClick={() => count.update((n) => n + 1)}>{doubled}</button>;
}
```

## How to fix it

Derive with a function or `computed`, and call it where you need the value:

```tsx
const doubled = () => count() * 2; // cheap derivations
const total = computed(() => expensive(count())); // cached
return <button>{doubled()}</button>;
```

If you really want the initial value only, read it with `count.peek()` or `untrack(count)` to make
that explicit.

## Related

- [Signals and reactivity](../concepts/signals.md)
- [Components](../concepts/components.md)

<!-- Generated from crates/lumiose_compiler/src/diagnostics/registry.rs by packages/lumiose/scripts/gen-error-docs.ts. Edit the explanation below the end marker. -->

# LUM2002: Signal write during render

**Severity:** error · **Category:** reactivity (2xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> A signal is written while a component or computed is rendering.

**Reported by:** the compiler.

## What it means

Component setup and computeds run during render. Writing a signal there (`count.set(…)`,
`items.push(…)` on a store) re-triggers bindings mid-render, can loop, and makes the output depend
on render order.

## Example

```tsx
export function Profile(props: { name: string }) {
  const visits = signal(0);
  visits.set(visits.peek() + 1);
  return <p>{props.name}</p>;
}
```

## How to fix it

Initialize the signal with the value instead (`signal(initial)`), derive with `computed`, or write
in an event handler, `onMount` or an `effect`.

## Related

- [Signals and reactivity](../concepts/signals.md)

<!-- source: errors/LUM2003.md -->

<!-- Generated from crates/lumiose_compiler/src/diagnostics/registry.rs by packages/lumiose/scripts/gen-error-docs.ts. Edit the explanation below the end marker. -->

# LUM2003: Reactive early return

**Severity:** error · **Category:** reactivity (2xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> A sync component returns early based on reactive state.

**Reported by:** the compiler.

## What it means

The body of a sync component runs once, so `if (!user()) return <Login />` is decided once and
never re-evaluated: the component keeps showing whichever branch it took first.

## Example

```tsx
export function Account(props: { user: () => User | null }) {
  if (!props.user()) return <Login />;
  return <Profile user={props.user()!} />;
}
```

## How to fix it

Move the condition into the JSX, where it becomes a memoised branch:

```tsx
export function Account(props: { user: () => User | null }) {
  return <>{props.user() ? <Profile user={props.user()!} /> : <Login />}</>;
}
```

Early returns on props or values that never change are fine; async components may return early,
because their body re-runs.

## Related

- [Components](../concepts/components.md)
- [JSX: compiled idioms](../concepts/jsx.md)

# LUM2004: Component called as a function

**Severity:** error · **Category:** reactivity (2xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> A component is called as a function instead of rendered with JSX.

**Reported by:** the compiler.

## What it means

`{Card({ title })}` runs `Card` inside the caller: it gets no owner of its own, its props are not
reactive getters, and cleanups, context and boundaries attach to the wrong component.

## Example

```tsx
export function List(props: { items: string[] }) {
  return <ul>{props.items.map((item) => Item({ label: item }))}</ul>;
}
```

## How to fix it

Render it with JSX: `<Item label={item} />`. To choose a component at runtime, use
`<Dynamic component={X} … />`.

## Related

- [Components](../concepts/components.md)

# LUM2005: Children inserted twice

**Severity:** warning · **Category:** reactivity (2xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> `children` is inserted more than once.

**Reported by:** the compiler. A warning.

## What it means

`children` is lazy: each insertion evaluates it, creating a second set of nodes (or moving the
first). Components below are instantiated twice, with separate state.

## Example

```tsx
export function Tabs(props: { children?: JSX.Element }) {
  return (
    <div>
      <nav>{props.children}</nav>
      <main>{props.children}</main>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## How to fix it

Insert `children` once. To render content several times, accept a render function and call it in
each place:

```tsx
export function Tabs(props: { renderTab: () => JSX.Element }) {
  return (
    <div>
      <nav>{props.renderTab()}</nav>
      <main>{props.renderTab()}</main>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Related

- [Components](../concepts/components.md)

<!-- source: errors/LUM2006.md -->

<!-- Generated from crates/lumiose_compiler/src/diagnostics/registry.rs by packages/lumiose/scripts/gen-error-docs.ts. Edit the explanation below the end marker. -->

# LUM2006: Reactive index escapes its callback

**Severity:** warning · **Category:** reactivity (2xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> The reactive index of a `.map()` row is used outside its row.

**Reported by:** the compiler. A warning.

## What it means

In `{items().map((item, i) => …)}` the compiler makes `i` a reactive index that belongs to the row
and updates when the row moves. Storing it in an outer variable, or capturing it in a callback that
outlives the row, keeps a stale index.

## Example

```tsx
let lastIndex = 0;
export function List(props: { items: string[] }) {
  return (
    <ul>
      {props.items.map((item, i) => {
        lastIndex = i;
        return <li>{item}</li>;
      })}
    </ul>
  );
}
```

## How to fix it

Use the index only inside the row's JSX and handlers. To remember a position, store the item (or
its key) and look it up when needed.

**Not reported** when the list maps a module-level `const` array literal (also with `as const`)
that the module never changes: no reassignment, no `X[i] = …`, no `push`, `sort`, `splice` or
other mutating method. Its rows never move, so reading the index once is safe:

```tsx
const CHANNELS = [{ name: "pulse" }, { name: "wave" }] as const;
export function Mixer() {
  return (
    <ul>
      {CHANNELS.map((info, i) => {
        const ch = i; // stable: CHANNELS never changes
        return (
          <li>
            {info.name} {ch}
          </li>
        );
      })}
    </ul>
  );
}
```

## Related

- [JSX: compiled idioms](../concepts/jsx.md)

<!-- source: errors/LUM2007.md -->

<!-- Generated from crates/lumiose_compiler/src/diagnostics/registry.rs by packages/lumiose/scripts/gen-error-docs.ts. Edit the explanation below the end marker. -->

# LUM2007: Own signal read in an async body

**Severity:** warning · **Category:** reactivity (2xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> An async component reads a signal it created in its own body.

**Reported by:** planned (not reported by this version). A warning.

## What it means

Signals read in an async component's body are tracked, and a change re-runs the component. Signals
created in the body reset on each run. Reading such a signal in the body therefore re-runs the
component whenever it changes, and the re-run re-creates the signal with its initial value: the
update is lost.

## Example

```tsx
export async function Book({ id }: { id: string }) {
  const book = await fetchJSON<Book>(`/api/books/${id}`);
  const open = signal(false);
  if (open()) console.log("open");
  return <button onClick={() => open.set(true)}>{book.title}</button>;
}
```

## How to fix it

Read the signal in JSX, handlers or effects, which are tracked separately from the body. If the
value should survive re-runs, create the signal in a parent and pass it down.

## Related

- [Async components](../concepts/async.md)

<!-- source: errors/LUM3005.md -->

<!-- Generated from crates/lumiose_compiler/src/diagnostics/registry.rs by packages/lumiose/scripts/gen-error-docs.ts. Edit the explanation below the end marker. -->

# LUM3005: Unused scoped selector

**Severity:** warning · **Category:** styles (3xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> A selector in a scoped `<style>` block matches no element of its scope.

**Reported by:** the CSS compiler (`lumiose_css`), in `@lumiose/vite`, `lumiose check` and the language server. A warning.

## What it means

A scoped block only styles the templates of its scope (the file, the component, or for a block
nested under an element, that element's subtree). A selector whose classes, ids or tags never
appear in those templates cannot match anything: usually a typo, leftover CSS, a selector meant
for a child component, or one meant for a sibling subtree. The message names the scope, such as
"matches no element in the `<p>` subtree of component `Tree`".

## Example

```stsx
export function Card() {
  return (
    <div class="card">
      <style>
        .crad { padding: 1rem; }
      </style>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## How to fix it

Fix the selector or delete the rule. To style an element rendered by a child component, pass it a
`class` (class passthrough carries your scope) or use `:deep(.child)`. For classes added from
outside the scope at runtime, use `:global(.name)`.

JSX returned by a helper function is not part of a nested block's subtree, even when the helper is
declared inside the component and called from inside the styled element:

```stsx
export function Form() {
  const field = (name: string) => <label class="field">{name}</label>;
  return (
    <form class="form">
      {field("Title")}
      <style>
        .field { display: grid; } /* LUM3005: the helper's <label> is outside this subtree */
      </style>
    </form>
  );
}
```

Move the block to the top level of the file (a file-level block styles every element of the file),
or write the `<label>` inside the `<form>` instead of returning it from a helper.

## Related

- [Styles](../concepts/styles.md)

# LUM3008: Non-constant `$` reference

**Severity:** error · **Category:** styles (3xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> A `$name` reference in CSS does not resolve to a build-time constant.

**Reported by:** the compiler, in `@lumiose/vite`, `lumiose check` and the language server. The
reference is left in the CSS as written, which browsers ignore.

## What it means

`$name` is inlined into the CSS at build time, so the value must be statically evaluable: a
top-level `const`, a `const` of the enclosing component (blocks inside it only), or an
`export const` of an imported module, made of literals, template literals, arithmetic, other
constants and members of `as const` objects. The message says why a reference is not:

- a `let` or `var` binding, a parameter or a prop (`$props.pct`);
- computed by a call at runtime: a function call (`$space(2)`), `Date.now()`, a signal;
- an array (`$sizes.0` is not valid JS);
- not declared in the block's scope (a component's `const` read from a file-level block);
- an import whose module does not export the name, or could not be resolved.

## Example

```stsx
export function Bar(props: { pct: number }) {
  return (
    <div class="bar">
      <style>
        .bar { inline-size: $props.pct; }
      </style>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## How to fix it

Pass runtime values through a custom property:

```stsx
<div class="bar" style={{ "--pct": `${props.pct}%` }}>
  <style>
    .bar { inline-size: var(--pct); }
  </style>
</div>
```

For a build-time value, make it a constant: `const` instead of `let`, an `as const` object with
named keys instead of an array (`$sizes.sm`), and constant math instead of a call
(`calc($space * 2px)` with `const space = 4` ships as `8px`).

## Related

- [Styles: JS values in styles](../concepts/styles.md)

<!-- source: errors/LUM3009.md -->

<!-- Generated from crates/lumiose_compiler/src/diagnostics/registry.rs by packages/lumiose/scripts/gen-error-docs.ts. Edit the explanation below the end marker. -->

# LUM3009: Hyphenated `$` reference

**Severity:** error · **Category:** styles (3xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> A `$` reference is followed by a hyphen, as if the name contained one.

**Reported by:** the CSS compiler (`lumiose_css`), in `@lumiose/vite`, `lumiose check` and the language server.
The `$brand` part is not substituted either.

## What it means

References are JS expressions: `$brand-primary` reads `$brand` followed by `-primary`, which is
almost never intended (design-token names often contain hyphens).

## Example

```stsx
const brand = { primary: "#4f46e5" } as const;

<style>
  a { color: $brand-primary; }
</style>
```

## How to fix it

Use an object member: `$brand.primary`. Name constants in camelCase or nest them in an `as const`
object.

## Related

- [Styles](../concepts/styles.md)

<!-- Generated from crates/lumiose_compiler/src/diagnostics/registry.rs by packages/lumiose/scripts/gen-error-docs.ts. Edit the explanation below the end marker. -->

# LUM3010: Misplaced `<style>` block

**Severity:** error · **Category:** styles (3xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> A `<style>` block is in a position that has no well-defined scope.

**Reported by:** the compiler (and the scanner for some positions).

## What it means

A block's scope comes from where it sits. Valid places are the module top level and inside a
component's static JSX as a child of an intrinsic element or fragment, at any depth. Inside a
component element (`<Suspense>`, `<Card>`), inside `{…}`, a conditional or a `.map()` callback, the
block would be created or discarded at runtime, so it is rejected.

## Example

```stsx
export function List(props: { items: string[] }) {
  return (
    <Suspense fallback={<p>…</p>}>
      <ul>{props.items.map((item) => <li>{item}</li>)}</ul>
      <style>
        li { margin: 0; }
      </style>
    </Suspense>
  );
}
```

## How to fix it

Move the block into an intrinsic element of the component (it styles the whole component anyway),
or to the end of the file:

```stsx
export function List(props: { items: string[] }) {
  return (
    <section>
      <Suspense fallback={<p>…</p>}>
        <ul>{props.items.map((item) => <li>{item}</li>)}</ul>
      </Suspense>
      <style>
        li { margin: 0; }
      </style>
    </section>
  );
}
```

## Related

- [Styles: placement decides scope](../concepts/styles.md)

<!-- source: errors/LUM3011.md -->

<!-- Generated from crates/lumiose_compiler/src/diagnostics/registry.rs by packages/lumiose/scripts/gen-error-docs.ts. Edit the explanation below the end marker. -->

# LUM3011: `<style>` as the root or in an expression

**Severity:** error · **Category:** styles (3xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> A `<style>` block is the root of a component's output, or is used as an expression.

**Reported by:** the scanner and the compiler.

## What it means

A block is not an element: it renders nothing and only attaches CSS to its scope. `return
<style>…</style>`, `() => <style>…</style>` or `const css = <style>…</style>` therefore have no

element to attach to. (For tools, the block is masked to `null` so parsing continues.)

## Example

```stsx
export function Theme() {
  return (
    <style>
      :root { --accent: tomato; }
    </style>
  );
}
```

## How to fix it

Put the block inside the element the component returns, at the file top level, or make it global
in a layout:

```stsx
<style global>
  :root { --accent: tomato; }
</style>
```

## Related

- [Styles](../concepts/styles.md)

<!-- source: errors/LUM3012.md -->

<!-- Generated from crates/lumiose_compiler/src/diagnostics/registry.rs by packages/lumiose/scripts/gen-error-docs.ts. Edit the explanation below the end marker. -->

# LUM3012: Custom property set but never read

**Severity:** warning · **Category:** styles (3xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> A custom property is set in a component's `style` prop but no CSS reads it.

**Reported by:** `lumiose build` (`@lumiose/vite`), once every module is compiled, `lumiose check` and
the language server: another file's CSS may read the property, so the check is project-wide. Not
reported in dev. A warning. `lumiose check` and the editor count the style blocks of the project's
modules, the stylesheets under `src/` and the stylesheets and Lumiose modules that the project's
modules import.

## What it means

Runtime values reach CSS through custom properties: `style={{ "--progress": pct() }}` plus
`var(--progress)` in a block. A property that is set but never read with `var()` by any stylesheet
of the project does nothing: usually a typo or leftover code.

The check collects the properties set in `style` props (object keys such as `"--fill"` and
`--fill:` declarations of `style` strings, on elements and components) and the `var()` reads of
every stylesheet in the build: the style blocks of every Lumiose module, imported `.css` files
(also Sass, Less, …) and those of dependencies.

## Example

```stsx
export function Bar(props: { pct: number }) {
  return (
    <div class="bar" style={{ "--progres": `${props.pct}%` }}>
      <style>
        .bar { inline-size: var(--progress); }
      </style>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## How to fix it

Make the names match, or remove the unused property. Properties consumed by another component's
blocks or an imported stylesheet are not reported. A property read only by CSS outside the build
(a stylesheet in `public/`, or a `var()` built at runtime) is still reported: read it in a
block, or ignore the warning.

## Related

- [Styles: runtime values](../concepts/styles.md)

# LUM3013: `$` reference before its declaration

**Severity:** error · **Category:** styles (3xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> A top-level `<style>` block references a `const` declared after it.

**Reported by:** the compiler.

## What it means

Top-level blocks are masked into the module as statements that read their references, so a
reference before the `const` declaration would be a temporal-dead-zone error in the code
TypeScript checks.

## Example

```stsx
<style>
  .card { border-radius: $radius; }
</style>

const radius = "12px";
```

## How to fix it

Move the block below the declarations it references. By convention, top-level blocks go at the end
of the file.

## Related

- [Styles](../concepts/styles.md)

# LUM3014: CSS syntax error

**Severity:** error · **Category:** styles (3xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> Lightning CSS could not parse a `<style>` block, or could not minify or print it.

**Reported by:** the CSS compiler (`lumiose_css`), in `@lumiose/vite`, `lumiose check` and the language server.

## What it means

Blocks are plain CSS, compiled by Lightning CSS. A syntax error it cannot recover from (an
unbalanced brace, an unterminated string, an invalid at-rule prelude) stops the block from
compiling. The message is Lightning CSS's own and points at the CSS.

A `{` without its `}` is reported too, at the brace, although Lightning CSS closes the block at
the end of the `<style>`: the rules after it end up nested inside the unclosed rule, which is
rarely what was meant (`.a { color: red; .b { top: 0 }` styles `.a .b`).

Blocks nested more than 64 levels deep, or parentheses (functions, `:is(…)`, media conditions)
more than 16, are an error too: the block is left out of the CSS. The parser recurses once per
level, and nested math functions take time exponential in their depth.

## Example

```stsx
export function Card() {
  return (
    <div class="card">
      <style>
        .card { padding: 1rem;
      </style>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## How to fix it

Fix the CSS at the reported position. Sass syntax (`$variables` with values, `@mixin`, `@include`)
is not CSS; `$name` only reads JS constants. CSS nesting is supported.

## Related

- [Styles](../concepts/styles.md)

<!-- source: errors/LUM3015.md -->

<!-- Generated from crates/lumiose_compiler/src/diagnostics/registry.rs by packages/lumiose/scripts/gen-error-docs.ts. Edit the explanation below the end marker. -->

# LUM3015: Invalid CSS ignored

**Severity:** warning · **Category:** styles (3xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> Lightning CSS dropped an invalid rule, declaration or selector from a `<style>` block.

**Reported by:** the CSS compiler (`lumiose_css`), in `@lumiose/vite`, `lumiose check` and the language server. A warning.

## What it means

Like browsers, Lightning CSS skips what it cannot parse and keeps the rest: for example a rule
whose selector uses an unknown pseudo-class, or a malformed at-rule. The output works, but without
the dropped part, which is usually a typo.

An unknown at-rule is kept as written and reported too, except Tailwind CSS v4's (`@apply`,
`@reference`, `@theme`, `@utility`, `@variant`, `@custom-variant`, `@slot`, `@source`, `@plugin`
and `@config`), which Tailwind's Vite plugin processes after Lumiose (see
[Styles](../concepts/styles.md)).

## Example

```stsx
<style>
  .card { padding: 1rem; }
  .card:hoverr { color: blue; }
</style>
```

## How to fix it

Fix or remove the reported rule or selector (`.card:hover`). If it targets a newer browser feature on
purpose, check the configured browser targets.

## Related

- [Styles](../concepts/styles.md)

<!-- source: errors/LUM3016.md -->

<!-- Generated from crates/lumiose_compiler/src/diagnostics/registry.rs by packages/lumiose/scripts/gen-error-docs.ts. Edit the explanation below the end marker. -->

# LUM3016: Invalid `:global()` or `:deep()` selector

**Severity:** error · **Category:** styles (3xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> A `:global()` or `:deep()` selector is malformed.

**Reported by:** the CSS compiler (`lumiose_css`), in `@lumiose/vite`, `lumiose check` and the language server.

## What it means

`:global(sel)` leaves `sel` unscoped, and `:deep(sel)` scopes only the part of the selector before
it so that `sel` can match inside child components. Both need a selector argument, and a selector
may contain at most one `:deep()`, not nested in another.

## Example

```stsx
<style>
  :global { color: red; }
  .list :deep(.item :deep(.icon)) { inline-size: 1rem; }
</style>
```

## How to fix it

Give the pseudo-class an argument (`:global(.toast)`), and use a single, top-level `:deep()` per
selector (`.list :deep(.item .icon)`). For app-wide CSS, prefer a `<style global>` block.

## Related

- [Styles: how scoping works](../concepts/styles.md)

<!-- source: errors/LUM3017.md -->

<!-- Generated from crates/lumiose_compiler/src/diagnostics/registry.rs by packages/lumiose/scripts/gen-error-docs.ts. Edit the explanation below the end marker. -->

# LUM3017: Invalid CSS value

**Severity:** warning · **Category:** styles (3xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> A declaration's value does not parse for its property, so browsers ignore the whole declaration.

**Reported by:** the CSS compiler (`lumiose_css`), in `@lumiose/vite`, `lumiose check` and the language server. A warning; the CSS is emitted unchanged.

## What it means

A declaration without a value (`color: ;`, `color: !important`) is reported too: browsers drop
it. An empty custom property (`--x: ;`) is valid and is not reported.

Lightning CSS keeps a value it cannot parse for its property as written, and browsers then drop the
declaration: `color: notacolor`, `width: 10 px` (a space before the unit), `display: flexbox`. The
check runs after `$` references are substituted, so a constant that holds an invalid value is
reported at the reference, with the substituted value in the message.

It also covers grid track lists that browsers reject although each part is valid: with
`repeat(auto-fill, …)` or `repeat(auto-fit, …)`, every other track must have a fixed size (a length
or percentage, or a `minmax()` with one), so `2fr repeat(auto-fit, minmax(9rem, 1fr))` is invalid.

The check is conservative: values Lightning CSS does not understand yet but browsers may (`var()`,
`env()`, `attr()`, `anchor()`, `if()`, `color-mix()`, `subgrid`, newer keywords, vendor-prefixed
values, CSS-wide keywords such as `inherit`) are never reported, and neither are custom properties
or at-rule descriptors. Unknown properties are [LUM3020](LUM3020.md). A value it does not report can still be invalid.

## Example

```stsx
const brand = "notacolor";

<style>
  .card {
    color: notacolor;
    background-color: $brand;
    grid-template-columns: 2fr repeat(auto-fit, minmax(9rem, 1fr));
  }
</style>
```

## How to fix it

Correct the value against the property's syntax (`color: navy`, `width: 10px`, `display: flex`).
For an auto-repeat grid, give the other tracks a fixed size (`12rem repeat(auto-fit, minmax(9rem, 1fr))`)
or move the flexible track into the `minmax()`. If the value is valid newer CSS that is still
reported, check the configured browser targets.

## Related

- [LUM3015](LUM3015.md): invalid rules and selectors that Lightning CSS drops
- [Styles](../concepts/styles.md)

<!-- source: errors/LUM3018.md -->

<!-- Generated from crates/lumiose_compiler/src/diagnostics/registry.rs by packages/lumiose/scripts/gen-error-docs.ts. Edit the explanation below the end marker. -->

# LUM3018: Unitless number from a `$` reference

**Severity:** warning · **Category:** styles (3xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> A `$` reference resolves to a plain number where the property needs a length, angle or time.

**Reported by:** the CSS compiler (`lumiose_css`), in `@lumiose/vite`, `lumiose check` and the language server. A warning; the CSS is emitted unchanged.

## What it means

Numbers are inserted without a unit: with `const gap = 8`, `gap: $gap` becomes `gap: 8`. CSS
requires a unit on every non-zero length, angle and time.

- **Lengths:** Lightning CSS happens to read the bare number as pixels and ships `gap: 8px`, but
  that is not CSS, and the same constant stays a bare number where a number is allowed (custom
  properties, `line-height`), so the output depends on where it is used.
- **Angles and times:** there is no conversion; browsers ignore `rotate: 45` and
  `transition: opacity 200`.
- **Math functions:** `calc($gap + 1px)` and `min(100%, $max)` mix a number with a length, which is
  invalid, so browsers ignore the declaration.

Zero is fine (`margin: $none` with `const none = 0`), and so are properties that take numbers
(`line-height`, `z-index`, `flex-grow`) or unitless SVG lengths (`stroke-width`).

## Example

```stsx
const gap = 8;
const angle = 45;
const duration = 200;

<style>
  .card {
    gap: $gap;
    rotate: $angle;
    transition: opacity $duration;
    max-width: min(100%, $gap);
  }
</style>
```

## How to fix it

Multiply the constant by the unit, which folds at build time: `gap: calc($gap * 1px)` ships as
`gap: 8px`, and `rotate: calc($angle * 1deg)` as `rotate: 45deg`. Inside a math function, multiply
in place: `min(100%, $max * 1px)`. For times, choose the unit: `calc($duration * 1ms)` or
`calc($duration * 1s)`; the warning has no automatic fix for them.

Or keep the unit in the constant: `const gap = "8px"`, or `` `${space}px` `` from a number.

## Related

- [LUM3019](LUM3019.md): a unit written after the reference with a space
- [Styles](../concepts/styles.md)

<!-- source: errors/LUM3019.md -->

<!-- Generated from crates/lumiose_compiler/src/diagnostics/registry.rs by packages/lumiose/scripts/gen-error-docs.ts. Edit the explanation below the end marker. -->

# LUM3019: Unit separated from a `$` reference

**Severity:** warning · **Category:** styles (3xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> A unit is written after a numeric `$` reference with whitespace in between, so it does not attach to the number.

**Reported by:** the CSS compiler (`lumiose_css`), in `@lumiose/vite`, `lumiose check` and the language server. A warning; the CSS is emitted unchanged.

## What it means

A `$` reference ends at the end of its name, so the unit must be separated from it: with
`const gap = 8`, `margin: $gap px` becomes `margin: 8 px`, a number followed by the keyword `px`.
CSS units must follow their number without whitespace, so browsers ignore the declaration.
(`$gappx` would read a constant named `gappx`.)

## Example

```stsx
const gap = 8;

<style>
  .card {
    margin: $gap px;
    padding: calc($gap px + 1px);
  }
</style>
```

## How to fix it

Multiply the constant by the unit: `margin: calc($gap * 1px)` ships as `margin: 8px`. Inside a math
function, multiply in place: `calc($gap * 1px + 1px)`. Or keep the unit in the constant:
`const gap = "8px"`.

## Related

- [LUM3018](LUM3018.md): a unitless number where a length, angle or time is required
- [Styles](../concepts/styles.md)

<!-- source: errors/LUM3020.md -->

<!-- Generated from crates/lumiose_compiler/src/diagnostics/registry.rs by packages/lumiose/scripts/gen-error-docs.ts. Edit the explanation below the end marker. -->

# LUM3020: Unknown CSS property

**Severity:** warning · **Category:** styles (3xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> A declaration's property is not a CSS property, so browsers ignore the declaration.

**Reported by:** the CSS compiler (`lumiose_css`), in `@lumiose/vite`, `lumiose check` and the language server. A warning; the CSS is emitted unchanged.

## What it means

Lightning CSS keeps a declaration with an unknown property name as it is, and browsers skip it, so
a typo such as `colr: red` silently does nothing. A property is known when it is in MDN's list of
CSS properties (standard, experimental, non-standard and obsolete ones) or Lightning CSS knows it.
When a known property is one or two edits away, the help names it and the fix replaces it.

Not checked: custom properties (`--brand`), vendor-prefixed properties (`-webkit-line-clamp`,
`-moz-…`), at-rule descriptors (`@font-face`, `@page`, `@property`) and names that are not plain
identifiers.

## Example

```stsx
<style>
  .card {
    colr: navy;
    backgrund-color: white;
  }
</style>
```

## How to fix it

Correct the name (`color`, `background-color`): the fix does it for close matches. For a value
you read with `var()`, name it as a custom property (`--card-color`). If the property is real but
newer than Lumiose's list, the warning is safe to ignore; report it so the list can be updated.

## Related

- [LUM3017](LUM3017.md): a known property with a value browsers ignore
- [Styles](../concepts/styles.md)

<!-- source: errors/LUM3021.md -->

<!-- Generated from crates/lumiose_compiler/src/diagnostics/registry.rs by packages/lumiose/scripts/gen-error-docs.ts. Edit the explanation below the end marker. -->

# LUM3021: Unsafe `$` constant value

**Severity:** error · **Category:** styles (3xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> A `$` constant used in a style block holds text that could end its declaration, its rule or the `<style>` element.

**Reported by:** the CSS compiler (`lumiose_css`), in `@lumiose/vite`, `lumiose check` and the language server. An error; the constant is not inserted.

## What it means

`$name` inserts the constant's value as CSS text into one declaration value. A value with `{`, `}`
or `;` outside a string, a `/*` comment, an unterminated string or a trailing `\` would end the
declaration or the rule and add CSS of its own, outside the component's scope; a `<` anywhere
(even in a string) could end the `<style>` element in the page's HTML. When the value comes from
data, that is an injection; even from the project, it silently breaks the scoping. So such a value
is refused.

## Example

```stsx
const accent = "red; } body { display: none";

export function Badge() {
  return (
    <span class="badge">
      New
      <style>
        .badge { color: $accent; }
      </style>
    </span>
  );
}
```

## How to fix it

Keep each constant to one CSS value (`"red"`, `"1px solid #000"`, `"\"Inter\", sans-serif"`). For
several declarations, use several constants, or set a custom property from a `style` prop and read
it with `var()`.

## Related

- [LUM3008](LUM3008.md): a `$` reference that is not a constant
- [Styles](../concepts/styles.md)

<!-- source: errors/LUM4001.md -->

<!-- Generated from crates/lumiose_compiler/src/diagnostics/registry.rs by packages/lumiose/scripts/gen-error-docs.ts. Edit the explanation below the end marker. -->

# LUM4001: Island component is not exported

**Severity:** error · **Category:** islands and boundaries (4xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> A component used as an island (`client:*`) is not exported from its module.

**Reported by:** the compiler.

## What it means

An island's server record names its module and export (`/src/Counter.stsx#Counter`), and the
browser imports that export to hydrate it. A component that is not exported cannot be imported.

## Example

```stsx
function Counter() {
  return <button>0</button>;
}

export default function Page() {
  return <Counter client:load />;
}
```

## How to fix it

Export the component: `export function Counter() { … }`. It may stay in the same file.

## Related

- [Islands](../concepts/islands.md)

<!-- source: errors/LUM4002.md -->

<!-- Generated from crates/lumiose_compiler/src/diagnostics/registry.rs by packages/lumiose/scripts/gen-error-docs.ts. Edit the explanation below the end marker. -->

# LUM4002: Non-serializable island prop

**Severity:** error · **Category:** islands and boundaries (4xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> An island prop (or SPA route data) is not serializable.

**Reported by:** `lumiose check` and the language server, at the prop, when its declared type cannot
be serialized; otherwise the server runtime, with the path of the offending value.

## What it means

Island props travel from the server to the browser as data-only JSON. Supported: JSON values plus
`undefined`, `NaN`/`Infinity`, `BigInt`, `Date`, `URL`, `Map` and `Set`. Functions, symbols, class
instances, promises and cycles cannot be serialized. SPA routes get the same rule for their data,
so `request`, `cookies` and `locals` are not passed in.

## At check time

With a `client:*` directive, the JSX types check each prop against its serializable form: a prop
whose declared type is a function, a symbol, a promise or an object with methods (a class
instance) only accepts `undefined`. `lumiose check` and the editor report the TypeScript error as
LUM4002 on the prop:

```text
src/routes/page.stsx:2:36 - error LUM4002: Island prop `onSave` is not serializable: it is a function. Island props are sent to the browser as data.
```

The same component without a directive is a server component and takes its props as declared.
Props typed
`JSX.Element` (slots), `unknown` or `any` are not checked; values TypeScript cannot see through
(a class instance without methods, a cycle) are still reported by the server when the page
renders.

## Example

```stsx
export default function Page() {
  return <Editor client:load onSave={(text: string) => save(text)} />;
}
```

## How to fix it

Pass data only. Do the work inside the island (it can call an endpoint with `fetchJSON` or post a
form with `submit()`), or convert values to plain objects before passing them.

## Related

- [Islands](../concepts/islands.md)
- [Data and actions](../concepts/data-and-actions.md)
