# LUM4003: Server-only module in a client graph

**Severity:** error · **Category:** islands and boundaries (4xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> Server-only code is reachable from the browser.

**Reported by:** `lumiose build` and `lumiose dev` (`@lumiose/vite`), when the client graph reaches a
server-only module: the build fails, and dev fails the module's request (the error overlay), with
the chain of importers from the client entry. `lumiose check` and the language server report it at
the import site, for the graphs of island components and of modules that import `lumiose/dom` (the
editor follows unsaved edits of open files). At runtime, server-only APIs
(`request()`, `cookies()`, `env()`, `renderToString()`, …) throw it in the browser build.

## What it means

`*.server.ts` modules (any `*.server.*` file of the project), everything under `src/server/`, and
the request APIs only exist on the server. Importing them into code that reaches the browser
(islands, SPA routes, client entries, and everything they import, directly or not) would ship
server code and secrets in the client bundle, or fail at runtime. Server code (pages rendered on
the server, endpoints, actions) imports them freely; stylesheets of `.server.stsx` files are fine.

Every way into the client graph counts: imports (static or dynamic, also `?raw` and `?url`), web
workers, and `new URL("./db.server.ts", import.meta.url)`, which would ship the file as an asset.
Files are matched by their real path (a symlink to a server-only file is server-only) and
case-insensitively; a sibling workspace folder outside the Vite root follows the same rule from its
own `package.json` folder. Dependencies in `node_modules` are not checked.

```text
LUM4003: src/server/db.server.ts is server-only, but client code imports it:
  src/components/Likes.stsx
  → src/lib/likes.ts
  → src/server/db.server.ts
```

## Example

```stsx
import { db } from "../server/db.server.ts";

export function Likes() {
  return <button onClick={() => db.like()}>Like</button>;
}
```

## How to fix it

Keep the server code on the server and call it over HTTP: expose an endpoint (or a form action) and
call it with `fetchJSON` or `submit()` from the island. In client code, read public config from
`import.meta.env.PUBLIC_*` instead of `env()`.

For the current URL, params and route in client code, import `url()`, `params()` and `route()` from
`lumiose/router` instead of `lumiose`. Those of `lumiose` read the request, so they are server-only
and throw this error in the browser; those of `lumiose/router` are reactive, follow client
navigations, and also work during server rendering.

Code that runs on both sides, such as a `defineState()` factory, may read request APIs only on the
server: guard them with `isServer` (`signal(isServer ? locals().user : null)`). The browser
receives the server's values. `isServer` is a constant, so client builds drop the guarded branch.

## Related

- [Islands](../concepts/islands.md)
- [Server](../concepts/server.md)
- [Data and actions](../concepts/data-and-actions.md)

<!-- source: errors/LUM4004.md -->

<!-- Generated from crates/lumiose_compiler/src/diagnostics/registry.rs by packages/lumiose/scripts/gen-error-docs.ts. Edit the explanation below the end marker. -->

# LUM4004: Browser API at module scope

**Severity:** warning · **Category:** islands and boundaries (4xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> A module that runs on the server uses a browser API at module scope.

**Reported by:** the compiler, for `.stsx`/`.tsx` modules: `@lumiose/vite` when it compiles a
module for the server (`lumiose dev` and `lumiose build` print the warning), and `lumiose check` and the
language server for every module except client entries (modules that import `lumiose/dom`) and `spa`
routes with `export const ssr = false`. A warning.

## What it means

Components are imported on the server for SSR. `window`, `document`, `localStorage` and similar
globals do not exist there, so touching them while the module loads crashes the server render.

## Example

```tsx
const saved = localStorage.getItem("theme");

export function ThemeToggle() {
  return <button>{saved}</button>;
}
```

Reported: `window`, `document`, `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, `navigator`, `location`,
`history`, `matchMedia`, `requestAnimationFrame`, `customElements`, `IntersectionObserver` and
similar browser-only globals, when they are evaluated at module scope. Not reported: code inside a
function (a component, an effect, an event handler, `onMount`) or a class, a `typeof window`
check, code guarded by one (`typeof window !== "undefined" && …`, `if (typeof document ===
"object") { … }`), and a local or imported binding with the same name. Plain `.ts` modules are not
analysed.

## How to fix it

Read browser APIs inside `onMount`, an effect or an event handler, which only run in the browser:

```tsx
export function ThemeToggle() {
  const theme = signal("light");
  onMount(() => theme.set(localStorage.getItem("theme") ?? "light"));
  return <button>{theme()}</button>;
}
```

## Related

- [Islands](../concepts/islands.md)
- [Signals: onMount](../concepts/signals.md)

<!-- source: errors/LUM4006.md -->

<!-- Generated from crates/lumiose_compiler/src/diagnostics/registry.rs by packages/lumiose/scripts/gen-error-docs.ts. Edit the explanation below the end marker. -->

# LUM4006: Hydration mismatch

**Severity:** error · **Category:** islands and boundaries (4xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> The DOM the server rendered does not match what the client renders while hydrating.

**Reported by:** hydration (`lumiose/dom/hydrate`, run by the island loader), as a console warning in dev, in two cases: the server HTML does not match the client render (the island is then rendered on the client instead), or an async component's await has no recorded value (the client awaits it again). In production there is no warning; the same fallbacks apply.

## What it means

Hydration claims server-rendered nodes in order. If the client renders a different structure (other
elements, a different branch, a different list length), or an async component's recorded await does
not match its replay key, claiming fails.

## Example

```tsx
export function Greeting() {
  return <p>{Math.random() > 0.5 ? <b>Hi</b> : <i>Hello</i>}</p>;
}
```

## How to fix it

Render the same output on both sides for the same props: move non-deterministic values
(`Math.random()`, `Date.now()`, `window` sizes, locale-dependent formatting) into `onMount` or
effects, or compute them on the server and pass them as props. Keep awaits in a stable order.

## Related

- [Islands](../concepts/islands.md)
- [Rendering modes: hydration](../concepts/rendering-modes.md)
- [Async components](../concepts/async.md)

<!-- source: errors/LUM4007.md -->

<!-- Generated from crates/lumiose_compiler/src/diagnostics/registry.rs by packages/lumiose/scripts/gen-error-docs.ts. Edit the explanation below the end marker. -->

# LUM4007: Non-serializable awaited value

**Severity:** error · **Category:** islands and boundaries (4xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> A value awaited inside an island is not plain data.

**Reported by:** the server runtime, with the path of the offending value.

## What it means

Values awaited in an island's async components are recorded during SSR and replayed during
hydration, so they are serialized into the page. A cached value (`fetchJSON`, `query(key, fn)`)
that an island awaited is sent once with the page, for the browser cache. A `Response`, a class
instance, a function or a stream cannot be.

## Example

```tsx
export async function Stock({ sku }: { sku: string }) {
  const res = await fetch(`/api/stock/${sku}`);
  const data = await res.json();
  return <p>{data.count}</p>;
}
```

## How to fix it

Await plain data: `const data = await fetchJSON<Stock>(`/api/stock/${sku}`)`. For `query()`, map
the result to plain objects inside its function. Remember that every value awaited inside an
island ends up in the HTML; never await secrets there.

## Related

- [Async components](../concepts/async.md)
- [Islands](../concepts/islands.md)

<!-- source: errors/LUM4008.md -->

<!-- Generated from crates/lumiose_compiler/src/diagnostics/registry.rs by packages/lumiose/scripts/gen-error-docs.ts. Edit the explanation below the end marker. -->

# LUM4008: Module-scope signal written during SSR

**Severity:** warning · **Category:** islands and boundaries (4xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> A module-scope signal is written during a server render.

**Reported by:** planned (not reported by this version). A warning.

## What it means

Modules are loaded once per server process, so a signal declared at module scope is shared by every
request. Writing it during SSR leaks one user's state into another user's page.

## Example

```tsx
const currentUser = signal<string | null>(null);

export function Header(props: { user: string }) {
  currentUser.set(props.user);
  return <p>{currentUser()}</p>;
}
```

## How to fix it

Define state that the page or its islands share with `defineState()`: its factory runs once per
request on the server (and once per page in the browser), and islands receive the server's values.

```ts
import { defineState, isServer, locals, signal } from "lumiose";

// Seeded from the request on the server; the browser gets the server's value.
export const currentUser = defineState(() => ({
  name: signal<string | null>(isServer ? (locals().user ?? null) : null),
}));
```

Request state can also live in components, props or context (`<Ctx value>` and `useContext`), or
in `locals` on the server. Module-scope signals are fine for browser-only state.

## Related

- [Sharing state](../concepts/state.md)
- [Signals and reactivity](../concepts/signals.md)
- [Server](../concepts/server.md)

<!-- source: errors/LUM4009.md -->

<!-- Generated from crates/lumiose_compiler/src/diagnostics/registry.rs by packages/lumiose/scripts/gen-error-docs.ts. Edit the explanation below the end marker. -->

# LUM4009: Unsafe URL blocked in a URL attribute

**Severity:** warning · **Category:** islands and boundaries (4xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> A dynamic value for a URL attribute would run script, so Lumiose rendered a placeholder instead.

**Reported by:** the runtime (`lumiose/dom` and `lumiose/server`), as a console warning in development.
The value is blocked in production too, without the warning.

## What it means

A URL attribute (`href`, `src`, `action`, `formaction`, `xlink:href`, `poster`, `data`, `cite`,
`background`, …) got a value from an expression whose scheme is `javascript:`, `vbscript:` or
`data:text/html`. Such a URL runs script in your page when it is followed, which is how injected
links turn into cross-site scripting. Lumiose writes `about:blank#blocked` instead, on the server
and in the browser alike (decision-29). The check ignores case, leading spaces and control
characters, and tabs or newlines inside the scheme, as browsers do.

Only dynamic values are checked. A string literal in your JSX (`<a href="javascript:void 0">`) is
written as it is.

## Example

```tsx
export function Profile(props: { website: string }) {
  // A user who saves "javascript:alert(document.cookie)" as their website gets a dead link.
  return <a href={props.website}>Website</a>;
}
```

## How to fix it

- Run code with an event handler, not a script URL: `<button onClick={save}>`.
- For user-supplied links, validate the URL when you store it, and accept only `http:` and
  `https:` (`new URL(value).protocol`).

## Related

- [Security](../concepts/security.md)

<!-- source: errors/LUM4010.md -->

<!-- Generated from crates/lumiose_compiler/src/diagnostics/registry.rs by packages/lumiose/scripts/gen-error-docs.ts. Edit the explanation below the end marker. -->

# LUM4010: Island reads context provided by the page

**Severity:** warning · **Category:** islands and boundaries (4xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> An island calls `useContext()` for a context that the page provides outside the island, so it gets
> the context's default value.

**Reported by:** the server runtime (`lumiose/server`), as a console warning in development, once
per island.

## What it means

Each [island](../concepts/islands.md) hydrates in the browser as its own root: nothing the page
rendered around it exists there, including the values the page passed down with a `<Ctx value>` provider. So
that the server HTML and the hydrated island agree, the island starts from a fresh root on the
server too. Its `useContext()` calls see only values provided inside the island, and otherwise the
context's default.

This warning means the page did provide the context above the island. The island does not see that
value, on the server or in the browser.

## Example

```tsx
const Theme = createContext("light");

export default function Page() {
  return (
    <Theme value="dark">
      <ThemeToggle client:load />
    </Theme>
  );
}

export function ThemeToggle() {
  const theme = useContext(Theme); // "light": the page's "dark" stays outside the island
  return <button>{theme}</button>;
}
```

## How to fix it

- Pass the value as an island prop: `<ThemeToggle client:load theme="dark" />`. Props are sent to
  the browser, so they must be plain data (`LUM4002`).
- Provide the context inside the island, in the island component or a component it renders.
- Share state between islands with `defineState()`: one instance per page in the browser, one
  per request on the server, with the server's values sent to the islands (see
  [Sharing state](../concepts/state.md)).

Contexts provided inside the island work as usual on both sides.

## Related

- [Islands](../concepts/islands.md)
- [Sharing state](../concepts/state.md)

<!-- source: errors/LUM4011.md -->

<!-- Generated from crates/lumiose_compiler/src/diagnostics/registry.rs by packages/lumiose/scripts/gen-error-docs.ts. Edit the explanation below the end marker. -->

# LUM4011: Non-serializable scoped state value

**Severity:** error · **Category:** islands and boundaries (4xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> A scoped state (`defineState`) that the page sends to the browser holds a value that is not plain
> data.

**Reported by:** the server runtime, with the path of the offending value, when the page sends the
state: the shell fails (the error page renders), or a streamed boundary keeps its fallback and the
error goes to `onError`.

## What it means

A state defined with `defineState()` that islands or SPA routes import is sent to the browser with
the page: the server's values replace what the factory creates in the browser, so islands start
from the same values the server rendered. Only the signals and stores the factory returns are sent,
and they must hold plain data, like island props: strings, numbers, booleans, `null`, arrays, plain
objects, `Date`, `Map`, `Set`, `BigInt` and `URL`. A class instance, a function or a promise cannot
be.

## Example

```ts
// lib/session.ts, imported by an island
import { defineState, isServer, locals, signal } from "lumiose";

export const session = defineState(() => ({
  // A class instance from the auth library: not plain data
  user: signal(isServer ? locals().user : null),
}));
```

## How to fix it

- Keep plain data in the state's signals and stores: `signal(isServer ? { id: user.id, name: user.name } : null)`.
- Derive the rest: computeds and functions the factory returns are not sent; they are created again
  when the factory runs in the browser.
- State that only server code uses belongs in a module that no island imports, or in a server-only
  module (`*.server.ts`): it is never sent.

Everything a sent state holds is visible in the page; never put secrets in it.

## Related

- [Sharing state](../concepts/state.md)
- [Islands](../concepts/islands.md)
- [LUM4002](LUM4002.md): non-serializable island prop

<!-- source: errors/LUM5001.md -->

<!-- Generated from crates/lumiose_compiler/src/diagnostics/registry.rs by packages/lumiose/scripts/gen-error-docs.ts. Edit the explanation below the end marker. -->

# LUM5001: Request API used during prerender

**Severity:** error · **Category:** routing and server (5xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> A request API is used while a route is prerendered: a `static` route, or an `spa` page with
> `export const prerender = true`.

**Reported by:** `lumiose build`, while it prerenders `static` routes and `spa` pages with
`prerender`.

## What it means

`static` routes (the default) and `spa` pages with `prerender` are rendered at build time, where
there is no request: no cookies,
headers, query string or `locals`. Using `request()`, `cookies()`, `locals()`, `response()` or
`url().searchParams` there (or `ctx.request`, `ctx.cookies` and `ctx.locals` in a static endpoint
or `headers(ctx)`) cannot work, and the build stops. Middleware still runs for prerendered routes
and may read the (empty) request; only route code is checked.

## Example

```tsx
export default function Home() {
  const theme = cookies().get("theme");
  return <h1 class={theme}>Home</h1>;
}
```

## How to fix it

Render the route per request: `export const mode = "server";` (for an `spa` page, remove
`prerender` or set `export const prerender = false`). Or keep the route prerendered and move the
request-dependent part into an island (in an `spa` page, `onMount()` or an event handler) that
reads it in the browser or calls an endpoint.

## Related

- [Rendering modes](../concepts/rendering-modes.md)
- [Server](../concepts/server.md)

<!-- source: errors/LUM5002.md -->

<!-- Generated from crates/lumiose_compiler/src/diagnostics/registry.rs by packages/lumiose/scripts/gen-error-docs.ts. Edit the explanation below the end marker. -->

# LUM5002: Invalid route file

**Severity:** error · **Category:** routing and server (5xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> A file under `src/routes` is not a valid route file.

**Reported by:** the route scanner (`lumiose check`, typegen, dev server).

## What it means

Route files use the Next.js App Router names: `page.stsx`/`page.tsx`, `route.ts`, and the
`layout`, `not-found` and `error` component files, plus `middleware.ts` (or `.js`) for folder
middleware. Any other file in `src/routes` is a colocated
module that the router ignores, and so is everything below a private `_folder`. The message says
which rule a route file broke, for example:

- a special file with the wrong extension: `page.ts`, `layout.ts`, `route.tsx` (an endpoint is
  `route.ts`) or `middleware.tsx` (folder middleware is `middleware.ts`);
- `src/routes/middleware.ts`: the app's middleware, which runs for every request, is
  `src/middleware.ts`; a `middleware.ts` in a route folder runs for that folder's routes;
- a Next.js special file Lumiose does not have: `loading`, `template`, `default` or
  `global-error`, a route file below an `@slot` folder (parallel routes) or a `(.)`, `(..)` or
  `(...)` folder (intercepting routes);
- an invalid segment folder (`[]`, `[a-b]`, `post-[id]`, a broken `(group`, unsafe characters), a
  rest segment that is not the last one, or a param used twice;
- `export const mode` that is not a string literal of `static`, `server` or `spa`, or `ssr` that is
  not `true`/`false`, or `let` instead of `const`;
- `export const locales` that is not a list of locale literals, `"all"` or a function, or that
  lists a locale `lumiose({ i18n })` does not configure ([Internationalization](../concepts/i18n.md));
- a warning for an export that has no effect: `ssr = false` outside `spa` routes, `prerender`
  in an endpoint or in a layout or page whose mode is `static` or `server` (a `spa` layout's
  `prerender` applies to the pages below it), or `locales` without `lumiose({ i18n })`.

## Example

```
src/routes/blog/loading.stsx        Lumiose has no loading files
src/routes/@modal/page.stsx         Lumiose has no parallel routes
src/routes/api/route.tsx            an endpoint is a route.ts file
src/routes/middleware.ts            the app's middleware is src/middleware.ts
```

## How to fix it

Follow the `help` text. Show pending UI with `<Suspense fallback={…}>` instead of `loading`, use a
layout instead of `template`, rename the folder or file, and declare `export const mode =
"server";` with a literal. To keep a file next to the routes without the router reading it, give
it another name or move it into a `_folder`.

## Related

- [Routing](../concepts/routing.md)
- [Rendering modes](../concepts/rendering-modes.md)

<!-- source: errors/LUM5003.md -->

<!-- Generated from crates/lumiose_compiler/src/diagnostics/registry.rs by packages/lumiose/scripts/gen-error-docs.ts. Edit the explanation below the end marker. -->

# LUM5003: Duplicate route

**Severity:** error · **Category:** routing and server (5xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> Two route files produce the same URL pattern.

**Reported by:** the route scanner (`lumiose check`, typegen, dev server).

## What it means

Each URL must come from one file. Groups add no segment, a folder holds a page or an endpoint,
and an optional segment also serves the URL without it, so different files can collide.

## Example

```
src/routes/blog/page.stsx
src/routes/blog/route.ts                   both are /blog
src/routes/(shop)/cart/page.stsx
src/routes/cart/page.stsx                  both are /cart
src/routes/docs/page.stsx
src/routes/docs/[[...path]]/page.stsx      both serve /docs
```

## How to fix it

Delete or move one of the files. Param names do not distinguish routes: `[id]/page.stsx` and
`[slug]/page.stsx` in the same folder also collide. For an optional segment, drop the page that
duplicates it (`docs/[[...path]]` already renders `/docs`), or use `[...path]`, which needs at
least one segment.

## Related

- [Routing](../concepts/routing.md)

<!-- source: errors/LUM5004.md -->

<!-- Generated from crates/lumiose_compiler/src/diagnostics/registry.rs by packages/lumiose/scripts/gen-error-docs.ts. Edit the explanation below the end marker. -->

# LUM5004: Head or status change inside a streamed boundary

**Severity:** error · **Category:** routing and server (5xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> The status, headers, cookies or head changed after the SSR shell was sent.

**Reported by:** the server runtime.

## What it means

A `server` response starts with the shell: everything outside `<Suspense>`. Once it is sent, the
status line, headers (including `Set-Cookie`) and `<head>` are on the wire. Content inside a
streamed `<Suspense>` boundary that calls `response().setStatus()`, `setHeader()`,
`setStreaming()`, `cookies().set()`, `redirect()`, or renders `<Title>`/`<Meta>`/`<Head>` is too
late.

## Example

```tsx
export default function Product() {
  return (
    <Suspense fallback={<p>Loading…</p>}>
      <Details />
    </Suspense>
  );
}

async function Details() {
  const product = await fetchJSON<Product>("/api/product");
  return <Title>{product.name}</Title>;
}
```

## How to fix it

Decide status, headers, cookies and head content in the shell: in middleware, in `headers(ctx)`,
or in components outside `<Suspense>` (an async component without a boundary holds the shell until
it resolves). Keep `<Suspense>` for content that can stream.

## Related

- [Rendering modes: shell first, then stream](../concepts/rendering-modes.md)
- [Head and document](../concepts/head.md)
- [Server](../concepts/server.md)

<!-- source: errors/LUM5005.md -->

<!-- Generated from crates/lumiose_compiler/src/diagnostics/registry.rs by packages/lumiose/scripts/gen-error-docs.ts. Edit the explanation below the end marker. -->

# LUM5005: Non-GET method in a static endpoint

**Severity:** error · **Category:** routing and server (5xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> A `static` endpoint exports a method other than `GET`.

**Reported by:** the route scanner (`lumiose dev`, `lumiose check`, `lumiose build`).

## What it means

`static` endpoints (the default mode) are prerendered by `lumiose build`: their `GET` response is
written to a file in `dist/client`, such as `sitemap.xml`. A file can only answer `GET`, so a
`POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `HEAD` or `OPTIONS` export would never run in production.

## Example

```ts
// src/routes/api/subscribe/route.ts
export const GET: Endpoint = () => Response.json({ open: true });
export const POST: Endpoint = async (ctx) => {
  await subscribe(await ctx.request.formData());
  return new Response(null, { status: 204 });
};
```

## How to fix it

Serve the endpoint per request: `export const mode = "server";` (or set it on a layout of its
folder). Keep the endpoint `static` only if it serves `GET` alone.

## Related

- [Rendering modes](../concepts/rendering-modes.md)
- [Routing](../concepts/routing.md)

<!-- source: errors/LUM5006.md -->

<!-- Generated from crates/lumiose_compiler/src/diagnostics/registry.rs by packages/lumiose/scripts/gen-error-docs.ts. Edit the explanation below the end marker. -->

# LUM5006: Prerendered page that renders only in the browser

**Severity:** error · **Category:** routing and server (5xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> An `spa` page's `prerender` is `true`, set on the page or inherited from a layout, but its `ssr` is `false`.

**Reported by:** the route scanner (`lumiose dev`, `lumiose check`, `lumiose build`).

## What it means

The two options ask for opposite things. `prerender = true` renders the page's HTML at build time,
and the browser hydrates it. `ssr = false` renders the page only in the browser: the server sends
an empty shell and never loads the page's modules. The `prerender = true` can come from the page
itself or from the nearest layout that sets it. The `ssr = false` can come from the page itself,
from a layout above it, or from the project default `lumiose({ ssr: false })`.

When both are inherited, the error is reported once, on the deeper of the two layouts. When the
page sets `ssr = false` itself, it is reported on the page.

## Example

```stsx
// src/routes/layout.stsx
export const mode = "spa";
export const ssr = false;
```

```stsx
// src/routes/page.stsx
export const prerender = true;
export default function Home() {
  return <h1>Home</h1>;
}
```

A browser-only page below a prerendering layout:

```stsx
// src/routes/layout.stsx
export const mode = "spa";
export const prerender = true;
```

```stsx
// src/routes/editor/page.stsx
export const ssr = false;
```

## How to fix it

- **To prerender the page,** let it render on the server: remove `export const ssr = false`, or
  set `export const ssr = true` on the page. Then move browser-only code (`window`, `document`,
  `AudioContext`, `localStorage`) out of module scope and component setup, into event handlers or
  `onMount()`.
- **To keep the client-rendered shell,** remove `export const prerender = true`, or, when it
  comes from a layout, set `export const prerender = false` on the page (or on a layout between
  the two). A shell without params is already written to a static file by `lumiose build`.

`lumiose({ prerender: true })` together with `lumiose({ ssr: false })` is rejected by the plugin
for the same reason. With only `lumiose({ prerender: true })`, a page that sets `ssr = false`
stays a shell without this error.

## Related

- [Rendering modes](../concepts/rendering-modes.md#prerendered-spa-routes)
- [LUM5001](LUM5001.md): request API used during prerender.

<!-- source: errors/LUM5007.md -->

# LUM5007: Route param named `locale`

**Severity:** error · **Category:** routing and server (5xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> A route param is named `locale`, which `href()` reserves with `lumiose({ i18n })`.

**Reported by:** the route scanner (`lumiose check`, typegen, dev server), only with
`lumiose({ i18n })`.

## What it means

With `lumiose({ i18n })`, the router handles the locale prefix of every URL (`/es/about`), and
`href(pattern, { locale })` uses the `locale` key to pick the URL's locale. A `[locale]` (or
`[[locale]]`) folder would give a route a param with the same name, which `href()` could not
fill.

## Example

```
src/routes/[locale]/about/page.stsx     "/[locale]/about" has a param named "locale"
```

## How to fix it

Remove the `[locale]` folder: `src/routes/about/page.stsx` already serves `/about`, `/es/about`
and every other locale it declares with `export const locales`, and `locale()` reads the
request's locale. If the param means something else, rename it (`[lang]`, `[region]`).

## Related

- [Internationalization](../concepts/i18n.md)
- [Routing](../concepts/routing.md)

<!-- source: errors/LUM5008.md -->

<!-- Generated from crates/lumiose_compiler/src/diagnostics/registry.rs by packages/lumiose/scripts/gen-error-docs.ts. Edit the explanation below the end marker. -->

# LUM5008: Folder middleware covering prerendered routes

**Severity:** warning · **Category:** routing and server (5xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> A folder `middleware.ts` covers routes that are prerendered at build time.

**Reported by:** the route scanner (`lumiose check`, `lumiose routes`, the dev server and
`lumiose build`), once per middleware file, listing the prerendered routes it covers.

## What it means

Folder middleware runs whenever the app handles a route, the same rule `src/middleware.ts`
follows: per request for `server` routes, for every route in `lumiose dev`, and at build time for
prerendered ones (`static` pages and endpoints, and `spa` pages with `prerender`). Production
serves a prerendered route's file without the app, so its middleware never sees those requests.
That is fine for headers and the HTML it shapes at build time, but a check meant to guard the
route (auth, a feature flag, a redirect) protects nothing in production, although it seems to work
in `lumiose dev`.

## Example

```
src/routes/admin/middleware.ts       redirects visitors who are not signed in
src/routes/admin/page.stsx           mode "static" (the default): prerendered, served as a file
```

## How to fix it

Render the routes the middleware protects per request: `export const mode = "server"` in the
page, in a layout above it, or for the whole app with `lumiose({ mode: "server" })`. If the
middleware only adds headers or rewrites HTML at build time, move the prerendered routes out of
its folder, or let the warning stand.

## Related

- [Server](../concepts/server.md)
- [Rendering modes](../concepts/rendering-modes.md)
- [Routing](../concepts/routing.md)

<!-- source: errors/LUM5009.md -->

<!-- Generated from crates/lumiose_compiler/src/diagnostics/registry.rs by packages/lumiose/scripts/gen-error-docs.ts. Edit the explanation below the end marker. -->

# LUM5009: Boundary still pending when streamTimeout expired

**Severity:** error · **Category:** routing and server (5xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> A `<Suspense>` boundary was still waiting for data when `lumiose({ streamTimeout })` expired.

**Reported by:** the server runtime, to the `<ErrorBoundary>` around the waiting component (or to
the boundary itself), to `onRequestError` with phase `"stream"`, and to the server log.

## What it means

A page render waits for its pending `<Suspense>` boundaries for `streamTimeout`, 30 seconds by
default. When it expires, every async component still waiting fails with this error: the nearest
`<ErrorBoundary>` around it renders its fallback into the stream. A boundary with no
`<ErrorBoundary>` inside keeps its `<Suspense>` fallback. Then the response ends, so a data source
that never answers cannot hold the connection open. In production the `<ErrorBoundary>` fallback
receives a generic error with a digest, as for any error (the log has the original).

A response that does not stream (`response().setStreaming(false)`) waits for the same timeout; there
a boundary with no `<ErrorBoundary>` fails the page, as any error inside it would.

## Example

```tsx
export default function Dashboard() {
  return (
    <Suspense fallback={<p>Loading…</p>}>
      <ErrorBoundary fallback={<p>The report is taking too long. Try again later.</p>}>
        <Report />
      </ErrorBoundary>
    </Suspense>
  );
}

async function Report() {
  const report = await fetchJSON<Report>("/api/report"); // the service never answers
  return <ReportTable report={report} />;
}
```

## How to fix it

Find the data source that did not answer in time (`onRequestError` receives the route). Give it its
own timeout or cache, render an `<ErrorBoundary>` around the component so readers see a useful
fallback, or raise the limit with `lumiose({ streamTimeout: "60s" })`. `streamTimeout: false` waits
as long as the client stays connected. Prerendering ignores the timeout.

## Related

- [Rendering modes: shell first, then stream](../concepts/rendering-modes.md)
- [Server](../concepts/server.md)
- [`lumiose()` options](../reference/vite.md)

<!-- source: errors/LUM6001.md -->

<!-- Generated from crates/lumiose_compiler/src/diagnostics/registry.rs by packages/lumiose/scripts/gen-error-docs.ts. Edit the explanation below the end marker. -->

# LUM6001: tsconfig missing options required by Lumiose

**Severity:** warning · **Category:** tooling and config (6xxx)

<!-- end of generated header -->

> The project's `tsconfig.json` lacks an option that type checking `.stsx` files depends on.

**Reported by:** `lumiose check`, on the option's key in the tsconfig. A
warning: the check still runs, but some files are typed wrongly or not at all.

## What it means

`lumiose check` type-checks `.stsx` files through generated shadow TSX files in `.lumiose/shadow`
(spec §4.7). That only works when the tsconfig sets:

- `"jsx": "preserve"` and `"jsxImportSource": "lumiose"`, so JSX is typed as Lumiose JSX;
- `rootDirs` pairing the sources with their shadows (`["src", ".lumiose/shadow/src"]`), so
  `import "./Card.stsx"` resolves to the shadow. The warning also fires when `rootDirs` pairs only
  `src` but a Lumiose package the project uses (a linked workspace package) has `.stsx` files: they
  are outside the pair and are not type-checked;
- `include` covering `.lumiose/shadow` (routes and other files nothing imports) and `.lumiose/types`
  (route types);
- `types` containing `"lumiose/env"` (Lumiose's globals).

## Example

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": { "strict": true, "jsx": "react-jsx" },
  "include": ["src"]
}
```

## How to fix it

Extend the tsconfig that `lumiose check` generates, which holds all of these options and pairs
linked packages too (decision-25), and add your own options on top:

```json
{
  "extends": "./.lumiose/tsconfig.generated.json",
  "compilerOptions": { "strict": true }
}
```

Or set the option named in the message, as its help line says.

## Related

- [Compiler and tooling](../concepts/compiler.md)
- [JSX reference](../reference/jsx.md)

# Diagnostics

> Every `LUMxxxx` code the Lumiose tools report, with its long-form explanation.

Codes are stable forever and never reused. Print one with `lumiose explain LUM1004`, or open
`errors/LUM1004.md`. Each diagnostic carries `{ code, severity, message, span, labels, help,
fix?, docs }`; `lumiose check --format json` prints them.

## File format (1xxx)

| Code                  | Severity | Title                                |
| --------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------ |
| [LUM1001](LUM1001.md) | error    | Syntax error                         |
| [LUM1002](LUM1002.md) | error    | Unsupported by this compiler version |
| [LUM1003](LUM1003.md) | warning  | Scanner ambiguity                    |
| [LUM1004](LUM1004.md) | error    | Unclosed `<style>` block             |
| [LUM1005](LUM1005.md) | error    | Unknown `<style>` attribute          |
| [LUM1006](LUM1006.md) | error    | Raw CSS in a `.tsx` file             |
| [LUM1007](LUM1007.md) | error    | `await using` in a component         |
| [LUM1008](LUM1008.md) | error    | `<script>` in a Markdown file        |
| [LUM1009](LUM1009.md) | error    | Content nested too deeply            |
| [LUM1010](LUM1010.md) | error    | Source nested too deeply             |

## Reactivity (2xxx)

| Code                  | Severity | Title                               |
| --------------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------- |
| [LUM2001](LUM2001.md) | warning  | Stale derived value                 |
| [LUM2002](LUM2002.md) | error    | Signal write during render          |
| [LUM2003](LUM2003.md) | error    | Reactive early return               |
| [LUM2004](LUM2004.md) | error    | Component called as a function      |
| [LUM2005](LUM2005.md) | warning  | Children inserted twice             |
| [LUM2006](LUM2006.md) | warning  | Reactive index escapes its callback |
| [LUM2007](LUM2007.md) | warning  | Own signal read in an async body    |
